EURJPY TRADE Further explanation on the 3 phases I am looking to enter the next trend or major swing but I don’t know where or when the current trend is ending or going to end so I have to tread very, very carefully. You might say well stay out until the new trend is established and I do that also but doing it this way provides me with a stimulating challenge which also positions me with a profit base which gives me the financial platform and confidence to do what I need to do further along the trade. The long hammer was a sign that we are putting in a bottom – might not be the bottom yet, but the Queen is basically saying she has had enough. Each time I see a long bar, no matter what the type, I always expect an IB. I want to establish my long position with a view to riding it to the very end but I know it may not happen on the first try. Until the bottom is in, I know I have to be on my toes and react to any price action which tells me the bottom is not in yet. This first stage is the very high risk area (listen to the words of House of the Rising Sun/Honky Tonk Woman). In trading terms, it is the first sign of Distribution. The long tail is usually the big boys unloading their positions. In our train analogy, the train has reached it’s destination and passengers are getting off BUT new passengers, who may be on the wrong platform, are also getting on. The second stage is after putting in a bottom, where do we go from there? Do we go straight into the next trend? Do we go in to consolidation? Do we form a double bottom or ? We KNOW something is happening – we just have to look and watch for the signs to tell us what is happening. We need to be taking all long positions but we can start to give the trade more room to breathe and relax our stops a little and maybe ignore what we think are insignificant price reversal bars. The more signs the Queen gives us that she is on her new route, the more confidence we have with our trades. This stage is still risky with regard to loading up on positions but nowhere near the risk of the first stage. This is the stage we EXPECT something to happen so we have to watch very closely and analyse each bar and the bars around each bar relative to where price is at. Hence Sting’s “Every Breath You Take”. In trading terms, this is Accumulation where new buyers, particularly the big boys, are positioning themselves for the next phase or trend. In our train analogy, the passengers have got on, the train has left the station BUT we don’t know whether it’s going on the turntable or on it’s way to it’s next destination. The third stage is after the trend has established itself, gone through a test, and passed the test, thus proving that it is for real. At this point, we believe the trend is at it’s strongest and everybody and his uncle are buying into it. This can take many forms but is always evident when you look back in history. The key is to recognize it happening in real time before your very eyes. This is my “Fat City”. This is where the “Fill yer boots” trades are. Hence the Everly Brothers’ “ Bye Bye Love (Buy Buy Love!). In trading terms this is the beginning of Distribution. The big boys have suckered every one into it, the analysts and talking heads are telling everyone to buy, everybody and his uncle are now buying – while the big boys are starting to unload. This can happen in a sort of organized fashion as this trade worked out or it can be a blow off top or it can go into congestion. In our train analogy, the train has reached it’s final destination and is pulling into the station. Some passengers are jumping off before it stops (the big boys) while the others are still on board, some still sleeping from their long journey. I recognized the shooting star as my exit but since I had profits coming out of my ears, I thought I would give it a “Dr. Joe” which I don’t normally do (I hate giving the Queen my pay checks). I wanted to show that Dr. Joe’s method IS for real and DOES work. My gut feeling knew that my last trade was a loser hence John Lennon singing “You’re Gonna Lose That Girl” and “I’m A Loser” and sure enough, it was. The third phase is where I throw away all rules and trading discipline and go into a “balls to the wall, pedal to the metal, seat of the pants” trading style. It is VERY RISKY to trade like this. It is NOT recommended and will NOT be taught on this thread. You can only SUCCESSFULLY do this when you have reached the point where you feel “one with price” and are “dancing with the Queen and feeling her heart beat.” This is where I become a “bit better trader” both in growth and money. I have over simplified these three stages as they come in many different forms. This was a reasonably “clean” example which is why I chose to share it. Many times, the stages are not easily identified and run into each other but, for my method and my style of trading these are the three stages I am always looking for. It also allows me, after identifying the stages, to jump in at a later stage but then my trading strategies are different. Don’t think it is as easy as this because it is not. Many times I am stopped out for losses of 100 – 200 pips in trying to position myself for the long haul. Hope this answers your questions

Strat What are your thoughts on looking for positions coming into bank holidays etc? Or weekends come to think of it? Or is it a case of price action and volume regardless? The problems with trading during holidays are lack of volume and "skeleton" staff in the big boys. Lack of volume causes prices to be stagnant and directionless but the real problem is "unsupervised skeleton" staff at the big boys. Without supervision of their "head" traders, these guys can put through orders which may otherwise have been held for normal working hours, which can cause erratic moves in the market. Often times they will run stops just out of sheer boredom. If you pull up charts during holiday periods, especially the big ones, you can see long legged dojis all over the place. I will not initiate positions during holiday periods and will tighten stops if I am holding substantial profits. I will hold existing positions through weekends but generally do not like initiating new positions on a Friday unless it's a 'no brainer".

Break out trading can be BOTH very profitable AND losing. First of all, it depends on the pairs . USDCAD is pretty volatile - look at the long wicks and tails - also, the big boys know where the break out orders are and frequently drive prices there to suck everybody in - called false break outs AND stop runs. Second , it depends where the price is relative to the Daily and BOSS trends. If it's in a strong trend either way, then break outs above highs and lows are USUALLY very rewarding. BUT, in a situation like USDCAD where it is basically oscillating around 1.2200, it is a very risky game. If you draw in the 1.2200 line which is so very important to this pair, you can see that it has mostly acted as support. Add to this that the 150 EMA is also providing support. On this basis, you would expect support to hold and prices go North but it is not sufficient for me to put my account on the line. Third , if I was expecting a trip South, I still would NOT place a sell stop below that support because of my first argument. I would much rather let it close below that line and then RETRACE and TEST that line as RESISTANCE and sell from there. This is really where it separates the men from the boys or the amateurs from the Pros. The boys/amateurs want to jump in with all guns blazing and get in from the beginning and make a big kill. (Sounds similar to what you asked - right?). The men/Pros want the Queen to reveal herself (maybe show Baba G her grail) and confirm she means to go South (by way of the test of resistance). Yes, there is the possibility that you will lose some profits and yes, there is a chance that the move may be so strong that there may not be a test but at least YOU HAVE NOT LOST ANY $ . Usually, there is PA somewhere to get you into a strong move. So it all comes down to how far you have grown as traders. Can you excercise patience? Can you excercise discipline? Can you think like Pros? Can you think more about LOSING and less about winning? Always remember - we want to play WITH the big boys NOT against them NOR be their breakfast! Hope this helps, if not, ask again.

Dr. Joe does electronic trading – Part I I have promised this many people shortly after my first Dr. Joe post and started it a few times but could not get it finished because I couldn’t find all my notes, paperwork etc. The Easter recess has given me time to get some of my stuff together. From Dr. Joe’s visit to CME, we know a little bit about what went on in the Futures/Commodities pits at CME in the early 90s. Before we move on to the crazy 21st Century world of trading with electronic wizardry and gadgetry, we need to understand how we worked with our brokers at that time. In the late 80s and early 90s BC (Before Computers) when we were drawing our own charts, doing our own indicator calculations and drawing indicators ahead of charting packages, we had a similar mechanical order placing process. Once we had decided on a trade, we had to place our order with our broker. We would call our contact at the broker (or fax, in my case, when I was living and working overseas) and give him our trade. Even though the broker knew what we meant, we still had to speak “their lingo”, so we had to say something like “Account abc123, Long 1 March Deutschemark at 2.1020 or better”. The broker would then give us a ticket number which we recorded in our files. The broker would then send our order, now with a ticket number, to either their “runner” at the exchange who in turn would give it to their assigned trader in the pit, or send direct to their trader in the pit depending on the size of the broker. The pit trader would read the order and try and find a seller to take the other side of the trade. Remember, this is a ZERO SUM BUSINESS , someone wins and someone loses – always. The pit trader would find a seller with his “hue and cry” by screaming and shouting and waving his arms frantically until another pit trader screamed, shouted and waved back with a price. That price was then recorded on the ticket number and sent back to your broker. Now, depending on your broker and how big of an account you were at your broker, he would either call you back immediately with your “fill” or wait for later to do all his calls. So then hours later, in my case, I would be notified of my “fill” against my ticket number which was duly recorded in my files. Sometimes I wouldn’t get my “fill” until a day later and after receiving the previous day’s data. Talk about “trading blind” After receiving our “fill” we would then call the broker with our Stop Loss order. “Account abc123, Short 1 March Deutschemark at 2.0020 on a Stop.” When it was time to get out of our position, we had to do the same thing again. Call the broker, “Account abc123, Short 1 March Deutschemark at the market.” In those days, and still with Futures and Commodities, you had to take the opposite of your original position to Close your order. The same routine then happened with the broker and their pit trader until eventually, they would get back to you with your “fill”. Because of all this “mechanical” delay, your fill would be nothing like you expected and often times when you were expecting a small profit or break even, your “fill” would be at a loss. In those days, the “little trader” really got stuffed between the brokers and the pits because we were a “nuisance to them”. Our little “1 contracts” were a pain in the armpit to them and the pit trader would always put these “little” orders to the bottom of his pile while he focused on the huge orders from the “big boys”. Instead of adding an extra “1 contract” to the big boys’ fills, which would have been at far better prices, the pit traders would wait while they had cleared all the orders and then start on ours. This meant that we would ALWAYS get the worst fills – our fill price would always be far away from our original price. Trying to use Limit Orders was a joke for exactly the same reason and they would never get filled. We had to keep meticulous records because there were so many errors and mistakes in those days. Most of the errors would be on our part where we would have extra positions still open because we would have not closed our open positions correctly. This got real crazy when you were trading different currencies and commodities. Now fast forward to the 21st Century AC (After Computers). I am indebted to this information from a Professional Trader of some 40 years trading vintage who visited the CME Exchange many times through his golf buddies who were either floor traders or in some way connected with the Exchange. I thought this information was from a couple of years ago but when I eventually found my notes, it was from 2005. How I wish my trading account grew as fast as my idea of a couple of years did! His initial observation in visiting the Exchange was one of shock. He had seen the Exchanges and Pits on TV many times and thought he knew what to expect. Like all of us, I guess, he envisaged a very busy open pit for futures trading but what he didn’t expect was the size of the Exchange Floor with hundreds of people each sat in front of a wall of computers! On closer inspection, each Market Maker had 30 or 40 monitors on his “wall” all linked together so that he could access each individual screen with a touch of his mouse. He was just absolutely amazed that one person could follow what was happening on so many monitors as he personally, had difficulty following his 3 monitors and still retain his sanity! What really surprised him was that there were very few charts, sometimes none at all, on the monitors. What was on just about every monitor was price, price activity, buying and selling pressure and other information related to price. “What were these guys doing with all that information?” he wanted to know. Well, 10 years or so later from Dr. Joe’s visit, with the latest computer hardware, software, electronic wizardry and gadgetry, these guys are not doing anything any different to what Dr. Joe observed. They are WATCHING and REACTING to PRICE. The big difference now is technology. The data shown on each monitor is integrated and networked into other computers and their software which automatically responds to changes in volatility, bid and ask spreads , volume spikes and abnormalities, exceptional order quantities, institutional trades, Government Bank trades and everything and anything influencing price activity. For example, if volatility changed on a particular instrument, the percentage increase or decrease was immediately reflected in the Market Makers bids and asks automatically without any human input whatsoever. Similarly, and at the same time, if there were bids and asks which were incorrectly matched or “discounts” based on their software, trades were instantly and automatically initiated by the software based on the programming and parameters set by the Market Maker. The Market Makers have their plans programmed into their software so that when all the criteria are met, their software takes over and issues the trade. This then highlights the importance of the trading plan. Where ours is mechanical, theirs is fully automated. So, the bottom line has not really changed, the Floor/Pit traders/Market Makers are still “piggybacking” on what the market does – buy when price goes up and sell when price goes down – it’s just that now, they have very sophisticated computers and software to give them advanced notice and automatically place their trades for them. Understanding what we are up against, (the big boys with their sophisticated hardware and systems), confirms how difficult it is (not impossible) for the little trader and how important it is for us to thoroughly know and understand PRICE ACTION and trade WITH the big boys (not against them). In Dr. Joe does electronic trading – Part II, we will discuss the role Brokers and Exchanges play in Forex

PASR , whether you use it for day scalps, 2 or 3 day positions, swing trading or trend trading, will provide you with a method to consistently make money from the market. Learn it until you can do it with one hand in your sleep! Once you are consistently making profits, FOCUS your attention on LOSING . Forget about how much you will win, your consistency will take care of that. Instead, focus on how much you could LOSE on each trade you take. Doing this will filter out MOST of your losing and unprofitable trades. By doing this, you will become a more profit efficient trader. After you prove you can be a profit efficient trader, you can then move into the realms of where the BIG money is made in trading.

--- 帖子 #111 ---
There are also two distinct and very different aspects of trading involved in this: 1) Technical analysis 2) Trading psychology We need to blend these two together sensibly and logically if we are ever to have a chance in making money at trading. No matter how good we are in our technical skills, once we have our money "on the line" (and the more money - the greater the STRESS and pressure), our emotions, greed and fear , kick in and take over control of our trade. Remembering the lurker who PM'd me saying something like "Assuming I have my emotions under control.......", Yeah, right! BUT it CAN be done but you then have to draw on two other aspects of trading psychology - patience and discipline. This is why I keep repeating ad infinitum , success and making money in trading is 90% trading psychology. Therefore, my answer to this will always be from the trading psychology aspect BECAUSE we have to keep our emotions, specifically greed and fear, under control as best we can. The best way I know to do this is through a TRADING PLAN You PLAN THE TRADE and then TRADE THE PLAN . If you do this, you will ALWAYS keep your emotions in check and away from any decision making. There are, however, provisos in this: You must have your $/pip not only at your M % risk level but also at YOUR EMOTIONAL TOLERANCE LEVEL . It is no good having a huge trading account which allows you to trade $10/pip contracts if you are a huge EMOTIONAL BAG OF NERVES during the trade. Reduce your $/pip to a level that you feel comfortable with WHEN YOU LOSE . You must always define your RISK (LOSING) before even thinking about profits. Forget about thinking (and dreaming) how much you will win. Instead, think and ACCEPT how much you will LOSE . Forget about profits - when you are CONSISTENT over a long period of time (at the very least 1 year), your profits will take care of themselves. So, let's go ever a typical scenario: You see and recognise PASR , so you want to make a trade. FIRST - where does my SL go? How much will I LOSE if this goes against me? Do I ACCEPT the RISK (LOSS)? If Yes, next step. If NO - reduce the $/pip until you ACCEPT the RISK(LOSS) or DO NOT TAKE THE TRADE . This is CRITICAL and VERY IMPORTANT - you have to be VERY HONEST with yourself here - you MUST be able to say to yourself "THIS IS THE RISK I AM PREPARED TO TAKE ON THIS TRADE AND I WILL UNCONDITIONALLY ACCEPT THAT IT MAY BE A 100% LOSS" If you cannot do this then YOU DO NOT TRADE ! SECOND (and only after accepting the RISK(LOSING) ), where do I take PROFIT ? As discussed in an earlier post, put on 3 contracts and take PROFITS at either the first and second levels of S &amp; R as appropriate or in increments of 50 pips - which ever polishes your knob! On the last contract, you trail this behind a suitable level which you are comfortable with UNTIL you are either stopped out or you see a PASR REVERSAL bar So, this is now YOUR PLAN THIRD - Do I believe in my PLAN? Do I have 100% absolute faith in my PLAN ? If the answer to this is NO - make a NEW PLAN Do NOT trade until you UNCONDITIONALLY ACCEPT YOUR PLAN FOURTH - Plan accepted so place trades. Enter SL and TP levels FIFTH - Trade Management - You are trading the Daily time frame so no need to check your charts UNTIL after 5pm EST - NY close. -right, Dan? IF you have been HONEST WITH YOURSELF and accepted YOUR PLAN then there is NOTHING TO DO! You will either be stopped out for a LOSS - which you have already accepted and is no longer a concern for you OR You have to start taking PROFITS There is NOTHING ELSE FOR YOU TO DO "Ah, but what if something happens and I see the trade going against me, what then?" I hear our high school student say. FIRST - YOU SHOULD NOT BE MONITORING PROGRESS DURING THE DAY ON A DAILY CHART . If you are doing this then YOU STILL HAVE THE MENTALITY OF A SHORT TERM LOSING TRADER . You must GET SERIOUS and CHANGE YOUR TRADING STYLE. SECOND - IF YOU ASKED THIS QUESTION THEN YOU DO NOT BELIEVE IN YOUR PLAN and VERY, VERY IMPORTANT - YOU HAVE CHEATED YOURSELF - YOU HAVE LIED TO YOURSELF ! YOU EITHER BELIEVE IN YOUR PLAN - OR YOU DON'T - it really is that simple. So, my short answer is: PLAN THE TRADE &amp; TRADE THE PLAN

Right - Hanging Man and Inverted Hammer: Here is my take: Hanging Man: Despite what the "experts" say, I don't treat a Hanging Man as a reversal bar. I have been caught out too many times doing that, thank you!. Instead, I use it as "EARLY WARNING" that a top may be coming in. I always need PASR after a Hanging Man before I will trade. A Hanging Man tells me that the sellers sent out a scouting party and the buyers rejected it. However, the fact that they could drive prices down, tells me that sellers are positioning themselves and the buyers are looking to take profits. There are other threads and forums that recommend selling a 50% retrace of the Hanging Man bar - NOT FOR ME - I need to see the bars BEFORE it and the bars AFTER it, before I do anything. Yes, I might lose 100 or so pips in profit but more likely, I haven't lost anything. Inverted Hammer: The Inverted Hammer at the end of a downtrend is what a Hanging Man is at the end of an uptrend. So, for me, it is EARLY WARNING that a bottom may be coming in. Similarly, an Inverted Hammer tells me that the buyers sent out a scouting party and the sellers rejected it. However, the fact that they could drive prices up, tells me that buyers are positioning themselves and the sellers are looking to take profits. Again, there are other threads and forums that recommend buying a 50% retrace of the Inverted Hammer bar - NOT FOR ME - I need to see the bars BEFORE it and the bars AFTER it, before I do anything. Yes, I might lose 100 or so pips in profit but more likely, I haven't lost anything. The Path of Learning focuses on the two more important reversal bars: The Shooting Star and Hammer Learn these, practice these and demo these and become an EXPERT on these before playing any other candles. There are many successful and profitable traders for which these two candles are the BASIS of their method.

--- 帖子 #118 ---
The best advice I can give anyone starting out on The Path of Learning is, after learning the basics and PASR, is to take the two MAIN reversal bars, the Shooting Star and the Hammer, and only trade those signals until you know them inside out and the tricks they play. Forget about any others - they are a distraction - focus, focus and focus. Look on Daily, Weekly and Monthly charts - these are where you find the strongest and most reliable signals. I also recommend you start and keep a journal on each Shooting Star and Hammer trade focusing on those candles - where were they? how long was the nose, body, where did they close? what was the sequence of bars prior to the candle? what was the size of the candle relative to the prior bars? etc. Observe where the next bar is after the candle, where did it open? where did it go? what did it do? Observe the swing after the candle, how long did it last? how many bars? Of course, all this should be done within the context of trends. Within your journal, you should take a snapshot of the candle, the bar(s) after it and the swing after it. I see too many new and wannabe traders taking a trade and not really knowing why they took the trade and worst of all, not analysing their trades. The analysis of your trades reveal EVERYTHING about YOU and where YOU are in YOUR trading. Those that don't analyse their trades have NO CLUE where they are in their trading development. Even worse, are those that do not analyse their WINNING trades. The analysis of a winning trade is EQUALLY as important as the analysis of a losing trade. We need to know what we did right and why we did it.

--- 帖子 #121 ---
It doesn't matter what the time frame is - you should only make a decision AFTER the bar CLOSES. I thought I had made this very clear in my "Timeframes" post but obviously not. If you see a potential trade on the monthly and want to trade it then you have made the decision to trade the monthly. You can drop down to a lower time frame to fine tune your entry but your trade management must be on the monthly chart. If you manage the trade on the daily after entry then you are trading the daily NOT the monthly. A monthly bar consists of 20 daily bars so if you try to trade the monthly using the daily then there is a possibility of being stopped out at least 20 times whereas you would likely still be in the trade on a monthly. Trading the monthly is more INVESTING than trading and requires HUGE SL and tolerance for drawdown - unless I am mistaken, you are nowhere near that level.

DIVERGENCE: As a previous, biggest, technical indicator junkie, I used to think divergence was the key to the Magic Kingdom. In reality, it is the key to Davy Jones' locker! How do you know when prices are reacting to divergence? Is it that small retrace of a couple of candles or is it a trend change? No-one knows and certainly NOT a junk indicator! If you still believe in divergence, go to a strong trend such as the majors from July last year to the end of November and add any indicator which supposedly identifies divergence. PASR RULES PRICE ACTION - end of story By the way, there are way better indicators to identify divergence and NO , I'm not going to tell you or anyone because I have been 'INDICATOR FREE" for years now!

Most of my analysis is based on the CLOSE of bars or closing prices in general. Most of the time I disregard the tails and wicks on candles as being either over shoots by brokers or stop runs by MMs or both. Obviously, there is an amount of buyer/seller input in there but very small when compared to the body of the bar. I use my TLs to identify SWING SUPPORT and SWING RESISTANCE in addition to using them to gauge MOMENTUM plus other stuff too advanced for this thread. So, on your USDCAD Daily chart, if you want to follow my methods, you were correct to start that down TL at the close of the bar on March 9, I think it is. This identifies the level at which the buyers were prepared to go, for that particular swing. We then need to identify the next level the buyers kindly identified for us (or sellers, using their open), which is either the close of the Shooting Star on your chart or the open of the following bar. Project this down and where the buyers close on the next swing, gives you an indication of their strength, whether they are gaining strength or losing strength. That is enough to be going on with for now. See the chart I posted earlier on USDCAD

On one of my psychology posts, I wrote about a guy on another thread and Forum who was trading a proven M5/M15 strategy but, for the life of him, could not make money at it. I knew he was a young guy, and, having been there, knew that he couldn’t afford to lose money. I saw all the signs of a guy wanting more to be seen by his peers as being successful than a guy wanting to make money, so I observed him as best I could. After seeing him write, post after post, how many pips he had lost, I sent him one of my “do you know what you’re doing type PMs”. He politely replied and carried on losing. It got to the point that I TOLD him to STOP trading and evaluate what he was doing wrong. Undaunted, he carried on trading and posting his losses. I then told him I hoped he was on demo. He replied it was REAL money so I sent him PMs begging him and pleading him to STOP before he LOSES EVERYTHING. Eventually he stopped and I am very happy to say he is with me on my thread and doing really, really good. Anyway, I wanted to get inside his mind to understand why he kept on trading when he knew he was losing trade after trade so, he has kindly sent me his story. For anyone in a similar situation – STOP TRADING RIGHT NOW! I was first introduced to spread betting and by extension, trading, by a work colleague who had been experimenting for about 3 years and seriously making good profits for about 2 years (thus 5 years exposure in total). He used a 'recommendations' service which sent out internet alarms and SMS text messages with entry, stop, take profit levels and covered GBPUSD, EURUSD, USDJPY, USDCHF, Gold, Oil, FTSE &amp; Dow. He also liked to trade the news. It has been an ambition of mine for a few years to be able to work from home, cutting out commuting time and hassle as well as facilitating focused work time (ie no typical office 'interruptions'). I have not yet been successful in finding any potential employer with my same view (although at present I am lucky enough to have negotiated working from home every other week, which is a step in the right direction). I was therefore more than interested in any opportunity that might facilitate my earning a living from home, which this 'spread-betting' appeared to do. I therefore signed up to this recommendations service, watched the daily videos explaining the technical analysis behind the 'calls' and placed a few demo trades. Having got to grips with the trading platform, I was already for the news of a Bank of England interest announcement. As soon as the announcement was made I placed a GBPUSD and a FTSE bet, both @ £5 a point. I used common sense for the trade direction (a cut in the rate would mean a weaker £ against the $, so that was short and would make UK companies more competitive, so that was long). For the first few seconds I had difficulty getting my ticket filled, but as soon as it was I was straight into green and the value of my bet was increasing phenomenally. (No idea of a target of course) after the first 5 minutes the 'spike' settled down into a down move, straight past my entry and after 15 minutes right to the 'automatic' stop applied to all trades by the company I was using. I lost about £1,300 (of my £1,500 account) in 15 minutes. After 90 minutes price was back up where I had originally been filled &amp; rising. I told the story to my work colleague who explained that he used a 'straddle' strategy (ie orders both a bit below and a bit above the price just before the announcement). That way you were guaranteed your fill price, but you had to be quick to close 'the other side' once one of your trades had been opened. He also told me he used much tighter stops (about 20 points) and had targets set (at the previous swing high / low price before the announcement) thus he usually looked to get 50 to 100 points. Having witnessed for myself the speed with which you could make (or in my case, lose) money trading news, and now armed with the 'correct' strategy to be sure I was always on the 'winning' side and was limiting my loss with a tight stop, I was all prepared for the next announcement. Unfortunately what I hadn't realised was that the stop levels used by my spread betting company were dramatically increased around news time, so whilst I was unable to place the stop as tight as I would like, and in the panic of the move both my orders opened, one I made a really good profit on, and the other I lost even more) so net I was down. After a few months of this and the sometimes right sometimes wrong calls of the recommendations company I was making some &amp; losing some, net was probably slightly down. (I had reduced my stakes greatly, as I didn't want to put any more money into my account). I started to research the internet to see if I could find a better 'recommendation' company and came across a Forex Forum and was particularly fascinated by a 'trader' who was teaching others how to trade. Here there was much more about key price areas &amp; levels and a candle formation called a 'pin bar. I took what I could from this excellent free advice site (as a lurker) and started to only look for pin bars on the four hour timeframe. I found the massive stops a problem, but never the less, found trading opportunities and traded them, often making quite good profits, only to let them all go back to loss or break-evens, because my targets hadn't been made (I looked to get twice the number of pips as the pin was telling me to risk). Whilst I read a lot of 'it’s not the pin, its the position that is important' I never fully understood what this meant or how to apply it. About a year or so after my initial forays into the spreadbetting world I saw some posts on another thread titled 'its all about the pips'. Their concept was that by trading for an hour or so a day, if you made a consistent 50 pips you could make enough to live on and actually spend your time living your life. Well I was sold, that was exactly what I wanted to achieve, work form home and have more time to enjoy my life and do all the things I never have either the time or the money for. Not only that, but here was someone who was actually doing it and willing to teach others. This thread led me to another and from there I joined their “live trading room”. The first few weeks were indifferent, I didn't take many trades and lost as much as I made, however after a month or so I followed USDCHF short (for about five hours) which they had explained where they thought the take profit areas were. Instead of taking part profits off at these levels though I added small amounts. Thus when the final (fourth) target was hit, I had three times my stake all making profit, with minimal risk as at each stage I had protected the profits with my stop movement). That really gave my account a boost and re-confirmed my belief in the “live trading room”. I then wrote myself a plan, how many pips I need to make each day to be able to grow my account to a suitable size to be able to make up a sufficient fund to have the equivalent of three months net salary (safety net) and a trading account where risking no more than 2% per trade, if I maintained my daily pip target, I would make my current salary plus still be growing my account. If I lost on a trade, I HAD to make that trade back and then trade again to get my daily pip target. If I didn't get the trades in the live room sessions I HAD to keep an eye on the charts to ensure I got the moves 'out of hours'. --- 帖子 #138 ---
Remember, a price reversal bar has not failed UNTIL the OPPOSITE extreme price has been taken out. For example, the Shooting Star: This fails when the high price is exceeded. Until it's failed, it's still valid. The Hammer: This fails when the LOW price is exceeded. Until it's failed, it's still valid. The Hammer I had on my USDCAD is now a FAILED HAMMER since the low of the Hammer has been taken out. Breaking of price reversal bars with "thrust" or "momentum" is very good for our trading psychology as it gives us a nice "buzz" or adrenalin rush.

--- 帖子 #139 ---
The funny thing about PASR is that people seem to have trouble with both PA and SR. I liked Strat's post on hammers and I thought I'd share a couple of other views that might help someone to see it . First, my own view comes from years of trading pullbacks where I decide on the probable trend then wait for price to pull back (which increases liquidity for a further move) and then continues. What one is looking for in this type of trading is a micro-version of the big PASR. a) You want probable support for the pullback - and the SR part could come from the high that price just broke out of or from earlier swings back. Once you have a zone then you have a good probability that if you get PA then you will be rewarded for taking the bet. b) Then you want an indication that this SR will hold and the trend will resume. SR alone gives you X% chance of resumption and some people will trade that. SR + PA gives you X+Y% chance and thats what Strat is suggesting you wait for. When you have SR you know that the big boys will be thinking "here's where its worth getting in again so we'll start buying as it approaches SR." And some of them will. But until the PA is formed you don't know whether the buyers are winning over the sellers. When the PA is finished then everyone (good pa can be seen by most people) will be saying "the buyers are winning" so everyone will see that, if they want to get back into the trend they have to start buying now. Hence the momentum. So I am looking for something that shows that price rejected prices below support. It could be a hammer, a doji, a pinbar, or it could be a test and then a retest. But first comes a zone where "everyone" can see that price is likely to stop and move away. That gets buying from some. Then comes PA that shows that the buying has been happening and it seems to be winning over selling. And that gets commitment from others. And the clearer the PA, the more people know that they have to get in now or miss out ... and you get support from all those buyers. Anyway - that's my view of why what Strat is teaching is worth learning.

I will always set a realistic TP1 area which might not offer good R/R, but allows me to release capital back into my account and move my stop to BE, protecting my balance. Then if it continues in my chosen direction, great! I’ll manage my stop to lock in additional profit. I know this has the disadvantage of not allowing the market to naturally retrace, but I am very very reluctant at this stage to ‘give up’ profit back to the market, even if it is a simple retrace before continuing – I’ve taken almost maximum potential from that move and if it is going to pause before continuing on its way, then PA should give me an opportunity to board the train again. Another thing which has naturally developed and which I didn’t think possible for me when Baba G mentioned early on was that I don’t even think about number of pips anymore, but instead think in terms of % account growth, % account risk etc etc. For example, I took two trades last week (plus one ticket on AUDUSD which wasn’t filled), which gave me 6% account growth - I couldn’t tell you the number of pips involved. When I remember trying to trade the 15M and thinking I had to make so many pips a day/week etc I don’t know whether to laugh or cry! My account now stands, in 6 weeks, at 13% profit, with fewer trades yielding more profit. I’m well aware these are early days for me and I’m not naive enough to think I’ve cracked it, but as quite a few people have joined the Path of Learning recently, I thought I should share the positive difference which this thread plus Strat’s, Gianni’s, advice, have made to my trading. I don't even feel like I’m being 'patient' anymore; I’m not 'waiting' for trades, I’m just taking the right opportunities when they present themselves. No pressure, no stress. I understand for some who are used to trading lower timeframes, it can seem like PASR is never going to show its head on the daily, but it does, and when it does...happy days! Anyway, enough from me and I apologise if this seems like a ramble, but just thought I’d share my experience so far and extend my thanks to Strat and his team for their patience and support Dan

You have missed a huge chunk out of this. To trade for a living, you have to treat it as a business, right? Now if you were setting up a business, what do you need most of? Capital. It is exactly the same with trading for a living. You set yourself up with a MINIMUM of 6 months living expenses or equivalent previous salary (1 year is much better). This is so that you can live in the event you don't trade or make a profit. This is independent of your trading account. You do not pay living expenses out of your trading account! Instead, you sweep a certain % into your chequing account for that purpose. This frees you up from having ANY targets whatsoever. Your income from trading will reflect and parallel the market. When the market is trending we make really good money, when it's doing nothing, we make nothing. Overall, in the course of a year, we will have made lots of money but it will have come in cyclic bursts so that one month might be peanuts while the next month may be equivalent to 6 months previous salary etc. We have no targets, nor do we need targets - we just take what the market gives us WHEN it gives us - as simple as that. Having a MINIMUM 6 months "living account fund" to live off is what most wannabe traders forget or ignore - they only think about funding a trading account. Doing without this is a recipe for fast failure. Does this explain why we have no targets?

--- 帖子 #155 ---
Re-visiting the Hammer &amp; Shooting Star Price Reversal Bars; Bond Hammer &amp; Shooting Star: Remember Bond? When he got down to the nitty gritty, it wasn't the REAL thing! So it is with a Bond Hammer and Shooting Star. It may "look like" one but it's NOT. There are many reasons for this and remember I'm talking a perfect world, which as rookie traders, you need to learn. Hammer: The hammer MUST be at the END of a DOWNTREND. It MUST have a long tail that has gone searching below looking for more sellers BUT found a level at which buyers were now prepared to buy at. The Japanese called it a HAMMER because it hammered prices down (nailed it!) Considerations: A hammer that will not produce a SWING LOW is more than likely a Bond hammer. Be very careful of hammers in STRONG TRENDS. Think, the STRONGER the trend, the BIGGER and LONGER the hammer. Hammers fool many people in strong trends. Look at the Bond hammer on EURUSD on Oct 6, 2008. I remember many people on the threads getting excited over this as it appeared on just everybody's data. Lot's of people took a TICKET TO RIDE (Beatles 1965) on this and burned in hell! It was a Bond hammer because it "looked" pale and insignificant compared to the bars preceeding it, it had not found support. It just was not "man enough" to STOP a strong trend that had been roaring since mid July. Now look at the hammer on GBPUSD on Oct 24, 2008. See the difference? This "looked like" it could STOP the same roaring trend and it did - for a while. It found support AND the level where buyers were prepared to buy again. As I have said many times, after a strong trend and BIG hammer, I expect an IB and, Oct 27, 2008 duly obliged with a Bond hammer. This bar was telling us "I've had another go at selling for you, pal, but, those buyers are giving me a hard time so I'm going to take a bit of a rest". Now for those that like FIGHTING strong trends and COUNTER TREND TRADING, this IB gave you an opportunity to enter on a discounted price at the high of the IB. You would have to stay on your toes to manage it properly to come away with 600 pips or so. For an example of PERFECTION in a hammer look at AUDJPY on March 5, 2007. Isn't she beautiful and downright drop dead gorgeous? If only she would meet me every week! See also CADJPY on Jan 21, 2009 for another beauty. I purposely haven't put up the charts for these because I want YOU to go to YOUR charts and study this. Now, while you are dreaming of how much you could have made if you had been in on that trend, LOOK at the 20. SEE how POWERFUL it is. SEE how it HELPS you determine the trend. SEE how it tells you which side YOU should be on. SEE how it provides DYNAMIC RESISTANCE. SEE how it has turned around and is now providing DYNAMIC SUPPORT. Never, ever, under estimate the VALUE and POWER of the 20 (right, Dan?) Talking about trends, my favourite method of trading, if you are DETERMINED, PATIENT and can PERSEVERE and can demonstrate at least 3 years of consistent equity growth, then you will be qualified to work with me on this money making machine. Shooting Star: The shooting star is the opposite price reversal bar to the hammer The shooting star MUST be at the END of an UPTREND. It MUST have a long wick that has gone searching above looking for more buyers BUT found a level at which sellers were now prepared to sell at. The Japanese called it a SHOOTING STAR because it was SHOOTING for higher prices and got SHOT! Considerations: A shooting star that will not produce a SWING HIGH is more than likely a Bond shooting star. Be very careful of shooting stars in STRONG TRENDS. Think, the STRONGER the trend, the BIGGER and LONGER the shooting star. Shooting stars fool many people in strong trends. See AUDUSD on July 15, 2008 for an example of a shooting star at the end of a "stair stepping" uptrend - it is not perfect, but good enough. Note how it produces a MAJOR SWING HIGH. See EURUSD on July 19, 2002 for a shooting star at the end of a strong uptrend. Conversely, a Bond shooting star in a rally in an already confirmed STRONG DOWNTREND almost always works but always trade with caution - see AUDUSD on September 22, 2008 for an example. Now, what you are going to notice with shooting stars is that they will almost never look as powerful and strong at the end of a trend as hammers do. Why? You must never forget we are ALWAYS dealing with ENERGY and The Laws of Physics/Nature. Just like a ball at the top of a hill, it will roll faster down hill, WITH LESS ENERGY, than it will rolling uphill. In fact, it won't roll up hill WITHOUT ENERGY. It takes a lot of energy (BUYING PRESSURE) to roll a ball uphill (uptrend). At the TOP of the hill, The Laws of Gravity are no longer fighting us; they are now on our side and the ball (prices) fall with less energy (SELLING PRESSURE). If you don't know already, prices FALL FASTER than they rise. It is because of this that we can accept a less than perfect or maybe a Bond shooting star at the end of an uptrend providing it meets all our other conditions. However, you must always trade price reversal bars with caution. One other point: Price does not always need a hammer or shooting star type bar to reverse it's trend. There are many other bars and formations which form swings and major swings. I could write a book on this but that's all for now.

--- 帖子 #238 ---
Moving Averages You have to be careful with moving averages and not get fixated on them. Like all indicators, which are DERIVED FROM PRICE , they are lagging and not really useful, in and of, themselves, for initiating trades. They are useful as DYNAMIC SUPPORT and RESISTANCE levels in conjunction with PASR . You will find that each forex pair has it's own unique moving averages which PRICE responds to. At the end of each trading year, I have a computer wiz run a program he developed for me to determine which moving averages to use in my Strat Shadow for the coming year. This program identifies the most accurate and effective moving averages across all forex pairs. Where you see me using 100 and 250 or 200 or any other moving average it is because that particular pair is responding to such moving average. An example of this is one of Trogger's posts on my "old" thread where he commented about EURGBP responding to the 200 ema. My advice to members of the expired private website who wanted to specialise on one or two particular pairs was to find the moving average(s) which PRICE responded to.

Weekly Control Candles Please identify which you consider Weekly Control Candles I would also caution you that, while they are very powerful when used correctly AND in conjunction with PASR , they are not some "magical" identity which alone, will make you a consistently profitable trader. Make sure you UNDERSTAND PASR before trying to apply Weekly Control Candles . Another caution is that I developed them for members on the expired private website to identify consolidation and a trading range to help reduce whipsaws in trading. If not really UNDERSTOOD , Weekly Control Candles will stop you from taking ANY trades. You must remember that a weekly candle consists of 5 daily candles and on a volatile pair like GBPNZD, a weekly candle can be in excess of 1900 pips ! which is VERY TRADABLE on the daily time frame.

--- 帖子 #241 ---
From the "old" thread Power of Time Frames 1) We take our direction from the BIG BOSS (Monthly) 2) We take our direction (and sometimes trades) from the BOSS (Weekly) 3) We time and initiate our trades on the Worker (Daily) So, when we do an analysis of a pair or any financial instrument for that matter: We identify our SR levels We find out where the BIG BOSS is relative to ITS trend AND where it is headed in the SHORT TERM relative to ITS SR levels Knowing the direction of the BIG BOSS, we review the BOSS. If the BOSS is fighting the BIG BOSS, it will be very difficult to trade so we WAIT until the BOSS aligns herself with the BIG BOSS. With the BIG BOSS and BOSS now in harmony (both moving together in the same direction) we drop down to the Worker. We wait for the Worker to give us PASR in the direction of the BIG BOSS and BOSS. Rewarding and stress free trades come when we time the Worker JUST TURNING into the direction of the BIG BOSS and BOSS at PASR (as shown on the attached chart) The MOST REWARDING and STRESS FREE trade comes when you can time the Worker turning into the direction of the BIG BOSS at THE SAME TIME as the BOSS turns into the direction of the BIG BOSS. It sounds SIMPLE and it really is that SIMPLE but to make it stress free we MUST trade with PASR. Trying to guess trades is the best known way to blow an account. WAIT until you SEE all the following happening. Attached Image (click to enlarge) https://www.forexfactory.com/attachm...1&amp;d=1504038080 1

Strat, Reference to post 276 where it was said, "THIS SMALL DOJI IS A WCC". Can it be said that a WCC is any bar (called here first bar) that has one or many inside bars following it? The breakout signal occurs at the close of a bar that is higher or lower than the first bar. There are 2 types of inside bars. Wicks within first bar or body within first bar. We are concerned with the body being within the first bar. I've applied the same practice to WRBs which mighht still prevail but WCC open a tremendous number of signals. --- 帖子 #360 ---
A weekly control candle is not a candle only followed by an inside bar. An inside bar is a bar with the total candle (high and low) within the previous bar. The bar following a WCC can have a high and low outside the range of the WCC but cannot close outside of its range.

--- 帖子 #371 ---
PASR This is a quick summary I have 28 charts open on a Profile but I only really focus on the "movers and shakers" - those pairs which are volatile and have high ATR(10) pip count. I want my margin used up on those pairs which have the highest probability of moving. My daily routine starts with, and revolves around the BIG PICTURE analysis on the BIG BOSS. I check the Big Boss at the end of each month and especially the end of each Quarter and get a "feel" for where the Big Boys are taking PRICE. This is recorded for each pair. I always check when the Big Boss PRICE is approaching, or near or at Big Boss support or resistance. At the end of each week, I check where PRICE is with regard to support and resistance AND where and how it is moving with respect to the Big Boss. I check for Weekly Control Candles AND which SWING the Boss PRICE is in. Each day, I have "a good idea" which pairs should be moving and focus on them. I also check other high ATR (10) pairs in case they are moving. I check if the Worker is in harmony with the Boss. I decide whether a trade is basic PASR or trend trade. When I get to my laptop each morning around 6am - 6:30am Pacific Standard Time, I already have a "good idea" (from the above) which pairs will be trending on M5 so I check my M5 Profile. I look for London and New York to have created a trend that I can trade the pull backs on since being on PST, most of the trends are already fizzling out. I also focus on the highest volatile pairs on M5. It is much more involved than this but you should get a good idea from this to create your own style and routine

You are almost correct with the AUDUSD example. However last week's Boss candle is a POTENTIAL WCC and won't be confirmed until the end of this week. This week's candle high and low can break both the high and low of last week's candle but as long as it CLOSES within last week's candle, last week's candle will officially be confirmed as a WCC. IF it CLOSES above or below the range of last week's candle, then last week's candle did not become a WCC and this week's candle will start out as a POTENTIAL WCC until it is either confirmed or the following week CLOSES outside of its range and so on and so on.

--- 帖子 #390 ---
I don’t think there is one. Weekly control candles arent necessarily for trading. They can signify a period of congestion in a trend Or indicate a possible bottoming or topping out of the trend. If you want to look at how to trade them probably the best way is from the bottom to the top in an uptrend or possibly if you have an extremely long ranging Weekly candle perhaps going against the trend to the middle range of the candle. These are just some of the ways I might use them take the time to look at them where they are in the trend how wide apart or close together are the moving averages, So a weekly control candle is not a trading signal but there may be ways to trade it on occcasions.

--- 帖子 #402 ---
Weekly Control Candles ANY candle, followed by the next candle which CLOSED above the high or below the low of the ANY candle is an ENTRY SIGNAL - not just Wide Range Bars. As Rick (glyder) posted, and as I did in an earlier post, I did not develop Weekly Control Candles as an entry signal. I developed them to IDENTIFY consolidation and trading ranges. My advice was always to not trade the Worker when PRICE was within a Weekly Control Candle - essentially a "NO TRADE" zone for the Worker. The number of pips of the Weekly Control Candle determined whether a trade would qualify a trade on H4.

Hi Guys All this recent discussion regarding Weekly Control Candle brings back lot of memory form private site. WCC is very useful when price is at Top or Bottom, the WCCs in between are just pause in the market. So if you make a rule to trade when price is closed outside WCC then you will miss lot of solid trade. All the candles that closed outside previous WCC are potential WCCs, so just bewared when price is inside an established WCC. JC

Hi Terry MT4 have a built-in save chart function. First click "File" form the menu then selection "Save as picture" next make sure you click on "Active Chart (as is)" this way you only save the information on the current open chart. If you select "Active Workspace" then it will save the whole screen including your A/C number on the top right. I hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #653 ---
M5 timeframe Strange thing about M5, Wild Thing. They have always been "hard work" and too time consuming for me. I occasionally looked at M5 and then one time, after seeing a nice run in London time zone, I realised I was using the wrong strategy. I was using basic PASR when I should have been using Swing PASR - a bit like trying to ride a bicycle with square wheels. Then I got really frustrated because most of the big swings/trends happen during the London time zone and for me, being 8 hours behind London, there were no swings/trend left. Then, I realised my being 8 hours behind London was an ADVANTAGE! Instead of trading the trend, I could trade the pull backs as long as the trend was being continued by New York. This reduced my risk, increased probability and allowed me to load up on my positions and position size. On top of all that, it only takes a couple of hours because in most cases, the trend fizzles out and New York trades opposite to London. Usually I am done by 9 am and then its off with the Trouble and Strife to relax by the Ocean. I don't know what M5 looks like in KiwiLand but take a look

I got as far as snapping the charts, but didn't follow through with my update until now. Apologies. As you can see from the chart below, it did indeed keep going up to take out the next two targets. So, that's 4 closed for 50, 100, 240 and 380 pips for the 4 positions. My fourth position off at 192 even. My fifth position was the one I intended to let run - and run it did - by another 335 pips all the way to 195.359 according to my broker. Sadly, when I went to look for it at end of week (17Nov) with a view to close monitoring/closing position, well blow me down - it weren't there! Nice little bonus position gone begging cos I thought I had pushed the button but I hadn't (or an internet outage prevented the entry being processed). Attached Image (click to enlarge) Moral of the story. Don't get sloppy! Always check your entries (and get the hell out if you have the wrong pair, or you put 100 times the amount on that you actually meant to (yes,it happens! - so check!)) Anyway, a little miffed, as I had planned to keep one position to add to my long term longs that have been running for a year or more now. Second point I will make about trading the plan is this: My plan is always to re-instate any position closed out if I get the chance i.e. price returns to original entry level. For this reason, I did scan the charts periodically and I did identify trough "five" as it was forming and the bar shaded in lime below (I dare not call it a "pin"bar as I'll be the recipient of Strat's next serve if I do!). Attached Image (click to enlarge) I was tempted, but did not re-enter at this level as price had not fully retraced and trough three was lower than trough one AND peak four had not surpassed peak 2. My rules are not to add in this situation. So I didn't (thinking I would still have my position 5 to run- having still not checked my entries and blissfully unaware that no fifth entry existed!) I did "console" myself on realising my fifth position missing by "revenge trading"- firing off a couple of shorts (3 actually) at 195 one of which closed out quickly for 150 pips and the 2 remaining still open (shown on chart above). I do NOT recommend this approach (revenge trading) - far better to check your entries in the first place!

That pdf goes along with this quote: "There are 101 ways to be a bad trader. But they all stem from an inability to maintain an analytical, objective viewpoint of the market. During the stress of the trading day, objectivity is often benched and replaced by any of these: anger, fear, jeal- ousy, ambition, hesitation, uncertainty, overconfidence, lazi- ness, depression, and countless other emotions. You as a trader want to be objective, but when you are playing a high-stakes game, your survival as a trader is always at stake to a greater or lesser degree. If you manage to be wrong big enough or long enough, you are out of the game. It is not hard to see why it is easy to get into situations in which decisions are not grounded in reason and logic."---Peter Steidlmayer

--- 帖子 #1040 ---
Do you know that your way of thinking show signs of confirmation bias? My advice would be to find what does it mean and why it is not good for you On the very graph you show and praise, you would be stop out 4 more times, as attached. And those 4 times come from a fact that your "barrier" or effective stop levels are very wide. With narrower "barrier", you would be stopped out more like 8-10 times. In fact, on that very graph, you could forget about any psar-based stops, you could choose either previous major pivot or in fact any larger stop level (like 50p or 100p) and you would get much better result On top of that, you show a period with clearly trending market. Show period with ranging or volatile market and count your stop losses there Or even better show 1000 different periods and build conclusion based on that. You make conclusions about "power of psar" based on several setups on one trending graph? Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #1119 ---
Indicators """""Moving averages and candles are both indicators"""" Come on, now you're trying to pick fly shit out of the pepper pot! Yes, moving averages are derived from calculations BUT PASR does not use moving averages in the conventional way most use them AND saying candles are ""indicators"" is a bridge too far! A candle is a ""visual"" indicator, I will give you that BUT , it is NOT derived from a formula or calculations as are stochastics, RSI, MACD, CCI, Williams %R etc., etc and all the rest of the indicator JUNK are. A candle is derived from: OPEN PRICE HIGH PRICE LOW PRICE CLOSED PRICE All those PRICES are FACT and PURE and NON-NEGOTIABLE whereas the indicator JUNK are first, second, third and sometimes fourth DERIVATIVES of that PRICE and therefore, are as much use as a crack in a glass eye!

BASIC PASR Hello Rina, I can UNDERSTAND anyone thinking basic PASR is reversal trading BUT the point is, with READING, LEARNING and UNDERSTANDING PASR , what might be considered basic PASR many times turns into a swing , or better still, a trend . We trade basic PASR when we SEE PRICE is in a trading range BUT , PRICE has to, and does, BREAK OUT of that range to make new swing highs and lows AND minor and MAJOR highs and lows. While the reversal traders are ALWAYS looking for reversal levels of many descriptions, indicator crosses, indicator overbought and oversold levels, indicator tops and bottoms, divergence, heiken ashi candle colour changes, and certain candles, candle patterns, PASR traders are WATCHING and WAITING to SEE what PRICE does at these levels. Once we SEE PRICE ACTION in accordance with PASR , THEN and only THEN do we enter into a trade. Please advise if you still have questions

M5 While we trade M5 with PASR we have to do it faster and very efficiently. We don't have sufficient time at the Hard Right Edge (where PRICE is jumping UP and Down) to do a full 3 time frame analysis while we are scanning our M5 charts for potential trading opportunities. Having found a trading opportunity, we FIRST have to add our support and resistance lines from M15, H1 and H4. At this time, make a mental note of where PRICE is on each time frame RELATIVE to M5. At the same time, we are scanning other pairs and all this could happen while we are already in other M5 trades. To trade many M5 pairs at the same time is stressful and more difficult than trading the Worker so, after many hours of trial and error and frustrating losses, I decided to just trade the prevailing M5 trend and IGNORE any immediate change of trend. This changed my take home M5 profitability by greater than a factor of 10 while at the same time, reducing the stress. Remember also that I do not trade London because of my time zone and instead look for New York to continue the trend set by London. If the trend does NOT continue in New York, it is a NO TRADE - NO QUESTIONS ASKED for me and I look for another pair. I also limit my time on M5 to a couple of hours so I close out trades sometimes leaving lots of pips on the table but I don't care . The important trait on M5 is to NOT BE GREEDY . When your GREED emotions kick in, you MAKE MISTAKES and end up LOSING . As I have previously stated, I average about 375 pips per week JUST trading the pull backs to the prevailing M5 London/New York trend and at a standard lot per position, that is the same sort of money that professional doctors and lawyers make. This is only M5 and does not include trades on the Worker and Boss. Finally, we are all individuals even though we are trading the same method and strategy and have to DEVELOP our own style in accordance with our comfort zone and circumstances so keep on doing what is WORKING FOR YOU even if you trade the Corrective Waves as long as you have PLANNED your trade. When the market move, it has ebb and flow with two different legs in it.... 1. Impulse move: are longer legs that trades/moves in the direction of the Trend. 2. Corrective move: are shorter legs that trades/moves against the direction of the Trend. See attached chart. I believe this is one of the charts Strat was making reference to yesterday. If you can see, the prevailing trend is downdtrend, the uptrend is the corrective waves/moves gainst the prevailing trend - downdtrend, until the uptrend mature/change of trend to uptrend, is still corrective moves. Trust Strat, he will come up with the details... Happy Trading, Yomi.

--- 帖子 #1319 ---
Premature Extrication! Ah, the little people playing games - again. I used to suffer from this a lot too. I do not know if your problem arises for the same reason mine did, but, in case it does, I'll offer a suggestion: If the reason you are exiting early is because you are afraid of missing out on profit - any profit - or worse, you are afraid of missing out on any profit and afraid that price will reverse, eat your (partial) profit, hit your stop loss and leave you with a loss for the trade then: Try splitting your entry into multiple smaller lots and set a variety of partial profits on some of the positions. This will help placate the little people. (It also often lets you get back into the trade over and over again taking small profits multiple times before the actual run to the target S/R that you were initially targeting). If it doesn't reach you original target, you can still come out with a small profit or, at worst, a really insignificant loss.

--- 帖子 #1320 ---
Here is an example. I've posted this trade previously. Been in it since 20 November: Attached Image (click to enlarge) I'm waiting to see if price whizzes back down the CC or if it breaks. Either way, I'm perfectly happy (and will sleep well tonight!) as I have closed 3 of 5 trades within the green (CC) area. I'm collecting interest, so I don't really care how long it takes from here, but I do know that one of 3 scenarios will happen: (i) It breaks up - I'm happy. I have money on the table. (ii) It heads south but doesn't close below the green area: I'm happy, as I can look for re-entry. (iii) It heads south and keeps going south - and this trade is over. In this case, I get out - I'm still happy as I have some profit already booked and I look for the next trade.

Trap ... Ignored First, Frank, congratulations on reading and understanding! Those posts were from 2010 and what I was doing then was trying to make students trade conservatively by calling PRICE in a trap when it was in the Strat Shadow so that they would think twice about taking a trade. Since then, students have successfully traded PRICE inside the Strat Shadow so now I only advise caution when PRICE is "trapped" inside a Weekly Control Candle . That is all it is - a caution, advising us that PRICE is going sideways, whizzing up and down within a defined range. It does not mean do not trade. Experienced students do trade when PRICE is trapped inside a Weekly Control Candle and glyder posted one such trade a while back. I hope this clears up the misunderstanding.

--- 帖子 #1420 ---
Shooting Star Good! A Shooting Star makes a new high attempting to reach the next resistance area but fails to CLOSE anywhere near it. Additionally, the real body makes very little or no progress in the bullish direction and is small in comparison to the wick. What makes it a Shooting Star is the long wick and the failed attempt at closing near the new high . Attached Image It is very rare to SEE a Shooting Star and Hammer in a sideways (consolidation) range since the Big Boys have no defined trading direction at this point and PRICE is just drifting from the actions of retail traders. If you do SEE a Shooting Star or Hammer with their tails/wicks projecting beyond the specified trading range then take note as that could be the final push.

--- 帖子 #1654 ---
This is all about an individual's personal style of trading. Many traders will bring their Stop Loss to break even once their profit equals their Stop Loss. Many will use multiple positions and stagger their profits. Some will trail a Stop Loss. Some will just wait for some sort of profit target to be hit. --- 帖子 #1793 ---
GBPAUD H4 A few comments to help. The higher the time frame, the bigger the reward and with that comes bigger risk which pulls in BIGGER Little People! You might want to consider reducing your lot size so that your Little People have less to pay attention to. You might want to trade a la Wild Thing - put on several small positions and keep taking profits early to satisfy the Little People. Looking at your trade which was a 1:1 risk reward, it would have been better to place your Stop Loss at your entry (break even) instead of where you did. This would have kept you in the trade to reach your target. Also, you could have traded 2 positions and taken profit on the first where you did and moved your Stop Loss to break even on the second position to reach your target. There are many ways to execute trades with PASR - just experiment and find what YOU are comfortable with in making profits.

Here's my usd/yen trade from this week, any comments welcome. I shorted the bearish engulfing, seen by the arrow. My reasoning was, Big Boss and Boss down, worker in agreement. You can see a few days before, a counter trend bullish engulfing printed, and failed. i entered an order a few pips below the bullish bar on the 17th, and on the 24th the order was filled. My initial plan was to enter 3 positions, and take profit at 50, 100 pips, and run my final position to try and tp at 180 pips, just ahead of the next S level. I'm only up to page 150 of the other thread, and i think this was being recommended then. However, when the trade was open,i realised my plan had a flaw, in that to take profit at those levels, i would have to be watching during the day. For me the whole point, is to plan the trade, and then check it the following evening at the close. So i amended the plan. the next day, price had moved down, so i closed 2 positions out- 2x 0.75R. and moved stop to b/even. i let the last position run. the following day price went lower close to my t/p, before retracing. I must admit when i looked at that candle the next day and the lower wick, and where price was, those voices in my head started chattering..As Strat keeps pointing out, its the fear and greed, in this case fear of giving back profits, that did it. Still, i stuck with the plan, and next evening i'd been stopped out on the final position for a profit of 1.5R. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #1998 ---
EURCAD H4 You are doing good trying to find the time frame which suits your trading style, personality and circumstances BUT don't rush it. It will take several trades/days/weeks before you get the ""feel good"" feeling. Now onto EURCAD First, did you make a PLAN before trading? What account are you trading - live, paper or (please don't tell me) demo? Be very careful with Shooting Stars . Many Shooting Stars signal profit taking while others are reversal candles. UNDERSTAND the context of a Shooting Star in a strong trend compared to that in a Swing. When does YOUR candle close? My charts which CLOSE at 5pm New York time do NOT have any Shooting Stars and the difference is not down to broker feeds/data. both EURCAD and EURAUD showed an interesting sign of exhaustion on H4 This is not exhaustion . Exhaustion is a totally different condition. What you see are PRICE levels where SELLERS are interested in selling and where buyers are taking profits. This is not exhaustion. with resistances on the Boss and Big Boss Yes, this shows you are UNDERSTANDING the Power of Time Frames IF you are going to trade short off a Shooting Star, you need to drop down to a much shorter time frame - at least M15 or M5. "Why" you ask. Well, because ""WE"" don't know yet if it is just profit taking or the start of a new down trend. Doing this will get you in earlier and with a smaller stop loss and your ATR(10) will tell you how many pips to expect. Next, and this is probably THE MOST IMPORTANT , in addition to finding "your" time frame, you MUST find out what type of trader you are. This involves a huge dose of Trader Psychology. On this thread you have 2 TOTALLY OPPOSITE styles of trading PASR , both of which are consistently profitable . Wild Thing (trogger) enters trades with many small positions when he SEES and UNDERSTANDS PRICE at support or resistance. He does not necessarily wait for a trigger candle. He knows that due to his position sizing he can sit through draw down and take profit as PRICE hits his targets. He likes to have many small positions hitting several targets along the way to the next support/resistance level. He ALWAYS has a PLAN and Trades his PLAN . Me, I can no longer tolerate draw down like I used to so I can't trade like Wild Thing. I also don't like lots of small positions. I SEE the opportunity to trade and enter on half my normal position size, usually from a shorter time frame, as my "starter". When I SEE PRICE moving in my direction according to PASR , I add on with my full position size and keep adding on as long as PRICE is supported by the Strat Shadow. My style is more that of a Swing/Position trader. My M5 Strategy is totally different. When, AND ONLY WHEN, my strategy conditions are met, I enter immediately with my full position size (because the stop loss is so small) and add on at every pull back. I get out and take profit when H1/H4 support/resistance is hit or after 2 or 3 hours or less if the Trouble and Strife gets on my back! I am still a rebel/cowboy and sometimes enter trades because what I SEE looks like an opportunity. So, which style of trader are you? Yet because I moved my stop to BE, I got stopped out and only could watch the price continue without me. Usual rookie/newbie trader mistake - your Little People kicked in with their GREED emotions. Read everything you can find on Trading Psychology (TITZ) especially my posts. Again, find out what your style of trading is. Do you want to profit 20 pips on standard lot sizes (or bigger) or profit on many much smaller position sizes? This will give you an idea of where and when to move your stop loss to Break Even. Moving to Break Even when your PROFIT equals your RISK is the usual starting point.

--- 帖子 #2055 ---
WCC - weekly control candle It is a candle which closed above the high/below the low of the previous candle. The following candle is unable to close above the high or below the low of its previous candle. Simply put, there are three candles to look at, from right to left, 1, 2, 3: the current candle is number 3, which is unable to close higher or lower than the previous candle, candle 2. And candle 2 had a close above or below the previous candle, candle 1.

--- 帖子 #2067 ---
Hi malu, Thanks for helping me understand how you're thinking of it. Your understanding of WCC is almost right. When a weekly candle closes above/below the high/low of the WCC, that doesn't make the new candle a WCC. the following weekly candle must close within it's extremes for it to become a new WCC. Here is a quote from strat (post 247): "Remember that we can only QUALIFY a Weekly Control Candle with 2 weekly candles. The last CLOSED weekly candle determines whether the previous weekly candle is IN CONTROL or not." Let me know if this helps Edit: Catalin_eros also gave a good explanation on the previous page if what I said doesn't help.

M5 GBP/NZD This is how I played GBP/NZD Friday morning. I'm trading around the time I have in the morning between when I get up and leave for work and when I have available time at work, so keep that in mind. On this trade I jumped back and forth between the M5 and M15 to confirm my entries and exits. My M5 entry was not the cleanest but the M15 helped confirm. I saw 2 Doji style candles on the M5 and some longer wicks on the M15 relative to recent PA. With all this combined I used this as an entry. The Red arrow was my entry, but you also see with my trade on the chart. Also, the BETTER entry would have been at 15:40, take a look and you will see why. Attached Image (click to enlarge) My exit was again a combination of the M5 and M15 confirming that price IS at a point of support and price action was telling me to call it. I had an area of support at 1.9028, see my M15 chart Blue rectangles. The M5 had some longer tails at this area relative to recent price action and the M15 showed the same. I also have support and BRN 1.9000 and a little below that at 1.8969. Price did end up going a little lower but I'm ok with that as the chart already told me to take my profit. Attached Image (click to enlarge) I wanted to post this because Strats post above on GBP/JPY is the exact process I go through when I'm going through my charts. If i see something that looks right, ill go through the higher time frames and pick out the S/R coming up, the PA that's happening, and how much more room there is until we get to the next S/R. The more you can line up in the direction you're trying to trade, the better! Hope this helps anyone out!

GBPNZD H1 My apologies, I thought you meant the candle marked by my blue arrows BUT the answer is still the same - no. The reason for the "no" is that candle I have marked with my blue arrows . That is a long legged doji which tells us of indecision - the buyers and sellers have reached equilibrium/balance and have agreed on PRICE . Simply put, neither the buyers nor the sellers have any interest in moving PRICE in their favour. When this happens at resistance it usually, but not always, means the buyers have "run out of steam". This tells PASR traders to either find another pair or WAIT for PRICE ACTION to tell us what to do. In the event you failed to SEE that long legged doji, your RISK to Reward would only have been 1:1 and only 30 or so pips which would have had a low probability of profit since PRICE is already at resistance. I know you are new to PASR but try and think of the traders trading behind the candles instead of ""just candles"" Attached Image (click to enlarge)
