The two things that I feel I lack (and need) most are patience and common sense... It comes from many things but primarily from the artificial pressure of daily trading I put on my shoulders, as it were a job where you have to produce a certain output every day. This has brought me into a downward spiral which ended up costing me more money than I couldn't believe had someone told me I would lose. I would have said "Of course not, I would stop before that", but the same goes for any addiction I suppose. It has nothing to do with strategy or method, it has only to do with psychology. PASR is simple, accepting it is complicated, as it is complicated to accept many simple things in life, it has to do with agreeing to accept reality for what it is rather than for what you want it to be. I believe there has never been any work done on the psychological profile of FF members, but I think that many people are not here just because they are only attracted by the get rich quick magic formula, I think there is a deeper need that has to do with not accepting reality as it is and wanting it to coincide with our expectations, even if it destroys us in the process. This appears on many other areas of life, be it relationships, marriage, parent/child interaction, work, and some of these probably stem from what happened in an earlier period of their lives. To some extent, it is a form of perceived injustice that losing traders try to fight, not just on the market battlefield, but to vindicate them for other perceived injustices in other parts of their lives. But there is no injustice, there is only what there is, looking at it with our own eyes shouldn't change what it actually is. The same goes in life, there is no injustice, only reality that one must accept and adapt to as reality will never adapt to you, the same way the Queen will never adapt to your trading decisions. Successful traders have many traits in common, but one that stands out is that they don't bring their emotions/ego/traumas into the trading zone. They are at peace with themselves. That's what I will work on rather than honing any other, yet highly needed skill. It is harder for those who are already in their mature years as there is so much to unlearn, so much waste to throw out, before being able to bring in and accept new information. I guess that tells you I am no spring chicken. Finally, I believe Strat's advice on trading on higher timeframes is somewhat less about maximizing profit but more about maximizing life spent doing something else, because, the rarest and most limited asset we all have is time, and it flees fast. This is probably the most important thing I have said in FF in all these years, don't get too old to realize it. With that, I will give Strat his soapbox back, but I wanted to bring a more human touch to our daily interactions. Behind charts, analyses, and CAPS , we are all people . A great week end to all

IF you can keep your head when all about you Are losing theirs and blaming it on you, If you can trust yourself when all men doubt you, But make allowance for their doubting too; If you can wait and not be tired by waiting, Or being lied about, don't deal in lies, Or being hated, don't give way to hating, And yet don't look too good, nor talk too wise: If you can dream - and not make dreams your master; If you can think - and not make thoughts your aim; If you can meet with Triumph and Disaster And treat those two impostors just the same; If you can bear to hear the truth you've spoken Twisted by knaves to make a trap for fools, Or watch the things you gave your life to, broken, And stoop and build 'em up with worn-out tools: If you can make one heap of all your winnings And risk it on one turn of pitch-and-toss, And lose, and start again at your beginnings And never breathe a word about your loss; If you can force your heart and nerve and sinew To serve your turn long after they are gone, And so hold on when there is nothing in you Except the Will which says to them: 'Hold on!' If you can talk with crowds and keep your virtue, ' Or walk with Kings - nor lose the common touch, if neither foes nor loving friends can hurt you, If all men count with you, but none too much; If you can fill the unforgiving minute With sixty seconds' worth of distance run, Yours is the Earth and everything that's in it, And - which is more - you'll be a Man, my son!

Just pulling your plonker, Rub! Am I reading this correctly that we are only really interested in the support and resistance levels from big boss, it's just fine tuning them on the boss and worker? Yes and No. We always start with the Big Boss, then toggle that chart to the Boss and fine tune those levels on the Boss. Add any significant levels from and on the Boss missed by the Big Boss. Then toggle that chart to the Worker and do exactly the same thing INCLUDING adding any significant levels missed by the Big Boss and Boss. Pay attention to the latest levels on the Worker as these are the last and latest footprints left by the Big Boys. Here is an example of my trading chart for GBPUSD Big Boss - only 2 levels in cadetblue - one above and one below where PRICE is NOW Attached Image (click to enlarge) Boss - Fine tuned the cadetblue levels to the Boss data AND added significant levels in blue Attached Image (click to enlarge) Worker - Fine tuned all levels to the Worker data but NO NEED to add any more significant levels Attached Image (click to enlarge) Do not forget that the Strat Shadow provides DYNAMIC support and resistance levels as opposed to the static lines drawn above. Does this help?

--- 帖子 #2791 ---
The Power of Time Frames I don't know where it is in my "old" original thread Frank but here it is again. Ideally we want all 3 time frames, the Big Boss, Boss and Worker to be moving in the same direction (harmony). In reality this is not always possible because the shorter time frames are turning first followed by the next longest and finally the next longest. When all 3 time frames ARE moving in the same direction we have a ticket to FAT CITY ; in other words a strong trend. Because of the disparity in time frame candles, the Worker will turn first which will then turn the Boss which finally will turn the Big Boss. Do not think this is opposite to PASR strategy . The Worker can, and does, turn many times without turning the Boss. Remember, there are 5 or 6 Worker candles in 1 Boss candle. Similarly, the Boss can, and does, turn many times without turning the Big Boss (4 Boss candles in 1 Big Boss candle). This is the ranging and corrective nature of the Market. NOW, when the Worker turns the Boss which turns the Big Boss that is when we LOAD UP. You probably think that does not happen much so think again. The Boss and Big Boss can both be moving in the same direction BUT the Worker can, and often does, move in the opposite direction. This is what PASR traders WAIT for. That Worker move against the Boss and Big Boss is just a corrective move so WHEN the Worker turns around with PASR into the Boss and Big Boss direction we get on board. Does this help or has it confused you more?

NZDUSD Thanks for the memorabilia, Frank. This timeline must put you around 86 - a senior senior! Did you ever see or meet the great man? 1. First PASR where three legs of the shadow are up and in harmony. BUOB took rising boss and daily as well as 0.6973 support line. Yes, PASR traders would enter here. More aggressive traders would have entered on the green candle 6 candles earlier. But (1) gives us a smaller Stop Loss. 2. Bueb of doji the day before Christmas. no trading on Christmas. So we would have entered a buy stop above this candle 3. BUOB and took support at 0.7065. Yes, an add on 4. BUOB and support at 0.7161. Yes, an add on 5. Bar wick is rejected by 2 Resistance lines as are the next 3 bars. Close to Dr Joe's get out BUT Daily Shadow still up. This is a long legged doji telling us that PRICE is in balance/equilibrium meaning that the buyers were taking a rest and the sellers were not interested in selling at this PRICE . A pause in a strong up (down) trend is usually, but not always, an opportunity to ADD ON. 6. Bar wick is rejected by 2 higher resistance lines. Yes. This is a very important candle for PASR traders. This tells us that the buyers had a big push up to resistance where the sellers could not accept higher PRICES so the sellers started selling to take PRICE back down. 7. Daily shadow turns down signifying exit. While it is good to ""SEE"" this, it is of no use for actual trade entries/exits as it LAGS too far behind PRICE . It does however tell us of the buyers losing their momentum and interest. What happens after candle 6 is an attempt by the buyers to take PRICE back up to the previous resistance so that they can take profit. The next double top put in by a Shooting Star like candle is made by all those buyers who missed out on taking profit at resistance earlier. They drive PRICE back up to those levels where the earlier buyers took profit (resistance). After taking profit, they are no longer interested in buying and hand PRICE over to the sellers. The sellers are not really selling in strength as they are probably wary of buyers coming back in. PRICE falls due to gradual selling AND because there is no buying leaving PRICE to fall (as if by gravity). Thanks for posting for analysis.

Hi BeeCee, Thanks a bunch for your input. Regarding the boss trend, we always want to take a trade on the worker in the direction of the boss primary trend. Toward the last 15% or so of Strat's other thread, it becomes more clear on how to determine the primary trend. From what I've understood, the primary trend is in the direction of the latest swing, unless the swing occurs in a weekly control candle. Once price on the weekly closes outside the WCC, the primary trend is in that direction. And doesn't change until a swing in the opposite direction (not in a WCC) or a break of the WCC in the opposite direction. There might be more to it than that but that's all I've got so far haha. Many of Strat's examples from the other thread, I've noticed, is also trading in anticipation of a primary trend change based on pasr on the boss. --- 帖子 #3016 ---
This tells me you don't understand swings and the way PRICE moves. Since this is a Boss chart, the swings are controlled by the Big Boss. I have marked the major Boss swings in green . What you have marked with black arrows and called a "swing" is just the "waves" PRICE makes when it is moving. PRICE moves in IMPULSE WAVES and CORRECTIVE WAVES. The "swing" you have identified is a CORRECTIVE WAVE meaning PRICE is pulling back AGAINST the trend. On this chart, PRICE is in a DOWN swing so we are looking for ""possible"" fibonacci ratios to be in confluence with PASR to identify the next support. We are not looking to identify turning points within swings or pull backs. That last DOWN swing has already declared its intent with a High, Low, Lower High and a Lower Low forming. It is also showing an A-B-C formation with A and C being the IMPULSE WAVES and B the CORRECTIVE WAVE. So what would be the point in pulling fibs on a CORRECTIVE WAVE? That does not help us in any way to determine confluence for the end of the major swing down. One more point; over the years I have found fibonacci to be less important in PASR trading and ONLY use it for confluence. Keeping overall risk the same, e.g. 1% on 3 pairs instead of 3% on one, or if you want to take another trade a couple of days later maybe you can put one to break even. There was an excellent money management post I found somewhere a couple of years ago that ran down fixed fraction vs. fixed percentage vs. optimal f and a couple of others. Wish I could find it again! Risk management is very much a topic entire books have been written about. End of the day though you've got to find what you're comfortable with. EDIT: maybe have a look at your recent trades and try to see what made the best ones, then try to be more selective. I know sometimes I'll notice one currency being weak like CAD recently. Probably worth bearing in mind you're trading the relative strength of a currency pair. Hope that's got my thinking through clearly.

Difference Between Brokers Charts Beyond the Sea kindly recommended a UK broker to me that uses US closes on their candles and also has no Sunday candle following a question I asked over the weekend. I've loaded up MT4 this morning and copied my templates and layouts over to look at the difference and it's quite dramatic in places. I've posted the two AUD/JPY charts below for the daily and highlighted a few areas that to me are quite significant. I know we all need to SEE the trades on our own charts so I'm not advocating there is one chart to rule them all but find it interesting that I SEE something different (more clearly in many cases) on NY close charts. Maybe it's just my eyes, time to go to Specsavers again? 1. The lack of Sunday candles means on my screen I have data going back to May 26th instead of July 16th. Not a huge amount but it certainly helps seeing an extra 35+ candles. The big picture becomes a little bit bigger. 2. The ATR is dramatically different without a Sunday candle and using NY close. Not hugely important maybe but for those of us looking to ATR to assist with stops etc in the early days there is an extra 22 pips there. 3. The strat shadow is in different places and interacting with price differently (more accurately to my eye) in a lot of places. The NY close and lack of Sunday candles really seems to change things in some cases when price is at important levels. Look at the areas marked with arrows on both charts. Price action seems clearer and in some cases could well have got me in a day earlier on trades. More pips with more accurate data? you decide. To me theres seems now to be a lag on my old brokers charts now. e.g. price not closing below/above the strat shadow and signalling to me when on the NY close charts it would have stuck out like a saw thumb and got me in a good trade. We need to SEE trades ourselves and it's up to individuals to choose their own brokers and data providers but to me having now looked at these two versions of chart data side by side my decision is definitely the NY close charts. The devil is in the detail as they say. Hope this helps clarify potential differences in broker charts for any others early in their journey. --- 帖子 #3107 ---
Yep, IG is for retail gambling IMHO, but the less I say the better. It's been ages since I ditched them but I recall they quote a decimal place less than normal MT4 brokers (just check this). While you are on demo enter a position for each pair and pull your stop loss to 1 pip and write down what each pip value is worth on each pair (or 100 and divide the GBP amount by 100) i.e. GBPNZD will be 100 pips (which will now appear as 1000 because you are now on a 5 decimal place pair) 1 lot @100 = £516 / 100 = £5.165 per pip 0.1 Lot = £0.5165 pence Now just use your pip value to calculate your risk on each pair. It might sound a bit complicated but it's really not when you see what I mean (you'll just automatically drop the last digit in your mind and calculate your positions correctly). Watch out for GBPUSD it has the highest pip value, also commission on GBP pairs is higher. Hope this makes sense, you'll get the hang of it, use centre mouse button and left click to get a feel for measuring pips (or control F), I don't know if you are new to MT4? Just play around for a bit on demo if you are to get used to it before going live other wise you'll think an 10 pip stop loss is an 100 pip stop loss.....

--- 帖子 #3129 ---
While the SEC and CFTC and everyone else likes to claim, "The past is no indication of future performance," the truth is exactly the opposite. The past is a GREAT indicator of future performance. Your own system, relying on S/R and a few candlestick patterns uses PAST EVENTS in an effort to predict what will happen in the future (the next candle). My point is that bashing on other indicators for showing what happened in the past seems a bit unfair. Just because the indicators work off of a system different than your own doesn't make their usage wrong and/or incorrect. In fact, what if someone took your system and added MACD or some other oscillator to it to provide additional indication of overbought/oversold conditions as a confirming indicator that the bounce predicted by your system is indeed likely to happen? Or used an Ichimoku indicator to see that the bounce point predicted by your system matches up with levels there as a confirming indicator. My point here is that your system works fantastically for you because it's how you think. You keep it simple because for you that works better. However it seems like you are putting down people for having a different trading style or method simply because it isn't your trading style and method. I'm not even remotely suggesting that your method doesn't work. But to suggest someone else's doesn't or that they are overcomplicating or whatever seems unrealistic (unless you know the person isn't a winning trader). Something to consider

--- 帖子 #3140 ---
I came across this while I was looking for the book. It doesn't replace it but could help others along the way. The teachings are very similar to what Strat has been saying for years... I put in red what resonated with me "I just finished reading the book “ What I learned losing a million Dollars ” by Jim Paul and while reading it, I couldn’t stop making annotations and highlighting passages. As the title suggests, the book deals with the aspects of losing money in trading and the author BRILLIANTLY describes the components of losing and dealing with losses as a trader. The following 14 quotes and re-phrased passages are, in my opinion, vital to understand as a trader. Jim Paul and Brendan Moynihan used some great analogies and examples that show why trading is so different from other activities and how these unique characteristics make it so “easy” to lose money if you don’t know what you are doing: The potential of initial and temporary success only exists in trading. You can’t just call yourself a brain surgeon and get lucky while messing around in someone’s head. And just stepping on stage and trying to give a violin concert if you have never touched a violin before won’t end too well either. Right, wrong, win and lose are inappropriate terms for describing the participation in the markets. In 20/20 hindsight, decisions might be good or bad but not right or wrong. With regards to the markets, only expressed opinions can be right or wrong. Market positions are either profitable or unprofitable. There are as many ways to make money in the markets as there are participants. But there are only very few ways to lose . A light-bulb manufacturer understands that 2 out of 10 bulbs will not work; a fruit seller knows that some apples will be foul. Those losses are expected . In trading, we don’t expect to lose when we enter a trade . Unexpected losses are hard to deal with. Acknowledging that losses are part of the game and accepting the losses are two very different things. In trading, losses are treated as mistakes and from early on, we have been taught that mistakes are bad and have to be avoided . If you know exactly how much you are going to win, but don’t know how much you can lose, you are denying losses. Trading is an activity without a beginning and an end. In an activity without an end, you can always make decisions and change your decisions based on the current situation. A football game, a roulette spin or blackjack have defined beginnings and endings; after the game is over, you can’t change anything. You have to accept the outcome. It’s not open for interpretation; you (your team) have lost or won. In trading, the “game” (activity) never ends and your trade (potentially) never ends. Because your trade doesn’t end, your loss is never final and it could always turn around. Rules are hard and fast. Tools have some flexibility. Fools neither have rules nor tools . A scenario might have been an acceptable trade based on someone else’s rules . Profitable opportunities will occur that you won’t participate in. Your rules will only enable you to engage in some of the millions of opportunities. You can’t calculate the probability of having a winner. You can only calculate how much you are going to lose. All you can do is manage your losses and not predict your profits. People usually pick the exit point as a function of their entry point and it’s usually some arbitrary Dollar amount. People rationalize a trade idea by expressing the trade in terms of the money odd’s fallacy – “it’s a three to one reward-risk ratio! I’ll risk $500 to make $1500”. The reward-risk ratio gives no information about the likelihood of winning a trade. People who ask, “Why is the market up or down?” don’t want to know why. They only want to hear the reasons that justify their losing position . The last moment of objectivity for the roulette player is the moment before he places his bet and the wheels starts spinning. After that, he can’t do anything anymore to lose more money. For the market participant, the last moment of objectivity is the moment before he places his trade. But after that, he can still do a lot to lose more money. That’s why all your decisions and plans have to be made pre-trade."

PASR Must use my H4 charts more in future Don't go crazy with this! There are only two ways we want to use H4 in our Long Term, Stress Free Trading. When you are trading WITH THE TREND and identify a trade on the Worker, you may get a better R:R by dropping down to H4 for your entry and stop level. When you are trading AGAINST THE TREND from a trade identified on the Worker, drop down to H4 for entry and stop level AND manage it on H4. I have been both an employee and a business owner at different stages of my life, and the whole mindset shifts from looking busy to spending your resources wisely. --- 帖子 #3222 ---
From the above book I posted. "I started conducting poker seminars for players newer to the game. When I used hands I had played as illustrations, I would describe the hand up to the decision point I was discussing and no further, leaving off how the hand ended. This was after all, how I had been trained by my poker group. When we finished the discussion, it was jarring to watch a roomful of people look at me like I had left them teetering on the edge of a cliff." "Wait! How did the hand turn out?" I gave them the red pill: "It doesn't matter." I was thinking. This is exactly our mindset as traders as we faithfully operate our proven trading plan. The outcome doesn't matter. I think about a lot of things when it comes to psychology and trading. The outcome of one, five, ten or even twenty trades doesn't necessarily mean much. Small sample bias. This is one reason so many people thread hop. First two trades go awry and "This system sucks" is the attitude. I have met a number of traders over the years with bazar differences in how they trade. One guy looked for ten pips, would sit there and wait for his setup 10 full lots. He gave it all his profit to charities, just loved conquering the market and the man in the mirror. That is just one example. The point is we have to find our path. A path has been laid out before us which Strat has so graciously made available. It isn't a super highway, a path with all the distractions it has to offer. Lurkers toting their wares, the newest whiz-bang shindig indicator, fear, greed, or any number of things. At times it may seem I am teetering on the edge of a cliff....It doesn't matter; stick to the path, stick to the plan, put on 1000 trades. Someday the path will be my own super highway complete with fishing holes loaded with trout waiting for my fly. Ah well. A little how my mind works.

Strat, Fundamentally, you are 100% right on the merit of trading higher timeframes, and ideally the daily. I see that everyday now that, for the first time, I am starting to try and understand the meaning behind every individual candle and how it relates to higher TF structures. Even on successful 5mn trade days, 5mn trades are successful because, on a higher timeframe, there is a more meaningful PA shaping up or continuing. Who wouldn't like to be part of the real mouvement instead of scraping 30-50 pips daily killing your eyes in front of your screens? The sad thing is that this is where I come from. I wouldn't have looked below a daily (and sometimes weekly) chart when I was an equities trader (more of an investor really). Then someone told me about technical analysis, lower timeframes and the magic indicators that help you predict the future (he went bankrupt since then, no kidding). I am a recovering low TF trader, it is a daily struggle to get back the serenity I once had. Except that, at that time, I had the "comfort" of fundamental analysis, which worked as long as you had enough money (and SL levels) for the market to eventually agree with your fundamental analysis. I held some of my positions for 2-3 years before getting 300+% returns. Thanks to your teachings, I believe I now have something much more powerful as it is directly related to price. As for my hesitations to move to higher timeframes, I am at a specific period of my life where I have enough time to practice and enough value per pip to keep it interesting. This may change, but I want to see as many real time candles as possible, work on my psychology, learn and unlearn a lot of things that respectively I lacked and was poisoned by. I will endeavor to enter higher TF positions, but I still see my shortcomings and hesitations on 5mn and I first want to feel stronger before I take the next step. I hope this clarifies where I come from. I am sure we all have complex backstories, and this is just part of mine. Again, again, and again, you are a great trader but, more importantly, you are a good and generous teacher. Trade well D

--- 帖子 #3408 ---
PASR vs Indicators I realize that I need to adapt my trading behavior to PASR after years of indicator-led bad habits. Indicators always signal an entry late and, more often than not, you catch the middle if not the end of a move that PASR would have identified early on. As a result, quitting the habit of rushing to exit trades, instilled after years of bad entries at the wrong time, is something that is crucial to succeed with PASR. Now that I am working consciously on this, I feel my overall trading is changing. First, things are slowing down, my approach is more serene when I start to begin to commence to understand what is really happening in the market. Second, instead of trying to identify "perfect" candles, I try to understand the "intent" of the candles. A Hammer, a BEEB or anything else remarkable is the result of intent , the shape is the consequence, not the cause. Finally, I am starting to really appreciate the phenomenal gift Strat is sharing. His journey, the different steps to where he is now and the way it is documented, is phenomenal. I just wish I was part of his group when he launched his website but I will keep working, the journey is what really matters after all. Happy trading to all

--- 帖子 #3447 ---
The area of a price chart on the right hand side where the next bar will be printed. We trade this edge of the chart not knowing what the result will be. We place our trades with the price action on the Hard right edge. Hope that makes sense...to me it is the head of a nail when I strike it with my hammer.

Profit Pip Count Our Profit pip count is the TOTAL number of pips from all the positions traded. I took Yomi's 300 pips from his chart. Attached Image (click to enlarge) If you have one position with 5 lots and that position is for 50 pips, your TOTAL pip count is 250 pips. Each position and lot counts to the TOTAL number of pips. Lot size is totally dependent on the individual trader's Money Management and Trading Style.

--- 帖子 #3621 ---
This is the last one I will dig up from the bowels of this thread for today. There is so much here if traders will take the time to read. I have read the whole thing once. Now going through it in detail taking notes. From post #60 I just wish I could remember all this stuff! ""Long, long ago, when the world was young and I was a broker, I had to find trades for clients. I found a great many good trades, yet I noticed that people would find reasons to get out of them. So I started asking people when I had a good trade for them, if they would rather I was right, or whether they would prefer to make money. Yup, you read that right. And I acquired something of a reputation for eccentricity. But I have often seen that choice presented to traders in the subsequent 20 years. Are you going to trade based on your opinion, interpretations, indicators, or are you going to make money? The fact is, most traders have so many transactions, they can't keep track of what they think, much less what their trading plan is. There's too much pointless activity, and you have to cut down on that type of time wasting. But when you do that, and you start defining a trading plan and what you are doing, you're going to find two things: Number one is that frequently, regardless of your trading method, you are going to have a loss on a specific transaction. And as we all know, you get right out of those trades. No thinking required, no excuses...right? Number two is that when you are finally right, you will start thinking you are on a hot streak, cracked the code, can do no wrong....basically, you'll think you're the greatest thing since walking upright became popular. There's just one problem. You'll start thinking . When you have a loss , it makes sense to cut the loss . If you have acquired any maturity as a trader, then the concept of NEXT kicks in. Small loss, part of the game, yadda yadda, next trade . But when you have a profit , there isn't a next right away. You literally have to make a new decision every time you look at that trade. Stay in or get out? And the reasons for getting out will accumulate. You'll keep checking new indicators. You'll talk to people without a position in that market. You will literally keep searching until you have found a reason to get out of that profitable position. But here's the thing...you never control anything in a market except your orders. Do you really want to follow a trading plan that relies on you being right? Saying a trend is going to end and getting out of a profitable trade is fully as dangerous as saying a trend is going to start and you'll stay in a losing position until it does...and make back all your losses with interest or whatever. Because without large profitable trades, eventually even small losses will break you. This is what amateurs do . They think about being right. They dream about it. Professionals think about risk. They dream of new and better ways to calculate stops, get a higher percentage of profitable trades, anything that helps to make up for being wrong. I know of millionaires that will only trade mini contracts. They know how easy it is to be wrong. They know they *will* be wrong. They *count* on being wrong! But they also try to find ways to make money in spite of being wrong. A trading plan is *not* about what you think . It's about what will trigger you into a trade, ( selection ), how you will avoid losing money, ( cutting losses ), and MOST importantly of all, the whole point, the reason you trade, letting your profits run . Once you have a trading plan, none of these steps should require further thinking. If they do, you need a new plan. And if you know you need a new one, why trade with the old one? As you pointed out, staying in a bond or note trade late last year could have made up for two years of treading water for you. This is why you undertake risky trading activity. This is what the effort is for. Not high percentages. Not smaller losses. Huge, profitable, trades. But you have to let your profits run to get them. Whew. I'm getting carpal tunnel syndrome."" There's no substitute for experience.

--- 帖子 #3767 ---
It was more than 1:2, SL of 20 pips and TP of 50. So like 1:2,5. here is the reason to my madness: I looked at D1 and I saw that after the BUEB, yesterday closed as a HH/HL candle. That told me there were bulls in the market. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Then I looked at H4 and I saw a breakout of a range/ inside bars, and I love range breakouts. That told me there were bulls in the market. Attached Image (click to enlarge) And lastly, H1 showed the definition of the tend. That told me there were bulls in the market. Attached Image (click to enlarge) So three time frames showed bullish signs. To me, that is a sign that the bulls want the resistance broken. And about the R:R, it can be improved with add ons, because in a bull market, we can lift the SL with every add on that we make, while keeping the TP the same. Therefore the risk gets smaller and the TP remains big. For instance, I enter with a 20 pips SL and a 100 pips TP. Once price moves 30 pips, I get another entry signal and I add on, while moving the SL of the first position at +10 and the SL of the second position is at the same level as the first position, so now I have a +10 and a -20. Then price moves up 25 pips, I get another signal, I add on, and I move the SL of the first position at +30 (+10 and +20), which is the BE of the position 2, so now I have +30 pips secured from position 1, a risk free trade from position 2, and the third position has a SL of 25 pips. The TP remains the same, so if now my SL gets hit, my R:R is better, because I have a 45 TP distance left and a +5 pips SL (+30 -25). So initial R:R was 1:5 (20 SL and 100 TP), and now I have a R:R of 1:7 (5 SL and 45 TP). And if we want it more advance, we can also lift the TP, if we have reasons to believe the market wants to go even higher, and in this case the R:R sees another increase.

--- 帖子 #4215 ---
Hi Bestof, my understanding regarding WCC is the following: Close of the new (potential) weekly candle has to be above/below the high/low of the actual WCC. AND (so the 2nd condition) the following candle has to close within the high/low of the (potential) new WCC to confirm (qualify!) it. Then the (potential) WCC becomes the new WCC.

A few truths that I wish someone told me when I started: - You can only go where the markets wants to go, this is not a place where you can lead, but only FOLLOW. - But following also means that you can't be the last guy following, that's what PASR is here for. Do you want to be the guy who bought Bitcoin at 20,000$ just because your were following blindly a trend? - Don't be too hasty about making money. First, learn to not lose money, that's the only thing that will keep you fighting for another day - Once you have eliminated all the rookie mistakes that Strat teaches to avoid, don't think you can walk on water, you are just starting to crawl, which is better than what most wannabies manage to do - A trader is like a professional athlete that is not bound by age limit, so long as your mind is forged with discipline and determination, you can go on for as long as your body can permit. So, take care of your body as well - Money doesn't matter that much, you don't need to be a multi-millionnaire to be happy. So if you want to be a trader, make sure you are doing it because you are in pursuit of a higher objective. Trading must set you free, not bound you into a life you don't want. - We are domesticated as a species from an early age, we are expected to follow a certain process to live, earn a living, and die. You must understand that this doesn't necessarily apply here, you can't expect to have your cake and eat it too, so be prepared to be judged, not to be understood, and, above all, to shape a different life that what you were expected to live. - Learning how to trade is doable by everyone, it is not a talent but hard, psychological work. Forget any preconceived idea about fairness, justice, merit, none apply here. You will be dancing on the edge of a volcan at every trade, but you can rise like a phoenix every time you are burnt. That's called money management. - Life is short, it is your most precious capital

Trading Psychology Posting this again as it seems that if it does not have a chart or is not about making pips, then people do not bother to read it let alone ABSORB and UNDERSTAND it. This is one of the most important aspects in trading you will never see written or spoken about anywhere. Ignore it at your peril! What 99.9999% of people on these public trading forums don't realise is that they need their trading brain to be working at 100% efficiency at peak optimum power when they are trading. Anytime you use an indicator to do something for you, you LOSE trading brain efficiency and your trading brain becomes lazy and expects you to find other things so it doesn't have to work. The more you use and rely on indicators, EAs and other black magic crap, the slower and lazier your trading brain becomes until eventually it goes to sleep and you empty your trading accounts.

Random things I have learned by practising PASR over the last few days: 1) The trend really is your best friend. 2) Don't try and be a hero by trading reversals. Wait for the trend to be established and jump in after the pullbacks after confirmation with PA at minor support/resistance. 3) Location, location, location. The best locations to take a trade are major support and resistance. Not in no-mans land in between. 4) Keep an eye on the news calendar. Don't gamble and try to predict news. That's what amateurs do. 5) The market makers at the London open will often take price to the nearest support/resistance in search of liquidity for the big move of the day. I see this time and time again. Let them show their hand before entering. Perfect example of this morning on the USD-JPY. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Happy trading!

--- 帖子 #4565 ---
A trading simulator solves this problem. With a simulator, you can "forward test" historical data as though it was in realtime. I'm currently trading the EUR-JPY from 2012, for example. You can pause the action, place your S/R lines (without seeing the future), and then continue. There are several sims to choose from. Some free, some paid. Google it and/or search this forum. I'm sure you'll find what you're looking for.

--- 帖子 #4573 ---
First of all, don't draw S/R lines for the whole Big Boss chart, I would get lost in there! Only draw S/R lines for closest Support and Resistance levels relative to where the price is now. We don't care about 1.09 region if Price is at 0.75 right now, all those irrelevant lines will confuse you and WILL distract you (been there, done that). Try to pick the levels which are tested again and again, these are really strong levels that generate great PA setups. If price touched a zone once, waited a little and continued with its direction, I don't usually draw lines to mark such zones.

--- 帖子 #4607 ---
I guess what ever communicates to you. I used to put all kinds of "zones" on my charts and traded them with price action. What I now realize is that subconsciously the wide zone on the chart was acting like a mental wall. Then this mental wall made for a tendency to make price hitting it more of an event then it really was. The zones became more important than the price action. Remember with out price action the zones mean nothing. Subconsciously how you see the chart will determine what is best for you. For me now S/R lines are faint, this way it forces my mind to focus on PA. Hope that helps in your decision. Rufus

--- 帖子 #4608 ---
Great explanation, thank you Rufus. I'll try both ways and see which seems to be best to me. Because right now, when I see that price crossed the S/R "line" my mind immediately wants to think that the zone is broken and that could often lead to bad trading decisions.

--- 帖子 #4723 ---
LeBon ….. About crowds. Mass psychology of crowds “Whoever be the individuals that compose it, however like or unlike be their mode of life, their occupations, their character, or their intelligence, the fact that they have been transformed into a crowd puts them in possession of a sort of collective mind which makes them feel think, and act in a manner quite different from that in which each individual of them would feel, think, and act were he in a state of isolation.” People change when they join crowds. They become more credulous and impulsive, anxiously search for a leader, and react to emotions instead of using their intellect. An individual who becomes involved in a group becomes less capable of thinking for himself. Watching a chart is watching crowd psychology. 1000's of traders are in this group. Most are following along as a crowd, making emotional decisions like the above explains. People tend to be more comfortable acting and/or being with a crowd. To be a successful trader we have to break away from this crowd mentality. When was the last time you saw a mob of people make sound decisions? Yet that is what traders will try to do once their emotions are in step with those of the mass of traders that are in this crowd. Our thought have to remain independent of the masses. When this happens our positions in the market will be ready when the masses take price and run away with it. We just sit back and collect pips. Just some thoughts. Ps. I also put social media into crowd psychology.

PASR But I feel that I am lost. Don't worry, that happens to ALL of us. You have only been with us since April this year and you are already well on The Path and doing good. PASR is not a set of rules for a given condition - it is a COMPLETE strategy for ALL Market conditions which takes thousands of hours studying thousands of charts applying what has been learned in both my threads. We have Basic PASR , Swing PASR and Trend PASR which can be used separately or all together DEPENDING on the Market conditions. When you feel lost, just focus on Basic PASR and trade that until you have mastered it and have consistent profits. Most get lost when they have little experience and try to trade everything they SEE. Do we use LL,HH,LH,HL in our analysis? Absolutely! This is Market Structure which is just a fancy name for PRICE ACTION How can I look beyond the candle? This may be too early for you at this stage of your learning but...................Instead of just seeing a candle, think of why that candle has its shape and proportions. Think of who/what made that candle. Who was in control - sellers or buyers? How does that candle fit in with the current trend/sentiment? What caused the body? What caused the wicks and tails? Where were the wicks and tails? Where is this candle, body, wick, tail in relation to the previous candle and candles? Where is that candle in relation to the immediate structure (Weekly Control Candle, Trend, Consolidation, Swing) etc. Am I right on the path? Yes, and you are doing good but remember, you can't eat an elephant in one bite, Rome was not built in a day and, understanding PASR is a Marathon, NOT a 100 metre dash.

What's the average time you stay in the trade for? This is akin to asking "how long is a piece of string?" As Rufus commented, it is "relative". We stay in a trade with a given strategy as long as the Market allows us. For example, using EURUSD (18th out of 28 on my Volatility list) and one position: A Basic PASR average trade could be 16 days and 500+ pips A Swing PASR average trade could be 58 days and 1,000+ pips A Trend PASR average trade could be 220 days and 3,200+ pips An M5 PASR Trend Trade average could be 2 to 3 hours and 50+ pips Remember, this is just ONE POSITION. Experienced PASR traders ADD ON with MULTIPLE POSITIONS I prefer remaining in trades for short period of time (max a couple of days) Why do you say this? You are new to Forex and Forex Factory and from your 3 posts, seem a very logical, down to earth and common sense guy with no history on here of posting on any trading system thread so what has twisted your mind to make you say this? After going through the PDF, would you advise me to start going through this thread or your old one which you have linked to in the first post? I ""thought"" it was "clear" from this Section (copied below) on Post 1 of my "old" original thread what to do next. Help me understand what I need to do/add on the Post 1 of each thread to make it "clear" that you READ, LEARN and UNDERSTAND each Post starting from Post 1 on each thread. This whole thread IS The Path of Learning. The Path of Learning takes you through the following progression: The very first thing we have to do is learn basic PASR . This involves learning and UNDERSTANDING exactly what PASR is. We then have to learn how to IDENTIFY accurate SR levels to SUIT our particular trading style. We then have to learn the basic price reversal candles – Hammer, Shooting Star, BUOB, BUEB, BEOB and BEEB, nothing else . At this point we have to learn the classical definitions of these candles. Do NOT think about or study other candles or patterns as they are NOT reliable and/or consistent for PASR trading. We then put this all together to do SIMPLE yet very profitable trading: Trade from support to 1st resistance and resistance to 1st support. At this stage, you would “paper” trade to exercise the technical content i.e., make sure your understanding of basic PASR is correct. Doing this will bring up many doubts on SR levels and candle types etc. This is part of learning and a stage where every doubt and question must be resolved. How long this takes is up to the individual but there is NO time constraint – you learn within your own time frame. When you have a very high success rate of doing this, you move in to REAL trading. You open an account with REAL money and trade the smallest lot size your broker offers. This will OPEN a whole new world of “little men in your head”, “the man in the mirror” and “gremlins and demons” in you. You will learn the importance of a believed, trusted and accepted PLAN . You will go through grief and pain UNTIL you learn to CONTROL your emotions. Again, how long it takes to master and control your emotions is up to the individual. You will continue to trade until you get to the point that you feel you can “walk on water”. Despite anything written on here, you will go through this emotion and do it. After you have been eaten up, chewed and spat out in little pieces you will learn that you are NEVER in CONTROL of your emotions and you ALWAYS have to be ON GUARD. As you continue to trade in this manner, things that were difficult to see will become clearer and more obvious. We will move from trading classical candle shapes, sizes and patterns to “SEEING” who and what is behind the candles, groups of candles, waves of candles etc. We will learn to recognize market behaviour by eyeballing a chart rather than in depth analysis of a chart. In short, we will be developing our “feel” for the market . This is a very, very personal attribute. Some get it early, for some it seems to take forever while for others, they NEVER get it. At this point, we move into other strategies and techniques.

--- 帖子 #4995 ---
PASR Is this reliable ?. Do we need confirmation to validate the pattern ? PASR does not trade candles or patterns. We use candles as part of our analysis to enter/exit a trade when all the other conditions of PASR are met. In your drawings the marked candle has a different color than the previous one (bearish candle for a spinning top, bullish candle for a spinning bottom), is that relevant ? It adds strength to the direction of the expected move. A red Spinning Top at the end of an up swing tells us that the sellers have already overcome the buyers. A green Spinning Top at the bottom of a down swing tells us that the buyers have already overcome the sellers. Just like Shooting Stars and Hammers, the key point is LOCATION - they must be exposed, on their own, with nothing to the left of them at the bottom/top of their respective swings.

Strat's 5 Steps to becoming a consistently profitable forex trader This has just been added to Post 1 on this thread: STEP 1 – Not knowing what the hell you are doing! You have read and heard that forex trading is a “ Get Rich Quick ” or at least, a fantastic way to make easy money from all the Marketing Promotions (SCAMS) you see and read out there – you know, the ones with a handsome $millionaire guy with his arm around a drop dead beautiful busty blonde in a short skirt leaning on his red Ferrari outside his 12 room mansion overlooking the Pacific Ocean. So, you jump in at the deep end (read trade) with both feet and subsequently drown – because you couldn’t swim! (Couldn’t trade). Bad luck – it won’t happen next time you think. PRICE only goes up or down so what’s the big deal, how hard can it be? Anyone can do it – right? When you jumped in at the deep end, you didn’t know that you couldn’t swim (trade). You then realise you haven’t got a clue what the hell you are doing. You take lots and lots of trades all with huge RISK. Those trades go AGAINST you so you have the bright idea to REVERSE and trade in the opposite direction only for PRICE to turn back again………and again………..and again….and again……..and again etc., etc. You will probably get one or two right “eventually” but at what cost of LOSING the rest? However, this is the TRADING DEVIL telling you that it really is this simple and so you start to trade more, RISK more and LOSE more money. Then you read something about Money Management and “Doubling Up” which you believe is the missing piece to your trading jigsaw. So you start trying to recover your LOSSES by doubling up on them each time you trade. You may be lucky doing that one time but in the end you will LOSE twice as much money! You still don’t get that you know diddly squat about how to trade forex so you continue to trade until eventually the Market sucks you in and blows you out in bubbles wiping you out and taking ALL your money! Then comes the next step: STEP 2 – Not knowing that you don’t know what you don’t know or, to give it a fancy name, Conscious Incompetence This is a light bulb moment when you realise there is a lot more work involved in trading than you first thought and that you might have to start reading, learning and understanding about trading. You finally accept that you can’t make a profit trading forex. Problem solved – buy “ Get Rich Quick ” trading systems, ebooks, software, join public forex Forums – search for the MOTHER of ALL HOLY GRAIL systems from all corners of the Earth. Before you know it, you are an “expert” in trading systems and start HOPPING from one method and system to another day by day, week by week, month by month, year by year never trading one long enough to give it AND YOU, chance to SEE it is profitable. Each time you find an indicator with more flashing lights and bells and whistles than the last one you will believe that THIS is the ONE to make money for you. You will mess with Fibonacci, support and resistance, supply and demand, Pivots, Fractals, Divergence, Price Action, ADX, RSI, MACD, CCI, DMI etc., etc., and everything you can get your LOSING hands on hoping that the next “thing” is what works. You will be such an “expert” with your “indicators” that you will start to pick tops and bottoms trying to trade when PRICE reverses. Losing trades won’t matter because you will always add to them because NOW you know you are RIGHT! Eventually, after more LOSING, you will subscribe to a “live chat room” which you are led to believe is full of Professional Traders trading for their living. You still don’t understand what the hell they are doing so you ask numerous “newbie” questions to the point that everyone ignores you. Then you start not believing what they are doing and the profits they are making and doubt their abilities because, after all, you know as much as them and they must be lying about how much they are making. If I’m doing what they are doing and I’m LOSING how can they be winning? Finally, someone takes you under their wing and gives you good advice but by now you are a stubborn idiot and ignore that advice and continue trading your way because you believe you know better. You then read about signals and signal services so you pay for that but, that doesn’t work either. Then you decide to stump up $thousands to attend courses held by those “famous” $multi-millionaire traders. But it all goes in one ear and out the other because, stubbornly, you know it won’t work and you really know best. This goes on for years and years because you are now ADDICTED to trading and you are sure you can beat this thing. Eventually, you either give up or you TROLL public Forums still searching for the MOTHER of ALL HOLY GRAIL systems. Statistics show that 60% to 75% of new traders give up after 3 to 6 months. Another 15% continue in the hope of becoming $millionaires only to wipe out their account. The remaining % stubbornly continue for around 3 years without success with a very small part of that % eventually moving on to being consistently profitable. Your addiction to trading takes you into Step 3 STEP 3 - The “Eureka” Moment At the end of Step 2 you realise that if trading really was easy, we would all be $millionaires! You begin to realise that success in trading is more about “ YOU ” and that “ YOU ” could make money with a really simple moving average system. You realise that Money Management and Trading Psychology really has a BIG PART to play in being profitable at trading. You buy, read and listen to everything you can find on Trading Psychology, and, what do you know, they are talking about YOU! Light bulbs flash at the speed of light and your Trading Brain kicks in to tell you that being profitable in trading is all about YOU and not the system, method or whatever. It’s no wonder you can’t find anything that works for you. You FINALLY realise that, just like Dr Joe, the NASA Rocket Scientist, who planned spaceship trajectories and moon landings, YOU cannot accurately predict what the Market will do either in the next 5 minutes, the next day or the next month. Then you realise that NO-ONE else can either! So since THEY can’t, YOU stop listening to them or reading others who think they can. Knowing that it is now YOU who is responsible for your profitability and not the system or method, you find one of your systems or methods that has a good record of winning and you feel comfortable with and FOCUS 100% on it upside down and inside out until you completely UNDERSTAND it. You FINALLY stop looking at other threads and systems because now you HAVE found the HOLY GRAIL which YOU now know is who stares back at you when you look in the mirror. Then, you paper trade it because you know that Broker demos are highly manipulated and encourage you to win. Then you move onto trading LIVE with your REAL, hard earned money. You don’t get angry when you lose because you know it is just the cost of doing Business. Then your profits and performance begin to spiral down out of control. Then someone tells you that you are trying to “ Walk On Water ” and that the last guy who tried that got hung on a cross. You finally wake up and realise that you had forgotten that your performance is all about YOU , not the system or Market so you beat yourself up and go back to Step 3 Step 5 - Autopilot Eventually, you avoid Walking on Water again and get back to profitable trading and then move on to Autopilot trading. You have become Consistently Profitable and you are now trading at an unconscious level or “In The Zone”. Reading Strat's stages of trading made me reflect too. Here's my trading backstory. I got into trading because I had some friends that were into it and I got 'the bug' from discussing with them. I then saw a course advertised by a 'guru' in Central London and was told that if I paid for the weekend course I'd get another place free(!!!) so I pooled cash with one of said friends and attended a 'masterclass' where the 'guru' proceeded to basically regurgitate the same tripe you can read in any trading book: i.e. 'Support &amp; resistance' gets a mention and you spend hours looking at shiny squiggly lines and (this may give away who it was) you routinely stand up and give each other massages. A bit of pop culture wealth psychology and boom! I was a master trader. Needless to say the only bit of decent advice in the entire course was to paper-trade first. I may have saved myself the course fee multiple times due to that alone because I blew up millions in demo accounts over the next couple of years as I proceeded to apply my 'mastery' to the markets. Realising I knew absolutely sod-all, and since I'm a scientist by training and vocation, I sought to plug the gap with knowledge: I read every book I could lay my hands on and joined a forum - not this one! Still it didn't matter how much I knew: any and all demo accounts went into deep, black holes. All any of them ever talk about is entries entries entries: no risk management, stop loss or TP. In the forum I was drawn towards people who posted chart after chart of winning trades. One of them I will call 'insect' grabbed my attention and I promptly asked to be invited to his free chat room. Insect quickly laid out his strategy to us all, which appeared to be very simple SR trading with iron risk management. I took that bit of info on board as he continued to wow us with chart after chart of winning trades and little else. He then solicited funds from people to see if he could run up an investment fund from a few hundred quid to a few hundred thousand and we gladly paid him a couple of hundred each for shares in the fund. He disappeared. By this time I'd taken his risk management approach to heart and this stopped the freefall in my account - more a steady decline. Back to the drawing board, I noticed a guy posting a strategy based on James16: no squiggly lines, plot support&amp;resistance, trade the reaction at those levels. This seemed way harder but also seemed to have much more ring of truth to it than what the gurus from squigglytown were selling. He also mentioned stuff like risk:reward and account management. All missing in a lot of the books and courses going around. I can imagine you could lose 1000 sales every time you mention the word 'risk' in a book. Putting all this together, I realised most of technical analysis was hoodoo, price responded at certain levels and with my own eyes the only thing I could see that told me anything else was moving averages (i.e. 'current form' in footie terminology). I removed my squiggles and learned to 'see' the price. I also started the realise that all the squiggly trading books I owned were worth lots of money on Amazon, but could be found routinely dumped in charity shops and costing pennies. I made a lot of money buying and selling trading books in this way (arbitrage!!) but the point is clear: these books are expensive to people when they haven't read them and worthless to those who have. Hardly the Tao te Ching or the Tao of Pooh which you can re-read periodically and learn new things! Case closed: squiggles were out. It was then that I started looking for a method to trade price action. This was about the time Strat started the 'old thread'. I lurked on a few forums and set upon a price action guru's thread. I shall call him Voldemort because he should not be named. Voldemort invited me to his private site for a nominal fee and for a while I felt I was learning his method. Then, based on experience with insect I started to second-guess Voldemort because I wasn't sure from his answers that he actually knew a great deal. Then he started acting like insect and soliciting funds from people. It was then that I ducked out. Later it turned out that Voldemort, like insect, took lots of people's money and disappeared and I had dodged a bullet. To sum up: gurus were all money grabbing bastards and fakes and trading was a zero sum game based on hope. The only profits I'd ever made were by buying and selling books containing dubious 'strategies' that were poorly explained and designed to attract people to 'mentoring' programs. On the other hand, as with insect there were things to be learned and Voldemort was advocating a fairly simple, trend-following methodology, and using that alongside insect’s tight risk management put me perilously close to being able to trade. I traded live with several thousand pounds for almost a year and my account stayed in the red but was always about 1 good trade from breakeven, so I’ve been screwed by 3 ‘gurus’ at this point and have only really learned: paper trade first, risk management/stop placement and go with the trend. This knowledge was expensively assembled and unprofitably applied. About this time I needed to buy a place so I took the thousands out of the account and left it with a float of like a hundred or so and decided I’d be back one day. That was about 2009/10. If all GBP pairs are in synchronisation(making the same patterns at the same time) you can make the best trade in your life or the worst, so be aware. I choose a pair with some legs left, by this I mean value left in the market for the traders. You can simply look on a higher time frame and guess or do what I do which is pull up a Worker chart: Attached Image (click to enlarge) So now I have the 10 day average ATR I can see that there is plenty left to go on this one. I plot a line from the Daily open (purple on my chart). I then wait for the London open and draw my line at that open and ask myself a few questions which I wrote on the chart for you: Attached Image (click to enlarge) I then wait for price action using the Strat Shadow, my London level and the PA. I want to see a pullback and retest to the open. I get this and a really good BEEB. Entry 1 is underway. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Now you will see my comments about the Asia low? I need price to take this out and I want a pullback back into my first entry, I am fully expecting a test here and I have no problems with my stop being taken out if I am wrong. ABSOLUTELY NO PROBLEM. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Sure enough I get a good run past the Asia low and my 1st position is in profit (20 or 30 pips I think). I can bag it now or press on, I choose to press on and wait for it to come back. It does and OH NO!!! it's taken my money! Actually yes it has but I'd planned for this remember? I accepted my risk ON MY 1st TRADE. So we have entry 2 under way (note these may not be text book after the fact, these are real time). BEFORE I entered any trade I had PLANNED my exit. For me this with MY RISK is MORE IMPORTANT THAN ANYTHING. So where do I get out? I used to use PASR levels but got greedy and always went for one too far away. AND LOST. Do not be greedy! Remember my Worker ATR chart? Have another look at it and figure out why I have chosen an exit WITHIN that ATR which also HAS to coincide with a PASR level. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Two trades in and we are now in what I call the grind zone which does happen a lot towards the end of a Bigger Trend. So for a couple hours I manage this with my stops above swing highs and I AM STILL IN IT until someone shows me I shouldn't be. AGAIN I HAVE ACCEPTED MY RISK on 2 positions. I have space left for a 3rd entry and I'm now waiting for it if the market permits me. It does but LOOK. I have NEVER extended my initial target, it is set and I close all 3 positions for a tidy profit. Attached Image (click to enlarge) My positions are all single standalone entries not split up. I think if you are going to do that then you may as well take 1 full position and stand on it to take full profit on the swing which I also do depending which mood takes me and the opportunity available but each to their own. Trading is a very personal thing and even when we have clear structure from Strat it's up to YOU to manage your RISK which isn't just about a stop loss. For every trade cut short because you can't deal with the psychology you are eroding your edge. It has gone and you will be TOAST in the market. Cut your position sizes on M5 until you trade like a reptile basking in the sun on a rock because those stop losses and small premature wins will beat you. I only try to post useful charts with real entries so we can all learn. I hope there is value for some in this post and stick with it. Higher Highs, Lower Lows, Strat Shadow, PASR and the best indicator there is being the one you were born with so use it. I'll be posting some higher time frame trades as and when I can but they'll be fewer. On a side note to M5 traders, use it to speed learn PASR then be patient and use your experience further up the food chain. That is where SCALE and REAL MONEY is. Cheers BTS

Candlesticks Be careful that you don't get sucked into the hype that "Candlesticks" are the "be all" and "end all" in trading. Candlesticks are only ONE of our tools in PASR . We don't trade candlesticks - we trade PASR . These examples are in a perfect world and completely out of context to any particular trading condition. Only study candlesticks in a particular situation - this is when you will learn more.

Trading Psychology Time for me to post this again: Trading Psychology Posting this again as it seems that if it does not have a chart or is not about making pips, then people do not bother to read it let alone ABSORB and UNDERSTAND it. This is one of the most important aspects in trading you will never see written or spoken about anywhere. Ignore it at your peril! What 99.9999% of people on these public trading forums don't realise is that they need their trading brain to be working at 100% efficiency at peak optimum power when they are trading. Anytime you use an indicator to do something for you, you LOSE trading brain efficiency and your trading brain becomes lazy and expects you to find other things so it doesn't have to work. The more you use and rely on indicators, EAs and other black magic crap, the slower and lazier your trading brain becomes until eventually it goes to sleep and you empty your trading accounts.

On trading during the holidays (Old thread #13,833) A thin market, because it is easily manipulated, will always move more (or not) - sometimes it is to our advantage while others it is not. I have seen many times where the market set up to move in our anticipated direction during a "holiday", trigger the trade the next day only for the big boys to come in and reverse it. Other times, there have been some very good moves triggered off a "holiday" market. In compliance with RULE No. 1, I prefer to WAIT to let the market balance itself out. Strat, I wonder if your thinking has changed over the course of 8 years. I see some PASR trade on Friday's close, I am hesitating if I should enter on Monday's bank holiday for US and UK. --- 帖子 #5304 ---
Break Even Break Even is mostly used by Amateurs and those who don't understand its function but mostly by those who don't really know what they are doing and how it fits in with their PLAN . This results from not knowing what, which and how you are trading a particular strategy. For example, if you are scalping, where your profit is only a few pips, you need, and must, go to Break Even as soon as you have enough profit to cover the spread and any commissions. In Basic PASR , the only time I would move my initial Stop Loss to Break Even is when PRICE has successfully closed above/below minor "wobble zones". In Swing PASR , and especially PASR Trend Trading, we mange our RISK as declared in our irreversible PLAN so that we allow PRICE room to BREATHE. The teachings of PASR allow students to UNDERSTAND that PRICE moves in "" steps "" rather than straight lines. In Swing PASR these are bigger "" steps "" than in Basic PASR . In PASR Trend Trading , the " steps " are even bigger and more often than not are some derivative of a swing. So, the ""trick"" is NOT moving your Stop Loss to Break Even as soon as possible and is just the opposite - UNDERSTAND what strategy you are trading and let PASR determine your Break Even if there is a need for one. The "trick", if there is one, is letting PRICE BREATHE in your chosen trading strategy. Finally, from Post 1 of my "old" original thread: We are NOT Amateurs. Amateurs manage money by taking RISK. PROFESSIONALS manage RISK by taking money.

--- 帖子 #5314 ---
The average true range (ATR) is a measure of volatility introduced by Welles Wilder in his book, "New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems." I have always thought the word "True" should not be in there. More for marketing in my opinion. My brain cell wonders "How can something be average and true at the same time?" In relation to price; the only thing that is "true" is where price is right now. "Average Range" just doesn't sound as good as "Average True Range"

--- 帖子 #5315 ---

It is just a number that Strat uses to find the most volatile pairs to trade on M5 in general, but absolutely not something that you should use in any way in my opinion. Just trade his favorite pairs (no pun intended), and you should be good to go

M5 PASR Trend Trading Bon matin, Fleur. I am rather of a patiente and calm nature. I do not think it's for fear of missing a trade. You may want to re-visit this as it is in conflict with what you posted Attached Image (click to enlarge) No matter how DISCIPLINED we "think" we are, our emotions (Greed and Fear) are always first in line when it comes to trading, especially the first trade of the day. It happens to all of us so just be aware of it. Here is my way of working 1-In the morning, before the opening, I like to analyze the strength of currencies. 2-I also look at the calendar. 3-I take it in my head to take only 1-2 max trades per day (I do not want to spend my day in front of my screen). 4-The ideal would be to trade only the London session. 5-After opening londre I analyze the reaction of currencies up to H + 1 6-From H + 1, if I see the criteria of your method OK, with a nice ratio possible, I open the trade with actually always my small SL This is very good but I don't see anywhere in there where you check for, and add, H1 &amp; H4 support and resistance levels. I open the trade with actually always my small SL As I have posted many times, this was the key component in developing my M5 PASR Trend Trading strategy. Not many on here have REALLY understood this so you may be paving the way for others to learn from you. What I found was that when PRICE was nearing the end of its pull back against the TREND (Strat Shadow), it almost always ended in a small doji or some sort of small range bar. This meant I could load up on my position size with only a few pips stop loss and my RISK still be less than 1% of my account. This, in itself, has proven to be the best filter I have ever come across in all my years of trading. For me, if my entry means I need a large stop loss then I know "something" is not right and WAIT for a better small stop loss entry. Yes, many times it means I miss out on a good trade but the bottom line is I have NOT lost any of my trading capital ( Rule #1 ). Remember, it is better to be out of a trade wishing you were in, than being in a trade wishing you were out! See the blue rectangles for examples. Attached Image (click to enlarge) I think you understand this very well but if you don't, ask and I will explain again. What is more of a worry is your lack of understanding of PASR . Had you really understood PASR , you would have known to GET OUT on the next candle after your entry which would have saved you many pips. Make sure you understand PASR . Thought I would share something here that has helped me out. In the past I had a tendency to way over analyze the charts. Draw trendlines, support and resistance, supply and demand, Fibonacci and 2 or 3 moving averages then try to make heads or tails of the mess and place trades. I don't know why it is human nature to over complicate things. Trading exasperates this piece of human nature. We will do all we can to understand the markets, reading and studying everything we get our hands on; but to what end? The writers of the books or the sellers of the latest whiz-bang indicator are the only ones turning the profit. So what is the key then. To me #1 is to simplify everything... Your life, your mind, the charts everything including your desk. Now to quote the great philosopher Yogi Berra Attached Image (click to enlarge) Trading is no less than then 90%mental as well. So we spend more time understanding ourselves then the market. Nobody will ever completely understand the market, it is impossible. But we can understand ourselves and how we react to the market. So we trade demo accounts. See some good results then go live. To quote Yogi Berra again... Attached Image Our brain gets in the way. Attached Image (click to enlarge) At some point we quit over analyzing things and just swing the bat...take the trade. It's baseball season and was thinking about Yogi Berra today. He was not only one of the greatest baseball players, was also a great coach, and a great man. So to some up my baseball and trading ramblings. In order to hit the ball you need to step-up to the plate and swing the bat, you can't do that if you are drawing lines and squiggles all over your chart. See the trade and take it. Rufus

Time Frames Somewhere in my "old" original thread I wrote several posts about Time Frames and the importance of finding ""YOUR"" time frame. Just about all new "wannabe" traders focus on trying to find the strategy, system, signals, black box etc., - that which will make them rich beyond their wildest dreams. They do this, not UNDERSTANDING that their mental, trading personality, is that which will decide their trading fate. We, the traders, are all unique and different, but with the same Market challenges meaning that what is a success for one is destruction for another. Long story short, before we can expect any success, we have to look inside ourselves and FIND what makes us ""tick"". The Time Frame YOUR trading brain functions best at is what you should trade - NOT the time frame others trade. You are right to experiment to find "YOUR" time frame without the influence of others. This is another reason why we need to spend thousands of hours studying thousand of charts. One of the reasons I posted my M5 PASR Trend Trading strategy was to help accelerate the PASR learning process for those on The Path . Keep your ""time frame"" mind open and you will find that "YOUR" time frame chooses YOU - not the other way round as 99.999999% of those on public trading Forums do.

--- 帖子 #5398 ---
Internal negotiation Something that I found interesting in my personal psychology and which could help others. I sometimes catch myself negotiating internally to convince me to take a trade because the sky is not clear blue and that the trade would have pros and cons. This is generally the sign I shouldn't take the trade and that I am hoping that odds will go in my favor even though the overall probabilities are against me. Now, when I start negotiating with myself, this is a clear sign I should stay away. I know the way I see the market is changing and there are things my "gut" sees but my brain cannot explain yet they are much more powerful insights than anything else. The chart is like a music partition, it won't speak to you unless you spend time to learn how to read music. And as Strat says, better to regret being out of a good trade you missed rather than regret being in a bad trade. Opportunities are infinite, your capital is not.

Hi Brian, Maybe I can answer for Strat and he can correct me if I am wrong. On the daily, unlike the lower time frames, price is "unaffected" by news because it has already been taken into account (don't you think the Big Boys have inside information/know the news in advance?). In my opinion and experience, the trend is more important than the news itself. If it is good news for the trend, of course the trend continues. However, if it is bad news, usually the market just needs 1-2 days to correct itself in a strong trend, or even an hour! If you placed your stop loss well, you will not be taken out. Look at the Big Boys who manipulated yesterday's buying of EURUSD. Throughout the day, price just went up and up. It went up even more 45 minutes prior (there was another 'red' news) to the ECB announcement! And in one fell swoop, the Big Boys took out every single buyers on the announcement. Hi Brian, I will wait for PASR (Engulfing candles/ Outside Bars/ Shooting Star/Hammer) to tell me the direction. As of the last candle, the doji tells me nothing, except indecision. It could mean a continuation or a reversal. It is important to keep an open mind of where price is going. Furthermore, price is in the midst of WCC, 200ema, 365ema. We should always trade with caution in this situation. it is no trend yet... We trade the immediate trend! On the Big Boss chart, what I see is that Price is back to 20ema of Strat Shadow, a place that was rejected last month, creating a "Bond Shooting Star". Now that Price is at resistance on the Big Boss chart, we wait for PASR on the Boss and Worker to tell us what to do. EDIT: The thing with chart patterns is that, 1) Bullish/Bearish patterns like wedges can fail. 2) Neutral patterns like triangles absolutely tells us NOTHING (more like a 50/50 coin toss) so I think it is better to ignore it than to cloud your judgement.

--- 帖子 #5690 ---
Hi Suranga 7% is excessive in my opinion. But what exactly Rub is doing, we don't know. He might have 100,000 stashed away and trading a small percentage of that. As for me. My trades run real close to 1% of equity at risk per position. When multiple positions are going, careful not to have risk doubled up in similar moving currencies. Risk is a very relative thing. Sometimes there is a dollar amount (regardless of the percent risk) that when you cross it your little people start screaming at you. You could have a $100,000 account and be squirming in your chair with 1000 at risk, 1%. Anyway some food for thought.

--- 帖子 #5691 ---
I'm working on $50 is an amount I am ok with losing, that is noticeable but not going to hurt (my beer money!). When I get to the point of risking serious money I intend to keep enough in my account for 10-20 trades at my risk %, and the remainder in my bank account. So I may be risking 10% of my account, but it's only 2% of my funds. e.g. $50,000 in funds, I want to risk 1% per trade so I transfer $5000 to my account to trade with. This gives me 10 trades, and if I blow the account it's a serious warning that I need to rethink what I'm doing, without destroying my funds completely. I explained what I'm doing above, but the why is more because I'm inclined to trust the stability of my bank to hold the majority of my cash vs. how often I read about dodgy forex brokers. While I don't think my broker is too bad, why take the risk?
