--- 帖子 #5722 ---
Markets are quiet. Thread is quiet. England is recovering from their celebrating. US is gearing up for 4th of July festivities. Good time for some reflective thought. Had an interesting thing happen the other day that taught me a lot about trading psychology. The event requires a little build up. I chart from an overseas broker and trade with a US broker. This is so there is access to NY close charts. So there is a semi constant juggling act to keep things in order. S/R on NY close charts corresponding with the S/R lines on the other. Then if I have a trade running on the US charts, it is marked out on the other charts. It works for me now....So I thought. Now comes the "Incident" I don't know if this happened do to a windows update, loss of power, or just a stupid glitch. But I lost all of my NY close charts. 16 currency pairs for the daily trading and 10 or so for the 5m. All the S/R, Strat Shadow, entries and exits laid out, all gone. Even tried to recover it with chatting with the brokerage gurus. No luck. So sitting down to the arduous task of setting up charts. The first step was to get all the currency pairs loaded with the Strat shadow on the daily charts. So one by one, open a chart, put on the Strat Shadow template, convert to daily, then on to the next. I probably had coffee in hand, because was also leaned back in my chair and was just clicking buttons. Figured I'd put the S/R on once all the charts were set up. Then I came across a pair that needed to be shorted. I couldn't read which pair so grabbing the reading glasses saw it was the AUDUSD. BUT I WAS LONG already. My first temptation was to leave the trade. Then thought "no that's stupid". Capital preservation is #1 rule. The next thing that flew through my mind is what Strat has on every chart he posts. IF TRADE IS WRONG - GET OUT. I took the profit. Now the psychology. Would I have seen the short if the trade was laid out on the chart? I doubt it. Probably would have held it to run its course. It was a very vivid incident to me. Our bias no matter how subtle or insignificant can never enter into our observation of the chart. Somehow every evening when sitting down to the days closing bar, I need to see the chart as if it is the first time seeing it. With a position in play, this time a long, the tendency is to see only longs. Or see things to only support your thinking that the long is the right move. One of my favorite quotes by Anais Nin “We don't see things as they are, we see them as we are.” Fresh eyes on the chart. For what it's worth for you guys. The incident taught me a lot about my brain cell. On a side note. I know nothing about Soccer, but I felt the intensity through social media of England advancing to the quarter finals today. I was constantly checking in, I could tell that there was a lot of stress eating and alcohol consumption. Congrats to England. I was pulling for you. Maybe soccer will find its way to my TV when England plays again. Take care all Rufus

--- 帖子 #5785 ---
PASR and VOLATILITY Since the Market is slow today................... Why volatility is important to my PASR trading. Simply put, volatility is the movement of PRICE over a given period of time. Volatility is the result of many things brought about by the perception of VALUE by those trading the Market. This is anything which changes the fundamental relationship between supply and demand such as geopolitical events or natural disasters. The greater the change, the greater the volatility. Volatility feeds on itself due to the interactions of humans (traders) and their psychology. This is easily seen when GREED and FEAR are driving PRICE as a result of crowd behavior causing traders to “trade with the herd”. FEAR is the most powerful of all trading emotions and is why you see PRICE falling much faster than it rises. Uncertainty of where PRICE is going in unstable situations is, in itself, a cause of volatility. Volatility feeding on itself is even more true when we consider the mechanics of trading. Fast PRICE movements trigger Stops and pending Orders thus increasing volatility. When PRICE , for whatever reason, is falling like a concrete balloon and therefore showing increased downside PRICE volatility, all hell breaks loose among traders. This causes traders, including the Big Boys, to be upside down as the fast downward movement of PRICE slices through any profits and moves them into a loss position. The initial reaction is to “”freeze”” but this is quickly expelled as losses start mounting exponentially. At this point, PANIC sets in triggering FEAR and the Big Boys quickly sell their positions. This, in turn, causes PRICE to drop even further and faster (increased volatility) which then causes other traders to sell which again increases volatility. This is the “domino” effect of volatility feeding on volatility. This volatility then causes VOLUME to increase. Increased volume is what drives PRICE and in a volatile situation, increases volatility. When I traded Futures and Commodities, volume was key to analysis. In simple terms, high volatility is with high volume while low volatility is with low volume. An increase in volume was usually a sign that volatility was about to increase. Unfortunately, volume is worth NOTHING in Forex as there is no central trading exchange and the volume we see on our charts is only that of our individual broker which is as much use to us as forex traders as fly shit in a pepper pot ! What does help us in Forex, a little, is ATR – Average True Range. This helps us see volatility over a given time period. For example, if the 10 day ATR of a given pair is 146 pips and we are in a trade generating 140 pips, we know to be ready to exit stage left at the sign of any weakness. Similarly, if we have only generated 70 pips, we can expect, “”IF”” PRICE is at the same level of volatility, to move further. The point to remember is “ Average ” - each day, volume is different, which therefore causes different volatility so using ATR is not exact. Some “experts”, “gurus” and self-proclaimed “authors and talking heads” say that volatility is cyclical and moves in cycles which can be measured and forecast. In all my 36+ years of trading I have never been able to “see” these cycles let alone forecast them. What I do know is that a period of high volatility is almost always followed by a similar period of low volatility. Knowing the condition of “volatility” we are trading is very important as it influences and affects our Trading PLAN . Over the years, my trading style has changed and even though my strategy is, and always will be, PASR , my trade selection is based on volatility as much as PASR . I no longer have the patience or desire to have my margin tied up in pedantic pairs like EURCHF and EURGBP which move at the lightning speed of a ten ton tortoise with 3 legs. I have much better things to do with my funds and time which is why I released my volatility list. Certainly when trading M5, I need to only trade the top 5 or so on that list which, in addition to making a short “watch” list, produces profits for me in the 2 hours trading I restrict myself to on M5.

From then on, PRICE is making the Low - High - Higher Low - Higher High structure and we KNOW that down trend is FINISHED. M5 PASR Trend Trading is SIMPLE when you trade the TREND but it is not as easy as that as explained above. --- 帖子 #5817 ---
PASR Supply and Demand is very different to Resistance and Support. You can do a search on the web and get some very fancy and complicated answers, most of which do not help in practical trading. There are self proclaimed experts, gurus and "know it alls" on here and other public and private trading forums who trade Supply and Demand - some profitably, others just pretending/dreaming. Still, there are others who understand it like no other yet can't explain how to use it in practical trading. Then there is the "herd" - the 95% who trade Supply as Resistance and Demand as Support and don't know the difference or how to use either. My ""SIMPLE"" understanding of Supply and Demand is what has worked for me over the years so I don't care whether it is "right" or "wrong" nor do I care what others think or say. Trading is SIMPLE (but not easy). PASR is SIMPLE (but not easy) so everything I do in PASR has to be SIMPLE. So, DEMAND, in PASR terms, is that PRICE level over a period of time (usually years and, the longer, the more accurate) where PRICE did not go lower and formed a mounting pad to ACCUMULATE (build) long positions from which PRICE made a HUGE move. Supply, in PASR terms, is that PRICE level over a period of time (usually years and, the longer, the more accurate) where PRICE did not go higher and formed a mounting pad to DISTRUBUTE (build) short positions from which PRICE made a HUGE move. In my SIMPLE trading mind, I think of Supply and Demand as the MAJOR SWING on the HIGHEST time frame of the PASR strategy I am trading. In between Supply and Demand are Resistance and Support and MINOR swings. This is an example of EURUSD Attached Image (click to enlarge) Again, this is MY understanding and USE of Supply and Demand with PASR . It may not meet the mainstream or others definition but again, I don't care, I trade PASR NOT what others trade or want me to trade.

--- 帖子 #5841 ---
Hi Rub, Sorry was away in Devon on a family do this weekend so just catching up on the forum. Wanted to reply to help you hopefully by talking through my thinking on that trade. I'm far from being an expert but have had multiple profitable months in a row now so there will be lots of things I could have done better in the trade. As Strat said try not to beat yourself up about not getting it all yet. It's taken me many years of trying this, that and the other to finally see what's going on and figure out what works for me. I've had multiple lightbulb moments over the last 6-8 months while trading price action. None more important than switching to a risk and probability mindset. The real battle with trading is having the confidence to pull the trigger and just get in the market to see if you are right or wrong. So many times I would see a support level I'd drawn and price would start to stall and I'd think, but WHAT IF, THAT COULD BE WRONG, BUT THERES THIS OR THAT THERE WHICH MIGHT MEAN..... Then I'd kick myself the next day as price just did what I thought it would. I've combated this by entering with small positions initially to "dip my toe in" and see whether price does what I expect. Send out the scouts and see if they come back with a favourable report. If price action tells me I'm wrong I either let it run for a while to see how it plays out (as long as it's within my risk tolerance) or get out. Small positions and a couple of little trades to start with helps me get in without worrying what price does. It has to move A LONG WAY against me to make me start to worry about a financial loss that will hurt. So theres no reason not to see if I'm right. This has always been the hardest part for me. You are either going to be right or wrong and price rarely just does what you want it to do straight away. You have to be patient and just let price do what it does for hours/days and get comfortable with draw down. I sit in draw down A LOT on most of my trades and I'm comfortable with it now. It's part of trading and when I realised that it changed my way of thinking and how I traded. I'll talk you through my exact thinking on that trade and my risk allowed which may help you understand why I took it and what I was thinking along the way as it played out. I check the H4 charts every 4 hours and see if there is a price action candle that grabs my attention or a S/R level that price has reached. Attached Image (click to enlarge) On the H4 chart I saw three things. 1. A resistance level , so I drew drew that in (the zone from tip of the tail to close of the candle) so I could see clearly where I expected something to happen. 2. A doji candlestick after a big upward move. That candle told me the market was undecided where it was going to go next. 3. The 200MA area which price often likes to have a re-think at, and looking back at the chart historically on this pair it had been respected. For me that was enough to get in with a couple of small positions to test if my edge was right. I put a big stop on the orders way above the resistance zone and that was well within my maximum risk allowance per trade. I personally think in £x risk not pips. I'm uncomfortable if price goes against me by £x and that's when I start to either reduce my position or get out completely with a loss. I move down to the H1 chart then and monitor and manage the trade from there. I was expecting price to consolidate a bit and then either carry on up or go down to at least test the bottom of the strat shadow or more likely much further. I don't have exact targets but watch what price is doing as I go. I know if I'm right it's likely to go a long way down but nobody knows. Depending on how many positions I have and what the P&amp;L looks like I adjust my targets along the way. More positions = less price has to move for me to make a nice amount of profit. I've no idea where it will go to but I do know what I'm comfortable losing. In this case is was £50. Attached Image (click to enlarge) The next candle after my entry re-tested the high of the last candle and closed below my entry so I added a little more to the trade. I now have 3 small positions as price has confirmed at LEAST it's rejected that resistance for the moment. 2 candles later we have another strong bearish candle so I added another small position. We're 3 hours into the trade and I'm gradually getting in as price is telling me my suspicion was correct so I added another small trade. I now have 4 small positions in the trade. 2 hours later and price action was again very bearish so I entered another couple of orders. I now have 6 positions and now my £50 max risk is still sitting above the resistance area so I've achieved 2 things. 1. I'm in the market . This is the most important part as without it we're not trading! Sounds silly but you have to be in it to win it.... I've sent out a couple of scouts (small trades) to see if price would carry on in the direction I suspected. I've added to the trades as price has confirmed my suspicion. I've got a good trade size in with confidence over a period of 5 or 6 hours. 2. I have my max risk if all these go against me still sitting above that resistance level so price has room to breathe. This is the real winner for me in my trades. Giving price room to breathe without me panicking and waking up the little people. They are the ones that make me lose and they need to be quiet. I've told them I'm happy to lose £50 so shut up and don't bother me until we're getting close to that. Job done. I'm in the market and comfortable. Often price will re-test a level (double tops and bottoms) so I don't really worry too much if that happens as it did in this case. It's not ideal and we all want price to just tumble in our direction but that rarely happens. I should have added to the trade at the second rejection but didn't for some reason. Either asleep or possibly had other trades playing out and just not concentrating enough. It happens. So now I'm in a trade and my only job now is to watch my P&amp;L and manage what happens. Now I'm thinking two things when I check that chart every few hours while I'm awake. 1. Has my max drawdown/risk been hit or are we getting close (£50 in this case)? 2. Has price moved sufficiently in my direction to make me enough profit for me to get out of the trade, in part or in whole? I just ask myself those two questions every time I check the chart. I'm not saying to myself has it got to 0.73170 yet as that's my target. I'm asking myself if I'm happy to stay in and do I think theres more room for profit. This was an important change in mindset for me. Rigid targets I found nerveracking. In this case I wasn't at the screen when price tested the bottom of the strat shadow on the H1 timeframe either. Again, can't remember if I was sleeping or just away from the computer. I may have taken some profit there but in all likelyhood not as there was no clear BUEB or hammer to tell me to. Anyway another retracement happened and the profit got sucked up, and in the past I would have been thinking "god I've missed my profit, better get out and break even" . Now I think " I'm nowhere near my max £50 loss I've allowed and theres no higher high there yet so we're still in the trade ." Price action in the last 12 hours has been massively bearish and it's because that resistance held twice. I think I'm right here and the big boys are agreeing with me. Or me with them, either way the trade is working so need to let it play out. The main thing that changed me into being profitable is my mindset. I'm thinking in probability and risk only now. I've seen price moving up and down so much I just expect it to do that at least twice before I get to anywhere near when I'm likely to take a profit . For me on the H1 timeframe I'm thinking of multiple day holds mostly unless theres a news event that takes me into instant profit at some point. When you just take trades with big breathing room and let them play out they seem to work. In the past I used tight stops and they ended up killing me as I took too many losses and had a low strike rate because of it. That's just me and I know many who use tight stops and make very good trades with them. I'm just a little too inaccurate at the moment. I especially love shorting because price climbs up the stairs and tends to fall down it. As demonstrated twice on that H1 chart. I was expecting another fall but if it didn't happen I'd have taken a loss and moved on. The next one or the one after that would have fallen for me and when they fall they always fall further for me than the ones that turn out to be losses. Probability or winning is only confirmed I think when you have done it and seen it happen over and over. That gives you confidence. Anyway back to the trade in hand. Price came crashing down again and I took partial profit at the bottom of the strat shadow. Mainly because price had tested that the day before and bounced so I wanted to get something in the bank. It could have happened again but I didn't know. I just knew I'd been in the trade for over a day and I wanted to bank some £. As price continued down it started to consolidate around the 200MA and there was some support there so suspected we may be hitting a hurdle for a while. I was well into my profit target by now and comfortable so decided to take what I had and bank it. As you can see I could have let it run and banked way more but too many times after 4-6 hours of consolidation price has jumped up against me so I'd rather fill the bank and miss out on some profit so I can move onto the next. That's an honest look at my thinking and you'll notice at no point did any little people pop up and start telling me to do anything . I'd told them I was happy to lose £50 and they never got a chance to even pipe up in my ear! Killing them is the real battle and moving to a financial stop loss and gradual scale into positions for me has shut them up. That's given me confidence to get in and trade and not worry. They do pop up and start to moan when I go into big drawdown but having lots of small positions give me an opporunity to close one of them out and instantly shut them up. This is rarely done as by the time I approach my max loss target the trade is usually confirmed as wrong so I get all out. The point is having multiple entries gives me flexibility in managing the trade. Hope that helps and apologies for the ultra-long post. You may need a nudge to wake yourself up now if you've drifted off!

--- 帖子 #5868 ---
NZDUSD H1 Brian, in addition to the very valuable comments from Darko and Samson: Have another look at your Set Up candle. The long wick and body with a short tail is NOT a candle to initiate trades on. Look at the red candles in the blue boxes prior to yours for examples of red candles we look for. Make sure you can SEE the difference. Now look at the PRICE structure from the bottom. Look at those 2 LARGE green candles in the black box . Those candles are telling you there are BUYERS buying at that PRICE level. Then look at what PRICE does after those two large green candles. PRICE continues to make higher highs and higher lows using the Strat Shadow as support. PRICE eventually CLOSES above the Strat Shadow BUT is held by the 200 resistance. This has now put PRICE "in balance" or "equilibrium" telling us there is a pause or confusion between buyers and sellers. At this point, neither the buyers or sellers know where to take PRICE as shown by the red and green candles. This, where you entered, is NEVER the place to initiate trades. PASR always WAITS for the Big Boys to SHOW us the direction they are taking PRICE . We WAIT to FOLLOW in the FOOTSTEPS of the Big Boys . This comes on the dragonfly doji or doji Hammer you highlighted with your 2nd arrow. This is telling us the buyers have more volume than the sellers. The sellers drove PRICE down to the bottom of the doji to a PRICE level where buyers were WAITING to buy at. As those buyers bought, others then followed and bought more thus driving PRICE up. With the buyers having more volume and therefore being IN CONTROL, PRICE continued to rise. So I enter short and went to sleep. Then you DESERVE all the LOSSES that come to you! If you are trading H1 then you MUST monitor your trades on a 1 HOUR basis . The only time you can enter on H1 and "forget it/go to sleep" is if that is an entry for H4 or Worker trades. Had you done this you would have SEEN the doji Hammer and closed your trade there. If you trade H1 then your Boss is H4 and your Big Boss is the Daily. Did you do this analysis which is one of the fundamentals of PASR strategy? Had you done this, you would have another reason NOT to enter short. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Yes I've just had a look through that on the daily and it's a hard one to pick entries on. Because it's such a wild pair with a big ATR the day candles are long. By the time they close theres not a lot of R:R there for you. On H4 though there were quite a few PA candles at the extremes although a couple would have resulted in losses most would have been big winners. Rangy WCC pairs I find if you trade basic PASR on them you have to be VERY, VERY patient as price swings up and down a lot obviously. I would go into profit, then in to DD, then into profit and so on a few times. Eventually though you get the big moves which make the money or stop you out. When they start they are obvious and thats the time to add another entry and then another and before you know it you've got a good sized position on it's way up to the top or down to the bottom of the WCC. You just have to sit on your hands (often in DD) and wait for the big boys to get involved. Maybe put a watchlist of those pairs in WCC together and stick them on a layout with H4 charts and follow what happens a couple of times a day. That is of course if you want to try another timeframe which is something only we as individuals can decide. Not for everyone which is why I left them alone early on but I'm finding them more and more appealing as my tolerance for DD and management of my trades are getting better.

The long wick and body with a short tail is NOT a candle to initiate trades on. Why? My understand is the long wick means the power of seller is larger than the buyer's, and the short tail means the power of buyer is smaller, right? WRONG! Just discussing the candle alone and nothing else - can you SEE the difference between candle A and those candles in B? Attached Image The candles in "B" are full blown selling candles - those candles consist of 95% to 98% SELLERS. Candle A is about 60% sellers and when it opened the buyers moved PRICE to the high which was a bargain for the sellers so they immediately sold it BACK TO SUPPORT Next, we trade PASR - not just candlesticks. Read and UNDERSTAND my Post 5868 to Brian again particularly what I wrote about PRICE structure. PASR is all about COMPLETE Price Action and Structure - NOT JUST CANDLES and SR. If you just trade candles and SR you will never be consistently profitable.

--- 帖子 #5916 ---
Perspective. It’s sometimes interesting and sometimes tedious for me when I read about analogies of life and trading. Hands up, I’ve posted a few. Here’s the question, what’s the point? I mean, if your life was aligned to your trading then maybe there is some value. But the reality check is that it isn’t and will never be, it’s an insane thing to even pretend this to be your goal. Recently I haven’t been posting charts, for a number of reasons but mainly because I’m taking one or two trades a week and not been active on lower time frames. So no real eye candy trades.. Also I’ve pulled myself up, for instance I traded the Boss candle last week and “only” netted 120 pips leaving more than that on the table because I didn’t close on the BRN. I did this because I’m tweaking my plan to work for me from a psychological and practical view to fit in with my work and personal schedule. So posting charts like these will not advance anyone’s learning and may only serve to confuse. Apologies for this but I’m a genuine person and won’t fit my charts to suit and look good for Forex Factory. That’s not helpful for anyone. So this post without any charts will no doubt be passed over by those who want action. Good. Ask yourself what are you trading? If you are trading for a better life, for more money, for gambling thrills, for boredom, intellectual stimulation... all of these reasons may lead to failure and self sabotage. I trade for all or most of those reasons and many more that I haven’t listed. Be honest. The drive and desire to sate these emotions can be harnessed into a resilience that becomes the very thread of the sword of Damocles and t he importance we put on becoming successful at trading can and does get in the way to becoming successful. Shift your perspective of your situation, should you be putting so much importance of becoming a successful trader? Should you be a trader at all? If you can honesty answer this without any bullshit then this message goes to everyone who trades. Stop whining, stop moaning. Suck it up and trade your plan. We live in a self absorbed society and one of my life’s mantras is that there will always be someone worse off than me. Think about the times you’ve experienced anxiety or worry. Isn’t it strange that these worries seem to be magnified when you can’t deal with them, like in the evening when you’re trying to get to sleep and then the next day you wonder what the fuss was about? These subconscious thoughts are with us all of the time and I believe make our decisions for us and maybe run our lives whether we want them to or not. Separating my life from trading and letting go of the superfluous egocentricity has allowed to myself to ask the question again. Am I cut out to be a trader at all? Are you? My answer to this is yes but at NO COST financially or emotionally. If you are expending anything other than time perhaps take a look in the mirror. If you are spending time away from your loved ones perhaps take a look in the mirror. If you need to be successful at trading take a look in the mirror. If you’ve been doing this years and still not where you want to be, take a look... Trade well and be careful what you are trading.

Hi Victoria First, to answer your question from about a week ago about my boots, they are called Packers. Kind of a lace up cowboy boot. I would guess out in the rural areas of Australia they have somethin similar. They actually lace up easily. I read more than 20 books and tried most of the methods I learned from those books I too have read a lot of books, shelves are full of them. Now I read more about psychology. There are some very good ones on psychology and trading out there, my favorite ones are seldom mentioned here on FF. I reach the conclusion that the PRICE and VOLUME are the most important elements for Forex I just want to make sure you realize that the volume you are given on your chart is only the volume from your broker. True volume in the Fx market doesn't exist like you would have in the Stock Markets. 'Volume' is not easy for Forex, 'time' is something mysterious for human Time is something that has always intrigued me when it comes to trading. I figure that the most important closings on candles are the Daily, weekly, and monthly close. Of these three I don't know if there is any one more important. Each represents the closing of something significant. Here on MT4 we have 1m, 5m, 15m, 1hr, and 4hr charts. The division of time is logical. But what if we had 6 minute charts, or 90 minute charts? The look of a chart can be vastly different. The market doesn't close at the end of a 5m candle like it does on a weekly one. So what my look like a standard looking candle on a 5m chart may be an engulfing one on a 6m chart. I'm not trying to over complicate things here so bear with me. I think this gets into part of what Strat talks about when he says "see the story behind the candles". Another thing I thought about with time and trading...The weekly candle is the only candle that when it ends the market closes on a weekly basis. I tend to think then that the weekly candle is the most important closing to show what the big players are doing. Which is also why trading boss swings on the daily chart can be very lucrative. I could go on. Spent a lot of time thinking about time... set up my goal step Awesome to set goals. But unlike what all the books tell you, I don't believe time constraints should be included. Time on the path of learning is not very predictable. We never know what psychological things will come along. To me trading has been more of a journey of self discovery then one of a "Method" of trading. So as each obstacle on "The Path" is encountered it is handled. Posting my plan in a public thread, I will feel ashamed if I don't do it Posting your plan is not required. If it helps though, super. One thing you will find is that your plan will evolve a lot as you progress as a trader. My lack of practice for PASR You are doing the right thing. Practice. Also because you are staying involved and engaged in the thread it can be the right practice. Hopefully this was some of what you are looking for. I always appreciate your posts as they make me put my thinking cap on to put to words my thoughts and actions when it comes to trading. Rufus

Hi Victoria, How I handle a trade and approach stops may not be right for you but have a read of this post which may help you understand how I approach risk. https://www.forexfactory.com/showthr...7#post11263487 Personally I like to set an amount I'm happy to lose on a trade and don't just get in once and set a hard stop. If price action starts to look like I was wrong I get out manually and take the loss. If you find you are getting stopped out a lot and price then moves in your direction, set the stops a bit bigger and enter with a smaller lot size. You can always add on to the trade when price goes your way. If you are new to trading or new to PASR you are not going to get in perfectly each time. Hell I don't get in perfectly and I've been on the path for many, many months now. I have a long way to go too. Trade small, let price breathe and see how price reacts and moves around the shadow. You can only do that if you allow price room and don't get stopped out all the time. Price will consolidate and spike up and down while the big boys are moving it around and you need to allow that space in your trading.

--- 帖子 #6003 ---
Hi Strat Once again thank you for your feedback... My feedback on what I have learnt below: "there is no ""June BUEB"" Agreed. The position is wrong. It should not be part of an uptrend like my example. To be valid it will as the last candle occurs at the bottom of a downtrend reversing the previous bearish candle. Body will be larger beginning the close or below the close of the previous bearish candle's body and the high of the BUEB body will close higher than closing body of the previous bearish candle's body. The April Candle on my chart is a valid BUEB "Big Boss - PRICE is REJECTED from RESISTANCE!" Yes. I missed that. I was fascinated by the triangle consolidation pattern forming that I did not realize price was respecting a SR at 111ish that I did not even have on my Big Boss and Boss charts. I did not see the June bullish candle stopping at this level. I was watching the July candle (possible Shooting star or Doji in process of forming) but did not pay attention that the wick was beyond resistance but the upper body of the candle was at the resistance level indicating that sellers are defending this level. Also I chose to ignore it because it has not closed yet. Wrongly, I guess as I should take notice of what the buyers and sellers are doing. The bulls have not yet been able to breach this level. This is even more evident on the Boss Chart where buyers were repelled at this level in May before testing it again during June before finally breaking through in July only to drop down again to retest this level. I did not see this. "short term trend WAS up - PRICE will likely go sideways" I agree that price will likely go sideways due to the consolidation that is in progress in the pattern. However my view was that the short term trend in play has not ended yet viewing it from the Big Boss perspective as the June candle is bullish, the July candle has not closed yet and although it is a doji indicating indecision or price agreement for now between the sellers and buyers, it is still bullish on my chart. As mentioned above I chose to ignore it and so missed the important interaction that is taking place now between the buyers and sellers...(just a thought that I can visualize...the current candle displays the realtime haggling going on between the buyers and sellers in the marketplace and even though it is not over, the lower frames shows the result of gains and losses made to this point in time within the movement of the higher frame candle - not sure if I make sense...but something for me to ponder on a bit more) "You missed the most important PRICE ACTION on the Boss" Agreed. I was reacting to the breakout from the WCC and not seeing what price was doing. See my comments above. "Be careful using trend lines - they can CONFUSE more they can help" Noted. And I think part of why I was missing important PA on the higher levels was because of the trendlines forming the triangle. i was not seeing what was going on price-wise inside the triangle. "but for each time frame concentrate on the most recent candles and PASR in addition to reciting history" Very important lesson for me. I am guilty of looking at the bigger picture of patterns forming such as trends, triangles, channels but not looking at what the candles are telling me that are forming that pattern. PASR does not just consist of a trendline between two SR levels with PA candles at both ends. Well, simplistically speaking it does seem that way but that is not the whole truth. It consists of individual candles forming the path of the trend from the swing where it started to the swing that ends the trend with each candle individually contributing to the trend. Each candle is a chapter in the story of buyers and sellers meeting, negotiating, sometimes calmly, sometimes frenetically haggling over bargains, sometimes not making sales or sometimes not having enough goods to sell....( I am now seeing pictures of a caravan of camels walking through the dunes to the market between the date palms by an oasis in a desert somewhere... :-) Sorry for waffling but I learn more by making visual connections. "Forget DSRI - I just made it up to have fun with and sucker in the Indicator crowd!" Yes, the Dynamic Support and Resistance Indicator, and you certainly did sucker them in....they were panting for the code and stressed out when it wouldn't work! They did not even SEE that it was compiled with Strats GoForthandMultply.Cum compiler although it was printed there in black and white in the code posted on the old thread! :-) But jokes aside, I was actually under the impression that it was a variation of drawing trend lines through the closes of candles instead of the extremes off the candles as with a classic trend line. A specific of use of these trend lines (or DSRI) through the closes was illustrated by Blackeagle to indicate trend line breaks and possible entries with PA candles at these breaks and several other posts through the old thread seemed to confirm this as well. The most recent references that confirmed this differentiation was one in posts 12985 and 12986 on page 650 of the old thread where I am reading now. If the term and the drawing of trendlines through the closes no longer applies I'll stop using it. I know you have mentioned in several posts that novices should stick to drawing trendlines from the candles extremes and not the closes as this applied to more advanced strategies. Thanks Pete

--- 帖子 #6022 ---
PASR work on all time frame. So you can go for whatever time frame you want. However, as a newbie of PASR, is recommended to follow the path and then start from daily time frame. What daily time frame do is allow you to take your time doing analysis, reducing the chances of making mistakes. The lower the time frame, the easier you make mistake due to rushing to trade, unclear thought, things that interrupt you which make you miss the entry/exit, etc etc. Plus, if you want to maximize the stress free aspect of PASR, daily time frame definitely where to go for instead. (Somewhat similar answer had been given multiple times by strat and the rest throughout the old thread and this post.)

Hi Victoria Here is a terminology thing for you I do to help with trading psychology. The only "bad" trade is one you execute not according to your trading plan, win or lose. --- 帖子 #6085 ---
Ali, If you are trading the daily chart (worker) you need to check your charts daily. I had the same issue as you at the start and it drove me mad. My little people would see price not doing what I wanted and would make me close my position. Then it would reverse and go my way. I started checking the charts just twice a day and then finally got down to once a day as it should be. Whatever time frame you trade you should check the candles when they close. For me in the UK daily candles close at 10pm. That's when I check the progress of trades and check for new entries. We only trade and make trading decisions when candles close. There's no point in checking them at any other time. Best advice I can give and I wish I'd done it earlier when I started out, is to close your charts and only open them at the daily close. It's hard but it's the only way forward to stop yourself panicking about what price is doing. Also as others have said, check your position size. If you trade too large you will worry and that will make you want to check the charts.

Happy weekend all Every year around this time I rethink all I do and not just with trading. This year is proving to be a revamping of a lot of what is done for trading. Detailing out in writing my trading plan for 5m PASR, Trend PASR, Basic PASR, and Swing PASR. There is a plan in place right now, mainly scribbled on index cards. I want specific things included that will ultimately make its way to my trading journal, which is getting a total overhaul. The Journal will be keeping track of not only trades and charts, but will also include things like day of the week, emotional state, time frame, just to name a few. Another August project that will continue for a number of months.... Working on using PASR during the Asian session. On my side of the globe especially in my time zone it would be handy. The way I figure, if there is a way to extract 20 to 30 pips daily on average from this session I will have to find it. Now for some psychology stuff. Two days ago a kid that works for me started arguing with me when I told him what he was doing was VERY unsafe. He refused to admit that he was wrong, I guess he would rather have fallen 16 feet down unfinished stairs than put a ladder square on the floor. Fiberglass step ladders can walk across the floor if they are not set up correctly. His would have walked down the stairs. I finally yelled at him to shut the F@@@ up and quit arguing with me about things I am trying to teach him to keep his sorry ass safe. So what does this have to do with trading? 90% of small business fail in the first 5 years. 90% of traders don't become hugely successful. Of this 90% what percentage refuse to take responsibility for their own actions? Could it be 80 or 90%? Blaming and pointing fingers seems to be the modus operandi for most of the employee, business, and corporate world. Traders technically have no one to point to but themselves. Sure they can blame the broker for stop hunting. Or Trump for saying something, or the guru who called the trade. But who placed the trade? Unless we are 100% comfortable with the outcome win or lose, 100% comfortable with accepting all risk, and also claiming all responsibility for actions we should not place the trade. When you are out and about doing things watch people shift blame from themselves to others or some other thing. It is an epidemic. I have yelled at people for years now for not taking responsibility for their own actions. God save them if they try to push blame toward me when it is not warranted. Or they push undeserved blame toward those that work for me. I guess when you have been self-employed for almost 30 years you start to not give a shit about stepping on toes. I digress... It may sound like I am a hard-ass to work for, but I'm not, had people work for me for 15 years. Just a hard-ass on those who do or say stupid things around me and not take responsibility. Anyway. Some weekend thoughts for you all. Rufus

GBPJPY &amp; EURJPY Don't have the account size to comfortably trade the weekly chart yet, So why do it? You adjust your position size to accommodate your RISK meaning that you can have a large RISK which is small in $ terms. If the Weekly chart is going to be your choice of time frame then you should drop down to the Daily chart for your entries which is another way to reduce the size of your RISK. but i will continue to trade them on demo so that when the time comes that i do have a larger account i can trade the weekly stress free and with confidence. You will have a very RUDE AWAKENING with a very blunt object when you switch to trading a REAL, LIVE account with your hard earned money which will be the opposite of "stress free". Again, how many times do I have to post that trading on ""DEMO"" is feeding the lions? I have stated the reasons for NOT trading on "demo" many times so do yourself a BIG favour and find what these are. You need to switch from "demo" trading to PAPER TRADING. From what you have posted it seems you have an understanding of PASR but STOP DREAMING of pips/profit and GET OFF "demo" and paper trading as soon as possible. Start trading with a LIVE account (but with the smallest position size your broker offers) with your REAL, HARD EARNED money to enter the REAL world of trading.

--- 帖子 #6345 ---
Hi Strat, I find the support I draw myself are having a large different from yours, taking the below EURUSD as a example, your price are still above the support, but mine is already became a new resistance. When I draw the support, I try to find a candle which formed as a peak or bottom, firstly on big boss chart then boss chart then draw a horizontal line at its closing price and the high / low, and check do the price response to my line, I will say this is a support or resistance if price reacted to it more then 2 times. Lastly slightly adjust the area to fit the candle which reacted with it. By the way, although I already try my broker with GMT+3 server time, but some candles are still different from yours, is GMT+3 not the correct time? Generally but not always, once price has moved significantly away from the shadow and the 9sma, one can expect a retrace. --- 帖子 #6486 ---
Mental Fitness My parents visited over the weekend, it was not particularly enjoyable. Rub, I'm sorry you are having to learn the hard way. I have posted on this many times but it is probably in my "old" original thread. Just like an athlete who can only perform to his/her maximum when they are "in shape" both physically and mentally, so too, must we only trade when we are "in shape" mentally and physically. I used to use trading as a refuge when things were "not right" in my "situation" only to learn that these were the times when my trading performance nose dived. It was hard to do, but eventually I learned to walk away from trading and get my mind onto other things when in this situation. Until you are mentally and physically 100% ""in shape"" to trade, do anything except trade. You will not miss anything except frustration and losses. Resolve your "problems", clear your mind and get back in to a "happy frame of mind" then decide whether you are "fit" to trade again. Lastly, don't brood over your situation - you are not alone, it happens to all of us - you will get through it - just give it time.

AUDJPY Good analysis Pete. Here are a few notes: Big Boss: Immediate Trend down. Price close below the SR 80,633 on my chart. PRICE doesn't care about specific PRICE levels except for occasions where the Big Boys have specific targets around BRNs - Big Round Numbers. GBPUSD is a pair targeted by the Big Boys on BRNs. Just be aware that our SR is areas or zones of SR rather than a specific PRICE . JPY pairs only have 2 digits after the decimal point so 80,633 is 80.63 Make sure you are aware that there is a huge support area between 80 and 72 Boss: Immediate Trend down. PASR Out of curiosity, has anyone ever tried de-trending the strat shadow? In my early pre - PASR days, I tried every indicator and indicator combination ever developed with all the flashing lights and bells and whistles you could ever dream of with every combination of settings on every time frame. There is no indicator ever developed or will be developed which can provide the analyst with more accurate information than PRICE . This reminds me of the report I did in my ""old"" (2009) original thread on Ronald MacD onald (MACD), so here it is again: ***************************************************************************************************** ""Here are just a few of the many failings of Ronald MacD onald (MACD) As I have said in an earlier post, indicators are for those who do not understand PASR. Having said that, I respect traders who make a profitable living using them and I am open to anyone who can show me how to profit consistently using the damned things! Let’s first remember that indicators are an EXCUSE for NOT understanding or being able to SEE what PRICE is doing. As such they are a derivation , and, many times, several derivations of PRICE and will always be at least one level of accuracy below PRICE depending on their formula/code complexity They were also developed to PREDICT future price action! The prediction being entirely subjective to the interpretation of the trader. So let’s take a closer look at Ronald MacD onald: To the newbie or inexperienced, I can see that it can be THEIR Holy Grail – in history and back testing it looks perfect – but any indicator will ALWAYS look perfect in history, back testing – HINDSIGHT . It has to, because it is using the latest information that CLOSED the last candle and candles depending on the number of bars it uses for calculation. However, while you are trading LIVE at the HARD RIGHT EDGE when PRICE is jumping UP and DOWN , well, good luck! As an exercise, put Ronald on ANY chart and scroll backwards or forwards and SEE this useless piece of crap jump up and down all over the place . In other words what you see TODAY is NOT what you will see when today is “ x ” days later. If you still don’t get it, today might show Ronald at the bottom but in 20 days time, it will be somewhere else. If you still don’t see it, take a screen shot of where it is at today and one 30 days later and SEE the difference. Let’s look at how Ronald is coded: MACD stands for ‘Moving Average Convergence Divergence’ and works by measuring the difference between a fast and a slow exponential moving average. The three components that make up the MACD Indicator are constructed in the following way. Signal Line = 12 Day EMA - 26 Day EMA Reference Line = 9 Period EMA of the Signal Line Histogram = Signal Line - Reference Line So, we are taking the exponential moving average of PRICE 12 days ago and from that, subtracting the exponential moving average of PRICE 26 days ago and calling it the Signal Line. Then, we are going to take a 9 period exponential moving average of THAT difference and call it the Reference Line. Then we will create a histogram of the difference between the Signal line and the Reference Line. An exponential moving average of an exponential moving average!!!!! No wonder this thing LAGS! So, using my Mark I eyeball, I can SEE , without any calculations whatsoever, the difference between PRICE 12 days ago and PRICE 26 days ago. Why does anyone need an indicator to do this? What does PRICE 12 days ago or 26 days ago have to do with where PRICE is at now? I want to trade in the NOW , not in the past. I can SEE with my Mark I eyeball where PRICE is NOW compared to where it was 12 days ago, 26 days ago, 50 days ago etc. Why do I need an indicator for that? Let’s use the Worker AUDUSD from Sept 2003 to March 2004 as an example: First, here are some restrictions on the use of Ronald: Gerald Appel, (Ronald MacD onald, the developer of MACD) claims that the MACD works better in trends and particularly in a rising market more than a falling market. It is also universally accepted that a buy signal is more reliable if the crossover occurs below the histogram and similarly for a sell signal that occurs above the histogram. Most newbies and inexperienced users of squiggly wiggly lines don’t even know this. Worse still, they also use it for exits. Despite claims that it is the perfect indicator for trends, Ronald is USELESS at monitoring trends for exit signals. This is because the reference line is an AVERAGE of the signal line (which is also ANOTHER MOVING AVERAGE ) and it will collapse into the signal line under constant trending conditions, causing whipsaws. This happens when the value of the signal line remains the same for any length of time, i.e. The difference between the 12 day EMA and the 26 day EMA is the same (constant). Look at what Ronald thinks of the trend between Oct 2003 and January 2004! How does that help anyone? In fact it doesn’t help – it keeps those people trading MACD OUT of trending trades! (That’s GOOD – more trend profits for PASR Trend traders!) But wait a minute! The Ronald MacD onald experts know the answer! When any indicator doesn’t follow PRICE it is called divergence. GREAT! So for 3 months we are in limbo because our cast in concrete Holy Grail Gospel is shouting out “divergence”. When do these Ronald experts know divergence is over? How do they measure divergence? Is 1 pip divergence? Is divergence expressed in terms of time? How many divergences are needed BEFORE PRICE moves? NOBODY KNOWS! Now, if you are in the Ronald MacD onald Elite Club, you will be told about Hidden Divergence. This is when PRICE does the OPPOSITE to what the indicator does (as in the recent EURGBP example). WHAT? PRICE does the opposite to what the indicator does? Give me a break – PRICE LEADS and NEVER, EVER does the opposite of any indicator! Who gives a flying shit what an indicator does – all we care about is PRICE . PRICE is KING, QUEEN, LORD &amp; COUNTRY I could go on, and on ad infinitum but hopefully you get the message.""

--- 帖子 #6621 ---
PASR When PASR fails as it does at times since no strategy/method/system/black box is 100%, always immediately CLOSE your position(s). Most of the time, when PASR fails, it is due to some unforeseen negative news event, geopolitical issue or geographical disaster/catastrophe causing the Market and therefore PRICE to go out of balance. Wait at least 24 hours and maybe more depending on the particular circumstance, for the Market and PRICE to recover and resume balance. Out of balance Markets under these conditions create volatility and high volume and are ideal for short term traders to capitalise on.

I think I know the reasons, as I've noticed that I get the same behavior pattern time and time again and only by focusing on breaking that pattern and sustaining a new behavior I can overcome it. I wouldn't call it over-trading as I do not act on just any PA setup but I seem to be taking 1:1 R:R trades and not picking the best setups available but rather taking most of the favorable setups that PA offers. The exceptionally good setups bring great R:R, great profit but then those mediocre setups some go to profit, some to loss and at the end of the week/month I get much less profit that I could have gotten if those bad trades were not taken at all. Then I wonder why do I take those low-reward trades? One reason, I think, could be that I do not want to jump into a trade too late, as I noticed that from some of the other members posting here. Maybe that's my risk aversion kicking in, but seems that I only take the last bite of the swing. I'll post some examples of those losing trades tomorrow.

PASR Now seems a really good time to quote extracts from my Dr. Joe conversations and faxes: From this came his very simple method: Buy when it goes up and sell when it goes down . He went on to make $millions doing this and I subsequently learned he passed away a very rich and contented man knowing that he had beaten the “whores” at their own game. “How do you know when to stop buying?” On the same fax was his handwritten reply, “When it stops going up.” So I wrote on it, “How do you know when it stops going up?” His handwritten reply, “When it starts going down.” So I wrote on it, “How do you know when it stops going up and starts going down?” His handwritten reply, “When people start selling.” After going round like this in riddles, I pleaded with him to “just give it to me straight”. He sent a fax saying this would be his last communication with me and that if I didn’t understand how to buy when it goes up and sell when it goes down, I had no business trading. His final paragraph was one which I ignored, like everything else he told me, until a couple of years ago when I realized what a dumb, stupid, arrogant, stubborn idiot I had been: He said I would only be wrong twice using his simple method: My understanding of what he was telling me is this: Buy when prices are moving up. Buy each retrace/dip. Keep buying until the last retrace becomes a trend change which is the one trade you lose on. Sell when prices are moving down. Sell each retrace/rally. Keep selling until the last retrace becomes a trend change which is the second trade you lose on. Sometimes I wonder if old Dr. Joe was smoking something but then when I see those long legged dojis before a significant move, I know he was right. Thank you, Dr. Joe

PASR Hammer It's all about probability so the more variables we can get on ""our side"" the higher probability of a successful trade. Conversely, the less variables on ""our side"" or the less favourable conditions, the lower the probability of a successful trade. It all comes down to RISK - our RISK tolerance and then how we manage that RISK. Does that help?

When I've had time in the last month I've been attempting to study Elliot Wave theory in an effort to help me get into fewer trades with a higher probability. My idea is to have extra confluence and narrow down my focus by having an idea when price may turn as well as where it's likely to go. Strat will probably tell me I'm overcomplicating the simplicity of PASR but there was a major change last month in the UK with margin regulations which has led me to concentrate more and take less trades. This margin ruling has meant I could get into less trades (only around 1/4 of my usual) and last month I fell foul of the new rules by missing good opportunities and let the bad ones run so had a bad month as a consequence. It's my fault for not managing it sooner but I'm proud of the fact I've picked myself up and refocused on what I can do about it. To my mind having less margin is only a good thing really but does mean upping my game and being less cavalier with my entries. Anyway to the point of my post (if there is one). While on my sunlounger on holiday I read my digital copy of Elliot Wave Theory while sipping my beer and peeking out of my sunglasses as the many scantily clad ladies round the pool. This made studying all the more difficult as you can imagine. At points my iPad actually turned off I got so distracted by the view. Anyhow, Strat has mentioned Elliot Wave many times previously and while not the focus of PASR it's another string to add to the bow for confirmation of price action at support and resistance. I'm happy with my timeframe now and with my basic PASR which is what I seem to have fallen into as my use of the strategy. New rules means the need to adapt to the market so I've topped up my account but still am not able to put on the volume I could before. Hence my plan is to look for A+ setups only in an attempt to increase my strike rate. Not sure if its the right plan but lets see how it goes. Elliot Wave I'm finding extremely complicated to both understand/remember all the rules/guidelines and also spot on charts and draw in. So many wave types of varying numbers but the basics are the impulse waves and corrective waves. You can draw a seemingly endless amount of waves and in different ways too. Ask me to put waves on a chart and then wipe it and ask me to do the same again 2 days later and I'd likely draw something slightly or radically different. It's just a guide to entry and forecasting like any other toll in the toolbox and can be interpreted differently by different traders. This is why we TRADE WHAT WE SEE and not what others tell us to. Before anyone shoots me down for polluting the thread with non PASR related posts I'm still trading PASR. This is basic PASR based on key support and resistance but adding a little extra confirmation into the mix with Elliot. What I SEE as Elliot on MY charts anyway. I'm looking only at one particular pattern of Elliot which is the 1,2,3,4,5 pattern and within that pattern ideally when wave 3 is complete. Reason being the main impulse wave (3) is easy to spot on a chart as it's the largest wave and tends to stick out once it's complete. I'm using this to look for key resistance above the bottom of wave 3 which will be the start of wave 5 at turning point 4. See, it all sounds overly complicated when you write it down as above but look at it on a chart and you'll see it's simple to spot wave 3s. It's also massively helping me set targets for my trades as if I'm right and Elliot plays out you know where price should go and how it should get there which is a massive confidence boost. I'm finding it's helping the little people stay calm as I know where it should go and it's not going to go straight there in one go. There are little waves on the way. Early days though and I'm still getting to grips with my understanding. Over the weekend I went through 10 charts and attempted to draw in waves by stepping forward candle by candle. Most worked as expected and some didn't but on the whole it does give you more clarity on short term trends. I'd be interested to compare with anyone else who uses Elliot Wave in their trading to help find PASR entries. Wonder if I'm on the right track identifying them. See chart below which is a trade I took on Monday. On the worker and boss this pair is horrible. Sideways action so no trend PASR trading to be had. The trade I took on H1 which isn't my usual entry timeframe but I probably would have taken this 2 candles later on H4 anyway if I'd been awake and seen it. I flicked to H1 to see how the Elliot wave looked closer in as I'm trying to get my head around the smaller waves within the bigger ones. the a,b,cs and zig zags etc. There I spotted the glaring 200MA price action candle. It's roughly around where the next wave SHOULD start IF the pair was going to follow WHAT I THOUGHT was Elliot Wave! Lots of ifs and buts but we all need a reason to get in the market and trade so I took it. As I entered on H1 I managed the trade on H1 and I'm now out. If I'd have taken it on H4 I'd still be in but that wasn't the plan so I'm missing a little profit possibly but I caught pretty much the whole wave anyway. I'm expecting a turnaround at my red support line anyway. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Attached Image (click to enlarge) I'm not intending to post Elliot Wave analysis here as it's not what we're about but if Strat doesn't mind the odd few numbers on a chart I'm happy to keep sharing my thoughts on it as a means of spotting possible entry opportunities and adding more confluence to my trades. What is required to attain this mastery? How long does it take? What are the secrets to mastering anything? Undistracted focused thought is required for that gleam of light to flourish. Yet we live in a world of distractions. Can you sit down without looking at your phone? When Michelangelo sculpted “David” he had reference points. Leonardo Da Vinci had reference points for the Mona Lisa. I have reference points for building a curved staircase. If something distracts you from price or your reference points, your focused thought and the steps to mastery are harmed. Michelangelo and Leonardo Da Vinci could have written a book about sculpting. When wisdom and knowledge converge we get understanding. We are then approaching mastery. Mastery is accomplished as an individual. No one can make someone else proficient in trading. There are no magic tricks, yet that is what many seek in looking for the holy grail indicator to accomplish all their dreams of wealth. The second trading turns to “magic” lines or indicators and focus is drawn away from price and the reference points, focus is lost and that “Gleam of light” is extinguished. So Strat can impart his knowledge. We then interpret this knowledge. Then as it is applied to the markets we get wisdom. Then gradually, bit by bit, we see the story behind the candles giving us understanding. Mastery is culmination of all. The most powerful and adaptable computer in the world is between your shoulders and on top of your neck. Use it to its capacity.

GBPUSD H4 So, you are a RISK TAKER! While it worked out for you this time, it will NOT over the long term. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Take a closer look at that Outside Candle - it had a 20 pips body, a 40 pips wick and a 48 pips tail. That is an "over grown" doji showing indecision with the buyers showing more strength than the sellers. Did you have a PLAN when you traded this or was it a sudden Adrenalin rush of blood? Let's look at your trade. You traded an Inside Candle inside a huge volatile, with no direction, candle. The ""accepted"" and widely used rule for trading off an Inside Candle is to enter with a Stop Order above/below the previous candle's extremes - see my yellow lines on your chart. GBPNZD 4Hr Study Please take this with the spirit it was written in and not a literal exact science. I have used a singular character to simplify the market for my own purposes, of course there are thousands of participants in the market but only a few that move them. 1. Confluence of Worker PASR level and 200EMA support. Big Buyer has come into the market challenging trapped sellers at point A. 2. Where are the sellers? Market pauses. The buyer from 1.9150 is still looking to buy. Are there more positions to buy from our trapped sellers at A? Yes. 3. Our buyer at 1. has bought the sellers orders and they may have also joined in the buying. We have reached a profit zone at 1.96. This part of the order is filled. 4. Sellers take the buy orders with a target back to point A. 5. Our buyer is still hungry and buys again at point A. Now price is at 1.95 he is going to always buy at 1.95 whenever he can because he now wants to sell anything he buys on the way up, maybe looking towards 1.98 6. He buys again. Anything at 1.95 is going to be bought knowing whatever he sells on the way up to maybe 2.0 he is going to make profit. 7. The market reacts. There are sellers at 1.9750 and 1.98, they have orders they want to sell at this price. 8. Our buyer is hungry, he takes all the market can offer him down to 1.9520. There are no more sell orders below this level. Our buyer has bought everything.The market has to move upwards because they are no sellers left at this level. 9. We have now reached our 1.98 target. Every buy order below this level is profit. Our buyer is now in control and he wants to SELL but can only do this to buyers who also see that 2.0 target. Our buyer offers them this deal. Our buyer is now the SELLER. 10. Our buyer stops buying and is now selling. He will sell anything above 1.80 until all of his buy orders below 1.80 are sold. So this is my view of a market move and how I am studying to develop this view. Point 6 and 7 "Strat's Periscope" identifies this particular buyer I think and the cat is out of the bag.. Can you guess when our buyer pops up again? (clue. he is living at number 6 and 7). Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #7479 ---
USDJPY Excellent, Terry, and thank you for doing this for your fellow traders - TRADERS HELPING TRADERS Just one comment about our MT4 charts - this is for all PASR traders: MT4 is not the best charting platform but it is FREE so we really cannot complain. One of its inadequacies is the DATES on the Weekly charts. MT4 always shows the BEGINNING of the Week starting on SUNDAY . As PASR traders, we have no interest in the beginning of the Week PASR traders NEED the END OF THE WEEK so we have to ADD 5 days to the date shown on our Weekly MT4 charts. Using Terry's example: The Boss Swing Low is correctly identified on our Weekly charts as April 08, 2018 Attached Image (click to enlarge) But that is SUNDAY and when we toggle over to our Worker chart on Friday after 5pm New York time, April 08, 2018 has been and gone and is in the past. What we SEE is FRIDAY, APRIL 13, 2018 so that is the earliest day we can include this information into PASR Attached Image (click to enlarge) So, when discussing dates on our Weekly charts, ALWAYS add 5 days to the date shown by MT4.

PASR Thank you, Ben for identifying Post 6370. There is so much value to take from that post as it was written by PASR student AstonDan on October 14, 2009 For the benefit of PASR students, here are the important points: At around this time I had also begun reading some posts by a crazy fella (Strat)who traded the Daily and Weekly charts and who was encouraged by Nicola (Elitejets) to start his own thread on his method so, on 27 February 2009, I suppose I actually began to understand. Slowly but surely I began to appreciate more and more what I was looking at (It’s funny to think I actually found it quite daunting to post my first chart). Strat took the time to help me see for myself, there were no easy rides and we fell out once or twice, but to his eternal credit, he stuck with me. I traded demo as if it was real money, I kept a detailed log, and during this time, I don’t think I actively read anything else on the markets – I simply read MY charts each day and kept a clean mind. So things were great, but we entered a period of consolidation (at least it was to my eyes then – I suspect Strat and others were trading quite profitably off the daily at the time, but my understanding was not there yet and frankly I am an impatient bugger – still!), so I ventured off into the world and found a few other traders who helped me further understand – particularly the fluidity of price and time, and trading truly naked. Over the summer I began reading (and trading) much more feverishly (by this time I was also live). I learnt more and more and continued to succeed, however small, because Strat and others helped me set solid foundations based on price, support and resistance. All that’s past is prologue however, so perhaps to say a little about where I am now gives greater credence to where I’ve been. Please note, the following is not to denigrate from anything Strat is teaching on the thread – I can only trade the way I do now because of how I was taught. It’s to Strat’s credit, not detriment. I’ve gravitated back to daily bars for three reasons: 1. Time means nothing to me, only PRICE. PRICE can be read perfectly well End Of Day so why spend time looking at them go up and down all day. 2. For want of a better descriptive, randomness. P RICE reacts to news. The reaction is not often indicative of the bigger (global) picture. The further away you stand, the more you can see. 3. Money. I’m more profitable taking the broader view. For anyone who is where I was this time last year, trading is dirt simple; establish a directional bias, and trade it. It’s only a two horse race. Strat is helping you identify that directional bias, and while that’s only part of the challenge we all face, its value cannot be underestimated. Dan is an example of what I always say " Read, Learn and UNDERSTAND PASR then FIND your own personal trading style". Just like many PASR students, Dan went on to become "" consistently profitable "" and probably achieved his dream of owning his Aston Martin. My only disappointment is that he, like all those who became " consistently profitable ", left the thread and public trading forums and had no desire to help others.

--- 帖子 #7528 ---
I did That kind of post are the ones that keep me going when I'm doubtful about trading (not too often). So thanks for bringing it out so I could read it again. I also love Dan's analogy of shop-environments (respect financial markets) he made in another forum (the link is in the mentioned post of the old thread) I have a particularly simplistic view on this which many may not agree with but there you go: I run a shop re-selling all manor of amazing widgets and gizmos. I do not manufacture, I’m merely a middleman trying to identify and profit from the demand of my customers. I try to buy my widgets and gizmos at a price which I think I can then sell on to my customers at a profit. Sometimes, I will buy an item whose value to my customer suddenly shoots through the ceiling. Sometimes my products show a steady and continues growth in demand. Sometimes there is no immediate demand for a product I have just bought, but over the coming minutes, hours, days, weeks, there is a steady increase in customers coming through my door so I will buy more of these products until I have saturated the market and demand dries up. Sometimes I buy a widget and nobody wants it, and in order to free up my capital to reinvest in products for which there is demand in the marketplace (or in which I judge there will be a requirement), I have to sell at break even or at a loss. My shop has many products in it. Some are in demand, some are not, and I balance my book accordingly. I particularly admire Leon, Pipmutt , Daytrading and some of the traders on here who seem to apply a far deeper understanding and intelligence to the market, however for me, the FX market is just another shop on the high street and is no different to selling bread or sex toys. Supply, demand, profit and loss. The rest, to me, is needless froth (yes, I am aware the term needless will be contested by many, including the aforementioned members). One poor selling product does not (or should not) spell the end for my business, one great product does not mean I’ll start arriving at work by helicopter. I will subscribe to one major difference with the general business model however that, as a retail trader (which most on these forums are), I often find myself akin to being sat in a dinghy in the middle of the Atlantic on a cloudy day with no sun or landmark to set sail for – welcome to world of FX, where the only constant is change; if you run a McDonalds or a typical retail chain, there are established blueprints for success (or expected success based upon establsihed best practice) whereas in trading, everything changes (please see the thread on negative expectancy in which far smarter people than me have debated around this). There is no holy grail in anything in life, whether you run a corner shop or an billion dollar hedge fund, but the problem with the retail currency market is it is incredibly easy to enter and is deliberately marketed as an easy way to make a lot of money. That combination generally attracts the kind of personality which isn’t going to set the world on fire in any field, at least not legally. And as for the whole 95% fail rate which is used to scare every newbie (of which I am one) away, 95% of people in life fail, just look around. Those who want to succeed will find a way, however long it takes and however hard the road. I think it was one of Thomas Edison’s quotes which sums it up best: “Opportunity is missed by most people because it is dressed in overalls, and looks like work.” Or perhaps Benjimen Franklin’s summed it up better: “If your head is wax, don't walk in the sun.”

This reminds me of something I read in a book a long time ago in which the author likened trading short term time frames to standing next to the highway watching the traffic speed by through a pair of binoculars. You can't see clearly because of tunnel vision and the cars moving so fast that you move closer and closer to see better until BANG, you get run over. Just another statistic. By standing back and watching the traffic flow past from a nearby hill (Trading the daily charts) you can view the big picture and the cars are moving a lot slower because of the distance which gives you a lot of time to make your trading decisions. I think this is very true for inexperienced traders like me to rather stand back and trade the longer term charts. --- 帖子 #7622 ---
Hi BTS Two reasons really: The New York close in my Time Zone is at 11pm local time which in itself is not a problem. Unfortunately my normal day starts at 4 am which makes staying up to watch the New York close a bit uncomfortable in the sense that I need my beauty sleep . By the time I get a chance to have a look see where the daily candle has closed the next day's candle is already 8 - 12 hours old. Not a train smash as this probably serves as a confirmation of price direction after the previous daily candle close. The problem is on the days when I only get a chance to look at the charts after I get home from work by which time the New York trading has progressed so far it is better to wait for the next New York close to check PA The above got me thinking that a Trading day can be divided roughly in three sessions: The Asian session gets going after the New York close (11PM my time) 8 hours after that (7AM my time) their session has progressed substantially and they are ready to hand over trading to Europe and London which constitutes the second 8 hour candle. The 3rd 8 hour candle kicks of at 3pm my time when New York starts coming online. This candle then reflects the New York Session. So in essence my reasoning is that 8 hour candles approximately coincides with the 3 main trading sessions of Asia, London and New York. This got me thinking that maybe the Big Boys might be making use of 8 hour candles or that their business day actions would coincide with these candles giving them some value in following the big boys of each session. So if these candles are of value for PASR purposes it gives me two opportunities to analyse firstly the result of the Asian session and secondly the result of the London session. Don't know if this makes sense but this is what made me think of 8 hour charts. If they are not really of use I will make another plan to use the daily candles as recommended. Another option is off course to focus on 4 hour charts and less but I was thinking that 8 hour candles could possibly be a usable compromise. Regards Pete

Hi Pete Interesting concept. Anything else in between these candles coincides with PASR levels. Using candles of varying duration at these levels is merely a view of where price is NOW and HAS BEEN in the past. It could be 15min, 4hr or 1 min but what is common will be where PRICE is now on the chart (hint Strat Shadow). I'm trying to determine what makes sense to me and you realise that we use all of this information to plan our trades. It's good to look at the Asian, UK and US Sessions in isolation and then put them together for learning purposes but unless you are planning on day trading these sessions it's more for interest than anything else(no need for 8 hour candles, draw some boxes instead). PASR This reply is for everyone. I also tried 365 on and off some times I only add this ""if"" I see the Big Boys are using it when I add S/R levels its too much lines. There are 2 aspects to this. First, you have to practice identifying SR levels/area/zones on each of our 3 time frames. This will have more lines than Kings Cross Station and is ONLY for practice. Second, your trading chart will ONLY have resistance above where PRICE is NOW and support below where PRICE is NOW . We are not concerned with anything beyond those levels/areas/zones UNTIL there is PASR . I still trying to figure out how to avoid unwanted lines. I have a very simple rule for this. Do not add anything to your chart which you do not use or adds value. If you have something on your chart which you never use or only occasionally use - get rid of it! Everything on your chart MUST provide value to you and assist you in your trading. If it doesn't, trash it. Trading is both visual and mental which triggers our psychology. Our psychology is both "full front" and sub-conscious. We use "full front" to SEE, EVALUATE, ANALYSE and MAKE DECISIONS. Our sub-conscious (Little People) is trolling in the background of our trading brain looking for things which are "not right" - they are interested in our SURVIVAL and will do everything to PROTECT us. Anything that "they" do not understand, they will "red" flag which will both affect and impact our "full front" psychology. Do NOT under estimate the POWER of our MIND, the POWER of our BRAIN, the POWER of our TRADING BRAIN. All these compute and make scenarios and decisions faster than any computer built by MAN now, or in the future. Those who don't believe this never had the communications I had with Dr. Joe.
