--- 帖子 #7750 ---
ADR = average daily range ATR = average true range ADR is the same as ATR when your timeframe is the daily chart. ATR displays the average range of the candles(distance high to low) on selected timeframe so ADR diplays only the average range of the daily candles

--- 帖子 #7751 ---
ADR and ATR ADR, Average Daily range and ATR, Average True Range measure the same range EXCEPT ADR does not include gaps in its calculation whereas ATR does. They do indicate volatility over the time period being calculated (5 days, 10 days, 4 hours etc) Many use it for setting Stop Loss and Targets. Newbies use it to exit trades when ADR/ATR is reached but as bistolis correctly wrote, there is no rule or law that states that ADR/ATR cannot be exceeded (which it does many times when volatility increases). Conversely, there is no rule or law that states that ADR/ATR will be reached (target) on any particular time period. As for using it in PASR : Roger (No1Optimist) used multiples of it as a Stop Loss in his trading. I do not use it in actual trading - I only use it to measure volatility on all pairs to compile my volatility list. So it comes down to your "personal style" of trading. If you don't use it, take it off your charts - SIMPLE as that. The question marks mean do I now understand them? Can you answer this now?

Although I have never blown an entire account I was never a consistently profitable trader either. I also found that I typically bought when I should be selling and selling when I should be buying. So, this was my basic problem, trying to establish where price might turn around or continue, hence my fascination with Elliot Wave Theory and Fibbonaci contractions/ expansions. Hello all, I've been meaning to get back into price action trading and posting some positions here after a break and some severe disillusionment with the markets. Now with fresh eyes I'm even questioning how to identify the trend for a pair. As I see it, the trend you pick up on for the big boss/boss/worker is wholly dependent on whether you're looking at a week, a month, a year, or 10 years of data and a directional bias for a year's worth of price of action means absolutely nothing when 6 months or 2 years gives a completely different trend. It also seems to me that it's far more useful to clearly define the big boss/boss/worker as a stretch of time rather than a time frame, which is just a consolidation of prices, when looking for short and long term trends. For example, the long term trend for USD/JPY is completely different when looking at price starting from April 2018 (uptrend) versus Jan 2017 (downtrend) vs 2015 (downtrend) vs 2013 (uptrend) etc. And this gets more complicated for me when determining how far back to look for long/short/shorter term trends, if there are such things, and if they align with one another or whether it's my own bias on direction completing the puzzle. I'd like to hear from more experienced traders on how they identify a trend considering how susceptible it is to change when taking into account more or less data on price for a pair. I'm also quite curious on how some here manage to profit on the M5 timeframe using PASR. There just seems to be far too much noise in an already volatile market at those time frames. PA always struck me as low risk low stress trading on the longer time frames using previously tested price areas and price action. The margin for error seems too unforgiving when trading H1 and below. Cheers and good luck.

--- 帖子 #7882 ---
Appreciate it bistolis, that's more or less how I went about it. Taking SR levels from the higher timeframes and then trading the daily or even H4 with the current momentum at those levels. The issue for me is that the current momentum can be incredibly deceiving even when relying on PA confirmation to enter trades. You're at the mercy of larger and smaller movements and the inherent volatility of the forex market. I'm thinking this is where the bigboss/boss/worker philosophy comes in to combat the high chance of entering on a short term trend based on recent price action and running against a more potent and longer term move. If you were to identify a downward trend on the daily for the past month ready to sell on a failed retest of a resistance level you may unknowingly be selling into a long term upward move waiting to continue its bullish ascent. But even if you identified this year-long uptrend, it could very well just be a small move up in an even larger downtrend lasting 2+ years. So in setting up a strict trading plan, I'm keen on clearly defining how far back to look for long/mid/short term trends in order to know whether the current momentum I'm jumping on aligns itself with previous price action. As is said in the first page and emphasized numerous times, the direction is taken from the "big boss" and "boss" and seeing how choosing direction for a trade is incredibly important in giving a trader his edge, I think it's helpful to get this part of trading PA as close to an exact science as possible and not susceptible to variation per trade. It's not very helpful to define the big boss as the monthly or weekly time frame but rather a period of time. If you're profiting consistently from just trading price action in the direction of the most short-term movement on M15/H1/H4 then I'm truly at a loss for words. I'm just wondering if it's possible to maintain that level of consistency through all market conditions and for years to come. Thanks

The Human Brain Excerpt from a book I have been reading "Mastery" by Robert Greene "… To become such sensitive observers, we must not succumb to all the distractions afforded by technology; we must be a little primitive. The primary instruments that we depend on must be our eyes for observing and our brains for analyzing. Brain processing speed From a study done at MIT... However, a team of neuroscientists from MIT has found that the human brain can process entire images that the eye sees for as little as 13 milliseconds — the first evidence of such rapid processing speed. That speed is far faster than the 100 milliseconds suggested by previous studies. In the new study, which appears in the journal Attention, Perception, and Psychophysics, researchers asked subjects to look for a particular type of image, such as “picnic” or “smiling couple,” as they viewed a series of six or 12 images, each presented for between 13 and 80 milliseconds. “The fact that you can do that at these high speeds indicates to us that what vision does is find concepts. That’s what the brain is doing all day long — trying to understand what we’re looking at,” says Mary Potter, an MIT professor of brain and cognitive sciences and senior author of the study. Lets say it takes 20 milliseconds for my slow brain to process VISUAL information... If my calculations are correct... My brain cell can calculate that visual information 15,000 times in one 5 minute candle. This is why Strat has been telling us that when we "THINK" it gets in the way of trading. Thinking gets in the way of your private processor your brain. The book "Blink" by Malcomb Gladwell is an interesting read on this very topic.

--- 帖子 #7986 ---
As a trend followers, we have no bias or preference to the long side or the short side. Our only goal is to trade on the correct side of any trend. This is what I do: Currency pairs that are in up-trend, I allow it to pullback (buying at low) offering a low risk opportunity and currency pairs that are in down trend, I will allow it to pullback (selling at high) will rally offering a low risk selling opportunity. If we want to buy currency pair, then we want as many sellers out of that pair, before we get in. On the other hand, if we want to sell currency pairs, then we want as many buyers out of that pair before we get in. This gives us a low risk entry that we can manage effectively. Happy Trading, Yomi.

I have no doubt about the usefulness of the Strat Shadow, as it prevents us on taking trades on the wrong side, especially when it trends really well like AUDUSD. However, there are situations (usually Basic PASR and Swing PASR )when the ribbon is green and signal is to go short. Take the EURJPY for example: Attached Image (click to enlarge) I like this signal a lot. The first arrow shows a Shooting Star, which sort of 'failed' in the next 2 candle as buyers were still willing to protect Price. A retouch and an engulfing candle 3 candles later (2nd arrow) confirms the Swing, and tells us to sell. This is how i study my trades/chart... 1) I hide all my "past orders", you know those arrows from where you entry and you exit. I just hide it first (because every week or every 2 weeks i remove those history trades) 2) I take a look the start of the week, the first candle to the right side, and then start moving out... 3) When i see a trade, i just active again my "history trades" and start watching if i made that entry or what entry i made. 4) If is the same entry and profit or loss, i study again that trade. If is different, i start studyng why i didnt entry here and why i entry in there... 5) After the week is gone, i move to the next currency and do the samething... That help me to refresh my memory and improve myself to do a better trades in to the next week. **** And OF COURSE, STRAT POST! --- 帖子 #8214 ---
Engulfing Candles For PASR : An Engulfing Candle is where the body of the current candle exceeds the body of the previous candle. An Outside Candle is where the body of the current candle exceeds the body of the previous candle and the high and low exceeds the high and low of the previous candle. A doji has no, or very little body relative to its high and low. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

PASR Then i understand that when you have a new candle close in a PASR Zone, looking for an entry you go down on timeframes for a better entry and then manage the target zone in Worker/Boss? Yes.............................but not always. If there is a PASR Set Up with good R:R on the Daily chart then there is no need to drop down to shorter time frames. We ALWAYS manage our trades on the time frame which gave us our initial PASR Set Up.

Indicators After that, I realized that the indicator is nothing more than an application to Price Action Indicators are NOTHING more than calculations and, reiterations of those calculations, of PRICE "" n "" periods back. The TDI is NOTHING more than a smoothed RSI of 20 periods Attached Image The more calculations involving PRICE and the more reiterations of those calculations, the MORE the indicator LAGS behind PRICE and PRICE ACTION . What these indicator junkies do not understand is that the cross of whatever they base their trades on does NOT happen until AFTER the candle ( PRICE ) has CLOSED . Put a wiggly, squiggly line on M1 and watch it for yourself. While they are waiting for their ""cross of something (anything)"", PASR traders are already trading PRICE ACTION . Worse than that, they then go and back test their indicator strategy with CLOSED candles in history which will always show perfect crosses and falsely indicate a winning strategy. They also don't understand that their indicator can "" lie "" to them - but they call it ""divergence"" - so how long does ""divergence"" last? While they are waiting for their ""divergence"", which is ONLY the indicator catching up with PRICE , PASR traders are already trading PRICE ACTION . Why trade a wiggly, squiggly line when you can trade PRICE and PRICE ACTION ? PASR traders do NOT care what PRICE did ""20 periods"" ago! PASR traders are only concerned with what PRICE is doing NOW relative to support, resistance, swings, trends, the Strat Shadow and other generic stuff (fibs, trendlines, etc., etc)

MT4 Thank you to all those who have replied to Scrumy on this topic - TRADERS HELPING TRADERS MT4 has severe limitations when compared to Professional charting software such as TradeStation etc., but, you get what you pay for. MT4 is free and, as long as I work and trade within its limitations, MT4 is fine for me. I occasionally check other chart trading software (the latest was Ninja Trader) but then I see Nicola (elitejets) telling me AGAIN - "there is nothing new in trading!" If I have multiple chart windows open, then I face on big problem: the chart window where I did my analysis and draw my SR lines DO NOT appear on another window. I don't think this is a limitation of MT4 but more of how you are using/not using MT4 as I constantly toggle from the Month to the Weekly to the Worker to H4 to H1 to M15 to M5 and to M1 each time with all my SR levels on. So this is my Set Up: I have a Profile called ""ALL" which shows 28 pairs on the Daily time frame all reduced in size to fit in that one screen. When I want to look at say GBPUSD, I enlarge that chart and change to Monthly - then I add my SR levels see below: Attached Image (click to enlarge) Then I toggle down to the Weekly chart by clicking on W1 on my Monthly chart to get: Attached Image (click to enlarge) And my SR levels are still there. Now this is one of the limitations of MT4 in that all objects do not transfer accurately when shifting time frames so we have to "fine tune" them for each time frame. You can see on my Weekly chart that those SR levels are not accurately transferred from the Monthly so we just have to make slight adjustments. Even when I toggle direct from the Monthly chart to M5, those levels are still there - see below. Attached Image (click to enlarge) When all is said and done, YOU have to trade the charting software which is comfortable for you and which YOU understand. Just like finding your own PASR trading style, you have to find your charting style. I hope this helps

Hi HappyTrend, I made the same mistake as you when I first started on The Path. When we draw too many Support and Resistance Lines, it confuses our mind. It is better to just draw 2 sets of lines: 1 above and 1 below the current Price. To do so, I first start from the Big Boss, and draw 2 lines that are the most obvious: Attached Image (click to enlarge) Then, I move down to the Boss and refine my lines. Attached Image (click to enlarge) I prefer to add in zones, so I add in a second line. In addition, I see an immediate line that is pretty obvious on the Boss chart, so I add it in as well. Finally, we toggle down to the Worker and fine tune it again. Notice how Price is reacting to these lines (PASR in action). Attached Image (click to enlarge) Hope this clears up the confusion.

Hi Huatzhi, Some prefer zones, some prefer lines. The important thing to take note of is that Support and Resistance is an area, not a fixed Price. Also I am missing a few lines as compared to your chart. It is not that I did not see them, but think of them as 'wobble zones' instead. Look at how Price reacted to that line on the Worker. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Box 1: Bounced off support, but downtrend resumed. Box 2: Bounced off resistance, but uptrend resumed Box 3: Wobble Box 4: Wobble up and down Box 5: Wobble with retest of zone (see BEEB) Now that Price is at Box 6, what will Price do? Is it a bounce, or a wobble? Hard to say.... That is why Support and Resistance lines drawn from the Big Boss and Boss are much 'superior' and 'reliable' than the ones from the Worker. Instead of drawing them, I keep a mental note of them. Remember, we trade the Boss swing, not the Worker swing. EDIT: Looking at the line again, I believe it can be seen more obviously on H4. --- 帖子 #8327 ---
Hi Tampa, Perhaps I can answer this as well, Strat and the others can correct me if I made any mistake. There are 3 kinds of PASR: Basic PASR, Swing PASR and Trend PASR. Basic PASR is trading from one Support/Resistance line to another Support Resistance line. R:R is measured before entry and is only made when acceptable. No add-ons. Swing PASR and Boss Swing means the same, and is simply waiting for confluence of Big Boss and Boss (and entering the trade on the Worker) and riding the momentum. We take profit when primary trend changes. (Hint: Look at the Power of Time Frames) Trend PASR is riding on the trend (think of M5 trading) and building up huge positions from smaller ones to rack up profits. As usual, we look at confirmed high/low. We exit when the trend is over.

Hi Miku and Tampa, I will point out a couple things that I understand differently compare to yours. Basic and Classic PASR seems to refer to two different entry types. The trades that refer to as Basic PASR by Strat are mostly those entry in confluence with Strat Shadow toward the next SR. Classic PASR often entry from a strong SR (often carry down from higher TF) toward the next SR. This understanding can sort of being backed with Strat referring Svolacius' #6218 trade as CLASSIC Basic PASR . I think it means this is the entry that confluence between a strong SR and Strat Shadow. While #6806 by Rub is referred as CLASSIC PASR and #6755 from Pete is referred as 100% Basic PASR strategy. One of the uses of Strat shadow is working as Dynamic SR Area, so PA on it consider Price Action on Support and Resistance. Boss Swing refer to "the swing of the boss". I think I tend to call it as ' immediate trend ' without understanding it properly, not sure if it refer to the same thing. If trading on 4H Daily Swing is your Boss Swing, and is the Swing that you want to trade along with on your worker. For me, I trade on Daily Chart so my Boss Swing refer to the swing on Weekly since Weekly control the direction of Daily. This is why a couple times Rub and Strat warned me on taking trades against the Boss swing on pass few pages. Thanks Miku, you frequently point out things that I missed, please keep posting .

--- 帖子 #8392 ---
PASR THE PATH The Daily is governed or controlled by the Weekly, which we call the BOSS. As long as we only trade from the Daily, then these two are all we really need. We can look at the Monthly for a longer, further out view, but as regards our trading decisions on the Daily, since the Monthly is two time frames higher (and controls the Weekly), we can disregard this. I see where there can be confusion. PASR is a 3 time frame analysis. Our ""Worker"" chart is the time frame on which we enter our trades after our 3 time frame analysis. The""Worker"" is controlled by the ""Boss" which in turn is controlled by its ""Big Boss". So our Worker can be the Daily chart, H4 or H1 where each is analysed and evaluated on a 3 time frame analysis. So, in the case of the Daily chart being our ""Worker"", we start with our 3 time frame analysis. Monthly (Big Boss) first which is then toggled down to Weekly (Boss) which, in turn is then toggled down to Daily (Worker). The Monthly (Big Boss) is used to identify swing and key support and resistance levels as well as using it as a ""Birds eye view/Big Picture from 50,000 feet"" to identify the overall sentiment and where the Big Boys (Investment Banks and Hedge Funds) are taking PRICE. We don't use the Big Boss to actually make a trading decision but there will be many times when it provides confluence with the Boss and Worker to give us added confidence in taking trades. Once we have our ""Birds eye view/Big Picture from 50,000 feet"" together with our Support and Resistance areas/zones/levels, we toggle down to the Weekly (Boss). We first adjust the Big Boss levels to the Weekly chart and ADD any key and immediate Support and Resistance areas/zones/levels to it. The Boss (Weekly) is what ""drives"" our trading chart, the Worker, so we need to find out as much as we can about what the Big Boys ( PRICE ) are doing. This chart (copied by so many) along with my Power of Time Frames , MUST be UNDERSTOOD to have any chance at being successful at PASR trading. Attached Image This chart clearly shows us that, starting at the left, the Boss, our PRIMARY TREND, ( green ) is in an UP SWING . It then tops out at resistance and then goes into a DOWN SWING . The Worker ( blue ) OSCILLATES around the Boss UP SWING until it tops out at the SAME resistance as the Boss. The Worker then FOLLOWS the Boss in its DOWN SWING again OSCILLATING around it. So, the key is to identify the Boss SWING and KNOW which SWING PRICE is in AT ANY TIME. We then trade the Worker IN THE DIRECTION of the BOSS SWING using PASR . Hopefully this clears up any misunderstanding.

Seeing beyond the Candles Hi Terry and Strat This is how I try and wrap my head around concepts such as this by using a technique Strat showed us on these threads. --- 帖子 #8715 ---
Daily Open Line I only use it on M1, M5 and M15 as a "balance line". I carried this over from my stock trading some 35 years ago! The idea on stocks was if PRICE opened and stayed above the open PRICE level in the first hour then it would be a PLUS day meaning buy all dips. Vice versa for closing below. Attached Image (click to enlarge) As you can see, it doesn't really work on Forex. I sometimes use it as a ""Reversion to the Mean" when PRICE isn't really trending and instead is oscillating around the open PRICE level (meaning there is no clear direction from the Big Boys). Although I don't normally trade H1 and H4, it can be used on them as support and resistance.

Gets to be kind of a imbalance trading problem when it comes to dollar figures in each account. But I found that it has been very easy and quick to move funds from one account to another if the accounts are with the same broker. So now, I treat the accounts as one account when it comes to figuring my position size. Set a target with one and a different target or no target with the others. Hope this makes sense. Short Terms Trading So Emotional➡ Lots of Mistakes➡, More Losses➡, Less Money. This just shows that you are not that comfortable on short timeframes. The same rule applies here as above. Because you pretty much have 5-15 mins to make a decision, that is why you need to be more selective. 3. MONEY If you focus alot on money gained , eventually you will be affected more when you lose money. Your priority should be to get used to lose money on each trade. EURNZD M5 PASR Trend Trading In the end (both strategies) where holding the same position size (sum of all trades lots), right? Yes. Both Money Management strategies used their same size - strategy 1 was large and strategy 2 was 1/10 of it. how would you manage your SL for each trade in strategy 2? This is where USA traders are at a big disadvantage to the rest of the trading world as we have to comply with FIFO - First trade in is the First trade out. We have to MANAGE that first trade so that a trailing profit stop does not take it out and with it, the potential for the whole trade. You should be able to SEE where my initial stop loss was on both strategies. I do not enter either a stop loss or a trailing stop - I use a mental stop. The PAUSE in the downtrend is THE obvious place to enter a protective stop BUT the Big Boys also know that and, more often than not, hunt those stops out. The stress is no different on either Money Management strategy save for the physical entering of orders. I do not watch each individual position - ONLY the PRICE ACTION. Recognising the trend and its strength and then its weakness is how I manage my positions - not with trailing stops or, counting the money. The trend, or lack of trend, takes care of everything and is the ONLY thing on my mind. Money Management on strategy 2 is just Dr. Joe and my Fat City in action.

Hi all, Been 3 weeks or so since I last came here. Had to settle some urgent issues and had no time to visit this thread on a regular basis. Now that that is finally over, I hope I can join you all again. After my last XAUUSD trade that ended in a disaster, I went through a lot of back testing and decided to learn Trend PASR well. I found out a few things: 1) TREND: Wait for trend to establish (Duh!). I prefer to think in terms of Swing High/Low. Make sure that you identify the correct Swing, because there can be false signals. Also, Big Boss and Boss being in harmony is a huge confluence. 2) MOMENTUM: We wait for pullback to the Strat Shadow for better R:R (think of it as the rubber band effect.) Candles touching the Strat Shadow gives much better R:R. 3) CONFIRMATION: We wait for signal (Outside Bars/Engulfing/Shooting Star/Hammer). Throughout my backtesting all the way from 2007 in Forex, I found out that just by doing all this was extremely profitable if you have good money management. This is the system that I will use and try out: 1) On valid signal, enter 2 trades. 2) Place SL below last Swing High/Low. Each SL should not exceed 1.5% of your account (Risk is 3%) 3) 1st target: ATR(10). 2nd target is trailing stop to last Swing High/Low. Perhaps today's USDCAD on the Daily will be a good example. Hey celguek, I have made myself a Strat Shadow in TV. Add this script to the Pine Editor and save it. //@version=3 study(title="Strat Shadow", shorttitle="Strat Shadow", overlay=true, max_bars_back=5, linktoseries=true) fastEma = ema(close, 20) slowEma = ema(close, 72) twoHundredEma = ema(close, 200) closePrice = plot(close, style=line) fastEmaPlot = plot(fastEma, color=#2ecc71, style=line, linewidth=1, title="Fast EMA") slowEmaPlot = plot(slowEma, color=#f00b0b, style=line, linewidth=1, title="Slow EMA") //twoHundredEmaPlot = plot(twoHundredEma, color=black, style=line, linewidth=1, title="200 EMA") color = close&gt;slowEma?green:red fill(slowEmaPlot, closePrice, color=color, transp=85, editable=true) //fill(twoHundredEmaPlot, slowEmaPlot, color=black, transp=90, editable=true) Additionally you could add the MA Ribbon as well. Best, Scrumy

--- 帖子 #9271 ---
Hi huatzhi, I would agree with Rufus. The close of the weekly candle has to be above/below the high/low of the actual WCC AND the following candle has to close within the WCC to confirm it. Then it becomes the new WCC. In your example: your second candle from the right did not close outside the WCC (third candle), so it is not a new WCC. Hope that helps. Greetings, Markus

So I stop trading about 10 years ago, also because of a change in my life: I moved to another city, so away from my hometown, started a new job and found the love of my life, who I married in the end. So trading was not a focus in my life. But 15 months ago my interest got caught again, when I was listening to the Podcast "Chat with Traders" (maybe you know it). One tader also mentioned the forum Forex Factory, that I did not know before. So I started here to look around and in the beginning I was pretty impressed, becasue of all these profitable traders (or who pretend to be successful traders). After opening a broker account I was starting with a "demo". In the meantime I discovered Strat's thread (the old one) and started to read it. After 3 month reading I decided to come out and post in the thread. I must admit that I did not unterstand everything in the old thread, but somehow I got caught and thought "this whole thinks makes totally sense to me". So I started my journey or my marathon (thats how compare it) on the path. I was impressed by the clean PA-charts and I also have to admit that indicator-land caught me in the past. In the last year I also made many mistakes, like: not triggering the SL, add to a losing position (in the hope to win back the loss), holding a position to long etc. Today I know it (hopefully) better and I guess it is a kind of good delvelopment. Posting in the thread helped me also to accelerate my learning Progress and so far I would say I learned the following things knowing I still have to improve/work on it in the future: Order of higher-time frames Drawing/Using SR-lines (to find the footsteps of the big boys) Power of the STRAT-shadow Importance of the CLOSE of a price WCC Confirmated swings PA candles ("seeing the trades") "Looking beyond the candle" At the moment I try to focus on M5 in the hope to accelerate my learning progress. But the most important fact to be here is the great support of STRAT. So thanks again! I appreciate your way of teaching (no spoon feeding!). Also a big thank you for keeping this thread "clean", so that all the willing students can particicpate in a proper way. Forex brokers Since volatility is very low and erratic today meaning no M1/M5 trading for me, I had time to put a few of my "paranoia" concerns with brokers together. In my 17+ years of trading forex, I have seen forex brokers come and go and more recently, the appearance of “scam” brokers so I am, more than ever, suspicious (paranoid) of any forex broker suddenly appearing out of nowhere. I was very spoiled with my previous broker before the FXCM fraud here in the US. I had been with an “introducing” broker to FXCM for many years. They were local to me in Southern California so that I could visit them in their offices where I became friendly with their President and Technical Software Manager, needing no appointment to meet with them. They told me many horror stories of how brokers scammed their Clients and assured me they were nothing like that and totally “up front” with their Clients. I trusted them to the extent that at one point, I had seven five figure accounts with them. I later reduced this to just two large five figure accounts. I never had a problem with anything with them and was shocked to learn that they too, were part of the FXCM USA fraud. The recent SNB manipulation of their CHF caused many brokers to go bankrupt, among them some large well known names like Alpari etc. This alone, warns me off brokers. Since then, I have not found a broker I can “trust” that I dare place a five figure account with, bearing in mind that, because of FIFO, I have to have 2 accounts. The things that I do not have reassurance (paranoia) from current brokers are, in no particular order: Are brokers sufficiently capitalized for their Clients and trades they make? (Alpari and others were not!) Volatility wipes out under capitalized brokers. Do they have strict Risk and Money Management procedures AND do they practice them? How did they survive the 2008/2009 financial crisis? What insurance do they carry for their Clients in the event of bankruptcy/liquidation? What is their leverage policy? High leverage, greater than 10:1 was always a problem for me although the US has restricted it to 50:1 Higher leverage favours the broker NOT the trader. High spreads What is their Spread/Commission structure – variable, fixed or percentage? Does the broker “hold” orders to widen the Spread? What are their Spreads during high volatility and outside normal trading hours? High commissions Is the broker racking up commissions at the trader’s expense? Called “churning” Are they a “Dealing Desk” or a “Straight Through Processing” broker? Does the broker have strict margin rules? What is their margin policy? Does the broker “offset” my trades? Do they charge for “pip hunting”? Do they “mark up” trades? Do they keep “re-quoting” prices? Do they engage in “Stop Hunting”? Do they “nickel and dime” their Clients? Do they have “hidden costs”? Do they charge “inactivity fees”? Are their “Swap Rates/Interest Fees” as per the respective Central Bank rates/fees or are they “marking them up”? For some brokers, trading is not a “zero sum” business – they increase commissions with increased trading volume. They ALWAYS win at the expense of their Clients. Do they have “long term” profitable Clients? Do they have “large account” Clients? Have they ever “boycotted” or sued their Clients? Does the broker have a good reputation? Can they show and prove it? Have they ever had Legal Action against them? Have they any outstanding Legal Actions? No “real” recommendations from Clients Can they demonstrate honesty, credibility, integrity, trust etc? Arbitrarily moving quoted rates to trigger Stop orders Will they guarantee Stop and Limit order fills or hit me with “slippage”? Do I have a relationship with the broker? Can I build a relationship? Do they have special rates for high volume/large account traders? Is the broker readily available at any time? Forex is 24/7 so must ALWAYS be available? Do they respond quickly to questions? Do they resolve issues/problems quickly? Do they dodge questions or give vague/unhelpful answers Withdrawal of profits/accounts – ALL questions related to this Are they US SEC/CFTC/NFA/FINRA Regulated? Are they located and headquartered in the USA? Is their website a sales pitch to lure unsuspecting traders in? Does the broker have fast MT4 or do they promote their own trading platform? Do they support MT4 technically and quickly resolve issues? Will the broker honestly answer all these questions or will they just refer me to their terms and conditions?

--- 帖子 #9372 ---
PASR THE PATH A PASR Lurker in from the cold and dark - welcome! So I've always been unsure about my SR lines (whether they're too cluttered or maybe too little lines there) Rub has helped you with this - Trader helping traders The first thing you have to do is identify SR, on each of our time frames, where PRICE changes sentiment (direction). When you are practicing it doesn't matter how many lines you have. What is important is recognising that change. If at first you can't SEE it, change to a line chart and do it and then switch back to candles to see how it looks. When you feel comfortable with that, remove those lines which are "noise" within the Swing on each time frame. Keep doing this over and over until you can do it without thinking. When you start trading and, as Rub has already told you, you only need SR above where PRICE is NOW. Finally, although PASR uses lines for SR, the Market does not. The Market uses a zone or area around our lines; the reason for this I explained in my old original 2009 thread.

--- 帖子 #9459 ---
Hi Peter, IMO, short answer, no. Long answer, if your SR is area, it would be easier for you to deal with that. If your SR is in line, you will add and adjust your SR on lower TF chart. If that price does matter, you will be able to see the price react to that price. (the high and low of the last closed candle do often matter though). We can also use the high and low of the candle to confirm the SR better as well. Here is an example GBPNZD BB Immediate support and resistance. A lot of closes around this resistance area as you can notice. Attached Image (click to enlarge) B However, when we zoom out, we see this. Attached Image (click to enlarge) There is a pretty consistent price close around that higher resistance. Most of the time I don't draw that as that is not the immediate resistance but for the sake of explaining my thought, I will draw here for now. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Then we zoom in, we see that price action respecting a closer but different level in recent price. Now I can choose to either just add a line there, or adjust my SR to suit the recent PA. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Now my BB chart look like this. Attached Image (click to enlarge) W When I get to worker chart, I see most of the SR fit well on the chart. However, there is one PA overshooting my resistance. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Again, that is not my immediate resistance, normally I might just leave it there as that is not the thing that matter to me right now (or next couple days). However, to "get it right", I moved it up to fit current price action. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Zoomed out a little, look at where our price get into now. Attached Image (click to enlarge) I can add an SR there, of best fit, as it is really an area rather than a line. Now my SR for this chart is complete, ready for my analysis. My BB's SR look like this now. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Again, does the high and low of BB matter? If it matter, we will still be able to pick it up in lower TF. Though I have past track record that not been able to identify my SR correctly, so... PS Different people draw their SR abit differently. You might want to find the way that suit your trade in later of the path.

Doing my end of year review and thought I'd put it up warts and all. 2018 year in review In broad strokes, I have gone from not knowing what I was doing (put myself at stage 2!) to a point where I have made money but I'm still very cautious of having made some pretty big stuff ups. So maybe I've got to stage 3, with having pretty much hit every part on the journey over the year. Anyway, broken down by quarters: Q1: Having found this thread in late 2017 I committed to trading real money at the smallest lot size I could. Ended the quarter down, but started to get the right idea. Took plenty of trades that I shouldn't have and started to work out candle recognition. Q2: This is where the struggle with greed started to rear it's ugly head. Moved to trading $50 a trade, sized accordingly. Of course once I was up a couple of hundred bucks in comes greed. "It's a couple of hundred, all profit, not your money anyway, chuck it on a trade and you'll soon be up a couple of thousand." I could swear my old mate greed comes from the underpants gnome school of thought. As you can see from the graph, lots of ups and downs, but by mid year I thought I had things in some sort of order so I funded my account to the tune of $5000. The idea being to start risking by %, rather than a fixed dollar amount and treat it seriously. Q3: Going into Q3, I decided I would risk 5% of my newly funded account. That was a mistake (hello greed!). Very quickly I was down substantially. At the time I wasn't in the right headspace to trade but did anyway, even mentioning it in the thread. Fortunately I pulled it together before I hit the point where I said I would walk away if I'd lost that much. There's a couple of things worth mentioning here, GREED getting the better of me being one, have your head on right being the other. I also made a pretty big mistake calculating my position size which fortunately took me back to profit (where I prompted had greed pay another visit. "It's all profit! Risk it all, make millions!"). Regardless, I see this as the most significant of the year as there was a little of everything that I dealt with, and I still ended up with a profit for the quarter. Q4: The final one for the year, ending in profit. A small drawdown from the peak then up to new highs. The main thing I noticed is if you take out a few goes at 5 minute trading, it was a handful of trades a month. I think this quarter shows I'm starting to pull things together and stopped making the same stupid mistakes. If I can keep this up I might actually make it! The year 2018: A year and a little bit I am comfortable with my progress. For me the basics have come together and I know what I need to work on. The big ones I am cognizant of are: - Recognizing when to exit. Currently been targeting the next major weekly support or resistance, and my attempts to recognize price telling me to exit have got there yet. -Scaling up in lot size. As shown by mid year, I'm still emotionally attached to the amount rather than thinking percentages and risk. Finding it hard to let go of losing XXX amount. On the other hand I'm not emotional about the gains, I'm tending to be more a "well, that's nice" and go back to what I've been doing than getting a emotional high from it. I was thinking and doing that in the past... After i trade for a while and taking notes about the trade, my emotions, my psychology... I start trading without partial profits and taking notes... (R&amp;S of weekly) The set up appears, for example short. I entry short with SL above of resistance swing D1 or H4 (all depends) with TP of a Weekly Support. Now partials vs full take profits. When the trade start going positive, most of times... the price do pullbacks before arrive to weekly support. Then i can add on... and continue going to my take profitzone... my stoploss nowbhas been going down to the last resistance swing. Then before it arrives to my TP Zone, the price make othee pullback but now i didnt see any PASR SETUP just ugly candles going down again i didnt entry again but now my SL is now behind lf it... then the price reverse and my SL hits before arriving my taking zone. (With that.. im trading with the trend and im out if my SL hits or TP if the price arrive to a BB B support). PARTIALS: Closing partial profits.. u are closing it because u have a reason.. Maybe 1) u are arriving to a worker (or a lower weak support) 2) you are watching a weak PASR against you 3) Because u have a set of rules of MM closing after a certain R&amp;R.. --- 帖子 #9576 ---
Hi Scrumy I work my stop losses in the trade. I have a hard stop somewhere at a level and then I work the trades and take much smaller hits. Sometimes I miss the trend because of this and I do not chase the price when this happens. I'm now taking many more 5 to 10 pips stops but these are now getting measured out by the smaller wins which are about the same when I am being defensive. When I hit on a trend and manage to add on it wipes out all these smaller stop outs for lots of profit. It takes loads of chart time to develop a style that suits you but I've learned that 5 min trend trading is not about setting and forgetting your trades. There is no edge there for me. The edge is having the discipline and will power to manage your stops and get out with profit. Time and again.

Happy weekend all Durring my time away from trading last month I did a lot of thinking... I think too much. So part of my trading plan is thinking less to not at all. If the trade is there, take it. As anyone approaches mastery in any field the time spent thinking and analyzing things become less to none. I am probably in the top 5% of carpenters when it comes to trimming out fancy homes with lots of details. There is not much thought to the process any more. People have asked how I know what to do or where to start or any other number of questions. My answer is something along the lines of "I just do". It should be the same with trading for me, especially after all these years looking at charts and watching price. Durring the holidays I read a great little book, The Traders by Sonny Kleinfield. The book came out in 1993 so home computers and the internet were in its infancy. He interviewed and followed around pit traders. It was an informative read. A common theme throughout the book was not thinking about and analyzing the trade. You would have thought Strat was one of the traders interviewed. These pit traders traded without charts for the most part yet could feel the momentum of the positions. I started reading a novel last night, it just didn't thrill my brain cell, so will put it down till a later date. I will re-read The Traders instead. So in conclusion, my thinking will be more for the process of entering the position. Analyzing the crap out of something is to be set aside. So if I post a trade that was just stupid and someone asks "Where was your head" to take it such a thing. Thank you for pointing it out first of all...My head was probably on the Henry's Fork river with a flyrod in my hand. Rufus

Hello strat, thanks for your comment and asking. I have made several mistakes there. The biggest one was trying out new things (H1 Basic/Swing PASR) with my normal position size. Second was jumping the gun entries, on M5 but also on H1, didn't wait for the bar to close. Also buying/selling into SR. And in general bad trade management. Taking too much losses, that should have been smaller ones/BE or profits based on PA. And at that one specific day (9 M5 Trades, 27.12.18), I wasn't in that state of mind to be in the market. First couple of trades went into loss, and after that everything collapsed. I was on full tilt mode. Not fully reckless, but hitting a loss after loss wasn't good for me. I was moving my SL on one trade, finally hedged the position and lost twice my planned risk. I need to work on that, therefore the new additional rule to quit for the day after 3 consecutive losses. On the next day there will be new opportunities, with a fresh mind. It all comes down to Psychology. Again and again. I know chances are pretty high to have 3 consecutive losses. By just using my current stats from the last three weeks I have a winrate of 44.83% on M5. Based on that the chance of 3 losses in a row are 16.8% - but that is ok for me. (If someone wants to calulate: (1-winrate)^consecutive losses, in my case (1-0.4483)^3 = 0.168 = 16.8%). Maybe with more experience I will change that rule. But for now I will protect myself from myself. Preventing the above mentioned mistakes makes a big difference in the outcome. I want to first proof to myself that I can be consistantly profitable, without putting too much money on the line. A big shift was going on in my mind: I was too much focused on my P/L - now I am more focused on R-Multiple. If I can keep a positive R-Multiple over the next two months P/L will follow automatically. Rather doing small steps while still learning. No need to rush.

Hi Scrumy I see Strat has already given you some advice... We all trade differently, I need to see momentum when I'm trading 5 min. REDUCE YOUR SIZE AND TRADE! Work on knowing when to get out.

Hi Scrumy, I think your entry is fine (if it the one I marked on your chart, blue arrow?). Regarding the management of the trade: If I would trade that one, I would have set a really tight SL (see red line) - as I do it for all my M5 trades. As BTS mentioned a few postes ago: when I (we) trade PASR M5 Trend Trading we look for a R:R of 1:4 or 1:5 or even higher. So price has to move in my direction pretty fast/soon. If not (see tight SL) I am out and wait for another PASR setup on this pair. If price moves in my direction I am looking for add ons on the way down (in this example). The first bullish candle would trigger me to ask myself to exit. Hope that helps. Greetings, Markus Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Quoting strat {quote} Not easy, especially because we have to admit that we where wrong Change your mindset, Markus. Being right or wrong or correct or not, has NOTHING to do with trading - we are here to MAKE MONEY (not be right, wrong, correct or not) If it doesn't feel right or if you doubt your trade or decision to trade - JUST GET OUT. Then re-evaluate and if everything is OK, get back in. This was one of the hardest things for me to turn around mentally when it comes to trading. Just because a trade was a loss doesn't mean I was wrong. Just because a trade was a gain doesn't mean I was right. What makes us right is obeying our trading plan regardless of the result. As soon I got the "right and wrong" mentality out of my head then progression toward profitability move dramatically. Then my next hurdle was bias. This mean little bastard blinds you to half the market. The opposite of your bias. Hi again Markus I had been thinking about this post off and on all day trying to come up with how this mindset changed for me. Just not entirely positive of the process. But I can come up with a few things that helped with the change for me. I don't know if I could call it "tips" for keeping the mindset of right and wrong in perspective. We each have our own psychology to deal with. I grew up as a perfectionist in a lot of areas of life. Thankfully not all areas. I still am a perfectionist, but now it is a little more controlled. My dad instilled a very strong sense of right and wrong in me, he was drill instructor in the US Army in the 50's. Things were done a certain way and god forbid anyone be in the way. Then I have dyslexia, so putting together sentences, spelling, reading and a number of other things were a chore all through school. So I put extreme pressure on myself and worked very hard to get good grades all through college. Right and wrong. It wasn't until I started running a construction business and trading that it became apparent that it was okay to be wrong, okay to make a mistake, as long as you learn from it. Then as time went on and more trades were clocked in, I started to realize that losing positions were a part of the game. Losing positions were not necessarily mistakes. One of the things I quit doing was trying to predict tops and bottoms. That just lend itself to a right and wrong mentality. Another was position sizing. 2% is my max position size. But there is also a maximum loss I can handle mentally. (Gradually working on increasing this). I will explain. Say you have a $10,000 account, 2% is $200. Suppose it is a 20,000 account. 2% is 400. Same percentage but different amount. Knowing this number has helped me as well. I don't know if this is of any help. It was a gradual process that I never just "willed" into being. It wasn't the result of hard work but more a result of consistency and learning. Consistency in trading and learning about myself. Studied much about dyslexia, about personalities. Right now reading a book on Emotional Intelligence. It has been a never ending process, I don't know if ever you just arrive to a state of the perfect mentality for trading. More than likely it is a constant learning process of handling each new challenge as it emerges in your life. Then faithfully trading a plan and clocking in each trade win, lose or draw. I still find myself thinking wrong or right at times, such is life. If things get to confusing I visit with my horse. Rufus

--- 帖子 #9817 ---
I am not trading today due to Brexit so I have time to add more insight. The last paragraph from Rufus is really when you make the transition from where you are now to trading without fear and without being right or wrong or correct or not. We all go through the same stages of learning to trade, some quicker and better at it than others. This is your "psyche" kicking in as you develop your trading personality. We have to endure losing trades from doing down right stupid things and bad judgement and decisions to those which are due to Market behaviour and out of our control. Understanding your chosen strategy and being able to apply it for profit is a must. It does not happen over night but rather through thousands and thousands of hours trading experience. We are no different to a boxer learning to become a Champion. We have to keep taking the hits to get better. We have to manage how we take the hits. We have to control our reaction to those hits. We have to learn how to take defeats. We have to get knocked down a time or two. We have to learn how to get back up to fight another day. We have to learn how to avoid taking more hits. We have to learn moves to miss being hit. We have to learn how to hit back. We have to learn to hit harder than we are being hit. We have to learn to "roll with the punches". We have to learn to "Float like a butterfly and Sting like a bee". We have to understand our opponents strength and weaknesses. We have to subdue his strengths and take advantage of his weaknesses. We have to learn to wear an opponent down. We have to learn and know when our opponent is tiring. We have to learn when to move in for the "kill"". We have to do this over and over in many bouts until we become the hunter instead of the "hunted". We do this until we are doing it on "auto pilot" or second nature and become The Champion. Once in "auto pilot" we have to keep training. We have to continue learning about the next opponent. To continue being The Champion we have to keep doing what got us there in the first place. Summary: There is no short cut to learning how to trade for consistent profit. You just have to "grin and bear" it to gain the experience. Hopefully others will share their experience.

My plan was: 1 TP in area 1.5850, moving the stoploss to BE. Let the other two positions run: one up to 1.5750; the other up to support 1.5350, paying attention to area 1.560. Naturally, I was ready to close positions in case of PASR reverse. But what is the probability? The probability is given by the daily closing under the Strat Shadow, by the weekly closing below 20 ema and BRN 1,6000 and by the price attitude of finding support (in this case 1,5850). Then I would have considered whether to close both positions or, if the price kept going down, to close them in the areas indicated above. Thanks again.

In my notes i already did: 1) Your first and second entry, in that level makes the HL. StopLoss above of it... Next entries, the stoploss is always above of HL... TakeProfit. 2) Your First entry and second entry, in that level makes the HL, StopLoss Above of it... Next entries, the stoploss above of candles that close lower of the previous candle... Takeprofit. 3) Your First entry and Second entry, in that level makes the HL, StopLoss Above of it... Next entries, the stoploss above of each candle entry... i mean split the stoploss. In all of those 3 Works and sometimes doesnt (obviously right.. haha, we dont know the price where is going to move 100% but we can know with a high probability) And i ask with my self, how i felt after doing that... and my chose is the #2 but maybe is because as u said.. i dont want the price go against me and lossing my floating profit. MartinGale is similar of Grid... GRID: You open a position for example 1 contract. For example: You Buy... the price go against you.. and you buy again with the same contract... the price go against you.. and the Gird is for example you set each 20 pips of distance and every 20 pips against you.. you continue open buy positions.. until your trade go to profits or... blow your accoubt... Martingale is similar but in here you are incrasing the lotsizes.. i mean, you entry 1 contract... and after # pips you entry with 2 contracts... after # pips you entry with 4 contracts... 8 contracts... until your trade go to Profits or blow your account... A lot of people (those of 95% of lossers) use that because qhen the market is in ranging... they made profits.. with big contracts.. when the price reverse.. and they are in profits.. sometimes they made a good profits with all those contracts.. but that is temporaly.. Because 100% of those traders who do that.. soon or later blow their account... when the price start to trend and then is a mega trend without pullbacks.. all of them are gone. So a lot of scammers sell EAs of Martingale.. they create accounts.. and if in one month they made profits.. they use that account for sell... but if you ask to a seller his myfxbook and if they show to you.. you are going to see that the history of that account is not more of 6 months.. or less sometimes they not survive 1 month... MT4 Picking up a post of me from November as I have an update on this. I use TradingView to do my end of week analysis for long term, stress free trades, because of it's ease of use. It enables you to define up to 20 pairs, through which you can just toggle via the arrow functions (up, down) and it also enables you to toggle between the timeframes (left arrow - lower timeframe, right arrow - higher timeframe). spending so much time bouncing around on different time frames There, straightaway is the major problem, Terry. This is just as bad as "Thread Hopping". Drop everything you are doing now and find the time frame(s) you, and your personal circumstances, are comfortable with. Then, focus on them and ONLY THEM. You understand PASR so it is just a matter of applying it on that time frame(s). PASR strategies work on ALL time frames so just find the time frame(s) you can comfortably and profitably trade. Do not force yourself to trade a time frame(s) just because others are showing their success on them. As I have posted many times, I spend 2 to 3 hours around 6:30am/7am Pacific Time each morning on M1, M5 and M15 which, for me, is really only one short time frame. After 2 hours, I am finished unless PRICE is still trending strongly, and even then will still get out after a big pip haul. I cannot trade M30, H1 or H4 as my lifestyle does not allow me to be governed by these time intervals so I never mess with them unless someone asks for my comments. I still trade the Daily and Weekly because they only take minutes for analysis and trade management. I understand your frustration, Terry, but it really is self inflicted. Find YOUR time frame(s), Terry - YOUR time frame(s) and IGNORE all others.

Hi Suranga and HT Agreed, you can see a periscope as from a submarine raising its periscope above the sea. In this case indicating how high price can go. A Depth Gauge is the opposite, think of dropping knotted lead lines overboard to determine how deep the ocean floor is below your boat. In this case indicating how low price can go. Regards Pete

Hi Scrumy It is good to be able to identify Weekly Control Candles but in my mind the question is, what do we want to do with a WCC? That is if we understand what a WCC means. (Talking about me, not you And thank you for posting the charts with WCC's that got me on this train of thought!) Lets look at at it from a Boss swing perspective. A confirmed Boss swing high or low is usually done and dusted within a couple of candles, two ,three or a few more which brings us into WCC Territory. Within a WCC price really is at rest until the higher powers decide which way price should go. So it could eventually be a confirmed high or low or price can continue on its way...the thing is we dont know. This leaves us with two choices. Trade within the WCC or wait for the powers that be to decide what they want to do and follow in their footsteps outside the WCC. trading weekly swings my choice would be to wait and trade the executive decision. But then again, there are opportunties within, especially when the bosses have given us some pointers. Lets look at the EurJpy WCC you pointed out. The Big Boss Immediate Trend is down with a Depth Gauge probing the limits. The Boss has a WCC in place and acknowleges the bottom probe BUT this is not all... within the the WCC, near the top of the WCC we have a Boss BEEB which in its own right would have been a confirmed high if it was not confined within a WCC. However in my mind this confirmes the Boss downswing from the confirmed high in September...and shall we say, Bob's your Auntie? Now where was I... sorry ...Its a Saturday night in sunny South Africa and my weekly (dare we say Boss) bottle of Red is doing its thing mellowing me out..oh yes! I think I need to refill my glass (If I'm not making sense I'll blame it on the Boss I am yust following instructions...hic!) Regards Pete

Hey BeyondTheSea, thanks. Maybe my wording is not 100% correct. I just want to say that when Price is "trapped" inside a Weekly Control Candle, that we can be in waiting position for Basic PASR trades inside the WCC. Sometimes price respects those WCC SR levels, but sometimes it just cuts through. I also was thinking about the importance of WCC's which are very young - like the one on GBPNZD, which is just 1 week old. A WCC can happen even in a rip roaring trend (think of an IB - pause bar) and does not mean that the WCC's top and bottom SR are set in stone. So my thinking is that an "old" WCC's SR - like e.g. on AUDNZD (9 weeks!) has much more importance than the one on GBPNZD (1 week). What exactly do you mean with confluence? Confluence of PA at SR? Confluence with the power of timeframes (which I think is not important for Basic PASR)?

To differentiate depth gauge and hammer, depth gauge are out-of-place/abnormally long hammer candle on worker chart(depend on which TF you trade on). As usual, it happen more often on lower TF, but its the first time for quite a long while for daily. You can expect an SR when price is around the tip of the long wick. Hope this would help. BB immediate trend is kind of directionless right now as price doesn't really close above or below that area. Also note that you might really want to know where price is relative to SR for all three chart. Here is my understanding, when that gravestone doji first appear, it show the sign of buyer exist around there. However, trend often could cut through SR like a knife to butter. Until the second attempt to test the SR again, so its confirmed that it is enough buyer to stop the trend. (also it could be due to TP isn't trigger due to spread, so it only trigger the second time when price overshoot a littler of SR, only Strat know which one is it). Addon to what Scrumy said, I think that is continuation of trend. When price hit SR, price often pause abit causing ranging or consolidation. When price stop ranging, it could just continue the trend (or reversal). Fib is still being use provide that one understand what is it for. Though I don't think dashurry draw it correctly.

--- 帖子 #10397 ---
You do not necessarily need an indicator to do that, Sachu. Just choose a red vertical line and drop it on the London open, then green on the US open when you start trading. The next day, you just can take the old lines and copy them per drag and drop + strg them to the new day. The advantage of doing this without an indicator is making you more aware of what is in the NOW. And it puts less pressure on your MT4 platform by saving it from running another indicator. The less indicators running in MT4, the more stable it is. But of course, that is very individual. I prefer to do it manually for the mentioned reasons. Respect, BTS! --- 帖子 #10523 ---
is it just NOT recommended for beginners to trade Basic PASR on M5 or what exactly is the difference between this post now and the post back then from bistolis? My early M5 PASR trading postings were purely TREND TRADING - trading pull backs to the New York CONTINUATION of the TREND set by London. Because of the limitation of my time zone and personal circumstances, I did not get to my computer until 7:30 am Pacific Standard Time. By this time, (10:30 am New York), volatility had died down leaving little or no trend for me to trade. I encouraged those in European time zones to trade the London trend and those in the New York time zone to trade the New York continuation of the London Trend. Since New York, many times did not continue the London Trend, I was missing out on M5 trading so I decided to trade M5 Basic PASR when I got to my computer. Unfortunately, the pip return for risk/reward and time spent trading M5 Basic PASR was anemic compared to PASR Trend Trading so I changed my routine so that now I get to my computer around 6 am Pacific Standard Time (9 am New York) and can catch what remains of the New York continuation of the London trend. I will still trade Basic PASR on M5 if PRICE is stuck in a range but only on my high volatility pairs and ONLY if I can get a minimum of 3 times Risk for Reward which is still pathetic compared to 5 and 7 times Risk for Trend Trading. There are times when New York starts its own trend but that it is usually after my 2 to 3 hours maximum at the computer for trading is over so I miss out on those. M5 Bootcamp and learning Basic PASR on M5 is a very good way to accelerate your PASR learning process. Whether you can trade live Basic PASR depends on the individual and where they are on THE PATH . M5 Trend Trading, because of its visual progress in conjunction with the Strat Shadow is what attracts everyone including the LURKERS and TROLLS . This is seen by those asking for the Strat Shadow template without learning PASR . If this doesn't answer your concern, Scrumy, ask again.

PASR huatzhi has given you a very good reply but since you are early on THE PATH , it may be a little over your head. In an ideal situation, which DOES occasionally happen, when the Worker turns into the direction of the Boss which itself is turning into the direction of the Big Boss we have a road map to FAT CITY. I love trading DAX. I trade all signals as it comes, without bias mostly, as the sentiment on M5/M1 can rapidly change. Sometimes I sell the market &amp; then - when in profit - I get to see we have arrived at some sort of support (H4 or H1), I enter long without questioning too much to see if I also get a long signal... I execute that long trade and use it as a hedge for short while I take some volumes off short. This way I am dancing with the market when/if its in ranges. The main trick here is to be sure we are in a range market.....and that often appear after a relative big move in the market - or after news, or even at the end of a session (LO or NY) Below is H1 with zoom on M5

EURAUD M5 Bootcamp My comments are based on M5 BootCamp as a means to accelerate the PASR learning process rather than comments on the M5 trend which are two entirely different subjects. I came around this situation with a hammer right at support (A). If I was short before it I would have exited right there and I think that would be the correct approach. Correct. That is text book PASR and shows the sellers taking profit at previous support levels. It is not PASR to enter long positions as this is against the immediate trend. My question is if the entry marked with an arrow afterwards would be an invalid entry (or high risk) because of the hammer at support and one should wait for the close below the low to reevaluate. This could confuse you because you are using an example of a strong M5 DOWN trend rather than an example of PRICE ranging to learn Basic PASR . In this strong M5 DOWN trend example, that is a text book PASR entry/add on into the trend. Had PRICE not been in a trend, and instead being in a range, then we would wait for a CLOSE above that hammer before entering long or a CLOSE below to enter short. I suggest you learn Basic PASR first and do the f12 exercise when PRICE is in a Range. This will accelerate your PASR learning and instill recognition of PASR in ranging situations where PASR is traded from support to resistance and vice versa. PASR Trend Trading is 1,000 light years away from Basic PASR which is why I suggest you f12 on trading ranges. Ask again if you are still confused.

--- 帖子 #10790 ---
I am trying to do a lot of work on myself recently and I thought I may share it here just in case others can relate. I did lose a lot over the last few months and it shook me immensely, especially after a phenomenal performance during the first 6 months I started to follow the path. I had many, many opportunities to make all that money back and then some in the last few weeks, or at least rebuild my self-confidence so that I can resume my travel on the path where I left it. Yet, even though most of my entries are in the right direction, I simply don't follow through. I was short on GBPJPY at 148, short on GBPUSD at 1.33, short on USDJPY at 111.72, long on Gold at 1290, etc etc. I have been really trying to understand that behavior and, after reading and listening to a few coaches such as Tony Robbins, some things started to resonate. I think losing or simply missing out satisfies one of my basic needs, something that allows me to complain or feel bad and get sympathy, something that has been deeply rooted in me and that I need to reprogram. You see, I had a very successful professional career up until a couple of years ago, and I was a rock that my friends and family would rely on, to the point that no matter what bad things would happen to me, people would always say "I am not worried about you". They meant it in a nice way, as in "you are too good to not come on top", but all I heard was "we don't care about you". So I guess I needed to create a situation so bad that people would finally be worried about me and give me the support I was craving for. As I am writing these words, I feel shaken to the core as I know this is how I really feel deep down. And I know it even better because my daughter functions exactly the same way, and I have been trying to explain that to her even though I was in the same pit as her. Your brain has a strange way of letting you know what it wants. In my case, it is by self-sabotage. My fear is not a fear of losing, it's the fear of winning (again) and not getting support, love, attention because, well, in my experience, only those in need/pain are getting those. Some may understand what I am trying to express, and lucky for you if you don't because it means you have a different relationship to trading. We are all different but we all function based on a similar set of needs. As I am realizing what I just wrote, I am also starting to undo the spell. I knew this would be an interesting journey, I just didn't realize where it would take me and I am still in awe. Basically, it seems I am not the receiving kind, life gives you what you need, not what you want. So I need to remain the giving kind and my return here is not a coincidence I guess. I need to give back more than I need to receive, not because I am better than others, but because this is what defines and satisfies me. I also think that this is how Strat feels. He is not after glory or recognition, he is a giver, and that's why from day one, I felt close to him. I am done with whining and crying over my wounds hoping for sympathy and commiseration, time to make some money Inserted Video

--- 帖子 #10857 ---
I have been asking myself a question about money management for some time: It is often said that the big money lies in long-term time frame. However, if we always risk 1% in the long term as a short term, and we always take a risk: Reward of 1: 3 at least, the M5 pays as much as the daily? Because on M5, since the stop loss is very tight, the position size is bigger while the stop loss daily is wider so the position is smaller. Example: $30 is my risk of 1% of my trading account. On M5 for a stop loss at 10 Pips, I will take a position of 0.3. On the contrary on the daily, I have a wider stop, to let the price breathe, so a stop loss of 150 Pips, the position will necessarily be smaller, like 0.05. So Suddenly, long-term positions are less stressful but as profitable as short-term transactions? I hope you will understand my thinking and especially correct me if I’m wrong Thank you friends

--- 帖子 #10859 ---
That is absolutely correct, the bigger the stop, the smaller the position. And this is also the reason, that you need a bigger account to trade larger time frames. Imagine you have a 500 EUR account, and you want to trade the Boss on GBPNZD with a imaginary SL of 500 pips. The smallest lotsize is 0.01 Lots. Then you risk already 30 EUR, which are just 6 percent of your total account - way too much. The short term time frames offer bigger Reward to Risk Ratios. But as I got the impression (on my very short trader's life), that on the shorter timeframe you reduce your risk to a lower percentage, cause you will trade far more often on M5 than on e.g. the Worker. But again, this is very personal to the trader. Fleurdelys for example does 1% position sizing on M5 and did very well on it. Depends also on your little people and how loud they scream at you, when you know that you have 1% of your hard earned cash sitting at risk and are being "able" to disappear in minutes on M5.

PASR Attached Image (click to enlarge) Attached Image (click to enlarge) https://www.forexfactory.com/showthr...49#post3025849 This determines your understanding of PASR and your ""style"" of trading. 1) I would place a stop loss 10 pips or so beneath the wick of the Hammer with a buy stop 10 pips above the high of the Hammer. (Not my preferred option as I would be risking more than I would be comfortable with). This is very aggressive and NOT The Path to consistently profitable trading. The problem is that the Big Boys know we will position buy and Stop Loss orders where you suggest and will HUNT those out until they clear the decks before moving in THEIR direction. This results in the spikes you see above Hammers and below Shooting Stars and, as you rightly say, the Stop Loss size is horrendous. 2) I would wait for PA on the next bar/s confirming a Swing Low with a close above the Hammer body, then look again for a better entry with lower risk. Yes! WAIT for the Big Boys to show their hand and then FOLLOW in their footsteps. 3) I would wait for a retrace to the 61.8% fib level taken from the Hammer with a buy limit placed and a stop loss placed 10 pips below the bottom of the wick and accept the loss if I am wrong. That is also aggressive and NOT The Path to consistently profitable trading. Another option is to drop down to H4 and look and WAIT for H4 PASR Consistently profitable trading is all about psychology and putting probabilities on OUR side. #2 will get you there safe and sound as long as you FOLLOW the Big Boys and don't try to guess, pre-empt or lead them.

H Alesiosc, I try not to over complicate it. I look for Big Boss turning points and start there. Then I move to a Boss chart, look at the structure and then move the lines. Finally I look to fine tune on the worker and use confluence points at these levels. It's a zone and not an exact price point. I don't class any support in terms of "strength" only the big players control that and it changes on a dime and at their will. Also you don't need support lines 500 pips away from your price unless it is part of your trading plan. I find less is more when find S&amp;R. Keep on practicing like in this post because it will help as you progress forward. There is a difference to what we do to practice than in actual real, live trading. Understand that we are identifying these levels to show us the footprints of the Big Boys and nothing else. We are trying to identify where they start loading up their positions, where they add to their positions and where they take profits. We are NOT looking to identify every twitch, nook, cranny and knee jerk, only where and when the Big Boys move THEIR money. Unfortunately, it is not as easy and simple as that because there are so many Big Boys each doing their ""thing"" which puts emphasis on different levels. There are Big Boys trading short time frames, Big Boys trading intermediate time frames and Big Boy investors trading longer time frames so we have to ""tune in"" to the levels on the time frame ""WE"" are trading. Do not worry too much about this until you get really serious about trading. For now, focus on identifying these levels and as Nathan correctly advises, they are PRICE areas or zones and NOT a specific PRICE level. I have explained the reasons for this many times but, to summarise, this is due to the Big Boys having to load and unload their positions in incremental volumes so as not to ""rock"" the Market. So, for actual trading, we are only interested in the immediate support below where PRICE is now and the immediate resistance above where PRICE is now so those are the only levels we enter on our chart. When one of those levels has been breached, we go back and add the next level above or below and so on. For actual trading on GBPUSD, identify and enter Big Boss (Monthly) levels. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Then fine tune these on the Boss chart, identifying any other key levels Attached Image (click to enlarge) Then fine tune those levels on the Worker chart, identifying any other key levels Attached Image (click to enlarge) Always remember that in PASR , PRICE is King, Queen, Lord and Country and the most important PRICE level is the CLOSE

--- 帖子 #11051 ---
Attached Image (click to enlarge) Very sad. I met Dick in the early 80s when he did concerts in Southern California. We shared a love of the Fender Stratocaster and raw, loud music. He was a ""leftie"" and learned to play guitar on a right handed guitar. Instead of changing the strings around as most ""lefties"" do, he learned his music and chords ""upside down"". This meant that when he eventually afforded a left hand guitar, he had to change the strings around - you can see this on all his guitars - the 1st string is where the 6th string should have been etc. This caused undue stress on the truss rod in the neck resulting in intonation problems above the 12th fret so Dick went to Leo Fender in Fullerton, Sothern California, who made special "leftie" guitars for him. Then, his "heavy attack" style resulted in breaking the strings so Leo Fender had a string manufacturer make special heavy gauge strings for him. Having solved that problem, his next problem was his volume and tones constantly blowing tubes in his amplifiers so Leo Fender made special "Dick Dale proof" amplifiers for him. Like many before him, he pioneered the way for what we have today. God bless and rest in peace, Dick.

Basic PASR Bootcamps - do this day in day out. Take Profit at next S/R. Just do it. Proof yourself, that you can be profitable with Basic PASR. Cause if you can do Basic PASR and be consistantly profitable and progress further on THE PATH you will be even more profitable, cause you would let Basic PASR trades turn into Swing PASR and even into Trend PASR trades. What I do for my Basic PASR Bootcamp trades: look at Big Boss (M15) for general structure Is price ranging? Then look for trades at the top/bottom. Is price trending? Then look for Basic PASR trades in the direction of the Trend (like your example of BlackEagle's trade) watch out on Boss (M5) for PASR. Only if you have a valid set up on M5, watch for an entry on M1 (or even pull the trigger on M5 as we "Sometimes take trades on the Boss") Worker (M1): as mentioned above look for an entry. In ranging conditions, I prefer to have Price already in the Strat Shadow, best when it is inside the Shadow on M5 as well. In Trending markets I prefer to have a set up/PRICE as close to the Strat Shadow top as possible. Post got longer than I expected. I will post trades the next days as well. I will show you what I mean with all the above.

--- 帖子 #11328 ---
M1 Bootcamp Example: Basic PASR Trade in the direction of the trend Big Boss (M15) Price on Big Boss is in an uptrend. Let us look at the candle at 10:30. It changes the primary trend to up. Price is supported by Strat Shadow and rejected support @1.128 massively. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Boss (M5) Dropping down to the Boss and moving our line to 10:45 where the Big Boss candle closes doesn't give us a valid PASR set up. The primary trend on the Boss is now down. But look at the candle at 10:55. A bullish engulfing, showing a nice tail into the dynamic support of the Strat Shadow top. Big Boss and Boss are now aligned. But PRICE closes at my next SR @1.12888. Depending on how someone draws the SR lines this could already be a set up to go long. Depends on each individual trader. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Worker (M1) At 11.00 our set up candle closes on the Boss. I have moved the red line therefore on the Worker. The next candle closes as a bullish engulfing, supported by the Strat Shadow and closing above my SR @1.12888. All three Timeframes are aligned. All Timeframes have price above the Strat Shadow. A lot of confluence across all three timeframes. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Now we need to check if there is at least a 1:1 Reward Risk Ratio possible. A conservative entry below the swing low would give you 4 Pips SL for a 5.2 Pips Reward (1.3R) at the next SR @1.12947. An aggressive entry with your SL just below the set up candle would give you a 1.8 SL (2.8R). And then: manage the trade well BUT only to the next SR line, take profit, really. That is crucial. With the time you will get a feeling when a trade won't work - all because you see what PRICE is doing. Sometimes you get hit direcly, but that happens. Other times the trade won't take off and then it is your decision to cut it or to leave your cash at risk. There is a fine line between Fear and Greed. I am still not at that level, but I am experiencing it every day and getting better.
