here's a little story I thought i would share. I will look towards it in the near future if the little men start playing the fool with my mind. at the moment I feel quite comfortable and in control of the little men but I do feel they could win the tug of war between them and I once I up the stakes and start trading bigger lot sizes. back in 1999 I promised my wife I would give up smoking and drinking the day our daughter was born. she was born on Christmas day 1999 and for all those smokers and drinkers out there who have ever tried to quit, you know exactly what I am talking about. I couldn't do it. fast forward two years. I came across Allen Carr's Easy Way to Stop Smoking. bought the book as many people had stopped smoking by just using the principles in the book so £7.99 was a small price to pay for a proven chance at giving up smoking. the main thing I grasped from the book was, it opened my eyes to how the sub-conscious mind works. I had no idea up until then how the mind works and what causes or controls addictions. suffice to say, reading the book did not make me stop but definitely opened my eyes. fast forward to 2004. I came across an advert to stop smoking through something called Bio-Resonance. again, I've never heard of this but with a money back guarantee I thought I couldn't go wrong. booked in at a cost of £500. it was explained to me by the man doing it that it worked by put two identical energies together to cancel out the addiction. similar to sound. apparently when you put two identical sound waves together it cancels each other out and gives you silence, similarly. I tried this and it actually works. Bio-Resonance works by putting what I was addicted to, the cigarette, into a test tube, then connecting that test tube to a machine. then connecting me, the addiction, to the opposite end of the machine. apparently cancelling out the addiction. he combined this with 1hr of, what he called, clinical hypnotism which I have since found out is also called NLP, Neuro Linguistic Programming. I left his offices waiting for my need to want a cigarette. I just didn't believe anything had changed. I didn't feel any different. after each hour passed and my urge for a smoke didn't come. I started to wonder. it was weird. the next day there was nothing, and the next day, and the next. the following week I still had no urge for a smoke. fast forward to 2019. I still have not smoked nor do I have any desire to smoke. I am not fighting it. no urges, nothing, unlike other people who give up using just willpower. rewind back to 2007. I saw an add in the paper, "Allen Carrs Easyway to Stop Drinking. Money back guarantee." with my drinking way out of control at the time I thought what the hell. I can't really go wrong. it either works or I get my money back. I got my wife to book it, paid another £500, and went for my appointment in London. to keep this short, there were 15 of us in the session. the session lasted about 4hrs. 3 of these hours were filled with Chris, the mentor, telling us and reminding us about the pros and cons of drinking. most of it we knew already. like when asked to name one thing that we liked about drinking. when we went through the variables we all realised there was nothing really nice about drinking except the merry feeling we got at the beginning, which then came with many consequences. when being absolutely honest with ourselves, we didn't like the taste, we didn't like the headache/hangover, we didn't like the smelly breath or the way we smelt the day after a heavy drinking session, we didn't like it when we fell over after having too much. in fact, there was nothing we liked at all. so why did we still drink. and more so, why was it so hard to stop. believe it or not. it's exactly the same reason why we can't control our Fear &amp; Greed in the markets. it's our sub-conscious mind. our sub-conscious minds were automatically programmed, after drinking so much alcohol, to need an alcoholic drink, especially in certain repetitive scenario's in our lives, and, what Allen Carr's did in its session, was to reprogramme our minds and kind of reset them to before we ever had a drink. now I am no expert on this so excuse me if I get some of this wrong. it's only what I have gathered on my journey, what I remember and the way I have come to understand the sub-conscious mind through my own experiences. so, in short, how the system worked was basically, reminding us about all the negatives of drinking, which we all knew already but just refused to acknowledge. then the last 45 minutes was about relaxing and cementing all we had gone over, in the session, into our sub-conscious minds. in effect, resetting our sub-conscious again, using Clinical Hyptnotism. I walked out of there never to drink again. no urges, no desires. I can now even keep alcohol at home and pour people's drinks without fighting an urge to want a drink. The moral of this story is, to see how training our Sub-Conscious or resetting it is what we as traders want/need. back in 2009 towards the end of my then, 2 year trading career, I sent a message to Chris and asked him if this method could work for the purposes of a trader wanting to control their fear &amp; greed. he told me to write down all the elements I wanted to address and he would put something together. with me having already lost most of my money and, at the time, not having a clear mind about what would be the best, most relevant points to send to Chris. it slowly faded away. but now, I think it is time to resurrect my desire in finding an Easy Way to control my Fear &amp; Greed as after reaching around Page 514 I have come across enough valid, important points to pass over to Chris to see if we can get something going. if anyone feels they can add anything please mention it and will add it to the information. Scrumy, My thoughts on GBPNZD. A WWC is a function of the boss. It: 1. has no direction ( it's a consolidation) 2. has a top (resistance) 3. has a bottom ( support) 4. has a range (which is the same on all lower time frames) 5. is meant to be traded with PA within its range 6. PA on daily normally has ATR to great to trade 7. drop to H4 to achieve a smaller ATR 8. I'm still trading the daily (worker) but doing so on a H4 chart to achieve smaller ATR 9. a breakout occurs when a WEEKLY close occurs outside of the range What have I forgotten guys. Add to it or argue with it. As you like. Best regards Frank

Additional informations on my previous post. In the old thread strat shows some PASR trades and declaring them explicitly as counter trend trades. So this confirms my "observations". Lots of examples starting here: https://www.forexfactory.com/showthr...41#post7108141 So for us beginners it is always better to enter those trades in the direction of the PRIMARY trend (the immediate trend on the next higher timeframe). I guess if we get more experienced at PASR, we can enter those counter trend trades that aren't aligned with the PRIMARY trend as well.

--- 帖子 #11417 ---
Trading Week #16 Review After two weeks of watching and trading Basic PASR on M1 Bootcamp, I was focussing on H4 Basic PASR trading this week. Here was my plan for week 16: Attached Image This week's trades: Attached Image (click to enlarge) And here is the week's summary: Attached Image I closed all of my trades on Friday, because I didn't want to leave anything open during the easter holidays. If you look closely, I have lost way more EUR than I have gained. But that is due to my small account size -&gt; on big stops I risk far more percentages. In total, the week was a (small) success, making 0.67R. Example: my GBPNZD trade on Wed, 17.04 resulted in a loss of 13.09EUR, which was 1R. Compare this to my trade on USDCAD on Monday - this was a win of 0.5R but only 2.42 EUR win. This is the limitation of a small acccount, because you can't go lower than 1 microlot (0.01 Lots). And how much you will loose depends on how far you put your stop loss. E.g. you want to risk 1% of a 500 EUR account. That is 5 EUR risk per trade. If you want to put a SL of 200 on GBPNZD that means you are already risking 11.90 EUR on a Microlot. Either you skip that trade or you accept the risk for this particular trade. To summarize: don't focus on PL on small accounts, focus on R-Multiples. Decreasing P/L doesn't necessarily mean you are a bad trader.

--- 帖子 #11679 ---
exponential moving average I use 72 E M A for every chart that I pay attention to. I am feeling comfortable after spending plenty of hours watching price action with those settings. Use whatever you prefer actually. Most people in here use 72 and 20. and then 200EMA (which is pretty much standard on any chart) what matters above all else is how the candles form and close around support/resistance. the shadow is powerful once you get used to price action (on your chart the candles are too small for my tastes) make your candles easy to your eyes put the shadow add 20EMA add 200EMA and you are ready to spend the next couple of years reading price action until you are confident with your decisions. and then keep on learning everyday That's pretty much it, and you might make it even more simple. PS: i recommend reading the 5 steps (page1) regularly

--- 帖子 #11899 ---
PASR - The Path, Progress Report Hey all, sorry for not being that active lately. As you may know I joined at around October 2018 to read about strat's PASR strategy. So this is my 9 month progress report. I am doing a lot of training via forex testing software to build confidence in the market. I can really recommend you to do that, too. I focus on the H4 timeframe (my Worker), with the Daily as my Boss an the Weekly as my Big Boss. The hardest thing in trading is really the psychology behind it. I had a lot of ups and downs the last months. I knew that I can trade PASR. I really knew it, but I haven't proven it to myself. My Demo and my small capital live account were showing the opposite, the balance was just drowning. Then some revenge trades, some up to 4% of capital and all went downhilll. Then I was figthing with my trading tools. On MT4 I have a pair switcher that can go through all pairs in the same window. But when you draw objects in that window they will get shown on another pair as well. I solved this now by using TradingView as my trade analysis tool and MT4 as just enter/exit trades. Additionally I was switching a lot between timeframes - to finally find the timeframe that suits me. But I guess that is just normal. You need to play around a little bit and get comfortable with what you are doing. And that again, just takes time. So my tip is to enjoy the path and don't rush things. As it was said many times: the markets will still be there when you are ready. It was just about 2 months ago, where I really started to make progress. I was focusing on just H4 as my Worker. Partially I was reading too much in the threads. I made myself plans to read at least 30 pages per week. But in the end, I was having very few sparetime and that was sometimes too much and I got exhausted. Why? I just wanted to get good at the method and learn as much as possible. So I still haven't read every single post, but I still read in both threads. With the help of the backtesting software you can build soo much confidence in your trading abilites that it just doesn't matter anymore if the current trade was a winner or a looser. Because you know that probabilites and thereby your edge are on your side. Just stick to what you will learn here and get into every trade that is according to strat's strategy. I bought a software to do that as the capabilities in Metatrader is a little too limited. But I have also found a way to do multi timeframe analysis on MT4 while backtesting - but that again isn't that usable as I don't like how you can proceed through the candles in MT4. It actually downloads the charts for your selected timeframes and you can then proceed candle by candle without seeing the future candles. That won't be possible while doing the F12 excercise. I set myself a plan to not go into the market again with a live account until I prove myself that I can be profitable. And there I am. Sharing my current progress while backtesting PASR. So just to show some statistics about my current performance on my backtesting. I am still doing a lot of mistakes and there is plenty of room for improvement, but I will fine tune them in the next 3 months. That is just the GBPAUD Performance over a period of over 6 years. The winner percentage is 44%. But you can see the winners are way bigger than the loosers (28 vs 15 USD). 0.25% risk on each trade. BTW: I already asked a while ago ("How about the fellow students winrates?"- what are your statistics out there? Attached Image As I found it hard to move the SL on a manual basis I started to add a volatility (ATR) based SL (sometimes referred to as Chandelier SL). This takes the emotions away and I have a purely mechanical way to handle the SL - sure, sometimes I get stopped out too quickly. But it currently helps me to build my confidence. Maybe in the future I will cut it off again and purely use PASR to get out of trades. TP is set to 2R. This again can be improved when using PASR. So this is how my workspace looks like. You see back then I had quite some better performance on my GBPAUD session (the screenshot was taken a bit earlier). On D1 (my Boss) and W1 (my Big Boss) I am only using a 10 EMA. This is not according to strat's strategy but I currently focus more on PASR without the Shadow, Basic PASR if you will but with addtional helpers. But I find myself adding more and more what is taught in the thread. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Those mistakes are: taking trades far away from the Strat Shadow/EMA's instead of trading the pullbacks (they are basically more breakout trades from SR) trading into S/R What I do right: Position sizing. I only risk 0.25% of my capital for each trade. I will increase when I progress further. But I do need more data of my trading performance. no revenge trades, just take trades that are according to the strategy not being upset by a loosing trade - but that only comes when having the confidence that the strategy works just pull the trigger when a set up occurs don't over analyze things, even A+ set ups will fail My 3 month plan: focus on backtesting further and build more confidence addtionally demo trade the real market on H4 further fine tune my strategy on H4 In October I am planning to enter an evaluation program for a prop trading firm. Basically you pay them the maximum allowed drawdown during the evaluation phase, which currently is at 4% of a 10k live account. Target is to reach 6% in max 6 months and 40 trades minimum. This gives me the needed pressure to perform on a professional level and staying accountable. All in all, it is important to read what stands here in the threads. To learn each tool of strat's toolbox (drawing SR lines, Strat Shadow, Power of Timeframes, Candlestick patterns (BUOB/BUEB, BEOB/BEEB)) but at the end it comes down to applying excatly that and getting a feeling for the market. Doing that in a live market takes a lot of time. Doing that in backtesting software is way faster. I am able to do an 8 year backtest on H4 in just 4 hours. That won't be possible while being in the market. There is a downside though: I wouldn't be able to get into each trade that I am able to take while backtesting. Sometimes I might sleep while a set up occurs. But that doesn't matter. It is all about the confidence you build. Build yours.

Regarding MT4 Charting with Oanda . Has anyone seen this ? I saw a message that stated beginning on August 16 a new order placed on a specific chart, for example Eur/Usd, could not duplicate in size an existing order already on that chart. So if earlier you placed an order of 1.0 size that had a SL and TP , you now could not place an additional new order of the same size 1.0 which also had any SL and TP . Apparently you could place a new order of a different size ... for example 0.5 OR place a new order of 1.0 that did not have a SL or did not have a TP . This info came as an Important Message in the Terminal section of the MT4 charting display, at the bottom. When I clicked on it there was a description of the new rule and several examples. --- 帖子 #11945 ---
The Pivot Point System is pretty nice to be stress free. Usage of pivot points has been done through the ages by floor traders as it gave them an easy method to obtain an idea of where the markets are headed on any given day utilizing a few simple calculations. The pivot points and the support and resistance levels calculated from them are known as pivot levels. They work simply because many individual traders and investors use and trust them, as well as bank and institutional traders. It is known to every trader that the pivot point is an important measure of strength and weakness of any market. The high, low and close of a market on a daily basis is the data that is used to find out the daily pivot points. The market opening and the pivot point can determine the type of trading to be expected for the day. If the opening of the market is above the pivot point then you can expect a day of long trades and if it opens below the pivot point then the bias is towards short trades.

--- 帖子 #11947 ---
All traders are looking for a stress free trading method they can use to make money from the markets. Whilst this method does exist it’s success depends more on the personality traits of the trader, rather than the trading strategy they plan to use. Position trading is where all of your trades are placed on the higher time-frames charts rather than the lower time frame charts. This type of trading is most commonly used by traders who have day jobs as their unable to be in front of the computer all day watching their trades. The main one being the trader who plans to start position trading. If you happen to be someone who is impatient, then transitioning from trading lower time frames to trading higher time frames is going to be difficult process for you.

GBPNZD M1 PASR Follow Up First time looking at FF and the thread for ages and just wanted to show how SIMPLE trading is when you UNDERSTAND PRICE ACTION and the MENTALITY and PSYCHOLOGY of those moving PRICE. Attached Image (click to enlarge) New York reversed London trading - why? - don't know, don't care. All I know is those moving PRICE during the New York session found support and bought off that support. They have to make money and build momentum by buying and buying (Hello Dr. Joe!). They reached their target and then others sold off that rally. In anyone's eyes that is a big IMPULSE move associated with Elliot Wave 3 (if you believe that junk). What follows, most of the time, is some sort of CORRECTIVE WAVE (Wave 4 in EW terms) that can be either SIMPLE or COMPLEX. In this case it was a SIMPLE A-B-C-D correction. Since PRICE was now again at DISCOUNTED PRICES, the buyers came in and bought and bought again (Wave 5 in EW terms). EW theorists will target the end of Wave 5 with Fibonacci extensions. PRICE purists will just continue to buy until the buying STOPS and selling STARTS. On a higher time frame, the M1 move from SUPPORT to 3 to 4 to 5 is itself an A-B-C-D move. So SIMPLE when you understand PRICE ACTION and the MENTALITY and PSYCHOLOGY of those MOVING PRICE ALL I do is FOLLOW IN THE FOOTSTEPS of those MOVING PRICE - "nutin' fancy" as Dr. Joe told me!

--- 帖子 #12041 ---
You can never be sure, what price will do. So even the best looking A+ setups will fail. And exactly that is the key in trading. A loosing trade doesn't mean it was a bad trade. Also a winning trade could be a bad trade. You have to find a strategy that works for you. That fits your personality. If PASR isn't the thing you are comfortable with, then try to find some other strategy. The good thing about strat's teaching is that he gives you very powerful tools and every trader needs to develop it's own style of the strategy. You could only trade Basic PASR. Or like others here (like fleurdelys) which focused only on M5 PASR Trend Trading and right at the beginning had great success doing it. Another thing is the time frame. Are you going to do the stress free trades or chasing M1. In the last couple of weeks I personally realized so many things. Sentences like "Cut your loosers and let your winners run" - at the beginning you think, sure, I will do exactly that. But the actions on that are quite the opposite: cutting winners and lettings loosers run. And in the end it isn't about the strategy. It is about you. The sentence I like the most is this one, page 1 in this thread: And that is so true. Success isn't depending on the system. It is about what you do while trading, how you prepare, how you approach trading, how you learn, how you reflect on your past trades, how you set goals and plans to improve, how you act and think after winners, how you act and think after loosers, how confident you are with trading your strategy (and especially for me: how well have you back- and forwared tested the strategy, a big confidence boost). Psychology and mindset are more important than the strategy. Soapbox moment. Sorry. But I hope it helps.

My understanding of basic PASR is it's taking little bites out of an existing trend, or trading top to bottom/bottom to top of a range. We are not interested in the current weekly candle, look at the overall picture on weekly, and what the last week's candle was. Look for significant levels, watch what price does there. Do the same for monthly, then refine it to weekly. Pretty much it in a nutshell! Glad to see everyone riding the JPY pairs down. Alesiosc, if I'm honest I'm not sure I understand the cryptic posts....? This post is in general and not specifically a reply to your post but you made a point that made me think.. I just trade what I see on the charts using PASR with the Shadow. I use basic support and resistance drawing my levels where "I think" I see price being halted, this can be on all time frames and often "seem" to happen as I'm trading in whatever time frame I'm looking at; when I see it, I use it. Same with the shadow as dynamic support or resistance. When I "think" I see my level and the shadow at the same points, or close enough I then wait for price action to show me the way. I don't fix myself to use a specific time frame although 1 min 5 min and 15 min are my favourites at the moment. There is no secret sauce or hidden method. Only chart time. Spend hours and hours trying not to lose money, day in day out and things begin to happen. When I post a chart it is for my own benefit because it makes me properly look at it and only then I realise that I've acted either out of sheer luck or subconscious learning. I often think, "who traded that? I didn't because I only remember my losers!" Speaking of losers I have plenty but now they are on average about 6 pips and getting less and less. (I use pips for money management to calculate my %risk. PIPS DO MATTER if you use them for their true purpose, which is to calculate risk..). I've developed my "favourite" setups not on purpose but it's just happened over time: retests, clear breaks of PASR, engulfing, SS, Hammers, stalls, pre news shadow directions. It's all there in the threads, nothing new or shiny, don't ask me, look for it! So I'll continue to post my charts but feel there is enough info on this thread for everyone to have a crack at it without the need for each trader critique. If you merge other methods, trade in different ways to what is laid out then so be it. There are many ways to make money in the markets and we all have to figure it out but lets try to keep this thread as it was laid out so new learners have a chance to pick up the path without falling off at the next corner. It really is very, very simple. No secrets, nothing new and the markets are the same and will continue to be the same depending what time frame you trade. Price At Support &amp; Resistance. Rock On

--- 帖子 #12197 ---
Hi Kneath, Welcome to the thread! As Bistolis had commented, you are overcomplicating stuff. Before you enter any trade, you need to do the three time frame analysis (starting from Big Boss, Boss, Worker). Read post #430 by Strat to give yourself a brief idea of what to do. To trade stress-free, all we have to do is follow the footsteps of the Big Boys. Learn about confirmed swing high/low until you can identify them at a glance. Look at hammers, shooting stars, Bond Hammers and Shooting Stars, Engulfing candles on charts and ask yourself why they work/didn't work. Learn how to identify consolidation Vs trend, because we never trade in a consolidation..! Also, remember Dr Joe's story by heart. Sell when it goes down, buy when it goes up. Never ever go countertrend for a start, unless you know what you are doing (think of a quickie..!). You'll only be wrong once. Look at NZD pairs. Those who buy are liquidity for the Big Boys! Lastly, 72ema instead of 50 ema. It works much better as dynamic support and resistance than 50ema. Try it and you'll see! P.S. I reread Dr Joe's story at least once a week, and everyone should too!

Hi Rub, I think you are having too much bias. For me, what clicked was looking at every chart individually. No correlation, no 'but USD is strong now, so USDCAD shouldn't go down!' mentality that hinders in entering a trade. Take a step back and wonder why AB chart is worth entering, while maybe DE chart is not worth. Maybe thinking as a game will help..? For example, I recently bought AUDUSD,AUDJPY and USDJPY which all ended in profit. As for moving TP, I rather you close the trade at the moment than moving TP. E.g. securing some pips in advance of NFP. It could also be a lack of trust with your initial trade plan, maybe your TP is too far away to be realistic..? How many TPs do you make in a trade? I think managing a trade is about capital preservation=accepting the risk of the trade+trailing SL to last swing high/low. Try keeping a 0.01 lot trade for the long term at BE, then trail your SL will help train your emotions and keep your fear and greed in check. If you get stop out with a huge pullback, then so be it. The market is always there for you. The next trend is always being planned by the Big Boys. Also, look at the recent NZD trend, as well as the recent bounce of the commodity currencies and you will see that a trend is much stronger than you think it is. Don't forget that we are here to trade Long Term and Stress Free. Just my two cents, hope it helps in any little way possible.

I know GBP moves more pips just like you always say, but when trading it, your SL is also bigger. Does that not mean at the end that it becomes like the same of trading other pairs? GBP pairs are "usually" more volatile than other major pairs and with that comes more RISK. REWARD is proportional to RISK so choose the pair which matches your RISK tolerance. However, if you carefully choose your pair, and particularly your entry, you can minimise your RISK while still enjoying REWARDS of 5 times greater than RISK - see SL and TP on today's GBPJPY and EURJPY. --- 帖子 #12394 ---
Interesting article that basically highlights everything that Strat has been teaching, but repeating the fundamentals over and over is necessary as we are human: Almost all traders are aware of the widely publicized statistic that “95% of traders lose money.” When you drill deeper, research implies that this number is likely higher. The profession chews up and spits out aspiring traders at an astounding rate. So why are so many intelligent people drawn to a profession with incredibly high odds of failure? 6 striking stats showing traders have it rough There are the obvious reasons — the appeal of working for yourself, sitting in your underwear on your couch all day making millions. There’s the (false) promise of “easy money” and the draw of independent wealth. The truth is, day trading is extremely difficult, emotionally taxing and far more likely to destroy your life than enrich it. Let’s start with a few key statistics , from online educational resource Tradeciety: 80% of all day traders quit within the first two years; Among all day traders, nearly 40% day trade for only one month; Within three years, only 13% continue to day trade. After five years, only 7% remain; The average individual investor underperforms a market index by 1.5% per year; Active traders underperform by 6.5% annually; Traders with up to a 10 years negative track record continue to trade. The last point suggests that day traders even continue to trade when they receive a negative signal regarding their ability. Astounding. Almost everyone loses, they lose fast, they underperform simple, mindless investments, and they continue trading even after being proven unprofitable. Why? The truth is, most would-be traders are woefully underprepared for the challenge ahead and learn many hard lessons with their real money. They underestimate the psychological challenges of trading and fail to eliminate emotion from their trades. They fail to trade with a defined system. When they have a defined system, they often take trades outside of their own, established rules. These are all obvious reasons. What is “random reinforcement”? Perhaps a less notable reason that traders fail is the principle of “random reinforcement.” This concept also explains why they often continue trading, even after failing repeatedly. As defined by Investopedia, “Random Reinforcement” is: Using arbitrary events to qualify (or disqualify) a hypothesis or idea; attributing skill or lack of skill to an outcome that is unsystematic in nature; finding support for positive or negative behaviors from outcomes that are inconsistent in nature—like the financial markets. The market has a tendency to reward bad habits, while concurrently punishing positive behaviors, especially with a small sample set. Let’s take a theoretical example to display this principal. Bob wants to leave his job and become a crypto trader. He sets aside some starting capital, follows the markets and the “big names” on twitter. He sees them talking about an altcoin, opens the chart and sees that price is rising fast. He buys, goes to take a shower, returns and sells for a quick profit. He does this again before lunch and strings together a few successful trades. Bob starts to feel confident that he is a talented trader. So what is the problem? Bob is trading without a system or a plan and is being fooled into believing that a successful outcome on a few random trades is indicative of likely success moving forward. The market has rewarded his bad behavior. We know how this story ends — Bob continues to make impulsive trades and eventually loses his capital. There is a flip side to this coin. Let’s say that Bob learns his lesson and spends months developing a trading plan, complete with risk management, proper portfolio allocations and trading rules. He identifies a trading opportunity that fits, takes the perfect entry and… stops out of his trade. He tries again. And again. He loses 7 times in a row. The market is punishing Bob for his good behavior. Bob starts to doubt his system and takes a high-risk trade that violates his system — and is successful. To his surprise, he tries this a second time and also makes money. Bob is now back to square one, trading without a system because the market has rewarded his bad behavior. Through random reinforcement, the market has re-conditioned the way Bob approaches trading by distracting him away from his trading plan. He has allowed himself to be manipulated into an impulsive, high risk, revenge based trading approach. Everyone was a genius in 2017 The concept of random reinforcement was never more evident than in the crypto bubble of 2017. During this parabolic bull market, it was easy to mistake luck for skill. Amateur traders were making money hand over foot by simply throwing cash into random altcoins and selling after massive, immediate gains. Everyone was a “genius” in the 2017 crypto market. Then 2018 happened — the bubble popped, and these amateur traders were ill-prepared to deal with the drawdown. They failed to sell their assets and held blindly until they had lost everything. Understanding that markets are dynamic and in constant flux is key to being profitable. A trader must learn to be able to determine when a certain string of losses or profits can be attributed to their skill and when it is random. This is done by trading with a defined plan over a long period of time . Every trader should have a well developed and tested (through paper trading) plan, with written rules for entries, exits and stop losses, position sizing and risk. They should NEVER trade outside their plan. Bitcoin trading: sticking to your plan No more than 1% of a trader’s portfolio should be at risk on any single trade — this is the key to sustaining multiple, consecutive losses. They should test and tweak their plan over a long period of time — hundreds of trades. A good system gives a trader an edge over a long time frame because randomness becomes less of a factor with a larger sample. A good trade should be defined as one where a trader planned their trade, traded their plan and managed their risk — those are all elements they can control. It is NOT defined by the outcome. A bad trade, on the other hand, is where a trader fails to follow their rules and executes trades against their better judgment. This is always going to be a bad trade even if it happens to be profitable. By developing a well-tested plan, traders can overcome the pitfalls of random reinforcement, eliminate emotion and impulse, and learn to be profitable. That’s how you become a part of the 5% that make it as traders.

Good article: There are millions of businesses in the market. And most businesses can be categorized as a high turnover business or a low turnover business. I’ll explain… A high turnover business usually has a small profit margin and they earn from the fast turnover of their inventory. The faster they “move” their inventory, the more profits they make. An example of a high turnover business is Walmart. On the other hand… You’ve got businesses with a low turnover but high-profit margin. They don’t sell regularly, but when they do, the profit margin is high. An example of a low turnover business is Rolex. Now you’re wondering: “How does this relate to my trading?” If you think about it, the concept is the same. Are you a high-frequency trader looking to capture a small move, or are you a low-frequency trader who prefers to catch a big move? This is important. Because if you don’t know what’s your trading business model, you’ll waste countless hours finding the “best” system that doesn’t exist. So my question to you is… What’s your trading business model? Do you know the cost of doing business? (It’s not what you think) Every business has a cost. If you’re running a restaurant, you’ve got to pay… The salaries of your worker The rental of the unit Electricity bills Groceries And it’s the same for trading. Now, you might not have to pay for the rental of your office (if you work from home), salaries, etc. But, there’s still a cost — and it’s the cost of losing. I don’t care how good you are at trading, whether you have a $1m dollar account or a $10 account, you’ll face losses regularly. And that my friend, is your cost of doing business. But wait, that’s not all. There’s another cost you must take into consideration. What is it? Your opportunity cost. Here’s what I mean… Let’s say you left a $60k /year job to trade full-time. And as a full-time trader, you make $40k/year. So how much did you make as a trader? Did you say $40k? Nope. You’ve lost $20k (60 – 40) because you could have been working elsewhere making $60k per year. That’s an opportunity cost of $20k to you. Don’t forget that. How to protect yourself in “bad times” Here’s a fact: The market moves in cycles. If you look back, there’s always a major recession once in a while. And as a business owner, it’s a huge mistake to assume the economy will always do well. For example: If you’re a Gym owner, you might have seen your membership increase every year (for the last 5 years). After all, times are good and people can afford to sign up a gym membership. But what happens when there’s a recession? Have you considered it? How will it affect you? I’ll tell you this… Your memberships will decline because people stop renewing it — or even cancel it altogether. So if you want to protect yourself, you must have enough cash flow to see through the difficult times. Now, why am I sharing this with you? Because it’s the same with trading! The market is always changing . It goes from an uptrend to downtrend, low volatility to high volatility, etc. This means your strategy might work for a few months and then it stops working. That’s why you must have enough cash flow to survive through the difficult times. If you can do it, you’ve got a good chance of making it all back (and more) when the market conditions are in your favor. If you want a ballpark figure, I recommend setting aside 12 months of living expenses (outside of your trading capital). The ONE thing you must do to survive in this business Let me share with you a real story. When I was a proprietary trader, most of us trade the Nikkei Futures. The reason is that Nikkei is traded on 3 different exchanges: SGX, OSE, and CME — which offers arbitraging opportunities. Here’s an example… Let’s say Nikkei is traded at 100 at SGX, 101 at OSE, and 100 at CME. This means you can buy Nikkei at 100 from SGX or CME, and then quickly sell it at 101 at OSE — for a risk-free profit of $1. Now, this was “easy money” back in the 2008 period. However, with the rise of algorithms (which are faster than humans), these inefficiencies faded. At this point, many traders left the proprietary trading business because their edge is eroded. However… There is a small group of traders who are still trading to this day. How? They adapt. Yes, that’s right. You must adapt to the markets if you want to survive in this business. Your trading strategy might work for a few years and then suddenly, it stops working altogether. And then what are you going to do? Do you call it quits and blame the market? Or, develop new trading strategies and adapt to the new market condition? How to diversify your risk When you first start a business, you’ll have one core product to fulfill the needs of your customers. For example: Amazon started with books. Apple started with Mac. Google started with search. Now… Amazon sells almost anything online. Apple offers multiple products &amp; services like iPhone, iPad, iTunes, etc. Google has emails, business applications, and are developing self-driving cars. Now the question is… Why did these companies increase their product offering? Simple. They want to diversify their risk. They don’t want to rely on just one product because what if… There’s a new law that bans everyone from reading books There’s a new technology to look for information faster than a search engine A Mac exploded killing everyone in a 10km radius I know these are exaggerations, but you get my point. That’s why businesses tend to develop new products and services — to diversify their risk. Now, what about trading? Well, it’s the same! As a trader, you’ll want to diversify your risk into different markets and strategies. Take me for an example… I started with Price Action Trading . Then, I learned about Trend Following and how to ride trends across different markets. And recently, I’ve developed systematic strategies to trade Stocks and ETFs. Why is that? Because I want to diversify my risk — so I can profit from the markets even if something fails. Does it make sense? Good. Moving on… How to start trading as a business — 5 powerful tips to dramatically increase your chance of success Now if you want to start your trading business, then here are 5 powerful tips to increase your odds of success. 1. You must trade with an edge, here’s how… Here’s the thing: I don’t care if you have the best trading psychology or the tightest risk management . Because if you don’t have an edge , you’ll never make money — period. You’re probably wondering: “So how do I find an edge?” Well, the easiest way is to find something that already works and adapt it. For example: Trend Following Momentum Trading Value Investing (I know this isn’t trading, but it works) Next, read books on these topics to understand the ins and outs of it (like why it works, how it works, and when it underperforms). Now with the concepts you’ve learned, develop your own trading strategy so you can find an edge in the markets. Next… 2. Grow your capital — the lifeblood of your trading business Here’s the deal: You need money to make money in this business, here’s why… Let’s say, you have a trading strategy that makes 20% a year. With a $1000 account, that’s $200/year. With a $10,000 account, that’s $2000/year. With a $1,000,000 account, that’s $200,000/year. See my point? You might have a strategy with an edge, but with low capital, it’ll lead you to take unnecessary risks — that erodes your edge. Here’s an example… You have a $1000 account and you make 20% a year. The $200 is probably not enough to meet your needs. So you have thoughts like… “All this work for just $200?” And the next thing you know, you take on too much risk and lose everything. So, what’s the solution? Grow your capital. And if you don’t enough capital, get a job and save up — there’s no short-cut to it. You might wonder: “What about borrowing money to trade?” Sure, you can borrow money to trade. But the psychological pressure that comes with “money you can’t afford to lose” isn’t something I recommend. 3. Set aside 12 months of living expenses Now… I know you want to make consistent profits every month. However, there are times when you just won’t make money. Perhaps the market conditions aren’t favorable to you. Perhaps you’re in a drawdown. Perhaps you’re not psychologically ready to trade. Whatever the case is, you want to have at least 12 months of living expenses covered. So, even if you’re at your worst trading performance, you can live through it and not worry whether you have enough to put food on the table. Imagine: How much more liberated you’ll feel when you know you’re covered for the next 12 months. Next… 4. Diversify your risk, here’s how… You can trade multiple trading strategies so you can profit in different market conditions. For example, Trend Following in trending markets and Mean Reversion in range markets. Also, you can diversify your risk outside of your trading business. For example… Have a fixed income job Work part-time (giving tuition, freelance, etc.) Have a side business (mentoring traders, referral schemes, etc.) The possibilities are endless. 5. Always be a student of the market Now in other industries, you might get away with learning a specific skill and using it for the next 30 years. But, it doesn’t happen in trading. The strategies you’ve learned 5 years ago might not work anymore, and if that’s your bread and butter, you’re toast (pun intended). So, the only way to stay in this business is to be a student of the markets. How? By learning from other traders, reading books, watching the markets, and testing new hypotheses. If you can do this, you’ll never worry what the market throws at you because you’re always adapting — a hallmark of a lifelong trader. Conclusion Trading is like any other business. You must make a profit, manage your cash flow, diversify your risk, and adapt to market conditions. I hope the strategies and techniques you’ve learned get you closer to trading success. And finally, here’s my question to you… How do you manage your trading business?

In my opinion, the best way to thank and honor your teacher and show that you have learned is to be able to apply the knowledge you have taken to other areas and instruments. Forex has been less volatile in 2019, and some of you must have been frustrated if you stuck to daily entries on forex. It means you beat your worst and most powerful adversary, the part of you who holds you back from greatness. And this doesn't mean to trade everyday, on all timeframes, it means you have accepted that you understand how trading works, that there is only so much you can do as a retail trader, and find success and satisfaction in the sections of the market movement you can capture without putting your health and capital at risk. Marking ideal entry points on a chart is something I now find unhelpful because it takes the emotional roller-coaster out of what real traders go through, at least in their early years. The only thing that really matters is how much risk you are taking, and make that acceptable so that you don't sabotage yourself, either by pushing yourself to financial ruin or not follow through your winners. So, I suggest you take the knowledge that is available here and make it yours, really yours. Don't rely on others, it will only make you weak and will erode your self confidence. They person next to you doesn't know more than you, don't yield that power to someone else, in trading or in life.

--- 帖子 #12576 ---
I came across a nice article today. Just wish to share with you all. How Gratitude Can Affect Your Trading Results by Mohammed Isah | December 25th, 2019 Are you grateful? This is a question that virtually everyone on the planet would say yes to and subsequently rattle off a list of items they are grateful for. This is generally true no matter if the individual is rich or if they are flat broke. It is especially true right now as this happens to be the gratitude season with Thanksgiving just around the corner. It is a time for families and friends to gather and celebrate by giving thanks while feasting and making announcements regarding those things that they are grateful for. Gratitude Has Overarching Effects The fact is that gratitude is an extremely popular notion thought to be at the core of being courteous and thoughtful, but actually, gratitude is much more than that. Most people would be surprised to know that gratitude is a powerful state of mind that has very real and tangible benefits which can be quantified and studied. Gratitude is far more impactful on the system than ever thought possible and it has neurological underpinnings which brings me to a personal encounter with this underrated emotion. Ten years ago, I was diagnosed with Parkinson’s, initially thought to be a movement disorder but now shown to be a progressive degenerative neurological condition that has close to 100 symptoms and is due in large part to a dopamine deficiency. Parkinson’s can affect the body in ways that include severe tremors, loss of balance, severe stiffness, rigidity and back and joint pain. As you can see, even with this very short litany of issues it promises to be a real bumpy ride; to which I can attest. Like Michael J. Fox, I noticed a small tremor in the index finger of my left hand that eventually caused me to go to a neurologist who let me in on the news. Because of this condition there are numerous challenges that get in my way. The other day was particularly tough as I was experiencing strong irritability and discomfort with little to no desire to be out and about. I was due to meet with friends that evening for dinner and considered canceling and letting them know that I would not be good company. Fortunately, there was also little desire to sequester myself either, so I used a couple of personal tools to change my internal state. One was to listen to an audio file that included frequencies designed to put my brain into a relaxed state, and simultaneously I sat mindfully still and began to list as many things as I could that I am grateful for in the span of 10 to 15 minutes. I often include gratitude in the morning and usually before meditation; however, that day I specifically used it to connect with my higher self and experience spiritual consciousness. After about 30 minutes I felt so much better and subsequently had a marvelous time that night. That mind/body response was not just a placebo effect. My body/brain experienced a neurobiological transformation associated with my brain’s release of a neurochemical cocktail directly related to the contemplation of gratitude. How the Brain Responds to Gratitude You might ask: What do our brains look like on gratitude? Initially there is a shot of dopamine – whether expressing gratitude for all the wonderful things in your life or for being grateful to someone who has extended a helping hand or shared a gift; the brain triggers the release of dopamine. Dopamine is a neurotransmitter that, among many other things, is secreted in conjunction with social connections, camaraderie and optimism. This hit of a special neurotransmitter encodes the experience in order for the individual to connect the act with feeling good. It all has to do with survival and the fact that social interaction and belonging are hard-wired into our DNA. This hard-wiring developed over thousands of years in response to things our ancestors relating the disconnection from the tribe, clan, or family as meaning certain death on the savanna, so sociability is rewarded to sustain the practice. Additionally, when you engage in being grateful, serotonin , another feel-good neurotransmitter, is released in direct response to positive thoughts, memories and expressions of thanksgiving. The region of the brain that lights up at that time is called the anterior cingulate cortex (a small area of the brain just above the temporal lobe on either side of the left and right hemisphere). Serotonin supports mood elevation very similar to anti-depressants, affecting will-power and motivation. Over the past few years there have been many research projects specifically aimed at deepening our understanding of how the simple state of gratitude affects the body and mind. One such study is featured in The International Journal of Workplace Health Management (Vol.2 pp.202-219). This research project noted that among nurses, gratitude was a consistent indicator of a number of productivity enhancers; such as, fewer absences, higher job satisfaction, more proactive behaviors, less exhaustion, less cynicism, greater health and increased safety within the work climate. In other words, gratitude brings happiness by not only expressing it to others but also having gratitude towards the self. Gratitude and It’s Affects on Trading Results So, what does this have to do with trading? Well, one of the ways to put this into practice and begin laying the groundwork for enhanced focus on what-matters-most and being in the now of the trade is to use a gratitude journal. This could be a brief but compelling paragraph every morning or evening that describes the day in terms of all the things that happened which involved a sense of well-being and high performance and being grateful for each of these experiences. As noted above, this exercise, due to the nature of the brain’s response to gratitude, would begin to lower stress levels, sharpen focus, support greater clarity and develop an increase in the brain’s ability to be coherent, communicative and coordinated, all of which are precursors to supporting your ability to remain centered, grounded and focused as you trade. Here are a number of other benefits directly related to the act of being grateful: pain reduction, stress regulation, the improvement of sleep quality and the reduction of toxic emotions, just to name a few. So, giving thanks takes on much greater implications for getting the results that you want both in trading and in life. Joyful Trading

--- 帖子 #12652 ---
So who are the Big Boys? A bit of a grind on GU today, these days this is the only pair I day trade with. So while I'm sitting through it I've found some info on the GBP Bank of England "Participants" for those interested in the GBP market... Aberdeen Standard Investments Aldermore Aviva Investors Bank of America Merrill Lynch Barclays Bank UK BGC Capital Partners BlackRock Credit Suisse Euroclear Goldman Sachs Greater London Authority HSBC The Investment Association J.P Morgan Asset Management LCH Lloyds Bank Newcastle Building Society Prudential Royal Bank of Scotland Santander UK Societe Generale Tesco PLC Interesting reading in these documents if you want to develop your "seeing the beyond the candles" knowledge. For example "Q14. What is market colour and why is it particularly highlighted? Answer: Market colour is the provision of information around market activity. In the past more information in some circumstances may have been given than was appropriate. An example would be telling a prospective counterparty who else had been in the market, at what price, size and when. The sharing of such details is not in line with the over-arching principles of the Code as this can lead to a loss of trust in the market. The Code acknowledges that some market information is helpful for an effective and functioning market, particularly when no data regarding overall pricing and volumes is published. But any market colour provided must be on an aggregate basis and anonymised, so that no specific trades can be identified. Trading London with Fakeout Today I had the chance to trade for some hours and study London GBP trading more. I've included a live working chart which I use and I don't expect it all to make sense, however this is how I now trade. NOTE THIS IS NOT STRAT's 5 MIN TREND TRADING - READ THE THREAD . I just used a 5 min chart today to fit with my own time frame! You'll see a version of this activity all of the time with GBP. The fakeout is usually the Asia session range give or take a few pips extended after the Londen open. My first trade was 5 min after the London open. This is a typical breakout situation which I don't trade. I entered this one because of the nice push up after the Frankfurt open. BUT i trade cautiously expecting THE TRAP. Sometimes this doesn't happen so I TRADE WHAT I SEE and will react accordingly, it could trend all day for 200 pips for all I know. Sure enough I get an add on. I enter but am on high alert. Price stalls and I move my stops up. I have gotten into the habit of drawing consolidation boxes. These help me visualise momentum and over come the time/price candlestick conundrum, this is better than guessing what you THINK price might do next. I've left these on the chart so you can see how I'm thinking. So next, price drops and pauses just at the London Open price. I enter a SELL pending here and close my BUYs. What I've learned trading BASIC and Trend PASR is that I have no bias and trade what I see. This should help some people. Don't try and trade a trend that isn't there. Let go and close at a small loss! LET IT GO! Price now drops below the London Open and I sell a 2nd trade BUT we are at yesterdays high which is ALSO the Asian high. Price pulls back but then drops into the Asia zone I get a 3rd entry but now I am cautious again. You will see BRN 1.31. Also I made a level using the previous 4 hr close, now if price closes below this level and 1.31 the current H4 candle will have reversed. IF this happens there is a high probability that I am in for a strong fast trend south, and I have a next zone I think the market will travel to if it does. BUT... no, we close back up above yesterdays high and I manage a small profit. We now have a reverse situation and I BUY. It has become a BASIC trade but also with a trend potential. Pull up a Boss chart and look at the structure, especially the 22nd Jan Candle. There are SELL orders above that and I'm guessing that was today's plan to find liquidity to get there. This is also 1.3150. No coincidence! The rest of the trades are managed accordingly. PS I made more out of the worker EU Basic trade than this and spent only 10 minutes setting it up but I enjoyed my chart time today... Attached Image (click to enlarge) PPS I've posted this to show people that it is much more important to learn how to manage trades and your plan. It isn't about indicators and perfect patterns. Today's trading was hard but completely manageable and predictable. My draw down despite a total number of 19 trades (which is way too many for me) was only about 12 pips. At the end of the session I'm in profit. This was a hard day. But the easy days, are REALLY easy. Keep grafting and ignore the fools.

--- 帖子 #12678 ---
@Rub Are you using the simple technique of line charts to draw your SR levels ? Turn your chart to line chart, and find peaks &amp; valleys, draw a horizontal line that connects as many as possible. The best ones are one that were used as support AND resistance. Do that on your first higher time frame (for example MN1), then jump to your second higher time frame (for example W1) and do the same, then turn your chart back to candles on your 'WORKER'/trading time frame (for example D1) and wait for signals ! That usually works pretty well. And if peaks &amp; valleys don't seem to align, drawing a larger zone, or placing your SR in the middle, should give pretty good results. Hope this helped ! Cheers.

Hi Max Extract from Strat's path...lesson for me as well... Regards Pete Power of Time Frames 1) We take our direction from the BIG BOSS (Monthly) 2) We take our direction (and sometimes trades) from the BOSS (Weekly) 3) We time and initiate our trades on the Worker (Daily) So, when we do an analysis of a pair or any financial instrument for that matter: We identify our SR levels We find out where the BIG BOSS is relative to ITS trend AND where it is headed in the SHORT TERM relative to ITS SR levels Knowing the direction of the BIG BOSS, we review the BOSS. If the BOSS is fighting the BIG BOSS, it will be very difficult to trade so we WAIT until the BOSS aligns herself with the BIG BOSS. With the BIG BOSS and BOSS now in harmony (both moving together in the same direction) we drop down to the Worker. We wait for the Worker to give us PASR in the direction of the BIG BOSS and BOSS. Rewarding and stress free trades come when we time the Worker JUST TURNING into the direction of the BIG BOSS and BOSS at PASR (as shown on the attached chart) The MOST REWARDING and STRESS FREE trade comes when you can time the Worker turning into the direction of the BIG BOSS at THE SAME TIME as the BOSS turns into the direction of the BIG BOSS. It sounds SIMPLE and it really is that SIMPLE but to make it stress free we MUST trade with PASR. Trying to guess trades is the best known way to blow an account. WAIT until you SEE all the above happening.

--- 帖子 #12780 ---
Another Extract from Strat's path...lesson for me as well... Which Trend ? Let's first just make sure we understand that even within one time frame there are several trends. We must establish what the dominant trend is and to do that, zoom out as far as you can go and it should be obvious. I have done this on eurusd weekly and you can see the dominant trend is UP as shown by the deep sky blue channel line. Then zoom in to find the intermediate trend as shown by the magenta line. Then zoom into that trend to find the short term trend as shown by the gold line. Then zoom into that trend to find the immediate trend as shown by the lime green line. You need to be aware of all these trends when trading the Worker to know whether you are with or against the trend. So, to trade the Worker, you need to know the IMMEDIATE BOSS trend since this governs the Worker direction. Remember also that if you draw TLs as I do, you can use them as your Momentum indicators which tell you far more than a squiggly line. So, where we are today on the BOSS, the IMMEDIATE trend is DOWN but it is at the cross - roads of it's short term trend meaning that something has to give. Whichever way this breaks IS the IMMEDIATE trend and will provide direction for the Worker. Don't forget that even 3 bars on the BOSS is 15 bars on the Worker.

--- 帖子 #12798 ---
Although they worked in your favor, # 1 and # 2 patterns are not engulfing: An engulfing pattern consists of a smaller first candle (known as the A candle) and a larger second candle (B candle) which has a higher high and lower low than the A candle, so that is seen to “engulf” the A candle. As can be seen, Pattern #3 is much closer to engulfing, could be or not... very close. But nonetheless it worked in your favor

--- 帖子 #12871 ---
Think about what a candle shows. Candle B shows sellers coming in and price is dropping in Candle B . So the sellers have kept the price lower than the high of the last black candle and at the end of the B Candle time period the sellers have kept the price lower than the high of the black candle. Candle A shows that although there are sellers, they were not 'strong' enough to push price in a lower direction before the candle closed. Now looking to the left at the last black candle, it was surpassed by candle A by the buyers. And when A closed the buyers were in control of the time period of the candle. So Candle A close shows buyers strength even when sellers pushed price down a little ... hence the wick on the top of candle A . Therefore Candle A shows the confirmation of a swing low. Does this explanation help ? https://www.forexfactory.com/attachm...1&amp;d=1583359585

--- 帖子 #12872 ---
1. The candle must close above the high. 2. Identifying swings will show you the support and resistance levels for the time frame you're in, and show you the current trend. 3. PASR is relevant on all time frames, but you might use daily S/R levels for trading the 4hr or 1hr charts. 4. I personally have trouble identifying decent levels, so I look for the blinding obvious ones like record highs or lows. Weekly control candles are a means on identifying consolidation, where you would trade the range. The EMA's show the state of the trend, such as if they are crisscrossing there's no trend, wide but coming together the trend is running out of steam. 5. I haven't watched your video, and as I mentioned, I can't seem to pick good support and resistance levels even now. So I guess someone else will have to answer this.

--- 帖子 #12895 ---
I will reply you this evening after session end CAPITAL PRESERVANCE STOCK marked is closed What is ‘limit down’? According to the New York Stock Exchange , a market trading halt may occur at “three circuit breaker thresholds” on the S&amp;P 500 due to large declines and volatility. The exchange classifies this at three levels based on the preceding session’s close in the S&amp;P 500. The rules, which apply to regular trading hours only, are as follows: Level 1: If the S&amp;P 500 drops 7%, trading will pause for 15 minutes. (This would occur today if the S&amp;P falls 208 points). Level 2: If the S&amp;P 500 declines 13%, trading will again pause for 15 minutes if the drop occurs on or before 3:25 p.m. ET. There will be no halt if the drop happens after that. (This would occur today if the S&amp;P falls 386 points). Level 3: If the S&amp;P 500 falls 20%, trading would halt for the remainder of the day. (This would occur if the S&amp;P falls 594 points). These circuit breakers have never been triggered in their current form during regular trading hours. The prior circuit breaker system was revamped after it failed to prevent the May 2010 flash crash. This current set of breakers were put into effect in February 2013. --- 帖子 #12898 ---
"NOW, when the Worker turns the Boss which turns the Big Boss that is when we LOAD UP. You probably think that does not happen much so think again. The Boss and Big Boss can both be moving in the same direction BUT the Worker can, and often does, move in the opposite direction. This is what PASR traders WAIT for. That Worker move against the Boss and Big Boss is just a corrective move so WHEN the Worker turns around with PASR into the Boss and Big Boss direction we get on board." As I understand it, that is saying to look at the current trend of the big boss, and the boss, and to look for trades on the worker when it turns in that direction. Bearing in mind I've gone back to the taking small chunks recommended to those starting out, and I think you're a long way ahead of me in having a "feel" for the market. --- 帖子 #12931 ---
Attached Image (click to enlarge) Dr. Joe reminder PURE GOLD Buy when it goes up and sell when it goes down . He went on to make $millions doing this and I subsequently learned he passed away a very rich and contented man knowing that he had beaten the “whores” at their own game. I learned all this in a few telephone conversations with him but he lost his patience with me when I still questioned his method. He wouldn’t answer my calls so I reverted back to faxes. Again, I can’t remember it word for word but I sent a simple fax saying: “How do you know when to stop buying?” On the same fax was his handwritten reply, “When it stops going up.” So I wrote on it, “How do you know when it stops going up?” His handwritten reply, “When it starts going down.” So I wrote on it, “How do you know when it stops going up and starts going down?” His handwritten reply, “When people start selling.” After going round like this in riddles, I pleaded with him to “just give it to me straight”. He sent a fax saying this would be his last communication with me and that if I didn’t understand how to buy when it goes up and sell when it goes down, I had no business trading. His final paragraph was one which I ignored, like everything else he told me, until a couple of years ago when I realized what a dumb, stupid, arrogant, stubborn idiot I had been: He said I would only be wrong twice using his simple method: “Once when you buy at the top and once when you sell at the bottom.” I just ignored this as a smart – ass answer but still tried to do what he said. Unfortunately, and as Sod’s law dictates, I tried to do it in a consolidation and lost on every trade which had me buying when I should have been selling etc. I tried and lost again and then eventually lost my way in the quest for the Holy Grail in Indicator Land. Now, with all my experience and thousands of lost $ behind me, the light came on! My understanding of what he was telling me is this: Buy when prices are moving up. Buy each retrace/dip. Keep buying until the last retrace becomes a trend change which is the one trade you lose on. Sell when prices are moving down. Sell each retrace/rally. Keep selling until the last retrace becomes a trend change which is the second trade you lose on. I have not traded like this as I have my own method/style now but on the look backs I have done it works very well. Obviously, the trendier the price, the better it works. In my later communications with other floor traders, I told them about Dr. Joe and what he told me, and asked them if it was true. As you would expect, each and everyone vehemently rejected it as absolute rubbish. Sometimes I wonder if old Dr. Joe was smoking something but then when I see those long legged neutral dojis before a significant move, I know he was right. Thank you, Dr. Joe

--- 帖子 #13035 ---
One of the biggest problems on the way to becoming a professional trader imho. How often did I put on a trade where I wanted to "learn discipline" and then stubbornly stuck with it, because it was 10 pips shy of the 250 pip target! Guess what happened ... it reversed and even took out the sl for a loss! But hey, at least you stuck with your set&amp;forget approach, clap your hands! But you LOST money! Had I just ignored this guru teaching earlier, I'd close out a ton of trades earlier in PROFIT because the market told me so and not some guru RR money management blablabla. What I started recently is just cutting out losses before they reach the sl if PA changes. Sure, I might take a loss that could have turned again here and there. But the losses are small now overall! If it does not make the full TP and the market reverses, I will just TP manually. The RR is what the market gives ... sure, I can aim for something and keep my risk small at all times. But this hyped set &amp; forget style never worked for me. I think it was Carter who has written about this in his book "Mastering the trade": "Do not make a fool of yourself for a few ticks!" I should stick this note to my screen once and for all!

RR &amp; Risk Since there have been a couple of questions on risk and RR theory, this is what I do: Attached Image (click to enlarge) See this latest loss. My entry has a fairly high "initial" SL of 25 pips. This is worse case scenerio and I'm looking to keep it moving. So I don't get the breakthough after the reload on my first trades. I can close at a small profit, BE or keep scouting for the move. I move my SL to where I will see when the trade is wrong. So it ends up been -6 pips which is ok with me. This theory of RR further confuses when you factor in multiple entries and moving stops as I see the market developing. Because of this I don't bother with RR and gave up on it along time ago. Although I think it is perfectly valid for Basic PASR set ups but you need to know your stats and probability of your set ups. Most of my BASIC PASR are 1 to 1 or 1.5 to 1 but then I might also add in on smaller TF if I see a high probability set up. So once again I can't see how RR can help me? For me it's a complete fallacy and why most automated trading fails (or will long term) why mechanical systems fail, why grid and martingales fail (eventually). IF THE TRADE IS WRONG GET OUT. PROTECT YOUR CAPITAL.

--- 帖子 #13134 ---
Regarding: Reward to Risk Ratio (RRR) and Set &amp; Forget Approach I want to add something to both of the above quoted and brillant texts. During my backtests I started wondering if I could just use a fixed RRR system and therefore have like a set and forget approach. As I was experimenting with both volatility based stops and also breakeven/close after X candles systems I came up with an excel sheet that analyses the outcome of my systems if they would have been performing better when having a fixed RRR. TL;DR fixed RRR systems are marginally less profitable - at least for the data that I have went through (and that are years of data on M5 to M30). As said many times: the market just doesn't care about any RRR of any person - it just does what it does. Details In my backtesting software I am able to see the maximum favorable excursion (MFE) and maximum adverse excursion (MAE). Just two terms that mean the following: - what was my maximum equity during a specific trade (if you can catch that point on every trade, you would be a superhero). - what was my minimum equity during a specific trade (drawdown) With those two parameters I can analyze how my system would have performed for several different R systems. Simple example We have a 100k USD trading account, risk 0.65% per trade. We enter our first trade which had the following output: - min equity: -450 USD (so we were in drawdown) - max equity: 850 USD - outcome 650 USD (SL got hit according to my trailing stop). I can now compare, how the outcome of the trade would have been for several R systems. A 0.5R system would have given us a profit of 325 USD (minus commissions). A 1R system would have given us a profit of 650 USD (minus commissions). A 1.5R system would have given us - and that is now the tricky part - the amount were my stop got hit, so 650 USD. I have setup an excel for this, where I am able to just copy my order history. The excel consists of: the Order History the Matrix of every trade outcome for each R system the Analyzation page the equity graph of just the "real" system Order History Attached Image (click to enlarge) Matrix Attached Image (click to enlarge) Analyze Attached Image (click to enlarge) What you can see is: the lower the R-factor the higher the win %. But as you can see, none of the fixed R-factor systems (highest score is 27% for a 1.2R system) comes close to my real system that uses volatility based stops (53% profit). Also: if I want to shoot for the moon trades with a 6R outcome - I would actually have lost money (-25%) Equity Graph Attached Image (click to enlarge) Just for completeness: this specific backtest was on M30, GU from 01 Feb 2018 to 17 July 2018. And just to give another interesting insight because often you think as a trader "I am leaving soo much money on the table" - that is also something I need to get used to. On the above system, the outcome in the backtest was 53% profit in 5.5 months = 52.720,68 EUR profit. If summarizing all max equities for each trade, the result would be 164.740,68 EUR profit. That means: I have left about 2/3 of my potential profits on the table. Be aware: those are just MY conclusions based on MY testings. Handle with care, it might be a candle with hair. Attached Image If you are using FT3/4 and want to get some insights in your backtest, let me know. I hope you might get something useful out of this post.

--- 帖子 #13136 ---
Now the numbers in the post are correct. Sorry for not checking the numbers initially for its full correctness. I might have introduced a bug while analyzing a breakeven system. The bug was this: when not reaching the desired R-factor the system would exit at the breakeven point minus commissions. But as I am using the volatility based stop loss we will get out of the trade at the stop of the real system. The real system produces a profit of 53% where now the most profitable fixed RRR system of 6R would have given us 49% profit (Edit: commissions are not considered currently for my R factors - with that system commisions would cost us about 3400 USD, resulting in around 46% profit). The difference isn't that significant anymore. What my system also shows: as I reduce my risk by tightening the stops the loosers get cut, and winners are free to run. Despite having the numbers initially wrong, the post still contains other useful informations.

About " do not trade in the WCC" i mean that i do not trade when the price is trapped inside the WCC. I used to trade like WCC does not exist. I checked what is happening and most of my losses were when price was trapped inside the WCC. From my reading in the forum I knew that the price is supposed to range inside the WCC, but i did not believed it fully. I do not trade the top or bottom of the WCC as basic PASR. I have never tried it. My results were 45 wins and 105 losses when trading like WCC does not exist. Total profit was 16% for couple of weeks. Not bad. After that i decided to do a test on the same period and pairs but without trading at all when the price is trapped inside the WCC. My results were way better. I god 20 wins and 26 losses with total profit 18% for the same period. I reduced the number of trades 3 times and my winning % was 10% higher. Also i noticed that when trading inside the WCC i got 7-8 straight losses. When i stopped trading when the price is trapped i never had more that 2-3 losses in a row. For me realizing this without keeping journal would be really hard. I am comfortable with this style of trading. Do not take my advise seriously, because i am still a newbie!!!! Check it for yourself.

Example of a gigantic WCC due to the length of the move March 15th. Price moved back to the top of the WCC and traded in a nice daily range providing PASR opportunities. Drop to H4 and trade that Potential WCC for a nice trend trade up to BRN .6500 where price closed last week with a new potential WCC. Price also closed above BB high (green horizontal line) so now BB and Boss are in up swing. Watch price action in this area. Bottom line is that by using lower time frames such as H4 through WCCs, good trend trades can be found using the strat shadow.

--- 帖子 #13241 ---
Hi voynich In addition to Lou's comments Strat did always emphasize the importance of the candle closing before making any trading decisions. The candle close values on the time frame you are drawing S/R levels does therefore become important. The high low values on that time frame could very well be close or open values on another time frame due to the fractal nature of the charts / markets. The more touch points to the SR line you are drawing through open / close /high /low the more valid that level becomes. Regards Pete

--- 帖子 #13416 ---
Hi Lou I have a 22 ADR (set to daily) with the range for the today on all my charts. I only use it for a reference as to how far price has gone for the day when I enter a trade. I never use it as a Stop nor Target. On each Time Frame Chart I also have an ATR for that particular time frame set to 1 - 3 &amp; 14. I can quickly glace at the ATR to tell me what the current candle (1) is doing and well as the last 3 candles (3ATR) the last 14 candles (14ATR). DR JOE REMINDER From this came his very simple method: Buy when it goes up and sell when it goes down . He went on to make $millions doing this and I subsequently learned he passed away a very rich and contented man knowing that he had beaten the “whores” at their own game. I learned all this in a few telephone conversations with him but he lost his patience with me when I still questioned his method. He wouldn’t answer my calls so I reverted back to faxes. Again, I can’t remember it word for word but I sent a simple fax saying: “How do you know when to stop buying?” On the same fax was his handwritten reply, “When it stops going up.” So I wrote on it, “How do you know when it stops going up?” His handwritten reply, “When it starts going down.” So I wrote on it, “How do you know when it stops going up and starts going down?” His handwritten reply, “When people start selling.” After going round like this in riddles, I pleaded with him to “just give it to me straight”. He sent a fax saying this would be his last communication with me and that if I didn’t understand how to buy when it goes up and sell when it goes down, I had no business trading. His final paragraph was one which I ignored, like everything else he told me, until a couple of years ago when I realized what a dumb, stupid, arrogant, stubborn idiot I had been: He said I would only be wrong twice using his simple method: “Once when you buy at the top and once when you sell at the bottom.” Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Hi Eushev You can trade both within or outside the WCC. However, please bear in mind that the a close outside the WCC on a lower time frame does not mean that the WCC is no longer valid. Price can just as easily turn around and head back into the WCC and you will see that movement as a wick above the WCC on the Boss chart. That being said you raise a valid point so it it is important to understand the Power of Time Frames and how Price reacts around and in the Strat Shadow. That may give you clues to what price is doing when in the vicinity of the upper or lower border of the current WCC. Pete
