Hi Udkox Below are a few extracts I made from Strat posts that may help you: Study and understand the image below: Attached Image Which Trend ? Let's first just make sure we understand that even within one time frame there are several trends. We must establish what the dominant trend is and to do that, zoom out as far as you can go and it should be obvious. I have done this on eurusd weekly and you can see the dominant trend is UP as shown by the deep sky blue channel line. Then zoom in to find the intermediate trend as shown by the magenta line. Then zoom into that trend to find the short term trend as shown by the gold line. Then zoom into that trend to find the immediate trend as shown by the lime green line. You need to be aware of all these trends when trading the Worker to know whether you are with or against the trend. So, to trade the Worker, you need to know the IMMEDIATE BOSS trend since this governs the Worker direction. Remember also that if you draw TLs as I do, you can use them as your Momentum indicators which tell you far more than a squiggly line. So, where we are today on the BOSS, the IMMEDIATE trend is DOWN but it is at the cross - roads of it's short term trend meaning that something has to give. Whichever way this breaks IS the IMMEDIATE trend and will provide direction for the Worker. Don't forget that even 3 bars on the BOSS is 15 bars on the Worker. Regards Pete Attached Image Power of Time Frames 1) We take our direction from the BIG BOSS (Monthly) 2) We take our direction (and sometimes trades) from the BOSS (Weekly) 3) We time and initiate our trades on the Worker (Daily) So, when we do an analysis of a pair or any financial instrument for that matter: We identify our SR levels We find out where the BIG BOSS is relative to ITS trend AND where it is headed in the SHORT TERM relative to ITS SR levels Knowing the direction of the BIG BOSS, we review the BOSS. --- 帖子 #13613 ---
Basics of power of time frames: BB up Boss up Worker waiting for signal to go up Your trade was counter trend with the BEEB on worker. Using strat shadow, your target would be to the top of the ss so minimal profit. Ideally wait for move down to shadow and get long on PA in that area. Dropping to H4 would have provided opportunity at bottom of ss and 200 ema. Just staying with worker, get long on break of IB at top of ss. Note: once shadow is up, take long trades on retraces and don't look for short term counter trend moves.

--- 帖子 #13618 ---
This is a perfect example of top down catching the BB, Boss and worker all turning at the same point. Using line chart it can be seen: The green horizontal line is the BB close in August Drop to Boss and see it turning Drop to worker and see first price reversal providing a first short opportunity Now that price is moving down catch the next shorts on retrace in October and November to/through the worker shadow. The key is being able to watch and catch these larger swings starting with the BB. By now there has been a 400 pip swing down since the BB topped out. We can wait for confirmation of swings on the higher time frames but in doing so a lot of pips are sacrificed. So while watching for confirmations, also look at the BB closes. By the time we get a BB confirmation the Boss and worker have made a significant move.

--- 帖子 #13619 ---
Using the same methodology on NZDUSD: Green line on BB close in August Drop to Boss and worker Price couldn't get any traction to the downside and it can be seen how the Boss and worker shadow provided direction for a move back up. So in this case the move the downside failed and price resumed up trend.

--- 帖子 #13749 ---
Hey there. Just wanted to share some experience, not sure if there is any value in it, but it saves me many times from getting in losing trades. Not a advice at all. Senior members will say if it is worth it to mention or not. Maybe it is already written in the both threads, not sure i read it as there is too much information. When trading WK/D1/4h combo i basically do not trade longs in the direction of the trend if price on 4hr did not close above the previous week's high /assuming that price is not in WCC/. Previous week high or low tend to act as S/R level in my opinion. Not a new discovery of course it was new for me and i realized it from watching charts and taking many disappointments. Once i "discovered it" i took less bad trades. Many times this signals as early pre"WCC" alarm. Many times i can spot forming WCC from the first candle, actually before it happens. Sorry if this is already discussed or mentioned or if it sounds stupid/irrelevant. Many examples on your chart, just mark the high of the previous week's high in up trends and see what happens when price did not exceed it. Of course like anything in trading this does not happen all the time and every time. Many times this means pause or reversal in 4hr chart, but not always. If this sounds stupid please ignore it

Attachment g As promised, this is a GBP/USD daily chart from March this year up to today. What I like about it is that it is a microcosm of the market. You have everything, easily placed S/R lines, which are established early on, and reverberate later for TP or SL placement. Nice clear price action bar formations, for example, Pin bars, Buob, Beob, Dhlc, doji even THLC!! However, in order to interpret this chart you need to understand price bars, and that takes time. If you had been riding this wave, bar by bar and S/R to S/R you would be very much in profit. There are 2 day pins, and the break down of price action bars to signal the other way. See it like a blueprint if you like. To my mind, and experience, if you cannot successfully trade the daily charts, with raw naked bars and S/R your not ready to move on. It's the nursery or kindergarten of trading. In one you learn the ABC'S in the other you learn the Pins, beob and Dhlc. By having a simple trading strategy, that is consistently repeatable in application, you can build a trading log, which leads to your P/L ratio, which leads to risk allocation, which is based on your P/L ratio. Price bar action tells you when to enter, and when to leave IF you can get out the way. Question: If you have a losing trade, where you wrong or did you misunderstand and misinterpret the markets. The problem is that you don't even know what you don't even know yet, because you can't think what you want to think, because you don't know what you need to know in order to think what you want to think. Which is fine because you act as my liquidity provider as I take all your money, and you didn't even know it was me. I bought your SL, I filled your TP, I filled your market order, why, because I look for them and I know what you need to know. Frightened?? You should be, because there are sharks in these waters. I am one of them. Before you think I suffer from delusions of grandeur, claiming that I AM THE MARKET, think about it. If I am not at one with the market, how can I be successful ? --- 帖子 #13778 ---
Each pair has a pip value based on the currency being traded against. For example: GBPUSD pip value is $10 per pip on a standard lot size determined by USD so all pairs trading against USD will have a $10 per pip value. GBPNZD pip value just now is $7.17 - all NZD pairs are $7.17 pip value just now. Except for USD (world currency), which is locked at $10, all other currencies change in accordance with current interest rates, supply and demand meaning that the pip value changes. --- 帖子 #13788 ---
Thanks for your questions. To answer how you trade the chart I posted. This is done by reading the price bar action, pin, beob etc. In order to do this you must undertake a study in price bars and become as familiar with them as you would a language. Secondly you need to make a study into S/R lines and their placement. Both of these studies take time and practice, and is something you may want to do as homework, when you are not pursuing and learning Strats lower time frame entry system. To clarify B/E, that is break even. The collapse of price bar action is when a set up is directing you to go down, but eventually goes up and breaks the downward pointing price bar signal. Price bars, and their formation are indicators that carry consensus. That is why they work. They also offer a clearly defined SL placement. Now, working with the correct placement of S/R, you can select a reasonable TP in or around the S/R, or let it run, or tighten your stop loss. The fact that a price bar action set up fails, is also by consensus, and so the opportunity arises for you to trade the price bar action in the contrary way. Higher time frame bars carry more consensus, and so they can direct you on the lower, as with Strats method. The downside is that there will be fewer signals on the daily, and bigger SL, and therefore less value to your pip. However, if you get really good at selecting your trades, you can increase your risk in line with your profit/loss ratio. Ultimately your goal should be to read and flow with the market, which takes years, and kick the can down the road on making millions. If you do your homework the millions will come.

Look at the immediate trend on the boss (weekly), is it up or down? Does it match the direction of the big boss? Once you have a better understanding of the price action you can then start to trade the swings up and down of the boss. The ideal is when they all turn back to the same direction in the overall trend.

Hi linkuva Further to the posts from Bistolis, Terry and Rub, below are some extracts from Strat's posts in the archives that could help as well. Pete Attached Image Which Trend ? Let's first just make sure we understand that even within one time frame there are several trends. We must establish what the dominant trend is and to do that, zoom out as far as you can go and it should be obvious. I have done this on eurusd weekly and you can see the dominant trend is UP as shown by the deep sky blue channel line. Attached Image Then zoom in to find the intermediate trend as shown by the magenta line. Attached Image Then zoom into that trend to find the short term trend as shown by the gold line. Attached Image Then zoom into that trend to find the immediate trend as shown by the lime green line. Attached Image You need to be aware of all these trends when trading the Worker to know whether you are with or against the trend. So, to trade the Worker, you need to know the IMMEDIATE BOSS trend since this governs the Worker direction. Remember also that if you draw TLs as I do, you can use them as your Momentum indicators which tell you far more than a squiggly line. So, where we are today on the BOSS, the IMMEDIATE trend is DOWN but it is at the cross - roads of it's short term trend meaning that something has to give. Whichever way this breaks IS the IMMEDIATE trend and will provide direction for the Worker. Don't forget that even 3 bars on the BOSS is 15 bars on the Worker.

A few of my thoughts on this pair: I have been using the most recent static S/R levels along with the daily strat shadow. The S/R levels begin with the December Big Boss candle and I have drawn in green the significant levels as I see them from that candle. At the end of December the BB closed below its high and the first week of January there was one worker attempt to go above that high which failed with a BEEB forming on the worker and a shooting star on the Boss. Price followed through to the downside and closed below the December BB high and into the shadow. One inside bar and then another rejection of the BB high and a further move down to January BB low with a doji forming and the Boss swing high confirmed. From there price retraced to the top of the shadow and turned back down to close below the shadow, BB low and BB 200ema followed by Friday's BUOB, which also closed below January BB low. So now we have the Boss and worker in alignment with both in down trend. Traders with less experience do not have this luxury yet. Or have not earned it, I should say. Hey Craig, My main comments are related to your focus being on the analysis of the Weekly Control Candles. The control candle concept was introduced in Strat's website that has now been discontinued. The main focus of this thread is PASR using our PA candles: Shooting star, Hammer, Bullish and Bearish engulfing and outside candle. I would suggest that you focus more on finding these candles in your charts and then looking to see if they are occurring at support/resistance levels. You can then decide whether a trade is warranted or not. As well, work on determining valid S/R levels and mark them on your charts. It is true that WCCs can impact these trades since price is probably consolidating or ranging within that range. However it should not be your main focus in learning and moving forward in your journey. If you find these and post the charts associated with them, I am sure you will receive many more valid comments from other members. Regards Terry

Got some of the USD/JPY move . Based my entry using a Strat Swing method as shown: In the last weekly swing.. Find the lowest price of a Daily bar. not the close... the lowest price. Draw a horizontal line at the Highest price of that SAME bar. That is where the swing should be confirmed. Enter at that point or on a Daily close above it.

To expand on the subject of risk and the application thereof, I would like to take you back to the beginning of my FX journey. I started off by learning from a guy that went by the name of James 16. This was before this site was public, carried ads and the retail FX market place was still relatively new. One of the first concepts to understand was that you where not supposed to even think about risk until you had a good 3 years profitable trading under your belt. 3 years of trading the daily, successfully. And only price action at that. Nothing else. The idea being if you can make 20% a year risking 1% a trade like that for 3 years you can move on. This was ghost or paper trading. This is very unpopular and requires all the usual cliches like, perseverance etc etc etc. No one does that. For me that is the first mistake. That is why I posted the daily charts which a few of you analyzed. Second is that we, the trader, must be a passive participant in the market and that the market is the active participant. You learn to let the market call the shots. Concepts such as " I want a 1:1 ratio on my trades" or " I want 20% a month/year/day" are all YOU imposing on the market. You have to learn to let market GIVE you what she wants by reading the bars and price action. Think about the ability of humans to see faces in clouds. Or patterns in the market. Is it real or not? 3 years will tell you. Then a blanket 1% risk will keep your psychology. James 16 had a dedicated thread just for traders psychology. The thread leader would beat the drum that if you move ahead too fast you would burn out. Most do. The D1 chart could be traded long or short and you would not look above or below you (time frames) for any further info. You where not trying to build a long term position or become rich. Just learning to read, call and win. Consistently. For 3 years. The learning was cut into 4 sections; 1 Entry 2 Management 3 Exit 4 Risk Each section was a stand alone discipline that needed to be worked on. Risk being the last. Time to completion was around 5 years at the very very least. That is how I did it. It is the only way I recommend. Not very popular I'm sure but that is how I got here. My advice is to put the 3 years in, then stick to 1% until you make 20% a year. During that time perform a full autopsy on every trade and see how the smallest of changes could have made it better. Sift through your data and separate the wheat from the chaff. When you have the annual number of trades (times 3 years), followed by the number of winners verses losers this gives you the profit to loss ratio. THEN you can allocate risk. Riddle me this, what is risk? Is it how much you put on a trade or how certain you are that your entry is correct. How certain are you? Do your trades have a 60% chance of winning, 70, 80 90?????? How will you know if you don't do the time...... you wont will you. According to my latest figures, my algorithm has a 95+ chance of winning. And that 5%+/- remainder, I have 4 early exit signals built in, in order to cut my losses early. It took me years to build this and more years to fine tune. As the years have gone on the good habits I learnt from James 16 have proved it's weight in gold. You all have a great system here from Strat and the level of analysis is great. I wonder if your doing the back office work of building your trading profile and not just posting a win snap shot here and there. It is not important if you win or lose today, but if you keep winning for years and years and years. My advise is to find a system and stick to it for 3 years, work on each of the 3 sections and when you get to the 4th section you will know. Good luck G

Terry's recent charts inspired me to post this. Here is a fib tool, a way to look at charts. I have no memory of where I got it. Giving some insight as to ....Where might this price action be headed .### PART A. this is the general explanation. Not part of the chart. PART B. this shows the tool in use on Terry's recent posting. Part A . 1. Draw the fib tool as usual * ... in this case high to low. * Note the fib values used. 2. Notice the area of retrace back toward the zero line. Shown in orange around the 38 and 23 fib lines. 3. Now look below that to the 100 to 138 fib lines, the lower orange block. This represents the target area when the retracement from the low goes back to the 38 and 23 lines and then price goes lower. 4. The blue blocks show the target when the retracement goes back to the 50 and 61 fib areas. This target being around the 161 to 178 fib. Part B. 1.This is Terry's recent chart showing the tool in action. ### This tool has no probability attached to it that I am aware of. Only the Possibility of where price might go based on where it has been. As Strat might say.. only what the Ice Cream man might serve you.

Thanks so much for all your questions, and believe me Strat you are no caveman apart from your love of that footy league you like lol In fact I am very impressed with the very high level of analysis here on this thread. To analyze a multi time frame system, with the object to ride a whole trend is amazing. And very very very difficult. But you have Strat and he has a great senior thread leader team. FF is lucky to have you and you are lucky to have each other. Cherish that. To the markets! Previously in my first post, the one I asked you guys to analyze, I wanted to highlight naked price action bars and their consensus forming power. I say consensus because that is what the signal has to form, in traders, so the movement occurs. I spent years just working on that aspect alone. Recognizing GOOD QUALITY price action. Not candles, but bars. Price bar price action is less forgiving in terms of quality and harder to recognize than candles. The price action needs to jump out at you, with the OHLC being exact to the formation. And I mean to the pip. That is where the 3 years goes. Watching, waiting, comparing for yourself. In so doing YOU own the understanding and YOU know why that particular Double high lower close is THE one you have been looking for. It is an understanding that when you have it, you know it "balls to bone." That is surly how you want to meet the market. Confident. Once you have this knowledge, or at least while you are in the process of quantifying the price action bars, you can begin to recognize where the support and resistance is. Again, this is by yourself and for yourself. Not because you got them from Strat or this thread. You need to own the understanding behind the placement of S/R. Over this time you will see the price swing from high to low, bounce off S/R and form the price action. Consolidation, trend, breakout, high volatility these are the cycles market goes through, as a pro you need to be able to navigate all these waters and to do this you must be able to read the bars. In my opinion to attempt to trade this FX market without this understanding is a waste of time, at it's best. Markets trend for only a small percentage of time and to attempt to call a trend is very very hard. But it can be done, as Start has shown (and Terry and others) but I am sure you struggle with consistency. This is probably because market does not consistently trend. There is a quote from the Matrix movie that I love which goes something like "we cannot see beyond the choices we don't understand." Market is like this too. It will change it's mind half way through and it will actively try to flush you out. The retraces price does on a trend, for example, is to pick up the orders to keep going. Also, is that trend retrace the end of the move?, the beginning of a period of high volatility?, a total change?, or a time of uncertainty with no clear direction. Here is where your superior UNDERSTANDING of price action bar formation and UNDERSTANDING of S/R will inform you. To quote Lao Tse " Sometimes we are helped by what is not, to see what is." Remember, moving averages are lagging indicators. Weekly and Monthly bars are lagging too really, they are formed and are forming as we analyze. Strats system and my algorithm are overlays to this basic understanding. My algorithm does not like trends. It is not a trend riding system, so I don't even try. I see them forming but I just let them run. In this environment, as your multi time frame analysis system triggers signals you should be all hands on deck. But what about the other times? It is in these times that the devil makes use of idle hands. This is where people drop down time frames, get frustrated and generally go to the flames as flies, when you may want to be practicing your daily price bar analysis. The fib chart I posted are of recent examples of good quality price bar formations at established levels of support and resistance. They had 2 things about them. A. They are good examples B. They are at established S/R or swings. If you don't have the ability to recognize both A and B you cannot move onto C. C. The fib I placed had the 100% at the top, if going south, or at the bottom if going north. You then drag the 0% so that the 50% is at the end of the price bar formation. This then gives you a target of where price is likely to go. There are so many ways to skin the cat once you have a great set up. Here are some examples. South bound or short; Sell stop at the 38 fib TP @ 23 fib Sell stop at the 38 go break even at 23 and let run to 0 fib Sell stop at the 38 and TP @ 0 fib Sell stop at the 38 and wait for Price action signaling a change for the other way Sell limit at 23 to add to sell from 38 Sell limit at 23 after full TP at 0 fib (Double down) Sell limit at 38 after full TP at 0 fib (Triple down) Sell limit at 61 after full TP at 0 fib (Quad down) and so and so and so.... Once you have markets money, get creative! Visa versa for Northbound or long. As you can see there is hundreds of winning combinations. And, it is one pair. Do you really need anymore? seriously....... All of these entries can be pending orders, with their individual TP and SL This, my friends, is why I say what is risk? This is why I say do the time, learn the bars, run your management practice, practice, practice. 3 years, One pair, 20% a year return risking only 1% a trade. I believe that with this new tool you will all be able to use Strats system with more accuracy, be more consistent and feel the markets. Good day All Just a couple of thoughts from my side induced by the nature of some of the posts lately. Trading is a highly personal and serious business. Ultimately there is no Holy Grail in trading unless you read the early posts from Strat in the old thread. The Holy Grail stares back at you in mirror. This is a particularly important concept that Strat tried to bring across. To be successful in trading you must own your own mind. I want to repeat that… you must own your own mind. Strat has given us guidance on many things on these threads and among others has shown the way to PASR and given us the Strat Shadow. However, he has never given us the silver spoon. That you need to find yourself. Strat has given us the framework. How you colour it in is up to you. Whether you study these threads or fill in the gaps of your knowledge from other sources (paid or free) is entirely up to you. To understand the concept of PASR is quite simple. Price Action at Support or Resistance, right? You buy low and sell high, right? Cool, you have plan and a method, right? So, go trade. Then you see PA, it happens at SR, you enter and then it ends up going the wrong way and you are out with a loss and you wonder why…? Which brings us to another point, trading PASR may seem simple but it is not that easy to do so at the hard right edge. So, Strat introduced us to the Power of Time Frames and the particularly good advice that we need to learn to see beyond the candles, and to follow in the footsteps of the Big Boys. All good and well, but in the nature of the threads the expectation is that we need to put all of this together and figure out for ourselves how to make it work for ourselves. Hence my statement above: you must own your own mind. My point of view is that you cannot blindly follow a recipe (paid for or handed down from your grandmother) and expect to be a Master Chef. You must understand the ingredients, what they do and mean, what they taste like and do for the dish. Not even to speak of baking or grilling, what temperature etc. Not to belabour the point, but to understand PASR you need to understand the ingredients of PASR. Know your candles or pin bars (your choice) but get to know them intimately. To understand the Power of Time Frames you need to understand why Strat instructs us to use the 3-time frame analysis along with the Strat Shadow, or not. To understand how to follow in the Big boys’ footsteps you need to see beyond the candles (or pin bars). Why does PA form where it does, why is SR relevant or not? Linguist and philosopher Noam Chomsky on seeking what is significant: "You can't expect somebody to become a biologist by giving them access to the Harvard University biology library and saying, "Just look through it." That will give them nothing. The internet is the same, except magnified enormously. ... The person who wins the Nobel Prize in biology is not the person who read the most journal articles and took the most notes on them. It's the person who knew what to look for. Cultivating that capacity to seek what's significant, always willing to question whether you're on the right track, that's what education is going to be about, whether it's using computers and internet, or pencil and paper and books." Source: The Purpose of Education My apologies for the long post … and one last comment. In all the time I spent on studying Strat’s threads (more than 3 years now) I have never seen him endorse fly by night methods or persons. Regards Pete

--- 帖子 #14250 ---
I didn't take this trade as I was not looking at this pair. However I recently posted on the use of BG's fib use as a good tool to add to our arsenal. The example I used was that once the fib was started as BG states, we also start a reversal fib from the projected 0 level. If price goes beyond the first fib, we can use the second fib for extension targets. In the case of the GJ, we can see by dropping to the H4, price had closed below and retraced to the shadow which is also the 78.6 and 23.6 fibs. The shadow then turned red and price continued down. Where did it stop? Right at the 200ema along with the fib extension 161.8 where it formed a doji then two candles followed by a BEEB which failed to move through the 200 and 161.8. So if one had been following this, a buy stop could have been placed above the high of that BEEB. Regards Terry

Welcome! 1)I have read, internalised and successfully practiced all the information in the archived stratsforextrading.com - Is that all the information required, or are there other resources and information that is recommended? That was a summary of PASR written for the website, so, as you are doing, read both threads starting with the original 2009 one. Yes, there is a lot of repetition but that is what you need - like muscle memory. In addition, read all you can on trading psychology as this is what determines your profitability. Specifically, learn and understand how to control your trading emotions - greed, fear, when to pull the trigger, when to enter, when to exit and, very important, when NOT TO TRADE. Reading and understanding is good but is of no use unless you put it into practice so feel free to post your analysis and trades. 2) I have already begun reading this thread, and will undoubtedly read every single post to the end - Will this serve to confirm the information found in stratsforextrading.com, or are there new concepts introduced? There are no new concepts in PASR as trading support and resistance is as "old as the hills". PASR takes that a step further by identifying when and how to trade the different market types - Range bound (Basic PASR), Swings (PASR Swing Trading) and Trending (PASR Trend Trading). The only change in PASR was the change of the long term moving average of the Strat Shadow early on in the thread. Since then, nothing has changed (only us traders getting older, more experienced and wealthier). 3) Some threads have people suggesting that trading is "harder" now in 2021, than it was around 2009, perhaps due to shorter trends or different market conditions - Can anyone who has traded since 2009 confirm if this has any truth to it, or is it an excuse made my struggling traders? To be successful in trading you have to find a method/strategy/system that you believe in , is compatible with your personality and , very important, fits your style and time constraint of trading. Once you find this, learn it like no other - inside out, upside down and every which way until you can just look at a chart and know what to do. When you do this, you will be so focused on your chosen method/strategy/system that you have no desire, need or time to look at other threads, forums, styles of trading or outside 3rd party media. When you "stray" on to other threads, forums or other trading related subjects, you are losing focus and this is where trading psychology "plays" with your mind - there is an old saying - "the grass is not greener on the other side" - I know this from experience in my personal life, my past career and my trading. If you find yourself looking at other threads then you have lost focus, belief and confidence and so the slippery downward slope begins until you disappear up your own chuff. Your statement IS an excuse given by losing traders and, new, inexperienced traders. It is true that computerised and now, algo trading, had an impact on the markets but the fact remains - nothing or no-one can do anything without leaving traces (footprints) behind. The question impacts short term traders (tick, M1 and M5) more than long term traders (D1, W and M) but again, that is because of timing rather than market structure. Trading PASR is no "harder" today than it was back in 2009 or earlier when I first started trading this concept. PASR trading is akin to waves on the Ocean - the ripples, the swells and the waves, until they disappear, PASR will always trade them. There will always be ranges, swings and trends but the when and where is out of OUR control and changes with news, geo-politics, events, war, natural disasters and the like. The bottom line is that PASR traders TRADE in the footsteps of SMART MONEY - the Big Boys - we do not lead - WE FOLLOW. Trading PASR will always be profitable until Smart Money finds a way of trading without leaving traces (footprints) behind. Hope this helps and feel free to ask more questions.

--- 帖子 #14389 ---
Once there is a weekly close outside of an existing WCC, the next weekly candle becomes a potential WCC and is only confirmed at the end of the week. So in both cases there is no current WCC, only a potential WCC. Hope this helps. Regards Terry

--- 帖子 #14391 ---
The whole premise of stocks is to invest for future growth (buy and hold strategy) which is why they tend to trend more. However, they do go through periods of chop and slop in addition to greater than average pull backs (not to mention crashes) which, just like in forex or other trading vehicle, plays havoc on the traders' psychology. Having traded stocks, options, futures, commodities and forex, the big problem with stocks is the account size you need. Unlike forex where you can buy contracts for a fraction of their price, stocks need you to purchase the full share price. In addition, you cannot short a stock unless you own it. So Apple is $125.43/share, Amazon is $3,203.08/share, Microsoft is $245.17/share, Google is $2,294.13/share. I don't know the account size of the "average" stock trader but lets say it is $10,000. How many shares of Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Apple can they buy to increase their account? In addition, how many times do you think these stocks can double in share price? When you look deeper into the statistics of trading stocks versus forex, trading forex always produces the quickest and biggest $ % profit growth. Why do you think forex volume is $6.6 TRILLION/day compared to stocks at only $169 billion/day? Now if I had the courage to trade 100% margin on forex, as I would have to with stocks, the average DAILY $ %profit growth on forex would take YEARS to be achieved with stocks. The biggest %profit growth is in trading stock indices with a retail broker offering MT4 which I am longing to trade but unfortunately. for us US traders, there is no FTC regulated US broker. Going to a Futures broker is the same problem with stocks - account size and margin plus they don't offer MT4 meaning you have to pay monthly costs for a trading platform and data. Yes, there are many, many offshore non-regulated brokers offering indices and MT4 to US clients but having my account stolen once by these sharks keeps my money safe despite others saying they have a "trusted" offshore broker - their time will come.

--- 帖子 #14442 ---
Several reasons in addition to using REAL market volume: stocks and stock indices trend smoother and longer with the emphasis on buying (investors buy stocks for the long haul instead of chopping and changing in and out of positions - the stock market is an investment vehicle rather than just a trading instrument. Trading a single currency is easier and more profitable than a currency pair. M5 trading on forex is getting more difficult with each passing year - even London and NY can't agree on overall direction. Price Action on stocks, stock indices and futures is much more accurate and less subjective than on forex. Similarly with support, resistance, supply and demand. The big bonus for me is trading the S&amp;P, Dow, Nasdaq and Russell Indices which give a way better BANG for the buck plus it is more socially easier since NYSE opens at 6:30am my time. I had a dormant account at TD Ameritrade when I traded Options which I have now re-funded. Unfortunately their Think or Swim platform is geared towards individual stock and Options trading and contains loads of superfluous junk that I don't need which means working around their platform is difficult. Like everything else, it will be OK once I am familiar with it which, as yet, I am not.

--- 帖子 #14558 ---
A two part method I have decided to try going forward. Part 1. Set up : On the Daily . Find the swing high or swing low of the past week. Draw a line at the low of the highest price candle for a swing low or above the high of the lowest price candle for a swing high. Set a pending order to enter on price hitting the line. In this case going short on last week's highest price candle at the green line. Result.. a nice short candle move today (Monday Aug 2 ) Part 2 is on my next post.

--- 帖子 #14559 ---
Part 2 of the swing method I am trying. Set Up: Plot BaBaG's fib on the shooting star set up candle. Note in this case the set up candle was on last Friday (July 30). Closed: Today Used the green line near the 50 fib for entry and the 0 fib for exit. this was Cad/J. Took pips on Cad/J + 40 and G/J +68 using this method .

That is not how Strat defined it. In the last sentence of his post he states : A Weekly Candle remains IN Control until another Weekly Candle Closes beyond it's high or low. That is how a WCC is formed. Looking at the chart .. So the hanging man candle was In Control until the wide range candle closed beyond the hanging man's low. That price action is what confirmed the wide range candle as a new Weekly Control Candle. This allows you to draw a horizontal line across both bottom and top of the New Weekly Controlling Candle as shown projecting them into the future as they are weekly Support and Resistance indicators respectively. Those S/R indicators can be used in the following days of trading. Until a new WCC is formed. Looking at the chart the wide range candle is the WCC for the price action of the week we are currently in, ending at Friday's Aug 27 close. If this week's price action Aug 23 to 27 remains inside of the top and bottom of last week's wide range candle (between the S/R lines ) then the wide range candle continues to be the Weekly Controlling Candle. However if the price action of the current week we are in closes (on Friday) beyond the high or low of the wide range candle then our current week's price range represented by the Weekly candle becomes a new Weekly Controlling Candle with it's low and high drawn as a new support and resistance going forward into the next week. And so it goes .

Weekly Control Candle - WCC I don't have forex charts anymore to explain these examples. A Weekly Control Candle is either "In Control" or its not - there is no subjectivity or ambiguity - it is either Black or White - never a shade of gray. A WEEKLY Control Candle is "In Control" when its CLOSE is above the high of the previous WEEKLY candle or below the low of the previous WEEKLY candle. No decision on a Weekly Control Candle can be made UNTIL the Market CLOSES on Friday at 4pm NY time.

So the first candle is the WCC for each of those 3 candles. BUT THEN the Red candle happens. So we have our discussion about the wide range Red weekly candle labeled #1 . It's close is beyond the range of the the last WCC (which was the first candle in the white box). Closing beyond the range of the last WCC makes candle #1 the new WCC . The WCC status happens immediately at the end of the week on Friday. In this case it's close price is beyond the range of the last WCC which confirms it immediately as the NEW WCC . The following Green weekly candle labeled #2 did not have it's open or closed price exceed the high or low of the last WCC (the red candle) so it cannot be a new WCC. The Red candle continues to be the WCC until it's range is exceeded by the open or close of a Weekly candle in the future. When that happens, that new weekly candle is confirmed immediately and then becomes the new WCC. The fact that it's open or close at the end of the trading week was beyond the previous WCC is the confirming factor that it is the new WCC . The H and L of a WCC can be used as S/R. I hope this helps

--- 帖子 #14603 ---
I think I can see why you are questioning. It has to do with 'two candles needed to confirm' . That is true . But the two candles are the current closed candle and the last WCC candle. Try this and see if it helps with understanding: Imagine that a weekly candle has closed, let's call it candle A. Now we will look back, to the left on the chart and compare A those other candles. One of those other candles has been a WCC and is currently in control. Let's call it candle Z. Horizontal lines have been drawn on Z at it's H and L prices showing the range that it controls going forward. To determine if A is a new WCC we will be comparing the open and close of candle A to the past range lines of candle Z . So we are comparing 2 candles. One is the last WCC Z and the other is the closed current weekly candle A. So two candles are being used and compared as you say. One is the current A candle and the other is the last WCC candle Z. So we are looking back from candle A , not ahead to see if A is a new WCC. If the open or close of candle A has not exceeded the range lines of candle Z then A cannot be a new WCC . It is simply an inside bar. But If the open or close of candle A does exceed the the range lines (H or L) of candle Z then candle A has just become the new WCC. Then Candle A's high and low lines can be drawn indicating the range of price that it controls going forward in time. To summarize : Once each Weekly candle closes we look back to see if it's open or close prices have exceeded the range lines of the last WCC. If they have been exceeded then this newly closed candle becomes the WCC immediately going forward . If not the last WCC remains in control .

--- 帖子 #14604 ---
I am not changing anything Strat as taught. A single weekly candle is compared to the past Weekly Controlling candle. If the single weekly candle is inside the past WCC then it is simply an inside bar and the past WCC remains in force. But if..when compared to the last WCC we find that the single weekly candle's open or close has exceeded the range of the past WCC .... then that single weekly candle becomes the new WCC... going forward.

4 HR Breakout Experimenting on CAD/JPY. Price closed above the Green Daily Control Candle upper line. Price had crossed the 9 ema several candles earlier.. pink highlight. Employ the Fib Tool. This chart is using MT4 retracement from the chart tools. Place the ZERO line at the bottom of the candle that crossed the 9 ema . Pink highlight. It should not move. Drag the Fib Tool so the the 50 line is at the top or close of the same candle . Note grey highlight. Try and do this as soon as manageable when the breakout has occurred and price has crossed the 9 ema. NOW what you see are possible Target lines for Price . When this is done these targets will be sitting out in uncharted space. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Hi First Major ... I suggest you look at this post by Terry Dawe... 14572 since it tells a great story. He follows up with other examples in later posts. Actually the chart you referenced has turned out to be a stepping stone to where I am working now, which is still a work in progress. It is all very new.. but it fits my style Essentially .. determine a set up. I started using a breakout of the Daily Controlling Candle from the week that just ended, just as we have always drawn the weekly controlling candle WCC, I draw the DCC. When price crossed/closed the DCC look for an entry. Using the 4H charts Then Terry suggested using the 9 ema as an entry. Next apply a variation of the BaBaG Fib to get target points. Use these targets to determine if you will close, continue, add on, move the stop ... trade management decisions. What turned out using the Fib was a happy revelation that the fib lines very often aligned with other charting areas of support and resistance . 4Hr. chart.

Where is our "edge" and who is on the other side of our trades? This is zero sum, we win, somebody loses, we lose, somebody else wins. If it is the institutions / market makers who create the liquidity are on the other side, then how do we have a long term edge in the market against them? I realize what are we essentially doing is trading the trend, but if the trend is subjective, I guess I am wondering, where is the data that we can take confidence in that we truly are making +EV moves? Like if Strat (seems legit and I have no doubt he is profitable) trades 1% of his account, his equity curve would look different than if I traded the same exact same way (entires and exits same position) but only with only 0.75% of my account, his equity curve would have more drawdown. Sorry, this is not a shot at the methods of this topic, but just more of a noob trying to figure out what the numbers truly say about our trading the FX market in general

The ATR in pips is a free MT4 download. google it . I tried to copy it from my indicator file to place here ... didn't copy. A Weekly Candle remains IN Control until another Weekly Candle Closes beyond it's high or low: The WCC is analyzed after the Friday Close and before the Sunday Open . It is used for S/R by drawing horizontal lines on it's high and low going into the future. It is the BOSS for price action going forward . It remains in Control week after week until a new WCC is formed. A new WCC is formed only IF the weekly candle of the just finished week has had price CLOSE either ABOVE THE HIGH of the last WCC OR BELOW the LOW or both. A new WCC is then formed. Draw the new horizontal lines. Depending on Price Action The new WCC may last for only the next week. Or it may be in control for many weeks. Hope this helps

Look at the structure of the shadow on #1 and #2. Now look at the structure of the shadow on #3. What would make #3 have a higher probability of follow through?

Hoping to start a discussion ..... What causes the Straddle is the first consideration, and the second , can it be predicted. Some things to consider First : The Strat Shadow is a lagging indicator because it uses moving averages. Price action is controlled by the Big Boys.. banks, institutions, hedge funds and many more. So retail traders follow their footprints for direction. They do not lead. Questions to be answered : Why are the moving averages of the Strat Shadow converging (in most cases). What is happening with price to cause this convergence? Then what causes price to suddenly and strongly move in the opposite (most often) direction which identifies the Straddle move ?

Strat once said that when the 20, 41 and 72 are all INTER MINGLED , this is the CALM BEFORE THE STORM . This means that AFTER THE STRAT SHADOW has inter mingled, there "usually" a BIG MOVE which follows. The degree of the ' BIG MOVE ' is dependent on the market conditions at the time. More often than not, the Strat Shadow will be inter mingled in a horizontal position but when they inter mingle in an up or down position, they foretell the DIRECTION of the BIG MOVE.

--- 帖子 #14790 ---
Count the candles using the chart you are on. ATR10 on the 1 minute chart would be calculated using the past 10 minutes. The ATR10 value would be the average range of price of a 1 minute bar over the last 10 minutes. On the Daily chart it would be the average range in price of a daily bar over the past 10 trading days, which is 2 weeks.

Hey Sangnt0904 ... something to try and think about : Using the 4 hr chart on U/CAD you posted.... find the green candle 6 candles back from the last candle posted. It's low should be at the low red support line you drew, and the selected candle is crossed by the 9 ema and just to the right of the small red candle. Now ... using that green candle, Take a regular fib retracement tool... put the zero Fib line on the low red line . Be sure it does not move. Now stretch the tool up along the selected candle until the 50 % Fib line touches the high of that candle . So the selected candle is bracketed by the 0 fib line and the 50 fib line. Lock the fib tool at that setting. Note how price action points align with the Fibonacci tool values as time moved forward from the selected candle. Not always perfect but in my opinion a good framework for price on the 4H . What do you think ?

Just because PRICE is below the 200 ema does NOT mean sell. Remember, the 200 ema is based on what happened 200 candles ago. You are trading the NOW - what is happening NOW - not what happened 200 candles back. I don't use the 200 ema on M1 and M5 although I have it on my charts UNLESS it is acting as SUPPORT/RESISTANCE. Your trading decisions must be based on PASR and NOT on a single moving average. PRICE starts off many times below the 200 ema in an UP trend and many times above the 200 ema in a DOWN trend. Smart Money does not care where moving averages are when they are DRIVEN by fundamental factors, natural disasters, geopolitical and news events, etc. Finally, never forget that PASR does NOT trade moving averages which are LAGGING indicators - PASR uses them as a guide NOT as an entry signal. Man, this system is awesome...I doubled my demo account from $250.000 to over $500.000 in just 4 days Sorry, but I don't like to spoil your party. Demo trading does not prove either you or the method is profitable. Here on PASR, we ONLY use demo trading to prove a trader's technical understanding of PASR. The reasons for this are: 1) Demo accounts are heavily manipulated by your broker to make you look good so that you will invest and trade more money with them. 2) Demo trading is a superficial process as it does not engage the trader's mind - it is no better than playing Monopoly. 3) Demo trading with any $ amount other than the $ amount you will actually trade with is a further falsification of the results. What I recommend is to first paper trade rather than demo trade using the actual $ amount you will fund your trading account with. Better than this is to trade live with the smallest lot size your broker offers. This brings you into the REAL, LIVE world of trading as it engages your trading mind which will bombard you with emotions you never knew you had before - particularly your FEAR and GREED emotions. When you are trading LIVE at the hard right edge - you will face gremlins playing havoc with your mind and physical being. The profitability in trading does not come from the method - it comes from trading psychology - how you control your emotions (fear and greed) in the heat of the battle AT THE HARD RIGHT EDGE and then apply them with DISCIPLINE to sound Money Management principles. Time to take some prop firm challenges... It is time for you to first prove that YOU can be consistently profitable with whatever method you choose. Man, this system is awesome PASR is not a system, it is only a method. It is subjective in decision making in that the individual trader has to decide what is PRICE ACTION (PA) and what is SUPPORT &amp; RESISTANCE (SR) within the teachings of PASR. A system has a concrete set of trading rules - "do this when this happens/when you see this" etc. But again, whether it is a method or system, neither is as important as Trading Psychology and Money Management. Thank you for taking PASR for a test drive and good luck.

I started in the indicator wonderland, tried all sorts of cross-over strategies, started a small live account to practice, lost 25% of the equity there, at some point I thought I had a working crossover strategy, started a prop firm challenge, failed that one big time (it was the most nerve recking month ever!) and then I said to myself, stop, nothing is working. I tried to apply all of that on demo but I wasn't approaching it structurally or methodically. All this changed when I started reading your original thread from Feb 2009, Strat's Long Term Stress Free Trading. For the last 4 months or so, I have gone over close to 600 pages and 11.3k posts on that thread. Overtrading: I'm mindful that its a decade long thread (and extremely long one, in length), but the basics remain the same. Given that I'm limiting myself to a small account and trading the Daily's meant money management becomes extra tough and extremely crucial. Time: I have an extremely time consuming and demanding day job (which I hope to leave behind at some point). Pre-PSAR: I was checking charts in and out during office hours, after hours, while pausing for a rest after a jog, while i'm at bed when the wife has dozed off, etc etc, and overwhelming my self, but nah, not anymore. i've got 27 currency pairs on a watch list which I can do a quick check before I go to sleep in around 30 minutes and not worry about it throughout the day. I'm hoping to finish that first thread and maybe catch up in this thread and contribute. I see a lot has happened since the original thread! . I posted on February 29th #14,958 the significance of the strat shadow crossing with example of NZDJPY. I thought I would post a follow up today. I have been reviewing my statistics in an effort to improve my profit efficiency. As a result, I am tweaking my PASR style along with my findings. My first action is to change broker as, among other issues, they refused to give me A1 order book status which I have enjoyed with other brokers. The disadvantage with my new broker is that they don't have MT5 and instead have their own charting platform and data. Since I don't have the desire to learn new platforms, I will use MT5 as my trading chart and the new broker for executing trades. I have settled on M1 time frame as my M1 overall profitability is better than M5. Another change is to trade less instruments. My findings show that Euro and Dow futures are more profitable for me. My style was always to load up on one instrument instead of sharing margin between several instruments. Having a currency and stock index allows me to trade the active/volatile instrument. A surprise finding was my Money Management. Over the years, my tolerance for draw down grew less and as a result, I used a tight stop loss and draw down resulting in lots of small losers and many big wins. My strategy was to exit on any sign of weakness and get back in when strength returned but I didn't always do that. Sometimes I would be distracted and forget to get back in missing a good move while on others I would get back in and the swing/trend would reverse on me. My findings show that I would be better allowing a larger stop loss and draw down in an effort to capture more of the swing/trend. This will be a huge mental and disciplined effort for me to do this but I'm going to give it a shot. I will post charts as I get up to speed with these new tweaks to my PASR style

Something else. The ema crosses have no special power. If they did price would bounce at the crossing point every time ... just as you have raised the question. It gets pushed up and traders are drawn in going long. Then suddenly price reverses and those traders are in losses or already stopped out. This process happens over and over again in the following hours, until that pattern ceases .... have the Big Boys gone to lunch ? Also something to consider. --- 帖子 #15162 ---
Hi Strat and all veteran traders, What I have read and understand so far. The strategy of PASR (Price Action at Support and Resistance) is as follows: (Please help correct me if I understand this wrong) 1. Select Worker, Boss, Big Boss timeframes compatible with trader. Let’s say 1H, 4H, 1D. 2. Direction of 4H and 1D should be aligned. 3. Draw S/R levels on the 4H timeframe (including any swing highs and swing lows) 4. Move down to 1H timeframe and draw additional S/R levels if identified. 5. When price in 1H reaches any S/R level (and also “Strat Shadow” for more confluence), look for a. Hammer or BUOB or BUEB candles for buying opportunities (in line with the 4H and 1D trend) b. Shoot star or BEOB or BEEB candles for selling opportunities (in line with the 4H and 1D trend) 6. Enter position with a Sell Stop or Buy Stop (so momentum is in the trader’s favor). 7. Set Stop Loss at swing highs or swing lows or at major S/R. 8. Set TP level for a desirable RR ratio, also exit when Price Action tells you to do so. Writing this down is helping me summarize all the things I read in this big thread. Please forgive me if I have missed some things or got some things wrong. Also I read and accept that this strategy is only a small part of becoming a profitable trader, the harder part is trading psychology and mindset – so I will be working on that as I spend more time with the markets. Thank you again Master Strat and everyone for sharing your knowledge on this thread. Have a nice day/night. Iris.

--- 帖子 #15192 ---
Good job for doing the exercise for so long. As you can see it is simple but not easy. That thing you did for simplicity (keeping 1:1 RR) could skew the result. Trading is simple but we should not do it too simple and trade like robots. The second most important thing after cutting loses short is letting profits run, which is really hard. It is good to lock in profits (avoiding being stopped out at loss or BE) but we need to be open to scenario that our trade will go ad infinitum in the right direction ( RR 1: ∞ ) Try maybe the same exercise but close the trade when you will see reversal candle, not at automatically at 1:1. Base your exit on PA, in the same way you do with entry. Trail TP behind the price using D1 candles. When the candle finishes get TP under the low/above the high of the candle. See if it changes anything. You can also try splitting the position in two parts, from which one you TP at 1:1 and TP for the second one you trail as I described above.

--- 帖子 #15196 ---
1. Select Worker, Boss, Big Boss time frames compatible with trader. Let’s say 1H, 4H, 1D. NO. You must practice on D1, W1 and M1 until you can consistently identify SR across those time frames 3. Draw S/R levels on the 4H time frame (including any swing highs and swing lows) NO. Identify and draw SR on ALL time frames. Go back and re-read the exercises on identifying SR. 4. Move down to 1H timeframe and draw additional S/R levels if identified. NO. Not until you have mastered D1, W1 and M1. 5. When price in 1H reaches any S/R level (and also “Strat Shadow” for more confluence), look for a. Hammer or BUOB or BUEB candles for buying opportunities (in line with the 4H and 1D trend) b. Shoot star or BEOB or BEEB candles for selling opportunities (in line with the 4H and 1D trend) NO, ABSOLUTELY NOT! Trading is not a "paint by numbers" activity - if it was this easy, everyone would be $Gazillionaires! 7. Set Stop Loss at swing highs or swing lows or at major S/R. NO. When you identify a Set Up/Trade, the VERY FIRST THING you do is identify how much you will lose if the Market goes 100% AGAINST you. Set TP level for a desirable RR ratio, NO. The Market/Smart Money does not have or know ""desirable RR ratio"", so why would you? We trade from PASR Set Up to PASR Exit. Iris, what you did was good for where you are on the FIRST STEP of THE PATH. You have a long, long way to go BUT it will get easier as you read, study and understand. Then, your learning will increase as you start to trade.

Hi The important SR is monthly&gt; weekly&gt; daily and so on. The biger the timeframe the stronger an SR might be. after you mark them fine tune them. most of those are not worth having on the chart. Some SR on the daily 3 years back might not be at all important, unless it happens to be a monthly. Start removing some that dont make sense on the weekly/monthly. and then you just need to watch the ONE above current price and the ONE below. I dont trade the daily charts , so I dont have much experience with all of PASR. The method and PA works on all timeframes not matter what though

Hey Strat Great thread! Just want to ask why you trade futures? In my experience, the cost of trading is larger when fees and spread are taken into account (as opposed to spot/cfd brokers like peperstone). But I guess you have your reasons so please share. Thanks

--- 帖子 #15209 ---
In my experience, the cost of trading is larger when fees and spread are taken into account (as opposed to spot/cfd brokers like peperstone). This used to be the case when Futures/Commodity trading was only for those with big trading accounts. These days, Futures trading is very competitive with the introduction of micro and mini futures on most instruments. My cost of trading Futures including commissions, Exchange Fees and NFA Fees is significantly less than that for Forex. My main reason though is that I used to drive myself crazy trying to find the Forex pair which was moving/volatile - many times I ended up on the wrong horse. With Futures, there is always action on the indices and major currencies.

DAX M1 On 10.06.2022 I traded New York session on DAX index. When I started observing market it started to make HH and HL. It turned out to be channel range trading. Attached Image (click to enlarge) 1. Seeing but not believing what this bullish Saddle candle is telling me. This was actually the second one showing what would be next bigger move. 2. Last call to enter bullish train. Candle piercing through Strat Shadow and entering M5 Strat Shadow. 3. The market went into small range and showed strenght on the seconed test of static support. Pulled the trigger - entered long but closed at BE after bearish OB. 4. Now I see third strong reaction to the support and I see that the price is at TL, price piercing Strat Shadow again. Nice confluence I think and I'm sure we are going north but I fail to pull the trigger because of few misclicks in a row (most of the time I want to enter with buy stop order). That was really frustrating to see market moving away in the right direction without me but I decided that I WILL NOT CHASE THE MARKET. 5. Great opportunity to enter long. Price at static support, dynamic support of 100 MA, moving out of Strat's Shadow 6. Risky short. Price moving out of Strat Shadow but TL was very close and I decided to close very near TL. In my experience prices makes almost always a small wobble at TL before breaking it, so I was expecting some reaction and it did come quite strongly. Attached Image (click to enlarge) 7. I decided to enter long when the price closed above Strat Shadow, it was also above static support. I said to myself I will not close as long as we are above 20. I exepected the price to visit channel's upper TL and M5 72 EMA. 8. After the test of the lower TL (where I started to think about going short) the price showed strenght again, so I entered long again. Unfortunately big bearish candle at static resistance and M5 72 EMA made me close this trade pretty soon. 9. After the market made LH and showed two big bearish candles I decided to enter short. Price went into both Strat Shadows (M1 and M5). I thought hmm maybe this is it and we will finally break lower TL of the channel. NO - she was not ready yet. But that's ok because she told me that with bullish hammerish candle, so I could jump out just in time just before the next rally. 10. Ok, if not short, not this way, maybe you want to go once again to the upper TL. I decided to go long, unfortunately because of misclicking I entered late and it looks like FOMO trade. It ended with small profit, because as it turned out later NOW she was ready. Unfortunately I stopped watching DAX just after this trade was closed, so I missed breaking of TL, which was touched 9 times before giving in at 10. The thing is that I missed almost all the trend move from the morning and when I returned it was over and wanted it to continue... So, whether you know it or not, you exhibited FOMO - FEAR OF MISSING OUT - your FIRST MISTAKE. Usually, but not always, after a strong trend, particularly in a previous session (London), the Market gets tired and stale and goes into consolidation/range. The following session (NY) "smart money" often waits for the Market to "settle down" before making their move. The CHOP &amp; SLOP is often we retail traders trading against each other. I have never been successful trading breakouts of any sort without having some sort of confluence present. Until you have the experience, before trading, ALWAYS check the next higher time frame to get the "bigger picture" view. Had you done this (on M5)and marked it up as I have done, the consolidation/range would start showing up like a "SORE THUMB"! At Globex Open (5:30am NY), the consolidation/range is already evident by observing: SR FLAT and HORIZONTAL Strat Shadow Long WICKS and long TAILS Unless you are a consistently profitable scalper on M1, you WAIT until there is a CLOSE below/above SR. To avoid the dreaded "fake out", WAIT for a retest of that SR and trade PA. You also might want to switch to trading M5 instead of M1 - I find it hard to trade EURO on M1 unless there is a rip roaring trend. --- 帖子 #15333 ---
And a lost trade by pip,my SL was wrong. No, your TRADE MANAGEMENT is wrong! First, are you giving this trade your 100% attention? If not you should! Taking a full hit on your SL is a fool's game promoted by the self acclaimed experts and gurus. To maximise your profits and become consistently profitable you must pay attention to PRICE ACTION and what Smart Money is doing and get out when PRICE ACTION tells you to - consider your SL as an Emergency Stop not as part of your managing your trade. Look at the yellow line A-A I have drawn on your chart. At the left "A", PRICE has made an attempt to go higher but cannot CLOSE above the candle below "A". Buyers continue to buy but cannot close above the yellow A-A line and Sellers drive them down to point "C". Here, the buyers come back and drive PRICE up to, and then with a CLOSE above line A-A shown by line B-B. This tells you the buyers are stronger than the sellers and is where you should get out. If you missed that chance to exit, PRICE drops a little then continues up to CLOSE above line B-B - this is your last chance saloon if you were not already out. The Sellers then step in and take control and push PRICE lower until they reach interim support at "D". Finally they CLOSE below support at "D" at which point you could enter a short recognising there is support at Line C-C. You could then enter on the candle CLOSING below Line C-C. In summary, you have to SEE BEYOND THE CANDLES and take in the whole picture and try and get into the minds of the Sellers and Buyers - hard to do but like everything else, gets better with experience. Hi Things cant go south if you can manage to not lose money. Just close the trade when you think its over and dont let a winning trade go against you (trend or counter trend doesnt really matter). So work with that and you will get used to identify which SR might be relevant for your timeframe.

Hi All I have been working hard, trying to get a better understanding of reading price, and learning to SEE beyond the candles I did some analysis this morning of my thoughts on some recent price action on the EUR USD chart (daily) I would love your input, maybe we could ALL use this as a learning opportunity... Attached Image (click to enlarge) Price hits support, counter trend traders come in here, and go long with there stop losses placed below the swing low Price forms a double bottom, more counter trend traders accumulate with long positions, stop losses below the swing low at a similar point to (1) Price eventually breaks to the downside taking out the stop losses of the long traders from points 1 &amp; 2. There would also be a large amount of sell stop orders here, for traders shorting the break out. All of this supply results in a large red candle. There is most likely still a big accumulation of sell orders at the breakout for those short traders who never got filled on the break out. This is visible to us whenever price returns to the supply area at (4) we see upper wicks/ rejection over and over again, whenever price attempts to penetrate the supply Eventually price breaks higher where it is met by more short orders (this is at about the price of the breakout) finally filling some of those traders who never got filled initially. Eventually We get price action in the form of a BEEB which is our opportunity to go short with a very low risk trade in the direction of the overall trend and a bunch of supply above us Note point 5 could also be seen by some as a liquidity sweep by the big boys wanting to go short. This a different theory to the one described above however both are seen as bearish... (which is fine by us)

--- 帖子 #15691 ---
Another way to look at this, is to determine which pair is the "cheapest" to trade... By cheapest, I mean what percentage the spread is of ATR ie lets say you have two pairs... pair 1: ATR of 100, spread of 3 pips = (3 % of ATR) pair 2: ATR of 90, spread of 1 pip = (1.1 % of ATR) yes, pair 1 may move more... however if you factor spread, maybe pair 2 is a better option? (especially if your trading the 5 minute!)

Morning. I try to trade what I see on m1. Not necessarily in the direction of higher timeframes, but its nice to have everything aligned. Ideally if you can manage to trade in the direction of higher timeframes you will have bigger profits , as long as you know how to manage staying in the trade (there will be big pullbacks along the way). I use m1 m5 h1 and the daily as well. My exits are usually at areas where I think there could be some SR my losses are for many reasons. primarily psychological, tight stops, taking a trade too fast without considering some aspects (like the one you mentioned) By the way, it is ok to try to get a plan going how to pick your spots to take a trade, and figuring out rules for that. BUT that part is like 1% of the whole process. 99% of the work is AFTER you put on a trade and what happens next. All you have to figure out before placing a trade is : how much you want to lose (risk) if conditions apply for you to enter (edge) Once you are in the trade it is a whole different story

Some say you can't just use the Strat Shadow but I try to use less and less other things including fibs, BRNs etc. I found that I was always adding all these things and it just made it more confusing with the cluttered chart, making it for a more difficult decision as to which way to trade. So using the SS, here is an example of how I use it. This is an example of the recent condition on the GBPUSD. Once the shadow gets to its maximum divergence I draw a box from the top to the bottom. As new candles are formed and the shadow is converging I shrink the box. Continue with this until a PA signal is formed providing a potential trade. In this case on the H4 the gray horizontal line is the worker 9ema while it was remaining flat for four days. The PA signal showed up in the form of the bullish candle marked with the arrow.

Good morning! You are doing good, bistolis. You are just going through the process of applying your mental psyche to your understanding of PASR. You will, and are improving with trade and screen time. FOMO is the Achilles Heel for all traders especially newbies and get rich quick idiots. Letting missed trades and opportunities go is just a discipline you have to acquire. Do not chase missed trades and opportunities, just let them go - there is ALWAYS another trade being set up later. Make sure you are comfortable with your position and SL criteria. Focus on candles - how they are formed, how fast they move, how they close, how they open etc - this is getting yourself in tune with those moving PRICE. Choose and focus on one time frame until you have mastered it and are consistently profitable before switching about. Act quickly on what you SEE and not on what your Little People are telling you. Remember no-one gets it right all the time, just take the losses on your chin and look for the next set up - make sure you don't let losses be personal - that is, affect your trading psyche. Thanks for posting

All these sell orders provide liquidity to the smart money to exit there shorts (buy back) The shorts are absorbed and as a result, price fails to close below the swing point Shorts are now trapped and price makes an aggressive move higher as their stops are hit on the way up (4) Long story short - is that smart money know where all the orders are likely to be. Fridays high is at (7) where the big candle reacted from In hindsight - the price action in the yellow box, marked at (6) gave us a clue that price was going to make a move higher The first candle breaks support (just) but fails to close below it The second candle makes a new low, but again, fails to close below support The third candle makes a new low once again, but also fails to close below support That's 3 strikes Sir! If I loose or gain I will loose or gain trading one instrument with strategy as finely tuned to it as I am able to tune it(construct it), taking into it all perceived particulars of a given instrument. There is difference between trading and investing. Trading does not demand many different instruments to spread the risk. Strat what a great choice of the Christmas song!
