The Weekly Control Candle was developed by me on THIS THREAD so if you take the time to read it you will find more information on it. I regret I am unable to explain in detail here as that would be unfair to subscribers of www.stratsforextrading.com where we have a separate thread discussing this in great detail. Our first 4 STAR trader then took the Weekly Control Candle and used it to filter out false swings. 2. Can you post 10 charts analyses/signal with SL/TP price (which will forecast price will moves in the future)? NO! There is NO TRADER currently living or in the past who can/could forecast PRICE into the future. All we can do is base our trades on what we SEE happening NOW . What we have NO CONTROL over is EXTERNAL FORCES . As an example, we can have everything, including the stars, all lined up for a Classic 5 STAR PASR (highest probability of success) trade and then War breaks out somewhere, or Nature inflicts deadly damage (Tsunami, Hurricane, Tornado etc) or a country makes a drastic change to its interest rate or, what happens when you least expect it, a major Bank intervenes and our Stop Loss is immediately hit. Dr Joe and Trends Thank you for the PMs on indicators and price action. Rather than answer individually, I will do it through this post, if I may. I’m not here to fight with anyone over whether to use indicators or not for we have a larger fight with the market makers than amongst us little guys. I respect the traders who can make consistent profits with indicators as it is something I have tried and cannot do. If anyone has an indicator that produces CONSISTENT profits then, please, show us the way. In the meantime, I will continue with what works for me: raw price action using price, S&amp;R, momentum, exhaustion, cycles, time, harmonic analysis, market sentiment with a splash of funny mentals thrown in. With regard to my transition from having indicators up the ying yang on my charts to now with just my Strat Shadow, I need to share my experience with an old time trader, Dr. Joe , which will also show how stubborn I was. Back in the early 90s when I was getting really serious with my trading, I was buying signals via fax. In those days there was no email and no computer trading and we had to either plot our own charts or buy them from a charting service. We then had to calculate our own indicators and then hand draw them on our charts. This really helped in understanding what indicators did (take the data from “n” days ago), how they worked and more importantly, what they didn't do. One time I faxed my questions back to the signal service and the reply I got back was that I had sent it to the wrong number. Also written on my fax was that I was wasting my money on signals and to contact Dr. Joe. After a few fax exchanges, he sent a handwritten fax saying something like “trading is easy, you don’t need nuthin fancy (he was a good old Texas boy) just buy when it’s going up and sell when it’s going down, that’s all there is to it”. Dr. Joe used to work for NASA as a nuclear physicist on the Space Program and was a Professor , PhD with just about every physics and maths qualifications there are or you could think of. He got fed up of the bureaucracy and politics at NASA and as a part time investor in stocks , decided to go full time as, in his own words, “the price cycles are just some sort of fancy sine waves with decay and acceleration distorting them and should be real easy to plot and forecast.” Well after over 5 years doing triple integrated, double differentiated Fourier transforms, harmonic frequency analysis, fractal filters and theorems and goodness knows what else that, although I have a PhD, just ran circles around me. He said he got so frustrated that although he could plan and predict space craft trajectories, orbits, landings etc, he could not forecast even one bar of prices into the future . Not one to quit, he decided that there was some external force that he was not taking into consideration and the only place it could be was on the trading floor where the action took place. Through his connections, he eventually got an invitation to the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) and was shown the futures or commodities pit (can’t remember which). His sole purpose of going there was as a spy or detective to find out exactly how things worked so that he could write it into his software. He told me he was “amazed and dumbfounded ” at what he saw and heard which forever changed his life. (I had all this written up in my trading notes in my files but I can’t find them so I’m using this post to “replenish my notes”). He arrived at the pit before opening time and saw all the floor traders congregated together in a meeting. He saw this as strange as he thought they were out and out competitors with each other. What he saw in the first 15 to 30 minutes he would never have believed even if his best friend had told him. At the open, the overnight trades, which were long positions, were put through but he detected the traders entering them were giving signals to the other traders. After the orders were put through there was “ nothing ” – they just waited to see how the market reacted to those orders. He then observed what he thought were illegal practices but later learned it to be what actually goes on each and every day. During this “dead” time, the floor traders were reviewing their orders in the pipeline and then on a given signal, a group started selling followed by another group. Then when a certain lower price had been reached, another signal was given and the same groups then bought back amongst themselves. He later learned this was called “Running the Stops” and what they had done was found out where all the orders were, which were below lows, swing lows and elsewhere, and just driven the price down to fill them and take them out so that they had a clean order sheet! Not satisfied with that, they then collectively took the price back to where it opened! After this and now with the market moving, orders started to come in and when a large order came in from a bank, fund or other large institution, the trader with the order gave a signal before entering it. After entering it, the traders went quiet again . They were looking to see how the market reacted to that order. When they saw more buy orders coming in, they just bought more and more and kept on buying until a signal from a trader that he had a large sell order. Again the sell order was entered and the traders went quiet as they waited for a reaction from the market . He learned that the floor traders were waiting to see whether the sell order was going to be accepted as profit taking or full blown shorting. He said this went on all day long with the floor traders just “piggy-backing” on which ever way the market moved. He said he could see no skills or qualifications (other than being a whore – a very rich whore, he said) whatsoever in what the floor traders did. On his way back to Houston, he thought about how to use what he witnessed to HIS advantage. His first action was to throw out all his indicators, forecasts and technical analysis. He told me that there is no analysis, indicator or other program now or in the future, that can analyse or predict human behaviour and specifically, human emotions . He had seen for himself that there was nothing technical or logical in how the floor traders (now better known as Market Movers) traded and therefore any analysis or thinking from “off the floor” was an absolute waste of time. His second action was how to beat “those whores” on the floor as he called them. He said he thought over just about every scenario imaginable and just as he was running out of ideas, it came to him. If you can’t beat, them join them although as a very devout and God fearing Christian, he didn’t think it was ethical. Unable to find another alternative, he decided he had no options left but to try and do, “off the floor” what they did on the floor. From this came his very simple method: Buy when it goes up and sell when it goes down. He went on to make $millions doing this and I subsequently learned he passed away a very rich and contented man knowing that he had beaten the “whores” at their own game. I learned all this in a few telephone conversations with him but he lost his patience with me when I still questioned his method. He wouldn’t answer my calls so I reverted back to faxes. Again, I can’t remember it word for word but I sent a simple fax saying: “How do you know when to stop buying?” On the same fax was his handwritten reply, “When it stops going up.” So I wrote on it, “How do you know when it stops going up?” His handwritten reply, “When it starts going down.” So I wrote on it, “How do you know when it stops going up and starts going down?” His handwritten reply, “When people start selling.” After going round like this in riddles, I pleaded with him to “just give it to me straight”. He sent a fax saying this would be his last communication with me and that if I didn’t understand how to buy when it goes up and sell when it goes down, I had no business trading. His final paragraph was one which I ignored, like everything else he told me, until a couple of years ago when I realized what a dumb, stupid, arrogant, stubborn idiot I had been: He said I would only be wrong twice using his simple method: “Once when you buy at the top and once when you sell at the bottom.” I just ignored this as a smart – ass answer but still tried to do what he said. Unfortunately, and as Sod’s law dictates, I tried to do it in a consolidation and lost on every trade which had me buying when I should have been selling etc. I tried and lost again and then eventually lost my way in the quest for the Holy Grail in Indicator Land. Now, with all my experience and thousands of lost $ behind me, the light came on! My understanding of what he was telling me is this: Buy when prices are moving up. Buy each retrace/dip. Keep buying until the last retrace becomes a trend change which is the one trade you lose on. Sell when prices are moving down. Sell each retrace/rally. Keep selling until the last retrace becomes a trend change which is the second trade you lose on . I have not traded like this as I have my own method/style now but on the look backs I have done it works very well. Obviously, the trendier the price, the better it works. In my later communications with other floor traders, I told them about Dr. Joe and what he told me, and asked them if it was true. As you would expect, each and everyone vehemently rejected it as absolute rubbish. Sometimes I wonder if old Dr. Joe was smoking something but then when I see those long legged neutral dojis before a significant move , I know he was right. Thank you, Dr. Joe Rock n Roll, Strat

Post 10,791 Quote Mar 19, 2010 6:51pm https://assets.faireconomy.media/nfs...ar94837_23.gif Strat Joined Feb 2009 | Status: 13 YEAR PASR THREAD Senior Member | 11,570 Posts Earlier this week I was on a plane sat across the aisle from a Chinese guy who was reading some trading magazine. He studied each price chart and I watched him use his finger to follow price up and down the chart. As he stopped at each swing high and low he would say “Ah so”. He would then put the magazine down and talk to himself and after 15 minutes or so go through the same routine again as if he was testing himself. After watching him do this for a couple of hours I leaned over and said to him that it isn’t as easy as it looks, is it? He said “Oh no, it very easy”. Acting dumb I said I thought most people lost money trading but he said “Maybe, but for me it very easy”. Intrigued, I asked him why it was easy for him. He showed me a price chart in the magazine and started at the bottom left swing low and said “Buy here”. He then went to the swing high and said “Sell here” and proceeded to do this all the way up to the top. I told him anyone can do that looking at what has happened with price in the past, the trick is being able to do it in real time. He said “It still very easy”. Taking the bait I asked him what he would do at the top. He moved his finger down to the previous swing low and said, “ Easy, I buy here so up there, I sell”. Still trying to tell him that it had already happened, I asked him what he would do at the end of the chart, the extreme right. He moved his finger to the last swing high and said “Easy, I sell there so I buy here”. Now really intrigued I said that the left side of the chart looked like prices were going higher all the time but then they reached a top where the prices started going down and how would he know what to do. He said, “It very easy”. He then put his arm in the middle of the price chart dividing the uptrend from the downtrend. He pointed to the left side (up trend) and said, “This climbing mountain” and pointing to the right side (down trend) said, “This falling down mountain”. Again I told him it was easy to see as it had already happened and how would he know what to do at the top. He said, “I just do same thing, buy, sell, buy, sell”. I told him that if he bought at the top, he would lose money but he said, “No, instead of buy, sell, buy, sell, I sell, buy, sell, buy”. No longer needing to act dumb, I told him I didn’t understand. He said, “You not understand, I just found God gave me very special talent to understand trading”. Still trying to understand, I asked how he knew on the left side of the chart he had to “climb the mountain” and on the right side “fall down the mountain”. He said, “It very easy for me but you not understand I try explain. Climbing mountain, more buy, less sell. Falling down mountain, more sell, less buy.” {{This, in very simple terms, is impulse wave (more buy) and corrective wave (less sell) and vice versa for down trend.}} I asked how he knew this and he said, “I just found I have very special talent for this”. Apparently he had never seen anything about trading before and “something made him buy trading magazine in book store”. At this point, a very eerie feeling came across me. Was I sat across from the reincarnation of Dr. Joe, or R.N. Elliott, or W.D. Gann or Charles Dow? Knowing that many Chinese believe in the after life, I jokingly asked if he was a Chief Trader in his former life. He said, “Oh no, I was ant in past life and not live long but I was “good” ant and this is God’s reward”. I said he must be very wealthy from trading; he said, “I never trade, I not know I know this but when I get back I get $50,000 from family and friends and make million dollar for them”. I didn’t know whether to laugh or cry. As we were waiting to get off the plane I wished him luck with his trading, he said, “I not need luck, I have very special talent to make money trading”. Then finally I said maybe we will meet again on another flight and he will tell me about his trading, he said, “Next time I fly, will be on private jet”. Not knowing whether I had met an idiot or the next George Soros, I couldn’t get what he told me out of my mind and since then, have been waking up in the early hours of the morning with everything he told me on my mind. I really thought I had brought my trading down to its simplest form but after this I’m not sure anymore.

Happy new year to all. I had trouble "emptying" my mind from everything I knew or thought I knew. Just watching the chart (only one now). It is still hard to just watch the numbers change , the candles dance around until they "lock" in place, and literally meditating to have an empty mind and not allowing my thoughts to start analyzing what is happening. To just watch and observe and then making a decision ONLY when the trade presents itself is very difficult but pays off immensely (or I pay abit when I get it wrong). I am not always able to be patient and wait until there is a trade of course. I am still learning how to trade and what I found out so far is that an entry is not so important (although it is nice to have a tight stop and good price). I was always uncomfortable to have a trade on the chart and that had an impact on my results. I was not adding to the trade when the market moved the way I wanted. I wasn't accepting the fact that I would NEVER know how price would move after I put the trade. I was not patient to wait for the next one around if I missed one entry. I took profit way too soon many times. So I went back to basics and tried to rectify my shortcomings (mental) as best I could I FORCED myself to add more to the trade once it started moving my way. There is absolutely no reason not to add once market tells you that you are RIGHT this time. And NEVER adding once the trade was going nowhere or moving against me, just taking it off the chart no matter how small the loss or profit. Once I had my trade I was moving back (physically) taking a few good breaths . And then accepting the fact that this could move ANYWHERE up or down, and since I dont know why not just accept the fact the probably I am wrong and make it easier psychologically. When I miss a trade or get a loss, instead of chasing price (and get more losses) I would force myself to sit tight and wait (as long as it takes even if it is until the next day) and since I dont have a trade on to just watch and observe how price moves (how fast, where it stalls etc and take notes that might be useful at some point). Once I had the trade moving my way, I would literally sit on my hands and watch. The possible targets would have been spotted in advance (like recent highs lows or other areas of price where it MIGHT be a good idea to exit). Most importantly though I would watch and let the market SHOW me if I should exit. And if I did I would go back to watching price to find the NEXT trade. Done is done and review will be done at the end of the day. One thing of advice to people that are really serious about trading is this: I am NEVER EVER comfortable having a trade on, and I don't know if it just me (probably not) but I accepted the fact and I am just trying to think about process and execution. And don't expect to learn much just reading posts or books. You will NEVER learn anything if you don't actually trade and experience having money at risk with your every decision. No matter how much you read it will not change the fact that you ARE going to make the same stupid mistakes that EVERYBODY is doing from time to time (if not every time). Once I read in a book that trading is a profession where the lessons come only after the test. Now I know how true that is. And if I may add that it is up to me to go looking for that lesson even if it means I need to doubt everything I know and do every day. If I am not willing to commit to the process of learning, then chances are I will never succeed in trading. (I could write a whole book but there are so many good ones that it would be almost a waste of my time)

Good day everyone. It's been a very long time since I last posted in this thread (actually it was the old one). I would like to share my analysis of a pair: NZDCHF I'm very rusted, but after reading and studying once again Strat's teaching, I would like to give it a go. On the Monthly, the trend is down. Lower highs and lower lows (dark green triangles) with a negative Strat Shadow and all EMAs in the right order. Currently we are in a pullback so any trade long would be counter-trend on the monthly (Big Boss). To be on a safer side, a trader could wait for a confirmed swing high to trade short, which is the direction of the overall trend. The black horizontal lines are major SR from the Big Boss and Boss charts. The horizontal lines in dark green, green and pale green indicate that if price closes below them, it will make a swing high confirmation on its respective chart. So, if price closes below 5713 a swing is confirmed to the downside on the Monthly. Same on the Weekly for 5843. On the Weekly, price is making higher highs and higher lows (green triangles), in line with the Monthly chart current pullback. SS is negative and price closed precisely at the 20 EMA last week. For me a swing is confirmed when the Control Candle is broken (1) and not when the candle gets broken (2). Perhaps not the best thing to do that's why on the Weekly it shows an unconfirmed swing high in place. On the Daily, price shows higher highs and higher lows (Pale green triangles). SS has shrunk and is compress now with small candles (dojis) for the past 2 weeks. On friday a Strat Straddle to the upside appeared. Today's candle so far shows long momentum. One could trade long following the signal from the Strat Straddle with a low risk placing the SL below the last swing low. That's it. Thank you everyone and get well soon Strat.

--- 帖子 #16051 ---
M5 EURO Trading during low volume and volatility with US Market closed is a great way to hone PASR and trading skills. My opening trade went straight into draw down testing my maximum draw down limit yet not being able to close below it. Subsequent PA led me to believe that London was building a base/launching pad for higher PRICES. Patience paid off (as it always does) with being able to close in profit at the confluence of SR and the down trend line. The second trade was much the same off the same base but again stalled at the same confluence of SR and the down trend line indicating to me that London had no real interest in taking PRICE higher and was going into a range bouncing up and down over what would have been US Open PRICE. Range trading is ideal for Basic PASR. I missed the CLOSE below the Market Open for my third trade and instead waited for a CLOSE below the up trend line. The trade was closed as soon as PRICE was rejected from the latest SR which was creating a higher low. I did not take the next long Basic PASR trade when it closed over the Market Open since it was only 15 minutes to London CLOSE at 4pm however it would have been another profitable Basic PASR trade. All in all, 110 points on low volume and volatility is not bad. The downside is the torment and anguish I went through for 40 minutes nursing my opening trade. The state of mind (trading psychology) on my opening trade is very important for me. A profitable opening trade sets me up in a positive state of mind for the rest of my morning while an opening losing trade puts me in a dark place. The low volume and volatility with no US Market put me into conservative mode, only trading one fifth my normal position size and no add ons. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #16079 ---
Same chart, better explanation (I hope): I used dark green color for marks on the Big Boss, Green for the Boss and Pale green on the Worker. Black horizontal lines are my SR lines from Big Boss and Boss. Before I enter a trade on the Worker, I always make sure I'm in alignment with the Boss direction. Pretty much like using PASR for Swing Trading, in this case from the Boss swing high to the Boss swing low. Once price breaks and closes below the green horizontal line on the Boss, the swing high is confirmed. This happened on the Worker after the close below the 72EMA (black arrow). &lt;&lt;Boss Check&gt;&gt; From here, I wait for 2 things: PA being supported by a negative Strat Shadow and LL-HL-LL. As price continues the SS goes from positive to negative (crossover). Now I wait for price to give me a signal to enter, in this case it gave me a doji and red bar which became a BEEB. &lt;&lt;Worker Check&gt;&gt; However, price is hovering above the support line and my Big Boss swing high confirmation line. In my short experience, I've seen price bounce from the Monthly Control Candle many times when everything was telling me to enter a trade. So I decided to wait one more candle to enter short and this next red candle that appeared broke both lines. I know my Bog Boss Swing High is not confirmed yet, but momentum is on my side. The problem with waiting for all lights to go green is that by then the move went almost all the way without me (as usual, it's a trade-off). &lt;&lt;Big Boss Check&gt;&gt; SL: Above BEEB TP1: 1st Support line (1st purple cross). TP2: Reversal pattern to the upside (2nd purple cross). I moved my SL above the hammer when TP1 got hit, but price kept on going down. Hope it's clearer. Cheers.

I usually enter the initial trade on M1/M2 and then manage it looking on additional TF like M5 and M15/M30. Time to slow down (the Big Boss says!) Since I am addicted to trading and have a really good understanding of PASR, I end up trading up and down M1 with and against the immediate trend which has been profitable but sometimes stressful. As I am advancing in years (75 in June), the Big Boss has already noticed me slowing down in other areas and suggests I give up trading before I wear myself out. Giving up trading for me would be like chopping my head off so I have agreed to slow down and spend less time in front of the one eyed monster. To do this I am forcing myself to only trade M5 and only in the direction of the immediate trend - no more counter trend trading. My statistics show that I am 19% to 26% less profitable on M5 but to offset that, I am changing my money management to trade larger positions, more add-ons and try and tolerate more draw down. Today was my first day doing this. Although M5 is SO SLOW it is less stressful but leaves me with 4 to 41/2 minutes of waiting time before the candle closes. During this period, I have time to make a cup of tea and a sandwich, read the News, Football latest and let the dog out and still be bored! It occurred to me that I have time to trade another instrument in this "dead" time so from now on, I will be trading M5 Euro and M5 Dow concurrently. PA was slow today on both instruments and I had to force myself not to look at M1. Trading a different account to my charting account presents a co-ordination problem as I found out this morning. As my set up occurred, I clicked "Buy" on my trading account to enter long based on my charting account only to watch RED P&amp;L figures when PRICE was going up. Straightaway, I knew that I had forgotten to change the instrument and quantities on my trading account before entering. Fortunately, I caught it in time so little monetary damage was done. Until, I get it ingrained into my memory, I have a Post It Note on my screen telling me to switch trading accounts! M5 EURO Attached Image (click to enlarge) M5 DOW Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Don't you wait for the candle to close? That is a good question, yes I normally wait for the candle to close, and my impatience assisted me greatly in taking this premature short entry. Have also taken the possibility that there might have been a double top below the pivot, and yes there was the automatic risk of a full gap closure, which indeed has happened and have added shorts from there. It is not only the candle closure that is important but also what immediately follows, and after taking that initial entry I got out of the position when the damage or profit is aligned with PA as it happens. I would not recommend taking short in that exact spot, before the candle close! In retrospect I have had a blind spot. Have ended that trade with a small profit, but yes a wasted situation. Got another short from below the Daily Pivot Do you find the Daily Pivots helpful? I find Daily Pivots very useful, and I use mid daily pivots which are very important to me. Attached Image (click to enlarge) First I use the Daily pivot itself as an important zone which is usually hit within few days, those that have not been reached are indicated on one of my charts, usually M30 or on higher TF, and I use that type of a "gap" as waiting to be filled. Usually clearly identified trend on M15 or M30 is enough to be a good aid, though occasionally it takes much longer. This is my observation on DOW only. Yellow horizontal lines are the D Pivots. The pivot indicator I use draws pivot on Sunday, when markets open late in the evening, Please ignore that pivot line when there are two pivot lines to one trading day. This chart is M30 zoomed out, the large candles indicate NYSE session, Daily pivots yellow lines indicate 24H daily TF. There is a bit more on that subject in my journal, the indicator I use atm is OGT Pivot Points Indicator v1.2 The yellow pivot line continues until the PA hits it, please observe, and make your own decision if it is of any use to your trading approach. Trading DOW cash future for intraday and scalping and DOW Quarterly future for trades lasting much longer makes sense, there are no overnight charges on the leverage charged when trading Quarterly futures,as long as the trade is closed within the quarter, but please check it with your particular trading platform. Mid Daily Pivots points are of great use to me, often there are days that can be named mS2/Pivot, like last Monday, often the PA is contained in between the mid pivots levels, like mS1 to mR1 and so on. It is not a hard rule, but it causes me to take more attention of PA around these zones. Particular bar formations are of paramount importance and when they happen around these pivot zones they provide kind of a confluence. They might be compared to a MA, but nothing is automated, every situation has to be confirmed by PA. I don't consider what happened prior to NYSE Open anymore as I find the US Session very fickle and only trade what I see on my charts. Absolutely right, PA at times is very fickle. If DOW or any other index opened on the level it closed the previous session there will not be any gaps. But there are gaps, at time big gaps in excess of 1% of the total index price. From London Open to NYSE Open there is six and half hours. During that time the price of DOW futures is all over the place, at times more than 1%, that is in execs of 300 points, though more often between 100 to 200 points. DAX follows DOW or NASDAQ during that time, so the PA of US Indices at that time must be important to make DAX to follow it. More often that not the PA at that time presents a low hanging fruit ready to be picked up. One has to make sure this fruit so nice and ready to be picked up is not the fruit from the forbitten tree. There is much more to investigate and organise the observation/s in relation to that. Living in the UK also makes it more visible to take this PA into account solely due to the Time zone reality. Sorry for a partial answers, Thank you for taking care and posting. Pleased that you must be filling better, and wish you to make all the adjustments making life easier.

--- 帖子 #16121 ---
It might well be that seeing the PA particular patterns and acting on them is more important that solely the issue of a TFs. There are different expectation regarding PT and trade duration according to the TF one uses as a primary TF. Observing myself, however much I would like to say that I am calm and constant in my emotional/psycho state considering trading, and that I am in a constant and always in a state of well balanced readiness to risk management, to say that it would be a lie. But that is not bad, however it is tragic to deny it and avoid to recognise it. I have to go on with what is given, or what is there. There are days that I am ready to take and manage bigger risk, and there are days that I am less ready to do so, subjective, yes it is, especially for intra day trading just as profit/loss is objective. I rationalise risk factor for intra day differently that for trades that last days if not weeks. When there are difficult thought on my mind, I am less prepared for shorter TF risk management. One of my friends used to be a well known trader in the City of London during 80ties early 90ties, a very pleasant man. He told me about one of his college who has been truly exceptionally profitable trader, in a very different league. However, he was able to trade only a small number of days, due to stress which affected his health and even physical appearance. My friend has left the private bank where he traded, went to college. trained as a pastor and served first in a very needy area in Bradford, and currently is in Leeds. Few years ago I told him I am interested in trading, he asked me, why??? I told him that among other things I always have been interested in politics, and philosophy which acts as foundation for a variety of ideologies, including political ideology, and that economics are also playing part in it, since my interest in the markets. He did not say anything. Sometimes silence from a friend is as loud as a thunder. I am still here, my interests have not changed, I trade, but trading is not the only activity I use my time for. I am not trading for a firm, therefore do not have a manager over me, with more objective and ongoing assessments, so I must to be careful and realistic. Have been semiretired for a while, fast approaching a further step in that direction. Cannot image what retirement is like, i will always do something. Have been truly blessed with lovely wife, family and even with grandchildren, so there is no point to force myself to take risks which might be to big to bear. Having been involved in many adventures and projects I always tried to be well prepared and give my good if not the best, trading included. I am reasonably well equipped and can display many charts at that same time, I have studiously red many books, like Strat participated in Delta Phenomenon years ago and a few like that, came as always to hit the reality that simple means simple. Back to the Time Frames. I basically initiate trade on any TF ( M1, M2, M5 ,M15, M30 for intraday)when I see the bar pattern which agrees with the strategy, however I manage the trade also on few TFs taking the Higher TF to carry more importance, weight. There is one constant feature for that intraday arrangement, a few displays that are in constant relation to the current PA and price levels/zones, these are Daily Pivots with mid points, and VWAP, which is always displayed in relation to PA alone on all TFs. Fibonacci also displays that same zones on all TFs as it is drawn from the exact price levels, irrespective of TFs. We all react to optics, even on that same TF zooming in and out changes the image upon which we try to make decision/s, so I am aware of that. Can you imagine a pit trader 60 or so many years ago being so concerned whether he should trad M1, M15 of M30? Long time ago I read that some have used pivot points quickly and manually calculated, scrabbled on the back of their cigarettes packages. If they survived few months they lasted for years. Jessie Livermore had even less to go by, often relying on old by our standard information, he must have seen something to make him take trades. Can you imagine his answer regarding the question M1, M2 or M15 TFs? So I take trades on whatever TF i am able to see them coming and than concentrate on managing them. That does not mean that is the objective and ontological "the best", but often it is good enough or the subjective best (rarely so )that I can or am capable to do. Please take the above as sharing some of my thoughts and experiences and not as telling others what to do or that I know more that many great contributors to this thread.

Many years ago while still trading forex and indices, I have observed that US close is an important zone, so I have asked for that indicator to be coded. It can be multiplied with all sorts of names, labels, zones. Initially the drawn line had additional top and bottom lines drawn with a chose amount of pips (points), and if chosen these values can also be displayed in a created label, so I could easily establish market order with SL and PT, according to the displayed price levels, for cable I used 20 pips either way, so My SL was set to be just above 40 pips. These MOs were set up after the US session close, and if not triggered they automatically expired before London open, so I could assess the situation, and possibly establish a new MO. ATM I use only the label, (white for US close) and a single horizontal white which continues until the following session close. I simply look at my watchlist displayed at least on one big monitor Attached Image (click to enlarge) Attached Image (click to enlarge) % ges are well displayed more to follow Edit No: 1 possibly the meat of todays session has been traded, not interested in polishing the butchers hooks, so I am flat. On H1 great marubozu (WRB) looks good. DOW has done dance, it has opened with three gaps; 1st gap to the lasts session High 2nd gap to the last session close 3rd gap to the session pivot All three gaps were filled pretty fast during the the current session. It says something about gaps. Please remember that these gaps are different to the gaps created by the absence of any PA, just like a solid jump or fall. These gaps are imposed on PA filled with candles by the grid made of various things like session close. D Pivot , a particular opening of close and I am aiming for these gaps to be filled, usually fast but sometime it takes a log time, since the Quarterly Futures trades as opposed to cash. After many years of dealing with these gaps, especially gap to the last session close, probably the most used one, I am of the opinion that if the over all move is less than1 to 1.3% that move away has a much bigger chance to be completely filled within the current session (I mean session immediately following that last session close), and PA resumes as if the move away from that pervious session close has been just a market dance allowing strong hands to get good entries. That has happened today, and many, many times in the past. However helpful this insight, very much a part of indices trading, nothing is guaranteed and automatic, if it was we would kill the possibility to trade, which rewards risk management. We have to manful of and thankful for the liquidity providers, and make sure we do not become one. Here we come to heuristic and statistical thinking and decision making. I have asked my son for assistance, we got the las 20 years of, DOW daily data, OHLC NYSE sessions only, and organise it in excel so there is a possibility of statistics based approach. It took him minutes what I could not do, and while the data is imported into excel, iy is amazing what can be done. Excel can create its own graphs, pie-charts ect. The effect I hope might be a statistic based confirmation about the % likelihood of these gap closure within the immediately following session. For now based only on observation of others and mine I think the risk is worthy, but has to be well managed. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #16233 ---
Hi bistolis, i know you know this and it is stating the obvious in our PASR method but: Two Large Red Rectangles: I don't know what time these are for you but they are times where you should sit and watch until the large wicks and tails disappear and the candles return to "normal". This could be FOMO where you want to get in as soon as possible in the hope of catching a "runner". I used to, and sometimes, still am guilty of this as it is a natural trader's mindset to trade what he thinks is his "set up" but we need the DISCIPLINE to WAIT until PRICE "settles down" and the large wicks and tails disappear. Sometimes they don't disappear during your trading session in which case, don't think of the missed trading opportunities and instead, think of the $money your DISCIPLINE has SAVED you. Thin Horizontal Red Rectangle on the Strat Shadow: When the Strat Shadow is thin and horizontal, it indicates directionless ranging PRICE and trading should be avoided. Basic PASR can be used to trade this but you have to have your finger on the "close trade" button as PRICE is always wicked in this area. Normal PASR Swing trading can resume when PRICE CLOSES below support as indicated by the RED Arrow. RED and GREEN Arrows: Explained many times in both of these threads, these are our "bread and butter", "sore thumb", money making trades. Look how they are STRESS FREE as they have a small SL, low risk, and immediately move in your chosen trade direction without looking back. Remember: The Strat Shadow gives you your trend direction in every time frame and unless you are very experienced, DO NOT TRADE AGAINST it - rather WAIT for PRICE to resume the direction of the Strat Shadow. Watching and reviewing your posts bistolis, tells me you are getting ahead of yourself in your trading experience and capabilities and I am probably guilty of influencing you by posting my trades - maybe I should stop posting them? I have said it so many times but here it goes again: nobody can trade like me just like I can't trade like anyone else; we are all unique as traders and have to find our "trading style" within any chosen method/strategy. Please don't be offended but it seems you "believe" you are better than you really are. If I was where you are at (and I have been there many times), and as I suggested before, go back to ONLY taking "bread and butter", "sore thumb" trades and FORGET anything else until you have built up a sizeable account and you are a MASTER at these trades. Again, good luck and stick at it and please don't take this as negative criticism. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #16252 ---
Hi bistolis, Gaps - different types of gaps - abbreviations PSCG - Previous Session Close Gap - is a gap created by the difference between the Previous session close and the open of the immediately following new or current session. This Gap has different ways to be utilised, and it depends also on the traded instrument/security. PSCGs are very useful for trading indices, and for me its utility is often limited to the session that immediately follows that close, although if that gap is not closed I keep an eye on that. ISG - Intra Session Gap - Gap between the different sessions what it has been https://www.forexfactory.com/thread/...hedging?page=6 post 114 DPG - Gap to the DP, when the DP is missed https://www.forexfactory.com/thread/...ow-with-missed ? Other gaps- Intra Day Gap and Intra Week Gap - These gaps are also flagged by PSCG and/or ISG Please note that intra day, intra week or indeed any gap that exists between the closing and opening bar on any TF, where there is a gap created by PA is a formidable display of market activity, and as such demands attention and purposeful action/response well prepared in advance. The above is copied from my journal's first page, the only page that can be continually edited, allowing for more updates. Do not want to clatter this tread too much, PA and the bar formation is most important and one can trade just using it, or having some other insights in the background, always giving priority to PA. Time allowing I will post some more, though trying to limit my posting activity, however I will always try to do my best.

Good luck in your journey. https://www.forexfactory.com/thread/...3#post14369483

I marked the Swing Highs and Swings Lows ( based on the break of the Control Candle ). The Swing Highs and Lows in PASR are determined by my method and not by anything else. According to your method, as I understand it, candle #2 is a possible swing high and gets confirmed when candle #3 closes (below candle #2 lower low). Now, what I 've been doing since a few years back (way way back when Roger introduced me to WCC) is to use Control Candles to define the swing and avoid ranges. Candle #1 is the Control Candle. Price can go up and down all it wants, but as long as it doesn't close beyond the high or low of Candle #1, it remains as the Control Candle. It is when Candle #4 closes below Candle #1 that it becomes the new Control Candle. And it is then that I marked my Swing High at Candle #2. Now, am I terribly wrong with what I just said? From this, I'm trying to be simpler on my approach. It seems you have not yet developed YOUR own PASR style. Keep trading a LIVE account and posting your charts with trades here so that we can help you find your PASR style. My suggestion is to find what is confusing you and eliminate it and see if that helps. Thank you. For instance, I want to make sure I'm not sabotaging me with the definition of Swing High, Low and Control Candle. Also the use of trendlines is something I haven't added to my repertoire. I will from know on. A common problem for new PASR traders is waiting for all 3 time frames to turn in the same direction. All movements start with the shortest time frame and then starts building the next higher time frame and so on so it could be a long time for all 3 time frames to turn by which time you will have missed many trades. As you gain experience, you will see this happening. For example in my M1 trading, I ONLY trade PASR on M1 with my only reference to M5 and higher when I see M1 trending. Another problem is the understanding of our SR lines. These are not lines but areas or zones where there is a high probability of PRICE either stopping and reversing OR slicing through and continuing in it's original direction. As Dexter and bistolis posted, they are also used as potential targets. Check my charts and you will see that the majority of my trades are closed at SR or Fibonacci levels, the rest on PA. Spot on! Waiting for the 3 timeframes to align... guilty. Forgetting SR are zones... guilty. I will keep practicing to gain that experience and be patient. Thank you very much!

--- 帖子 #16605 ---
Having started with forex myself, which is heavily marketed, I can only suggest for new traders to start their learning curve on something that has a beggining and end throughout the day (index). forex pairs can and will be moving at random times during the day, since that market is open 24/7. On the other hand for example DOW (or any of the other indexes) have an open and close. That gives you a schedule to work around and not be influenced by fear and greed.

--- 帖子 #16751 ---
I really think it's a zen thing, because there is no objective way to predict the stop level, even after the fact - it is essentially random, and more and more random as the TF's get smaller (if looking at candles for reference). Even on a tick chart, there is no SL predictability in the data. So, with regard to learning, suggest searching for your Jedi rather than trying to harness rules - the rules will work when they work (confirmation bias) and when they don't work, feel personal, like failure. Conditions that correlate with previous wins, sure, but not rules - keep the mind as clean as possible.

--- 帖子 #16769 ---
Handling DD might be the wrong way to look at it - you only "handle" DD in game theory or frequency-based strategies running iterations of trades. This is subjective trading with discrete entries and exits. You have winners or losers - if you don't have an SL level in mind when you enter your trade, you have already failed. If you are advanced, I could potentially see a reason for moving the SL during the trade, but moving it against your own interest obviously adds risk to an already amorphous model.

Many times ago I have come to similar conclusion/s and decided to safe time and effort, no regret or resentment on my side, just taking into account some of many facts of trading and of life in general; - it is a positive and honorable desire to help others, though often "others" are not able to be helped for myriad of reasons - PASR a great concept applied to trading, both a simple and a complex one ( Is SR part of PA, or something outside of it?, for me SR is part of PA, noetically it is difficult to be otherwise, but others might have valid reasons to treat that issue in a different way. While interpretation of PA apply to every TF, which TFs are to be taken into account, similar question is to be raised in relation to S/R. How one defines S/R and on which TFs. What is the relation between PA and S/R. What constitutes trending/ranging market and how it relates to the above. What is a market structure, ect. These issues and many others have been well addressed on this thread but even a careful student and there are only a few of them is likely to treat this with well entrenched biases, many of them well hidden.) - Trade management, money management, time and effort set aside for studying and trading - Emotional side of trading - Statistic based versus heuristic approach ( while there are many well written books on other subjects, I would draw your attention to two books on the subject os statistic v heuristic, Daniel Kahneman, Thinking fast and slow, and Michael Lewis, The undoing project, obviously it is up to everyone to decide how to invest time and resources.) The above list is very selective, just an illustration of things involved in trading. IMHO statistic base approach has a huge advantage above heuristic, unless one learns new heuristic habits based on statistics, eg, trend holds 75%, market is range bound between 70 - 80%, if one cannot understand and apply that understanding, it is better to do exact the opposite to what one intends to do, if one decides to trade, do not trade to begin with, if one decides to sell, just buy or vice versa and manage the trade and one is more likely to do better that otherwise, try it on small lots and see. The reason for what at first time appears as madness is that the market is constructed to take advantage of unlearned heuristic decision, based on false assumption/s and hopes. Throughout this thread Strat pointed many times to these issues and I do understand one can be tired of repeating that same in finito. My great appreciation to Strat, his patience and commitment. Continue to enjoy a well deserved weekend break. 2be

--- 帖子 #16874 ---
Very good point Strat. I understand that everybody reading this is a trader, or espiers to be trader. Salutations and congratulations to you all for joining the club of retail traders (versus commercial traders) where about 80 - 90% are losers, Pareto distribution clearly enacted. If one decided to have an operation would one choose a hospital that have at the very best only a 20% rate of success? Interestingly the retail traders do it of their own volition in contradistinction to necessity. That's for starters! Lets consider fear and trading. Fear is the word we use to describe our emotional reaction to something that seems dangerous . Fear might have a paralysing effect and as a strong emotion it is often accompanied with stress and anger. We are all afraid of pain, one ultimate fear is a painful death. Not surpassingly we do our best to avoid pain, fear playing an important part in that natural process. There are at least too opposite side to fear, positive sight, like fear of snakes,flood, fire and pain, and a negative side like fear of dentist, fire and pain. Fire and pain are in an interesting category in relation to fear, where fear is clearly falling into the both categories, positive in some cases and negative in other, depending on circumstances. There is a pain associated with loosing trades and loosing traders have grown a distinctive, entrenched and well developed fear of the pain of loosing. That is natural and stands well with survival instinct, however in trading itis one of the important mark and identifier of a loosing trader belonging to the overwhelming majority of loosing traders club. Profitable traders who are in a tiny minority have done some in-depth work on that issue and are continually aware of it and are in process of implementing what they have worked out so far, and they are continually furthering understanding of themselves and the issue of fear and the fear of pain. Many books and the articles have been written on that subject. In trading, adding to the losing trade, mark of a losing trader, is a bad practice of avoiding pain of losing, the fear of the pain of loosing is often strangely correlated to hope, and the loses get bigger. Recognising and embracing the pain of losing, makes one being less afraid, preferably not afraid at all of the pain of losing. The healthy and desirable fear in that respect is the fear of not implementing our own resolve. Adding to the winning trade ia a mark of a profitable trader, who has replaced the fear of pain of losing smaller profit/s, acts on PA trading what he is able to see and actively manages the trade hoping for a more optimum outcome - bigger profit/s. Pure scalping is a valid exception of not adding to the winning trade, but when one implements many trades based on PA when following trend is a part of strategy, that in a way in a way might be considered of a type of adding to the winners. In view of the above one might agree with the mantra, that when losing one should not have hope but fear, and in reverse, when in profit replace fear with hope. The above is just a very limited number of issues relating to fear and there are many more worth investigating, like fear and pain as stimuli or playing positive and necessary part, where for example a lack of physical pain is a serious illness ect. There are some very insightful books on that subject, if interested please PM me, my suspicion is that study of this kind and particularly study of ourselves is rarely on the agenda of the majority of losing traders, if it was not so they will not constitute such big majority. Good long weekend to all, 2be

Yes Strat, you have been posting and investing your time and effort for a long time, to some lesser extend I have done it myself too. My current conclusion runs along the following lines, market serves out what is well deserved and it does so without partiality and lies. Every individual is constructed with similarities and differences and we all have to confront ourselves in all different areas and address different areas related to trading. When driving a car could you imagine trying to solve an inquiry as to which of many wheels is the most important. The situation is resolved for a while when one wheel is punctured and deflated. For a while one is forgiven to assume that for that short time that punctured wheel usurps the position of the most important, or more important than other wheels, including the driving one. That example presents us with the dilema, with the possibility that the question/s are misleading as to be useful in figuring out the best outcomes. In trading many areas are important, and at times one is tempted to focus on one to the determent of others, yet focusing on specific areas one by one is the way human usually operate. Multitasking is desirable, and multitasking with necessary precession demands training and stamina of all kinds. Trading and multitasking, do they have anything in common? Things get even more complicated by adding indicators, adding yet another task to already busy arrangement, crowding the limited ability to comprehend whats is going on on any given TF. That is one of the main reason that information overload presents a problem. Chart reading skills, PA , S/R, TA, Fundamental Analysis, timing, trend/range, money management, trade management, emotional state and management of emotions, physical state, tiredness,worries and concerns , fear, pain greed, discipline are just a few to mention. All of them are important and demand our attention. These and many other are the extremely interesting issues one discovers when involved in trading, as they are unveiled and brought up to the attention of the skilful observer. Absolutely nobody is perfect, but one needs to be committed to work, study and and be truthful to oneself to start with. The question is if one needs to be concerned when self deluded traders are committed to be perpetual losers? Similarly, is one to be concerned when people with limited finances spend large proportion on alcohol, cigarets, drugs and slot-machines. I am concerned and sad, but concerned individual/s have to desire to change. Being a residential landlord in south east of England over several decades, I have seen and experienced all sort of situations. Some tenants pulled it through, and investment in them brought good fruit, while sadly others decided to self destroy themselves. My suspicion is that in trading, the overwhelming majority is in constant danger to self destroy themselves and their accounts, and in severe cases causing themselves and their families pain and discomfort of various degrees. I would like to encourage one to be truthful, starting with trying to be truthful to oneself. If one is not able to do that, a good start is to stop laying to yourself. Well, again I might have written too much, hope have not waisted your and mine time. Wishing all to have a great long weekend, 2be

What happens with a coin flip if it comes up heads 10 times, change coins? NO! I have learned to keep moving with controlled risk. A post by a well-meaning trader could derail this and I start second guessing myself, then nothing was gained for me. There is currently a position that has been held for weeks, the original target was the 52-week high, Friday's price action blew right through it. Still holding it with the add-ons. Entering on the 1 instead of the 3 (wave off the shadow). Knowing those stats will make you comfortable with taking losses as well as re-entering on the 3 after the 1 loss.

Hi Zebi, It is not surprising to me that humans use words, and record them, including writing. No other creatures on this planet are able to do that, which does not mean that they do not communicate. If it is otherwise, please let me know when the book written by a pig, tree or a fish is published. In my opinion WORD - LOGOS - being a hugely important way of communication, and much more than that, demands our careful attention. Of course there are other ways of communication like art, music, body language, ect. Charts fall into the category of no verbal communication, but still communicating, or at least being an attempt to communicate by people who post them. Illustration is a form of communication, otherwise why to illustrate. It it dangerous and certainly not adequate or precise enough to predicate that a given chart will communicate that same message, content and insight to everybody perusing it. If it was so, there would not be Pareto distribution among "trades", which IMHO is still very generous apportioning only 80% ratio of losers to 20% of winners. as it is very possible if not likely that losers constitute more than 90%. Yet majority if not all use charts with a great degree of similarity between the charts. I use charts extensively and have posted many of them in the past and still occasionally do so, but after many years of doing so have arrived to a sobering conclusion that it is naive to expect that the posted charts will result in replication of that same insights and understanding which have been intended by the exercise. I view it as a common human dilemma regarding perception and communication. My hope is that being aware of the above, will increase profits in the very exacting activity of trading, which demands precise and practical application/s of common sense, self preservation and others in many areas of a human being, with nobody being excluded. One more thing I would draw attention to is not to allow any forum, thread or misinformation to stand in a way of maximising profits. Wishing you many profitable trades, 2be PS Attached Image (click to enlarge) what can you see? rectangles? circles? both? Victor Frankl once observed that the same object can be rightly represented by a rectangle and a circle at that same time. Seamingly two shapes that exclude one another, but not so when another dimension is added. Trading is an activity with layers of many things and "dimensions".

A good question. S/R or/and PA. There are some possibilities like S/R &gt; PA, S/R&lt;PA, S/R=PA or S/R unrelated to PA Everyone wights differently the importance of insights that are gained from all the available data and charts. While there are common "things" applied to the majority of traded instruments, there are also some specific "things" related to a given instrument and/or a group of instruments. On the top of that there is an obvious semantic problem. A simple example, what does PA mean and how a given definition and understanding of it can potentially be applied in relation to many other factors, not excluding the emotional sate of a trader. Having access to a very large amount of data, different TFs and the way that information is processed, it is no surprise that one can easily be well confused. Possibly a good starting point is the term "loss". In trading it is a less complicated term, and limiting loss is an important concept applied to trading. --- 帖子 #17052 ---
The top spots in ES are the top spots in NQ, and make up virtually all of the gains since April, so for anything other than micro TF's, they are very highly correlated. Using one to predict the other is silly though - for the exact reason given above - if one is lagging the other, it's because of the variation in breakdown of the indices, and those differences, by definition are what is lagging the other. Obviously, AAPL is doing the same thing in each index... So, by using correlation to predict one vs the other, you are effectively pitting a lesser known S&amp;P component vs a lesser known NQ component. Or, another way of looking at it, you are finding a reason to do what you already know the top components are doing - going up, and are timing it with a correlative aspect of the lesser known components - not good. The only caveat to that is if one makes a large technical break, which may cause a reaction that spurs movement in the other.

Sorry I didn't realize it was US30 and not YM/MYM. US30 will display a similar price as YM/MYM, but can also use decimal places, whereas the CME products do not. I think Strat and I thought you meant $1, due to the minimum moves in CME products. --- 帖子 #17117 ---
There are no rules that are consistently profitable over time. Every day, there will be MA crosses that are perfect, and others that take only losses. However, every MA, and every rule for that matter, is profitable sometimes, given some long list of caveats (other rules). So, each rule is a variable, and a solution exists for this very long and complex multivariable equation for every trade period of all time... but it's not possible to solve. Coming up with some set of rules that is rigid, yet shows expected return over any longer time period is setting oneself up for disaster (unless game theory based, relatively high frequency, and funded with beaucoup bucks). So, your "system" must be dynamic and fluid. Strat has set this up to give you as many guidelines as possible without pigeonholing you with rigidity. When price is trending, ema's might be a guide. For a reversal off of an extreme, they are relatively useless. Suggest take a few days to read the thread, and study Strat's charts before anyone else's. You should get into the nitty gritty within a week or so if not sooner.

PASR with volume may have got you in on the first down candle - I can't check because I no longer have Forex charts. However, the 20 MA doesn't cross the 50 MA until a dozen or so candles down. Why wait two weeks for the cross? As bistolis pointed out, PASR does NOT trade MA crosses nor does it use the 50 MA. I further developed the two MAs, known as the "Strat Shadow", for trending trading purposes only. Using them for anything else, especially in a range/consolidation is, as Barbaresco remarks, useless, which is why and where we use Basic PASR. For the purposes of this discussion, please ignore the TDI/Stoch windows, I have been using Trading Made Simple method and seeing if it is makeable into a system PASR ALWAYS ignores indicators and all other 2nd degree + lagging tools. Any indicator system will work sometimes, but not consistently enough to trade large contracts to make a decent living. Expanding on Barbaresco's comments, you can use any MA to create a system/strategy/method - it is how YOU understand what that MA means in the context of PA, Price Structure and higher time frames. The rules generated around that MA system/strategy/method will work sometimes, just like any other, but the fragile, feeble, infidelity nature of the Market coupled with Institutional Trading, makes sure it does not work ALL the time meaning that, at best, over the long term, and, as Barbaresco points out, is break even at best and a loser when commissions and exchange costs are included. NOTHING works 100% of the time which is why we need GOOD Money and Risk Management.

--- 帖子 #17155 ---
If you trade the CME contract, because it goes through a centralized exchange you can purchase level two data and look at the ladder / DOM which will show you where all the pending orders are stacked. Traders are trained to put their stops below old lows and above old highs, that's what all the books teach us to do, breakout traders place their orders above old highs and below old lows. Large funds who are trend following by nature, trail their stops under old lows and above old highs. The higher the time frame, the larger the quantity of orders. Also, its important to note too that just because a trader has his stop hit, doesn't mean he has lost money, he may have trailed the stop up and be in significant profits. Its just the order / counter party that smart money need, be it a profit for some or a loss for others. Orders are orders. I realize my post is a little contrary but I like to share my thoughts with like minded people (price action traders), otherwise it can be quite a lonely endeavor. Unfortunately my big boss ain't that interested!

Hi Strat, August is almost gone, time seems to go so fast. Have been having some breaks with grandchildren, now time to gather some apples and get some points from the indices. Hope you have had a good summer so far. Market takes its most important task very seriously, this task is to survive. Needless to point it out, market is very efficient in fulfilling this task, while luring a hopeful trader with the self asserted and too often delusional vision of great profit/s. To survive is also the most important task of a trader, trader has to survive before he/ her becomes profitable. Therefore the risk factor is to be considered well before the desirable profits are at the center of trader's attention. Never add to the looser, do your best to add to the winners, that is what makes trader profitable to a greater degree. adding to a losing trade is like going to the dentist for a simple check up, and coming out with a broken nose, it makes sense to get our well before the eye is gouged out. Adding to a winner, is like building property portfolio, once the first one is making sense, why not to add another one and sensibly manage both? In a ranging market on any TF, adding to the winners, especially aggressive adding can be problematic, care needs to be exercised. Is the market ranging or trending on any given TF, an important question to be answered. Every TF tells its story, everyone gives priority to some TFs over the other TFs. TFs that I pay more attention for intra day trading are M4, M30, M5, especially I observe the play between M30 and M5. I have possibility like all of us to display other TFs too, but do not use them that much, except of M1. In the background for some time I have been using P&amp;F charts, the benefit of P&amp;F charts is simplicity, especially when things have not worked out as they might have. P&amp;F charts complement well bar charts, they both have their different advantages, a fast glance is all one needs at times, especially after good preparation before the active trading. For indices trading gaps and well marked active sessions are of great use to me as well as pivots, and at times fibs, especially when I can clearly see the impulsive early in the session, then after measured retracement, I aim at measured extension/s. I have resumed trading DAX from the XETRA open, and also trade NASDAQ, as well as DOW. I also look at seasonal charts, like one below, and pay attention to inter-market performance as the day unfolds. This NYSE DOW session has been a good example, as the DOW session's H was asymmetrical compared to S&amp;P and NASDAQ. VIX and USD index was in agreement with the eventual DOW's move down, just a ranging market on higher TFs. https://www.forexfactory.com/attachm...l?d=1688194934

Longer profitable periods are proof to me that it is possible, but other things - mostly psychologically - were not in place. There were also flaws in my trading plan. For this, I have rid myself of all trading systems of the past, fibonacci, pivots, breakouts and whatever it was and traded only price action for the last relevant years. But this time, I will also rewrite my trading plan and ONLY focus on the path / PASR methodology with IGNORING everything else, except trading psychology. My plan has been unfolding during the past weeks while I am studying in my free time after work. Thanks for offering such an abundant ressource for years, I often wish it was the first thread I had discovered in trading - unfortunately, I was in for a long term ticket to most confusing and annoying places! Now it is time to complete the unlearning of all this nonsense and only keeping what works ... Thanks again for laying out decades of trading wisdom to the public.

just wondering if there is a preferred method for TF selection before the open. It's just visual, Barbaresco. This probably doesn't help but much of it depends on volatility - if there is little volatility, I have to use M1 to see PA and Structure. If there is ""normal"" volatility, I check PA, Structure and Volume between 5am to 5:30am and 5:30am to 6am and choose the time frame which I "understand", i.e., good volume coupled with PASR candles, logical, not erratic PA, and good repeating Structure. Once in a "trading time frame", I keep toggling between higher and lower time frames looking for one which more accurately reflects the current PA, Volume and Structure. Today was low volatility so M1 only but erratic PA and Structure which I did not understand even moving through the gears up to M5 which increases Risk and the dreaded draw down. So in summary, it's subjective based on experience/intuition etc.

So far I made it through the first 250 pages in two weeks, reading every post and taking notes. It is shocking what a slow learner I am nowadays, yet I want my plan laid out in detail before putting my hard earned money on the line again. At least it brought me a lot of "light bulb moments" so far. While working on my trading plan, which also deals with trading psychology, I have discovered a very hard thing that has probably held me back for years. Maybe others can relate to it, as Strat also said that we need to check the cause of repeated errors. So here is what I found to be true for myself: Do we sometimes take bad trades because of the urge of "doing something"? We do! I remember some certain people when I was very young, usually the ones going with convention, telling me that I had to "go for it" or "should start making money somehow". From their point of view, there was "nothing to wait for" in life or time to "waste" on things like studying life, arts or culture: Everything had to lead to financial gains, or at least something countable, it could also be a relationship to a person that would offer you any benefit. These people with their overly egoistic beliefs and mindsets pressed hard on me for years, because by nature I am interested in culture, history, arts and healthy relationships without taking advantage of a person. I thought about this deeply and came to the conclusion, that this early influence might still lead me to chase chances, which is totally wrong in trading. In life, there is financial pressure and we need to have an income to pay our bills and often also to be accepted by others (whatever this kind of acceptance is worth). Partly because of these experiences, I have been working hard in different jobs for years and sometimes feeling like I had to prove that me (humble, interested in "non profitable things not worse the time") could find my place / persevere in society among these people and it has turned out I can ... However, in the market it is totally different. Nobody can force me into a trade or an action. There is no boss (except the BIG BOSS and BOSS) to call my actions and I am the one who decides if i take the trade and I do not have to prove anything to anybody or persuade them using logic. I need to make this clear to myself again and again ... I hope this makes sense, if not, please ask.

--- 帖子 #17273 ---
I have created a folder for the collection of my biggest trading mistakes Good - better would be to stick notes on your monitor or add them to your template. GBP/NZD "Whip to death trap" on M5: Apart from AUDNZD, all NZD pairs are notorious for whipping your ass. the last candle of the trend was very long and also had a long wick. That candle is an Exhaustion Candle - if it was on a Futures Chart there would be abnormal selling volume. This is telling you that particular down trend is over and done with and to expect consolidation until a new Swing/Trend starts. These Exhaustion Candles leave a very important "footprint" behind - learn and understand these. However, just before that, PASR provides us with very important information that the down trend is in jeopardy. Look at the yellow rectangle before it. This shows a CLOSE above the Strat Shadow telling us that the buyers are gaining strength. Subsequent PA continues to show this until either the new UP trend is confirmed or that Exhaustion Candle is violated. Experienced PASR traders would also recognise the Strat Shadow going horizontal as shown by the 2nd yellow rectangle. Because as you can see from my chart, any PASR trigger bar in the direction of the trend Understand all the above and you will see there is no PASR trigger bar in the direction of the trend Good job, Hickson - the tortoise is already outperforming the hare! --- 帖子 #17385 ---
Spot on, bistolis! One question to add: After my trade, there was a shooting star rejecting support (second chart) that as a trigger would have resulted in a s/o according to M5 PASR Trend Trading Strategy. First, that is not a Shooting Star. A Shooting Star and Hammer have to be at the top/bottom of a swing/trend with no candles to the left of them. Second, as bistolis, correctly points out, this is a RED FLAG for the trader selling short. This candle is the result of buyers coming in at that level and pushing PRICE up until the sellers sold it back down again. The trader should be alert that buyers are coming in and looking to accumulate positions at those levels.

--- 帖子 #17404 ---
If you trade arrow 1, then your stop is the swing high and TP a new low. If you trade any other arrow, your stop could be a close above arrow 1, with a TP anywhere from 1:1 all the way down to a new low. The point is that all of this analysis is still subject to randomness - all you are trying to do is put your thumb on the scale, not ensure a winner every time. So, trade all of those arrows, or whichever one satisfies your requirements, but trade all opportunities that satisfy, every time, so that your thumb on the scale is actually realized. Otherwise, with very few trades, there will be no statistical significance, and your confidence will be impacted not by the outcome of your intended strategy, but by the outcome of your individual subjective trades.

Hello Strat.. following your posts but still only trading currencies. It's an Old Dog -- New Tricks thing . On the M1 S&amp;P 500 posted chart... which I cannot call up on my own charting, I could not help but seeing a possible application of BABAG's use of the Fib Tool to find TP areas. BUT using Terry Dawe's important modification. Since the candles in the upper left corner are a DHLC pattern, Terry/BBG would use the pattern as a signal to use the Fib Tool to set possible TP areas. Terry's modification is to Put the 0 line at the top of the pattern . Then draw the Fib tool down so that the 50 line is at the bottom of the DHLC candle pattern . The resulting fib lines would give some profit target lines. My experience is that the 100 , 138, 161, and 200 lines are areas of interest for taking profit. Of course price may move beyond that or never hit those lines. If you care to do so, it would be interesting to see where the possible TP fib lines showed up on the chart.

--- 帖子 #17428 ---
Hi bistolis This market we trade is not what we think it is, looking at candles without knowing how the orders were executed inside is a recipe for disaster. Any good bullish candle or up thrust candle is only caused by a sudden increase in selling limit orders entering the market. It’s pull back sellers get caught and not profit taking. It’s caused by limit orders and not market orders. After looking at DOM for a few years, I got to understand that mostly Sellers liquidity creates bullish moves and also Ask spoofing also creates bullish moves. It’s not Buyers but 90% driven by limit orders. The only time Buyers move the market is when the market becomes unbalanced and big players have to sweep into the market to push price upwards to create a balanced market again. Also 50% of directional movement is not on purpose but rather a side effect of big player arbitrage. An example is hedge fund buying US shares and selling the US500, they will close out one side if they see a edge, whether it goes up or down is irrelevant. Trading is hard enough, mainly because price moves against traders entry bias always. An example would be a special price at the supermarket where pork is being sold for $10 a kilo discount so everyone buys. Those same people also place long limit orders on the chart creating a bearish move. The bears see this and thinking they are smart, start loading up lots of sell limit orders above price. So now all liquidity is above price so we now get the pull back you were talking about. It’s generally about a 30% imbalance of sell limit orders to get bistolis’s profit taking candle. Therefore it’s now sellers losing, before it flips back to buyers losing. The damage is caused by HFT algo’s from one of over 50 Quant trading firms that have coded their Algo’s to attack increasing limit order imbalance levels on the books. Better to join them and piggyback their movements. This still proves Stat’s strategy is correct, just don’t label green candles as buyers - it’s bloody well isn’t. It’s a bitch of a game, makes you want to pull your hair out which explains why I have stuff all.

$25k rule does not apply to Futures. You could look at Tradestation : ( TS can be used with Tradingview chart package as can AMP and Tradovate) In the UK they supply free data for Futures. Micro Futures ( Nasdaq, SP500 etc) require a small margin for intraday trading ( not holding trades overnight) The intraday margins in other firms such as AMP ( example $50), Tradovate or Ninja are lower but you pay for data feed ( whether Level 2 or the cheaper Level 1) You would need to contact them via phone or chat or email for clarification but they are better than the pirate you are dealing with at the moment. Although you have these low margins you would be wise to have about $500 or more for trading the Micro's. Maybe the above and others may be worth your investigation? https://www.tradestation-internation...tures-trading/ CME website: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/equ...l#venue=globex Hope this helps as an introduction.
