One of my favourite patterns which occur over and over again. The highlighted area is the weekly (Boss) hammer. I identify my hammers and shooting stars as such regardless of where they form. If a hammer forms at the top I call it a momentum hammer. Same for the shooting star but in the opposite direction. The failure of a hammer or shooting star for me is a signal in the opposite direction. Once the weekly hammer appeared to be failing (indicated by the daily outside down candle on Monday with price barely breaking to the upside and then turning right around). Early entry is to short below that candle. More conservative entry is break of the bottom of the Boss hammer which confirms its failure. As of EOD today, price hit bottom of November BB low which coincided with the bottom of the shadow.

--- 帖子 #17527 ---
Hi Strat, DAX has two openings and two closes, XFRA (Frankfurt open GMT -1 one hour before London open) and XETRA (Zurich open, coincides with London open), for intraday I trade XETRA open and often finish when XFRA closes, yes it sounds confusing, best to look on internet to get your own bearing. To make it simple I trade from London open, take advantage of rumors and expectation before the major news is released in the US, the news being released often an hour before the NYSE opening. Often DAX follows US indices, at times NASDAQ is the one closely followed. DAX reaction to the major US news release is often slower, or a bit muted compared to the US indices. DAX is influenced by some other specific news releases by its own, and is also sensitive to USD index, VIX ect. Trading from UK makes it more natural to start trading DAX at the London open, together with trading pre-market open NASDAQ. DAX at times proposes good opportunities when its reaction to the US indices is "delayed" till the following morning, and this reaction when confirmed by PA is often well done within the first 3-4hrs of XETRA (Zurich mix session), after which is the US data release, followed by NYSE open, when at times "muted"DAX just holds and follows US. Otherwise I follow many of the insights that I apply to trading other indices like PA, gaps trend ect. If you like have a look at Brixen, he is a profitable DAX trader and assumes that principles like PA and others are already firmly established in those who peruse his threads. You might enjoy the music posted within the 1st post. https://www.forexfactory.com/thread/...-december-2023 This is very selective and chaotic kind of intro to DAX. Like DOW and NASDAQ I trade DAX cash and Quarterly Futures.

--- 帖子 #17588 ---
What is your opinion/attitude towards traders who prefer to keep things simple and systematic if possible? That is the main goal of profitable trading but, since the Market is fickle and changeable, it is not always possible. PASR is simple, systematic but subjective depending on the trader's experience with, and understanding of, PASR, the Market conditions, and the instrument he is trading. Can this work or do you have to analyze the cr@p out of charts all day It all comes down to the trader's particular and unique style of trading. I started out analysing everything on a chart, many times suffering from paralysis of analysis until eventually I had built a mental data base of PASR trading situations involving thousands of hours of charting and trading time over many years that I now trade on instinct or "Zen" as Barbaresco coined it. Dropping down to minute and second time frames put an end to over analysis and reduced it to a more "visual" style. can you do something simple like: "I trade a maximum of ONE and the same instrument every day regardless of "market condition", during specific trading hours," Yes, that is exactly what I do trading only the ES S&amp;P 500 Index from NY Market Open until volume and volatility dries up. "according to clear and objective/replicable rules," PASR does not have "clear and objective/replicable rules" as it is subjective based on the trader's experience with, and understanding of, PASR, the Market conditions, and the instrument he is trading. The nature of the Market ensures that anything with "clear and objective/replicable rules " is not profitable over the long haul. "finally able to make a living from it" This has nothing to do with methods, strategies, systems etc., and is 100% down to each individual trader and how he/she deals with emotions at the "hard right edge" as their understanding of a "Set Up" appears, if they are able to "pull the trigger", control their psychological emotions once in a trade, how they manage the trade and risks etc. Over these last coming up to 15 years on here, I have seen many who have understood PASR and yet have been unable to actually trade it profitably while there have been others who understood the concept, took it and "tweaked" it to suit their own individual style of trading. Some have used it as a stepping stone on to other strategies/methods. maybe someone could guide me in the right direction so that I don't spend another 10 years doing things that don't take me one step closer to that goal. With the utmost respect, if you haven't made it in 10 years, you may not be suited to trading. Thank you for your post

I can say focusing on one thing is a better way. Stay away from GBP pairs while sill trying to figure it out (I also made the same mistake of going for GBPUSD - which is good for scalping and day trading). You can go for EURUSD or AUDUSD, instead. Stay away from lower time-frames until you can be profitable using the higher time-frames (you can keep W1, D1, H4 and H1 on your trading platform). In addition, try to look for trades that can last for 2 to 3 days - targeting the High or Low of the week is much better than going for the High or Low of the day when you are still trying to figure it out - you can see Price Action better. The High and Low are predetermined and price can only move Up and Down (and therefore you must have a demarcation line/point) - this should be your number 1 guiding principle.

Dear Strat &amp; Co, I've been lurking around here off and on for about five years, but I finally decided to make PASR my permanent home. Five years ago when I first stumbled upon Strat's strategy I didn't know what to make of it because there wasn't a "method" per se, yet the members were successful. It began to dawn on me that there was a bit of a learning curve to the whole thing, but at the time I either didn't have the determination and patience or I was undecided on whether or not this type of strategy was worth the time investment. I could see from the get-go that it would require a considerable amount of that. Again and again I'd revisit this thread and see, again and again, that the people who put in the time and accepted Strat's reproofs were successful. Gradually, I became convinced that it was a worthwhile endeavor. I was way too addicted to indicators though and would be until fairly recently (which, for me, was a refusal to accept responsibility for doing honest analysis and the willingness to be wrong after giving it my best effort). For the decades of effort I've put into learning about the markets, the ONE thing I never confronted directly was the "little people" in my head. Instead of doing that, I kept looking for the magical thing that would circumvent the pain of uncertainty. For the last seven years I've been conditioning myself to accept uncertainty and to embrace it as a kind of spiritual adventure; a means toward realizing my own potential. In a very general sense, I live that way in all areas of my life and it's made me a much better, kinder person because I learned what uncertainty does to human beings - how it makes them crazy, etc... by seeing what it does to me. This trading endeavor is a kind of test to see whether or not I can accept what the market is willing to share with me - or take away. For me, it's a kind of 'right of passage.' I've tried my very best to make this a continuous outlook with respect to each and every moment and I'm so very curious to see what happens when I deal with the market again. It's been over 10 years so it should be interesting. Strat, I want to thank you for your years of patient effort in teaching and supporting others. I'd also like to thank all the people who have posted their charts so regularly. It's inspiring to see people who are trading successfully using simple methods, irrespective of timeframes and markets. It gives me such joy to see people being successful and who are willing to demonstrate it. I'm sure it feels inconvenient at times; particularly when some of you have been doing it for many years, but it really is appreciated; at least by me. I know I haven't learned everything with respect to PASR, but I'm opening an account anyway to trade micro E-Minis and micro Dow futures. I set aside $1000 to lose; at least I'm willing to use it as a kind of "tuition" to confront my little people and nothing more. I'm sure I'll screw up. I'll probably make horrible mistakes as my mind goes numb, gets panicky, wants to make exceptions to the rules, gets lazy, impatient, too greedy, too fearful, too cautious, sees things that aren't there and so on. It's just par for the course. It has to be done. It MUST be addressed directly and seen for what it is, metabolized and moved beyond. I guess I needed to publicly state an intention or something. I hope to be posting my mistakes to this thread fairly soon; at least that's what I'm pretty sure will be happening, irrespective of my "positive thinking." I'm actually very optimistic overall, but I know what's in store for me once I put actual money on the line. Thanks Everybody!

--- 帖子 #17786 ---
Since long term stress free trading works best on established trends, thought I would post some thoughts on trends as a reminder to those looking for and trading trends. A trend can be looked at as having phases. Clearly a newly established trend behaves differently than a mature trend. There are varying phases. 1 - The establishment of a new trend (can be volatile). 2 - The beginning leg of a new trend (systems help establish trend). 3 - The mid-point saturation (trend is widely recognized and mature) 4 – Late stage trend (systems support trend at this stage) 5 - The ending of the trend (can be volatile) Phase 2 and 4 often exhibit large moves in the trend direction.

--- 帖子 #17881 ---
For intra day trading I use the gearing between M30 to M5 extensively. One on the charting software I use displays any and all drawn simple objects like rectangular boxes or trendlines on all open charts of a given instrument, very useful, even when I put a cursor lets say on M30, it s indicated as a vertical box on lower TFs , or as a line on higher TFs, so one can see PA inside that M30 bar on M5 or whichever other TF one wishes to examine that PA. That also applies to fibs, also useful with significant WRB, useful for beginners, as experienced traders see these things without too much drawn fibs, or other objects. Wishing all a great weekend, 2be

--- 帖子 #17994 ---
I am sure things will work out for you when you look at profits, and compare over all the ratio of exerted effort versus result. Personally I agree with what Strat has posted on the subject of trading more than one instrument. This is a very subjective practised opinion, and other traders have different approach. I can only drive one car at a given moment, though it does not mean I do not have or drive other vehicles. Not that long ago when there was the possibility of pit trading, trader has been limited to trading in a given pit, when profitable, there was no need to look or go to other pits, when loosing, there was nothing else but to leave the floor or become a clerk, or a message boy if the person was good enough in doing that. John Murphy in 2004 has written Intermarket Analysis, after he wrote Technical Analysis of the financial markets, in 1990,both books still well worth reading. Intermarket Analysis draws attention to the flow of capital between four different groups of financial instruments, stocks, bonds, commodities and currencies. One can add to it crypto and the real estate as different groups, though very interconnected with the previous four. For the last 30+ years I have been involved in real estate, very often as a back burner activity due to time limitation and the urgency induced by other projects. I am writing the above with the intention to point out that different groups, or classes of instruments demand precision and a mix of that same skills and in addition a different set of skills particular to a given class, or even particular to a different instrument in a given class. I have started trading indices, FTSE and DOW, than moved to Forex including forex options, and now for a log time I trade only indices, mainly DOW. I also look at some other instruments in different classes in the overall analysis, but do not trade them. I would find it very demanding to trade other instruments with similar intensity, even though they are in that same class. Trading different instruments in different groups are too demanding for me. That does not mean I will never buy gold or silver coin, or bar. Where I live in the UK, a reasonable property years ago would cost about 2kg of gold, now that same property is at least 5 to 6 kg of gold, not including the yield the property has provided over these many years, which is very substantial (this yield also can be measured in a number of 1kg gold bars often well above the current price) one can do the maths on that. Different classes, different instruments, different time frames, demands specific skills and perspective. Is the real estate unique, not really, some made it work well for them others have not. Lots of my close friends in the US are happy with 401k, other are also happy with investments in other instruments, and some are happy missing it all together. For me it is a high time for espresso and back to the marina when the lady parked on the grass is in need of attention, before we put her back in the water where she belongs. Happy trading, 2be Edit: Hi bistolis, I have written the above and posted it without knowing you have made your last post. Without trying one would not gain the experience. Good trades to you!!

--- 帖子 #18121 ---
Using volume: Attached Image (click to enlarge) 1 is huge buying volume BUT the candle is RED meaning that the sellers are stronger than those coming in to buy - this is probably profit taking at the end of that swing. 2 is above average buying volume coming in BUT the candles are small meaning the buyers are not sufficient to take out the sellers and usually indicates a pull back. 3 and after is selling volume greater than buying volume meaning the sellers are really strong and determined to take PRICE lower. 4 is huge selling volume usually signifying exhaustion meaning that many sellers are taking profit. 5 is a second exhaustion candle meaning that the remaining sellers are taking profit. 6 is higher than previous buying volume meaning that buyers are beginning to outnumber remaining sellers and is first sign coupled with PASR that this down swing may be finished. 7 is huge buying volume outnumbering remaining sellers and that an upswing is in place but NOT a change of trend - yet.

part 1/2 Hello Friends The recent discussions around the higher time frames &amp; the beginning of a new month has encouraged me to share my thoughts and what I would like to see eventuate in the index future markets for the month of September First of all, when I say "Index Futures" I am referring specifically to the ES and NQ CME contracts which are positively correlated 96% of the time. Intermarket correlation insights can be found here Here is the monthly chart of the 2 x contracts as at Sept 1st, 2024 Attached Image (click to enlarge) It doesn't take Dr Joe (a rocket scientist) to suggest that we are bullish. however, lets dig a little bit deeper and read the price action candle by candle April , both pairs create the middle candle of a 3-bar swing low formation June , both pairs "displace" higher, out of a small consolidation, printing a new all time high July , ES closes "UP" and confirms a bullish imbalance. (July's low "gapped" up from May's high, due to an imbalance of buy orders) as shown by the open portion between the two green lines. These imbalances give us a clue that deep pockets are participating. NQ closes "DOWN". This is a "crack" in two highly corelated assets and gives us a clue that a retracement could be under way... August , Both assets make a deep retracement. NQ makes a lower low, however ES fails to do so... another "crack" in correlation and a clue that these markets are still very much under accumulation. The rapid retracement (aka manipulation) lower, shown by the wicks serves two purposes 1. Spook out longs 2. Entice new shorts to chase the move lower This is perfect ^ for large volume traders (smart money) who need large sums of counter party, to pair longs On August 5th, the big big boss (my wife), who knows nothing (or even cares) about the markets, warned me that "the stock market was crashing" . (God bless her!) The very same day NQ happened to dip below (and reject) a level where long term bullish trend traders are likely trailing stops General public sentiment which opposes a trade thesis + a crack in correlation + discounted liquidity, at a higher time frame key level is some very nice confluence! ES is clearly the upside leader here. Therefore any longs I take will probably be in that market whilst NQ will be favored for shorts With this analysis, in part 2 ill discuss just HOW I plan to trade September, WHAT ill be looking for and WHEN ill be looking for it TBC...

part 2/2 Scenario 1/3 - This is my favored scenario for September. Ill pre-empt by saying that unfortunately, as we all know... the market does not care what we, as traders want and we have to be very careful falling in love with a bias, and marrying a narrative as it can make you do silly things! to get around this we can use time, price and a narrative to create mile markets along the way that either validate or invalidate the thesis Attached Image (click to enlarge) So - if I'm bullish on the monthly, Id expect it to expand higher... What would that look like at the end of the month ? A bullish up-close candle with ideally a small wick below the open and a small wick above the close (see diagram above ^) If you go back and have a look at all the bullish up close candles you will see that most of them will have a small wick below the open price, and a small wick above the close, this insight can help us tremendously to predict when and where turning points "should" occur if this scenario is to play out ... Therefore, our first mile marker for scenario #1 is the lower wick, it must be shallow and it must occur in either week 1 or early during week 2 As a smart money trader, ideally during bullish expansions we want to position ourselves below the open price, inside the wick. Conversely, we want to unload our positions in the upper wick to less informed speculators, profiting on the displacement made in the printing of the body Now, if we split the monthly candle into 4 x weekly candles we can build a narrative as to how each week "should" print within the month... Week 1 It would be fair to say that in order to create a low below the open price, week 1 could be bearish. In fact, this is what we want to see... a drop below the open price (but not to low ) . A run higher, straight out the gates on week 1, without putting in any low first would be another invalidation for this scenario. A text book week 1 would be a drop below the open, lethargic side ways price action ( smart money building a book ), then a run on the lows of the range creating the low of the month Week 2 Bullish expansion week, basically a fractal version of the same scenario. ie Monday / Tuesday: range, stop hunt, low of week, small wick, Thurs / Friday high of week etc. note : If price is yet to trade through the monthly open, we want displacement through it (yellow box), and then for it to provide support Week 3 repeat of week 2 Week 4 reverse the logic of week 1 Final thoughts. We can also use the economic calendar as a tool to help validate the thesis. Generally speaking, the five largest volatility drivers are... - NFP - CPI - FOMC - PPI - PCE I do not care what the numbers are (good or bad) but I expect volatility and therefore these reports "should" create either turning points or large displacement (see diagram ^) we can use the calendar as our road map for the month. Interesting how we had a bank holiday on Monday and Friday we have NFP right ? I have 3 of these scenarios, I can share the other two if anyone is interested, they are all fractal for example, I am an intraday trader, I try to catch daily expansions buying the low / high of the day in either London open or equities open with the goal of catching the daily range, selling at around 3.30 pm EST with an intraday sized stop loss and when I'm lucky additional pyramid entries Ill leave it here with a quote by the man himself Attached Image (click to enlarge)

Is one more relevant than the other? Difficult to say. The one here which you are on is more current and has the latest posts and my heart and soul went into the first thread but I tried my best to pass everything over from that old thread into this one. Maybe those who have read both can give you some enlightenment. It seems you already have a good understanding of PA and Market Structure so what I "suggest" is keep what "works" for you from that and augment it with the added PASR strategy. I notice you refer to "pin bars" which is a pet hate for me because "pin bars" are more often than not "Bond Bars"! All "pin bars" are NOT created equal which is why PASR separates them into SHOOTING STARS and HAMMERS with clear defined qualifications. Also, PASR has clear rules on qualifying "Swings". This thread lost most of it's subscribers because I switched to trading M1 Forex and then, M1 &amp; M5 Futures, BUT, what those who left this thread (longer time frame traders) did not UNDERSTAND, was that because the Market is Fractal, the reasons for taking trades (PASR Set Ups) is STILL valid and had they studied those trades would have seen that they were there on whichever time frame was their choice for their trades. Yes, the higher the time frame, the more reliable are the technicals and their analysis BUT even on 15 seconds, a Hammer is still a Hammer, a Shooting Star is still a Shooting Star, a BEOB is still a BEOB, a BEEB is still a BEEB, a CONTROL BAR is still a CONTROL BAR, Support is still Support, Resistance is still Resistance, Supply is still Supply, Demand is still demand etc. Having said all that NOTHING is perfect in trading as the Market does what it needs to do to satisfy it's goals so we just trade our "edge" with tight Risk and Money Management and move on from any losses.

--- 帖子 #18458 ---
You're correct with your WCC since it closed outside the previous WCC. However one thing about WCCs is that their size can be significant in understanding what is going on. What I mean here is that small weekly candles following large candles have the probability of not finishing the week as a control candle. So what I watch for is false breaks of WCCs using daily candles to close back within the previous WCC. In this case the two bearish daily candles that formed at the top of the new WCC provided a potential opportunity for a reasonably low risk short entry.

--- 帖子 #18459 ---
I was hoping someone would comment on my post regarding weekly control candles. However it doesn't appear that this is going to happen so here is an updated explanation of weekly control candles. Attached is the NZDUSD weekly chart with the last WCC highlighted. The marked WCC was in force until we got the first close outside of its range. There has been no new one formed because the requirement is that a weekly candle is followed by the next one closing within its range. So at the moment price has retraced back into the most recent one.

--- 帖子 #18460 ---

--- 帖子 #18461 ---
In case we have an opening gap outside the wcc how is it considered? Taking into consideration only the closures is it ignored for the identification of a new wcc? Is it correct?

--- 帖子 #18462 ---
Forget closes and opens when looking at WCC formations. So in your example the WCC that is in force remains in force since there has been no weekly close outside of its range. IF there is a new weekly close outside of its range, that removes it as a WCC. However the candle that closed outside of the WCC is not a new WCC. In order for that candle to form a WCC, the following week candle must close within its range.

--- 帖子 #18468 ---
You need to read again because this candle did close outside of the existing WCC range but until it has a anew weekly close outside of its range it is not a control candle. And since it did not get a weekly close within its range it was never a control candle. There seems to be a lot of confusion as to what a control candle is................

--- 帖子 #18469 ---
Regarding the weekly candles in the box. Going from left to right. The first green candle in the box became a WCC because it's Opening or Closing Main Body is outside of the Hgh/Low range of the green candle to it's left. So from the formation of this new green candle for price action within the next 7 DAYS it is the WCC. Then at the end of the week we look at the range of the new Weekly candle which is red and we notice that its main body did not close outside of the H/L range of the prior green candle . So the green candle continues to be the WCC. And we trade for 7 more days noting the range of the green candle.. the first one in the box. The next candle is green BUT it's Main Body does not close outside of the range of the first green candle so it cannot be a WCC. We trade another 7 days using the range of the first green candle in the box. The next green candle has a Main Body range that Does Close Outside of the range of the first green one SO It Becomes the New WCC . And we trade for the next 7 days using the range of this new WCC. The next weekly candle (doji) Main Body appears to me to close just outside of the prior week's candle range. So the doji Now Becomes the new WCC. And we use it's range to trade for the next 7 days. The last bar (red) Main Body closes outside of the range of the doji .. so it now becomes the New WCC. And so it goes.
